role.title: Sr. Director, Operations
role.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

role.title: Plant Manager Job
role.description:
Arkema's Birdsboro, PA site is seeking a Plant Manager (PM) with a proven track record of change management, people leadership and continuous improvement. The PM has direct responsibility for the overall operation of the Birdsboro plant. This position is responsible for the Birdsboro sites Replacement Asset Value (RAV) of approximately $120 million (original purchase cost of approximately $65 million), Replacement Plant Earnings (RPE) of approximately $12 million, annual variable costs exceeding $75 million (including monomers), and annual CAPEX of $4-5 million.

This position has 6 direct reports, each in a site leadership role and indirect responsibility for all other hourly and salaried employees. Birdsboro is a union site.

The PM has full P/L responsibility and provides leadership, direction, and management for all aspects of the plant’s manufacturing operations. The PM assists in the creation of the organization’s vision and growth strategies and executes the business and operations plans to achieve revenue, profit, and performance targets while continuing the plant’s record of success and high levels of safety and customer service.. 
 
The Plant Manager directly supports Plant Staff to manage activities and lead continued improvement in the areas of Operations, Maintenance, Human Resources, Engineering, Accounting, Purchasing, Quality, and Laboratories. The PM possesses a strong, working knowledge of and ensures compliance with; external regulatory requirements, industry best practices, and internal policies and procedures (specifically capital, accounting, purchasing, and HES).
 
 
**Essential Duties & Responsibilities with % Breakdown:** 
Safety and Environment – 20% 
HSE responsibilities include but are not restricted to those outlined in Leadership expectations such as reporting any incident in a timely manner. 

* Ensures plant is in full compliance with Arkema guidance and directives along with all applicable regulations.
* Foster a culture of Safety as a core plant value.
* Directly participates in core Arkema programs such as BBS.

Operations – 50% 
Ensures that safe operating procedures and practices are in place and followed. Ensures that mechanical integrity of all plants is maintained or improved to allow safe and efficient operation. Ensures that the plant produces at volumes to meet demand requirements set forth in S&OP plans. Ensures that adequate training is provided for a safe and efficient plant operations. 
Human Resources – 10% 
Works with site HR to see that employee activities related to hiring, promotion, layoff, salary, etc. are handled professionally. Provides an atmosphere for open communication between all employees. 
Financial–10% 
Directly accountable to prepare various budgets (fixed, variable and capex) then monitors and controls to ensure these budgets are met. 
Others: 10% 
o Communication: direct contact with both internal and external stakeholders 

* Mentoring/Coaching: Develop close working relationships with plant personnel and places a strong focus on improving both individual and team performance supporting programs such as SMART

**Minimum Qualifications and Education Required** 
Min Years of Experience 

* Minimum of 15 years of progressive manufacturing experience in plant operations, process design, and engineering, preferably in both a large and small-size integrated process manufacturing company

Education and area of focus 

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering required.

 
Certifications/Trainings: 
Lean or Six Sigma certification preferred

role.title: Director of Product Engineering (NPI
role.description:
Kauffman Engineering is seeking a highly strategic and hands-on leader to build and scale the product engineering capability across the full lifecycle from customer technical requirements and RFQ support through New Product Introduction (NPI), APQP, PPAP, and launch readiness.

This role provides strategic and operational leadership for Quoting, New Product Launch and other related product and manufacturing engineering activities such as ECN’s and the like. This leadership role ensures engineering execution is disciplined, scalable, and aligned with operational readiness. The Director of Product Engineering plays a critical role in reducing execution risk to NPI programs, improving launch success (Accuracy, Cost, Quality, Speed, Customer Experience), and ensuring the company can support growth without compromising quality, delivery, or margin.

**Key Responsibilities:**

Quoting Engineering

* Ensure technical feasibility, cost assumptions, risks, and manufacturability considerations are incorporated into all quotes.
* Lead a cross-functional team to improve the speed and accuracy of the quoting process through process improvement and technology adoption.
* Ensure accurate engineering input into cost models, BOM assumptions, labor estimates, and tooling requirements.
* Challenge quoting assumptions to identify cost and improvement opportunities in Operations and the Supply Chain.
* Maintain a current view of the capabilities and capacity of each manufacturing site to make informed decisions when allocating quotes and programs.
* Establish a formal feedback loop that brings production and launch performance data back into quoting standards and assumptions.

Product Engineering

* Lead all New Product Introduction (NPI) engineering activities across all plants, including the onboarding of new customers and programs.
* Own NPI on-time delivery (samples, PPAP submissions, and first production run) and program introduction lead time, leading cross-functional teams to build a predictable, fast, and reliable launch process.
* Ensure NPI teams fully execute APQP activities across all phases, including PPAP readiness and launch execution.
* Lead continuous improvement projects that apply a lean, end-to-end approach from quoting through NPI, improving safety, speed to market, quality, delivery, and cost.
* Manage NPI timelines, resource planning (including equipment capacity, tooling, and other resources), and execution to ensure on-time, on-budget launches.
* Review and present NPI status, risks, and readiness to senior management on a regular cadence.
* Drive consistent launch governance, gate reviews, and escalation processes across sites, including confirming that initial production orders are manufacturable.

Process Standardization & Systems Development

* Develop, implement, and maintain standardized engineering processes.
* Reduce reliance on tribal knowledge by establishing repeatable workflows, documentation standards, and control points.
* Improve consistency and quality of engineering outputs across plants and teams.
* Identify and mitigate technical and execution risks early in the product lifecycle.
* Evaluate and adopt better engineering methodologies and tools, and strengthen cross‑functional coordination.

Plant Integration & Cross‑Functional Collaboration

* Act as a key engineering partner to plant leadership to support execution, troubleshooting, and readiness of new program launches.
* Drive alignment between engineering and operations to ensure manufacturability, capacity readiness, and process capability as part of the launch hand-off to the manufacturing sites.
* Support plant teams during launches, ramp‑ups, and significant engineering changes.
* Collaborate with Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and Operations to ensure integrated execution.
* Lead engineering CAPEX planning for new programs and long‑term capacity needs.

Talent Leadership & Capability Building

* Assess current engineering organization structure, skills, and capacity.
* Develop and execute plans to upgrade engineering capability through hiring, development, and role clarity.
* Lead, coach, and develop the engineering team, setting clear expectations and holding team members accountable for results.
* Build a future‑state product engineering organization capable of supporting multiple concurrent launches.
* Promote a culture of accountability, discipline, and continuous improvement.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Industrial, Mechanical, Electrical, or equivalent preferred); advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum 7–10 years of engineering experience in manufacturing or industrial environments.
* Demonstrated engineering experience in the design and manufacture of wire harness components in a high-mix, low-volume environment.
* Demonstrated experience leading engineering teams and managing engineering functions, preferably across multiple sites.
* Proven experience with APQP, PPAP, and launch execution in production environments.
* Strong knowledge of Core Tools (APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, MSA).
* Experience driving engineering standardization and process improvement.
* Understanding of material and labor costing, manufacturability, and cost drivers.
* Project management and cross‑functional leadership experience.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, and Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* Strong communication, organizational, and problem‑solving skills.

**Work Environment:**

* This is an Hybrid position at our Reynosa, MX facility.
* Ability and willingness to travel to U.S. and Mexico manufacturing locations (approximately 25–40%) to provide on-site plant support as business needs require.

**Compensation & Benefits**

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $135k-$155k. Actual compensation decisions are dependent on the minimum requirements outlined in the job description, qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location, external market conditions, as well as internal equity.

Our company benefits provide full-time employees with a wide variety of benefits to meet the needs of our diverse workforce. We offer the following benefits: health, dental, and vision insurance, prescription drug benefits, flexible spending accounts, voluntary life insurance, AD&D insurance and a healthy incentive credit. We also provide company paid life insurance and short-term and long-term disability insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO and 9 paid holidays. Annual Company Performance Bonus Program based on achievement of annual goals.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

Kauffman is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to a diverse workforce, providing equal employment and advancement opportunities to all qualified individuals. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

*This employer participates in the E-Verify program.*

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Are you able to travel to visit and provide support to our Reynosa, Mexico facility?
* Do you have any experience with Arcadia ECAD, Cadonix or Cableteque software? (If yes, or if you have experience with relevant Harness design tools, briefly explain)

Experience:

* Wire Harness Manufacturing: 1 year (Preferred)

Language:

* English and Spanish fluently (Preferred)

Willingness to travel:

* 50% (Preferred)

role.title: Sr. Director, Operations
role.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

role.title: Sr. Director, Operations
role.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

role.title: Sr. Plant Manager - Painesville, OH
role.description:
**Location:** Painesville, OH

**Employment Type:** Exempt, Full-Time, Onsite

 
**Shape the Future with Us.**

At Lubrizol, we’re bringing to life the chemistry behind clean water, efficient transportation, reliable infrastructure, critical medicines, and the products people rely on every day through science, sustainability, and a culture of inclusion.

As part of our global team, you’ll be empowered to make a real impact - on your career, your community, and the world around you.

 

**How You’ll Make an Impact**

The Sr. Plant Manager leads the Painesville manufacturing site and is accountable for safe, reliable, and effective performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, people, capital, asset reliability, and continuous improvement.

 

This role sets the site’s strategy, builds a culture of safety and accountability, develops organizational capability, and partners across functions to deliver operational and business priorities.

* Champion personal and process safety, environmental performance, regulatory compliance, operational discipline, and risk reduction.
* Set and execute the site strategy and annual operating plan across safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, people, and continuous improvement.
* Lead Manufacturing, HSE&S, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Logistics, and other site functions using performance metrics and effective management systems.
* Strengthen process safety, mechanical integrity, asset reliability, preventive maintenance, and overall equipment effectiveness.
* Apply Lubrizol standards and operating systems, including ISO 9001 and RC14001, to reduce risk, standardize work, and improve performance.
* Manage operating and capital budgets, ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, and within budget.
* Drive productivity, cost, quality, automation, and continuous improvement while protecting safety, reliability, and customer service.
* Build an inclusive, accountable, and engaged organization through talent development, succession planning, workforce planning, and constructive employee relations.
* Maintain a visible site presence and communicate effectively with employees at all levels.
* Partner across Operations, Supply Chain, Procurement, Commercial, R&D, and support functions to meet business and customer needs and share best practices.

 

**Required Qualifications that Enable Your Success**

* Safety-first leader with demonstrated success building safety culture and improving performance.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field; Chemical Engineering preferred.
* At least 10 years of chemical plant and/or manufacturing experience, including 5 years of progressive manufacturing leadership.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing operations, process safety, risk management, environmental and safety regulations, and asset reliability.
* Proven ability to lead, influence, develop teams, and engage employees at all levels in a matrixed organization.
* Strong problem-solving, continuous improvement, financial, and business skills, including operating and capital budget management.
* Effective communication and relationship-building skills, with the agility to learn, adapt, lead change, and challenge the status quo.
* Proficiency with Microsoft tools and flexibility to work outside normal hours as needed.

 

**Preferred Qualifications that Drive You Forward**

* Advanced engineering degree or MBA.
* Leadership experience in a complex chemical manufacturing facility.
* Knowledge of SAP.
* Project/change management and Lean or Operational Excellence experience.

 

**Your Work Environment.**

At Lubrizol, we’re committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and empowering environment where you can do your best work—whether in a lab, on the production floor, or in a hybrid office setting. Depending on your role, your work environment may include:

 

* Standing, walking, or operating equipment for extended periods.
* Working in a lab or manufacturing setting with appropriate PPE provided.
* Use of computers and digital tools in an office or hybrid environment.
* Occasional lifting or movement of materials.
* Adherence to rigorous safety protocols and ergonomic standards.

 

We continuously invest in our facilities and technologies to ensure they support your well-being, productivity, and growth. If you require reasonable accommodation, we are committed to working with you to ensure an inclusive and accessible experience.

 

**Benefits that Empower You.**

* Competitive salary with performance-based bonus plans
* 401(k) match + Age-Weighted Defined Contribution
* Comprehensive medical, dental & vision coverage
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Paid holidays, vacation, and parental leave
* Flexible work environment
* Learning and development opportunities
* Career and professional growth
* Inclusive culture and vibrant community engagement 
 Learn more at benefits.lubrizol.com!

 

**Lubrizol: Imagined for Life. Enabled by Science. ™ Delivered by You.**

 

For nearly 100 years, The Lubrizol Corporation, a Berkshire Hathaway company, has been at the forefront of innovation to enhance everyday life, advance mobility, and make the modern world work better. Our specialty chemistry solutions—from engine oils, performance coatings, and skincare to medical devices and plumbing systems —are powered by the expertise, passion, and commitment of people like you. We tackle the world’s toughest challenges with science-based solutions, deeply understanding our customers to deliver innovative chemistry and differentiated value.

 

Our inclusive culture, dedication to safety, and incredible global talent drive our success. Our solutions meet the evolving needs of the modern world—brought to life by science and, most importantly, delivered by you. Whether you're in the lab, on the production floor, or in the office, you'll be part of a team around the world that empowers you to think boldly, drive results, and contribute to solutions that shape a better, more sustainable future.

 

**We win because of you. Let’s build the future together.**

#LI-AM1

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

role.title: Director of Quality Management
role.description:
The Massachusetts Department of Mental Health (DMH) is seeking an experienced and dedicated Director of Quality Management to lead quality improvement, performance monitoring, and risk management efforts across its Northeast Area (NEA). DMH is committed to improving the lives of individuals with mental health needs by providing access to quality treatment, rehabilitation, and community-based services that support recovery, independence, and well-being. In this important leadership role, you will help ensure that programs and services consistently meet established standards of care while identifying opportunities to strengthen service delivery and improve outcomes for the individuals and families served. Working closely with Area leadership, clinical professionals, and community providers, you will help establish a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and responsive, person-centered care.

As the Director of Quality Management, you will oversee a broad range of quality assurance, performance improvement, utilization management, and risk management activities that directly influence the effectiveness of mental health services throughout the Northeast Area. You will lead a team of professionals, collaborate with internal and external stakeholders, and use data, investigations, and performance evaluations to guide meaningful improvements in service quality and organizational operations. This position offers an opportunity to influence policies and practices, address complex operational challenges, and contribute to strategic decisions that strengthen the delivery of mental health services. The selected candidate will play an essential role in ensuring that DMH programs remain responsive to the needs of the communities they serve while advancing the Department's commitment to high-quality, accessible, and effective mental health care across the Commonwealth.

***Duties and Responsibilities (these duties are a general summary and not all inclusive):***

* Develop, implement, and oversee comprehensive quality management programs and performance improvement initiatives designed to strengthen service delivery, improve client outcomes, and enhance organizational effectiveness across the Northeast Area.

* Lead the monitoring and evaluation of Area-funded programs and contracted providers to assess service quality, identify performance concerns, and ensure adherence to established standards, policies, and regulatory requirements.

* Direct the review and analysis of critical incidents, complaints, and service delivery concerns, ensuring appropriate fact-finding activities, timely responses, and implementation of corrective actions.

* Coordinate contract monitoring and performance review activities for community-based services, including Adult Community Clinical Services (ACCS), to evaluate provider performance and identify opportunities for improvement.

* Establish quality management priorities, performance measures, and reporting processes to assess organizational progress, identify trends, and support informed management decisions.

* Oversee risk management activities, including identifying potential service delivery risks, evaluating organizational vulnerabilities, and recommending preventive and corrective measures.

* Support the Performance Improvement and Corrective Action Planning activities, including identifying performance issues, supporting PIP and CAP development by providers, and monitoring progress. Participate in identifying escalation protocols and support communication and planning between the Northeast Area Office and DMH Central Office.

* Direct utilization management and review activities to evaluate the appropriateness, effectiveness, and quality of services provided to individuals receiving DMH-supported care.

* Support setting metrics/targets for quality improvement at both the Northeast Area, at the Site Offices, and in partnership with providers.

* Develop, review, and recommend Area-wide policies, procedures, and operational practices that promote regulatory compliance, consistency, accountability, and continuous quality improvement. Advocate for needed policies or procedures as needed/warranted.

* Lead and coordinate emergency preparedness planning activities, working with Area leadership, Site staff, and community partners to strengthen organizational readiness and response capabilities.

* Supervise and support assigned quality management, risk management, utilization management, and administrative staff, providing direction, establishing priorities, and promoting professional development and accountability.

* Collaborate with Area leadership, clinical teams, program directors, contracted providers, and DMH Central Office representatives to address complex service delivery challenges, coordinate improvement efforts, and promote consistent quality standards.

* Prepare and present quality management findings, performance analyses, and recommendations to leadership, using data from multiple information systems to guide planning, support corrective actions, and improve organizational performance.

* As a member of the Northeast Area leadership team, actively participate in NEA REI activities, including chairing/co-chairing committees and coordinating event attendance.

* Support procurement and re-procurement of contracts for the NEA by participating in review committees as needed/warranted and appropriate.

 

***Preferred Qualifications:***

* Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and managing quality assurance and performance improvement programs within behavioral health, mental health, healthcare, or human services organizations.

* Strong understanding of quality management principles, regulatory compliance requirements, risk management practices, and performance monitoring methodologies applicable to healthcare and community-based service systems.

* Knowledge of the Massachusetts Department of Mental Health service delivery system, including community-based mental health programs, contracted provider networks, and services supporting individuals with complex behavioral health needs.

* Proven ability to lead and supervise multidisciplinary teams, establish operational priorities, manage competing demands, and foster a collaborative, accountable, and results-oriented work environment.

* Skilled in analyzing complex data, interpreting performance indicators, identifying service delivery trends, and translating findings into practical recommendations for organizational improvement.

* Experience with critical incident reviews, complaint investigations, fact-finding procedures, corrective action planning, and processes designed to strengthen client safety and service quality.

* Familiarity with contract monitoring, provider performance evaluations, utilization management, and oversight of publicly funded healthcare or human services programs.

* Demonstrated capacity to develop and implement policies, procedures, and quality improvement initiatives while balancing regulatory requirements, operational considerations, and the needs of individuals receiving services.

* Excellent written and verbal communication, analytical thinking, problem-solving, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to prepare reports, present findings, facilitate training, and build consensus among diverse stakeholders.

* Track record of successfully coordinating cross-functional initiatives, collaborating with senior leadership and external providers, and using multiple data systems to support strategic planning, emergency preparedness, and continuous quality improvement.

Proficiency with Tableau and Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Word, Excel, Outlook, SharePoint and Teams.

**About the Department of Mental Health (DMH):**

The Department of Mental Health assures and provides access to services and supports to meet the mental health needs of individuals of all ages, enabling them to live, work and participate in their communities. The Department establishes standards to ensure effective and culturally competent care to promote recovery. The Department sets policy, promotes self-determination, protects human rights and supports mental health training and research. Total Compensation: As an employee of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts you are offered a great career opportunity influencing a wide-spectrum of services to the diverse populations we serve — but it is more than a paycheck. The State ' s total compensation package features an outstanding set of employee benefits which you Should consider towards your overall compensation. including: - 75% state paid medical insurance premium - Reasonable Dental and Vision Plans - Flexible Spending Account and Dependent Care Assistance programs - Low cost basic and optional life insurance - Retirernent Savings: State Employees ' Pension and a Deferred Compensation 457(b) plan 12 paid holidays per year and competitive Sick, Vacation and Personal Time - Tuition Benefit for employee and spouse at state colleges and universities - Long-Tem Disability and Extended Illness program participation options - Incentive-based Wellness Programs - Professional Development and Continuing Education opportunities - Qualified for Public Service Student Loan Forgiveness Pre.Hire Process: A criminal background check Will be completed on the recommended candidate as required by the regulations set forth by the Executive Office Of Health and Human Services prior to the candidate being hired. For more information, please Visit http://www.mass.gov/hhs/cori and click on •Information for Job Applicants. • Education, licensure and certifications will be verified in accordance with the Human Resources Division ' s Hiring Guidelines. Education and license/certification information provided by the selected candidate(s) is subject to the Massachusetts Public Records Law and may be published on the Commonwealth ' s website. If you would like to request an ADA or religious accommodation, please click on the link and complete the Reasonable Accommodation Online Request Form. For questions. please contact the Executive Office of Health and Human Services Office of Human Resources at 1-800-510-4122 and select option #2. For questions regarding this requisition. please contact Carol Duggan at carol.duggan@mass.gov or can (978)851-7321 Ext 2395.

**Qualifications**
------------------

MINIMUM ENTRANCE REQUIREMENTS:

 

Applicants must have at least (A) five (5) years of full-time or, equivalent part-time, professional, administrative, supervisory, or managerial experience in business administration, business management, public administration, public management, clinical administration or clinical management of which (B) at least one (1) year must have been in a project management, supervisory or managerial capacity or (C) any equivalent combination of the required experience and substitutions below.

 

Substitutions:

 

I. A certificate in a relevant or related field may be substituted for one (1) year of the required (A) experience.

 

II. A Bachelor's degree in a related field may be substituted for two (2) years of the required (A) experience.

 

III. A Graduate degree in a related field may be substituted for three (3) years of the required (A) experience.

 

IV. A Doctorate degree in a related field may be substituted for four (4) years of the required (A) experience.

 

**Salary placement is determined by a combination of factors, including the candidate’s years of directly related experience and education, and alignment with our internal compensation structure as set forth by the Human Resources Division’s Hiring Guidelines. For all bargaining unit positions (non-management), compensation is subject to the salary provisions outlined in the applicable collective bargaining agreement and will apply to placement within the appropriate salary range.**

**Comprehensive Benefits**

When you embark on a career with the Commonwealth, you are offered an outstanding suite of employee benefits that add to the overall value of your compensation package. We take pride in providing a work experience that supports you, your loved ones, and your future.

Want the specifics? Explore our Employee Benefits and Rewards!

role.title: Director of Operations & Manufacturing Excellence
role.description:
Innovation, craftsmanship, and a customer-first mindset fuel our growth at Alloy Precision Technologies. Step into a role where your leadership elevates safety, quality, delivery, and cost—every day.

**A day in the role**
---------------------

Your morning begins with cross-functional huddles, aligning production, supply chain, maintenance, and planning on the day’s priorities. You review dashboards that track delivery promises, schedule adherence, inventory health, and quality metrics. Midday finds you on the floor diagnosing a throughput constraint, coaching leaders, and reinforcing safe work practices. In the afternoon, you refine the operating rhythm: standard work, real-time schedule visibility, and continuous improvement plans. You close the day mentoring team members and shaping the next wave of operational objectives that sharpen customer service and profitability.

**What you will lead**
----------------------

* End-to-end oversight of manufacturing operations, including production, supply chain, maintenance, production planning, and warehouse activities.
* Deployment of robust quality and efficiency standards that achieve performance targets and elevate product excellence.
* Ownership of safety leadership and environmental stewardship across all operations.
* Proactive resolution of production issues—investigating, analyzing, troubleshooting, and driving timely recovery plans.
* Design and implementation of on-time performance tracking to keep schedules visible and reliable, ensuring strong margins, responsive service, and consistent quality.
* Regular reporting on operational health, highlighting opportunities, risks, and results.
* Implementation of lean manufacturing and other flow/business process systems to reduce cost, improve quality, and increase profitability.
* Stronger cross-functional communication and collaboration with corporate teams and adjacent functions.
* Team building through mentoring, motivation, and effective delegation—empowering leaders to deliver results.
* Annual operating plans and programs that guide manufacturing, service, and distribution performance.
* Execution that meets or exceeds customer commitments and complies with AS9100 and all applicable regulations.
* Domestic and international travel as needed to support operations and customers.
* Additional assignments as directed by the President and Chief Executive Officer.

**Supervisory scope**
---------------------

* Direct supervision of group leaders, supply chain, and production planning; scope may evolve as the organization grows.
* Full-cycle people leadership aligned with APT policies and applicable laws: recruiting, hiring, onboarding, training, work assignment, performance evaluation, recognition, corrective action, issue resolution, and career development.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Industrial Management, Industrial Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering.
* 10+ years of manufacturing leadership experience; background in precision welding (TIG, laser, brazing, soldering), CNC/manual machining, and light assembly is advantageous.
* Strong digital fluency: Microsoft Office; experience with databases/ERP (e.g., Visual Manufacturing) and developing labor standards for cost structures is a plus.
* High energy, results orientation, confidence, and strong interpersonal influence; able to build rapport at all levels.
* Strategic, proactive, and persistent; comfortable juggling multiple projects and customers in a fast-paced setting.
* Adaptable and resilient within a dynamic, evolving culture; passionate about excellence and continuous improvement.
* Working knowledge of lean manufacturing required; Six Sigma experience is a plus.

role.title: Director, Contract Manufacturing Operations
role.description:
### **The Elevator Pitch**

Imagine the world you can help us build—one that leverages cutting-edge technology and innovative thinking to realize our vision of safer places to live, work, learn, and play. We are looking for a few more great minds to join our team as we continue to grow the world’s leading AI-enabled weapons detection company. 
 
If you join Evolv in this newly created position as our Director of Contract Manufacturing Operations, you will lead our outsourced manufacturing strategy and execution. You will work cross-functionally to ensure our contract manufacturing partners deliver high-quality products on time and at scale. As Evolv’s manufacturing operations lead, you will drive operational excellence, supplier performance, and production readiness while building a scalable manufacturing infrastructure.

### **What does success in the role look like?**

Execute and manage Evolv’s contract manufacturing strategy that supports scalability and cost-effectiveness. Specific responsibilities include product cost, manufacturing variances, and inventory management.

**Within the first 30 days you will:**

* Establish relationships with key internal stakeholders (Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal) and contract manufacturing partners.
* Conduct a comprehensive assessment of current outsourced manufacturing operations, identifying immediate risks and opportunities.
* Define initial KPIs for supplier performance, production efficiency, and cost metrics.
* Begin development of a scalable manufacturing operations roadmap aligned with company growth goals.
* Gain proficiency in internal systems including Salesforce, Arena PLM, and NetSuite.

**Within 90 days you will:**

* Implement a supplier performance dashboard with real-time metrics (e.g., on-time delivery rate, defect rate, throughput).
* Launch a pilot continuous improvement initiative with at least one contract manufacturer, targeting a 5–10% efficiency gain.
* Finalize and begin executing a cost-down strategy with measurable targets (e.g., reduce product cost by 3–5% over 6 months).
* Align production planning processes with demand forecasts to ensure 95%+ production continuity.
* Establish a cross-functional cadence for reporting operational performance to executive leadership.

**Within the first 12 months you will:**

* Achieve a sustained 98%+ on-time delivery rate across all contract manufacturing partners.
* Reduce manufacturing variances and inventory discrepancies by at least 15% through process optimization.
* Fully integrate manufacturing operations with Salesforce, Arena PLM, and NetSuite for end-to-end visibility.
* Build and lead a high-performing team (production planning, test engineering, repair/refurbishment) with clear roles and development plans.
* Launch a formal risk management program that proactively mitigates production disruptions, with quarterly risk assessments.
* Support at least one successful new product introduction with a seamless production ramp-up and zero major delays.
* Deliver quarterly executive reports with actionable insights and progress against strategic manufacturing goals.

### **The Work: What type of work will you be doing?**

You will have the opportunity to define and build the outsourced manufacturing function from the ground up. This role is both strategic and hands-on, requiring a balance of long-term planning and day-to-day execution.

**Strategic & Operational Leadership**

* Develop and execute a scalable outsourced manufacturing strategy aligned with company growth.
* Lead cross-functional initiatives to improve supplier performance and production readiness.
* Translate business goals into actionable manufacturing roadmaps and KPIs.
* Balance long-term strategic planning with hands-on operational execution. Work closely with internal stakeholders to forecast demand and ensure production continuity.

**Data-Driven Decision Making**

* Define and monitor supplier performance metrics such as on-time delivery, defect rates, and throughput.
* Analyze production data to identify trends, inefficiencies, and cost-saving opportunities.
* Align production planning with demand forecasts to ensure 95%+ production continuity.
* Use dashboards and reporting tools to communicate performance insights to executive leadership.

**Technical & Systems Proficiency**

* Gain proficiency and integrate operations with Salesforce, Arena PLM, and NetSuite for end-to-end visibility.
* Apply lean manufacturing and Six Sigma principles to reduce variances and optimize processes.
* Support new product introductions with seamless production ramp-up and zero major delays.
* Ensure compliance with contractual and regulatory requirements in manufacturing operations.

**Supplier & Partner Management**

* Manage top-tier contract manufacturers to meet contractual obligations and performance standards.
* Launch and oversee continuous improvement initiatives targeting 5–10% efficiency gains.
* Develop and execute cost-down strategies to reduce product costs by 3–5% over six months.
* Conduct quarterly risk assessments and implement mitigation plans to prevent production disruptions.

### **Compensation and Transparency Statement**

The base salary range for this full-time position is $160,000- $200,000. In addition to base salary, this role offers a competitive target bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. This range reflects our commitment to pay transparency and equity, in alignment with applicable state laws. Our compensation ranges are determined based on factors such as role, level, location, market benchmarks, and internal equity. The posted range represents the good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this role across U.S. locations. Actual compensation within the range will be based on the candidate’s skills, experience, education, and geographic location.

In accordance with state and local pay transparency laws—including those in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, New York, New Jersey, and others—we disclose salary ranges in all job postings and provide additional information upon request.

During the hiring process, your recruiter will share:

* The specific salary range for your preferred location
* A general overview of our benefits and equity offerings
* Insights into how compensation decisions are made, including factors that influence starting pay

We are committed to fair pay practices, and we regularly review our compensation programs to ensure they are competitive, equitable, and aligned with our values.

### **What is leadership like for this role?**

The Director of Contract Manufacturing Operations will report to Evolv’s Head of Supply Chain and Procurement. The initial focus will be on building a robust outsourced manufacturing infrastructure to support rapid growth and innovation. As the company scales, the operations team may expand to include program managers, production planners, and manufacturing engineers. We offer a collaborative, mission-driven environment where innovation thrives, careers grow, and every employee plays a vital role in protecting lives through technology.

### **Where is the role located?**

Our ideal candidate for this role is located in the Midwest near Chicago, IL or the Boston area. There is approximately 20% anticipated domestic travel required for supplier visits and Contract Manufacturing management.

 
 
**Benefits**

At Evolv, we’re on a mission to help make public spaces safer through innovative security technology. So, we're looking for future teammates who embody our values, people who:

* Do the right thing, always;
* Put people first'
* Own it;
* Win together; and continue to
* Be bold, stay curious.

**Our Benefits Include**:

* Equity as part of your total compensation package
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* A 401(k) plan (and 2% company match)
* Flexible Paid Time Off (PTO)- take the time you need to recharge, with manager approval and business needs in mind
* Quarterly stipend for perks and benefits that matter most to you
* Tuition reimbursement to support your ongoing learning and development
* Subscription to Calm

Evolv Technology (“Evolv”) is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We welcome and encourage diversity in the workplace, and all employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, disability, HIV Status, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, veteran status, or any other status protected by law in the locations where we operate. Evolv will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics.

Evolv is committed to offering an inclusive and accessible experience for all job seekers, including individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of the job application process, please connect with us at careers@evolvtechnology.com. 
 
Evolv participates in E-verify for all employees after the completion of Form I-9.

role.title: Head of Quality
role.description:
Head of Quality

**About Rite Stuff Foods:**

Rite Stuff Foods is a rapidly expanding, frozen appetizer and specialty potato product manufacturer in the United States. We offer a growing range of tasty finger foods which include twice baked potatoes, potato skins, battered and breaded wedges, fried and filled skins, breakfast bites, extruded products, cheese sticks and other assorted batter and breaded vegetables.

Rite Stuff Foods’ parent company, Frostkrone, is based in Rietberg, Germany. Frostkrone is a leading finger food manufacturer, with portfolio companies and manufacturing operations throughout Europe and the United States. We continue to explore expansion in North America and around the world. Our company is driven to innovate and delight consumers & customers worldwide, with high quality, good tasting food.

**Position Overview:**

Reporting to the Managing Director of Rite Stuff Foods, the Head of Quality serves as an important member of the Rite Stuff Foods leadership team and is responsible for establishing, leading, and maintaining a food safety and quality culture throughout the company. The incumbent will ensure adherence to all food safety & quality management programs in the company so that there is no risk to our customers, the general public, and our employees, and our product quality meets or exceeds expectations.

**Responsibilities:**

· Responsible for leading the Quality and Food Safety efforts in the company, and ensure highly disciplined compliance with all regulatory and company-defined food safety systems, procedures, and practices.

· Lead and manage a team of Quality and Food Safety Mangers and Technicians and empower them to take charge and embrace accountability.

· Collaborate with Operations management and with all senior leaders in the safe operation of the facility and driving a “safety first” culture.

· Carry out RCA (root cause analysis), where needed

· Lead preparation for and interaction with third party audits and auditors.

· Liaise closely with regulatory bodies, like the USDA, and key customer QA representatives.

· Ensure proper execution of product Food Safety and Quality testing and reporting.

· Lead the day-to-day implementation of HACCP, QMS, and other supporting pre-requisite programs to meet the SQF Food Safety standards, working closely with the SQF Practitioner.

· Lead the training and development of the Quality Assurance Technicians, scheduling and delegating tasks outlined in the Food Safety Plans, SOP manuals, and other supporting procedures, including monitoring and verification activities to assure products meet regulatory and customer standards.

· Management of the Non-Conforming Equipment and Product Program.

· Provide guidance, leadership, and assistance in problem solving efforts for SOP’s, GMP’s, Quality, Food Safety, and Process Improvement.

· Ensure compliance with FDA/USDA regulations.

· Ensure proper Product Specification management and Document Control management are in place and followed.

· Must have the desire to lead the team and company to the next level of Food Safety, quality and accountability.

· Coordinate recall program, initiate mock recalls, and update as needed

**Qualifications/Experience:**

· Bachelor of science in microbiology, food science or equivalent experience

· 7+ years Quality Assurance experience.

· 5+ years supervisory or management experience.

· Experience in frozen potato or appetizer industry is a plus

· Competent in leading and developing people

· Competent in Quality/Food Safety and Good Laboratory Practices

· Good understanding of hygienic design

· Theoretical and applied knowledge of HACCP/Food Safety Preventative Controls/SQF (or equivalent GFSI scheme)

· Development of SOP’s, Policies, Specifications, etc.

· Internal Auditing

· Microsoft Excel, Word, Access, PowerPoint

**Location:** Twin Falls, ID area (incumbent must live in the area)

**Benefits:**

Competitive Salary

Health, Dental, Vision, Life, & LTD Benefits

401(k)

Holidays, paid vacation, and sick days

Opportunity to build your career in a rapidly growing international company

**Status:**

Full-time

*The RSF Companies are equal employment opportunity employers. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.*

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Referral program
* Relocation assistance
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

**Plant Manager**

Beckley, WV, United States | req34508 Work Schedule: 1st Shift

* Coordinate daily production activities and distribution requirements, including local delivery routes and shuttle scheduling
* You will lead reliability, compliance, quality, and safety initiatives to meet governmental and environmental regulations Ensure temployees are trained and committed to Linde Safety and Quality systems, woring closely with the Compliance Manager to coordinate training
* Monitor production performance and manpower levels to maintain efficiency, anticipate problems, and develop contingencies
* Identify operational challenges and lead improvement efforts related to production processes, shift scheduling, and training; report progress and findings to plant management
* You will manage and escalate equipment and product quality issues, maintaining adequate inventory of production supplies and support 5S and Lean Projects and hazardous waste activities, continuously identifying ways to reduce plant operating costs through Operational Excellence strategies

**What makes you great**

* Bachelor's degree is preferred; high school diploma or GED is required in this role
* You have a minimum of five (5) years of experience in an industrial plant environment
* More than five (5+) years of experience in Driver, operations, distribution or quality roles
* You have at least three (3) years of experience leading and developing employees
* Willingness to work in a unionized Environment is required

**Why you will love working with us**

Linde is a leading global industrial gases and engineering company with 2025 sales of $34 billion. We live our mission of making our world more productive every day by providing high-quality solutions, technologies and services which are making our customers more successful and helping to sustain, decarbonize and protect our planet.
 
 
Linde serves a variety of end markets such as chemicals & energy, food & beverage, electronics, healthcare, manufacturing, metals and mining. Linde’s industrial gases and technologies are used in countless applications, enabling space exploration and launch technologies, delivering ultra-high-purity and specialty gases for semiconductor manufacturing, providing life-saving medical oxygen and enabling clean hydrogen production and carbon capture to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Linde also delivers state-of-the-art gas processing solutions to support customer growth, efficiency improvements and emissions reductions.

**What we offer you!**

At Linde, the sky is not the limit. If you’re looking to build a career where your work reaches beyond your job description and betters the people with whom you work, the communities we serve, and the world in which we all live, at Linde, your opportunities are limitless. Be Linde. Be Limitless. 
 
Linde offers competitive compensation and an outstanding benefits package. Enjoy access to health, dental, disability, and life insurance, paid holidays and vacation, an employee discount program, and opportunities for educational and professional growth. Additional compensation may vary depending on the position and organizational level. Build your future with us while making an impact every day!

**Have we inspired you? Let´s talk about it**

We are looking forward to receiving your complete application.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other reason prohibited by applicable law. 
 
Linde Gas & Equipment Inc. acts responsibly towards its shareholders, business partners, employees, society and the environment in every one of its business areas, regions and locations across the globe. Overview:

**WHO WE ARE**

As the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the nation's largest producer of clean and reliable energy, Constellation is focused on our purpose: lighting the way to a brilliant tomorrow for all. We have been the leader in clean energy production for more than a decade, and we are cultivating a workplace where our employees can grow, thrive, and contribute. Now integrated with Calpine, our portfolio includes 55 gigawatts of capacity from nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar facilities, with the generating capacity to power the equivalent of 27 million homes. 
 
Our culture and employee experience make it clear: We are powered by passion and purpose. Together, we're creating healthier communities and a cleaner planet, and our people are the driving force behind our success. At Constellation, you can build a fulfilling career with opportunities to learn, grow and make an impact. By doing our best work and meeting new challenges, we can accomplish great things. Join us in meeting the country's energy needs today and tomorrow.

**TOTAL REWARDS**

Constellation offers an extensive selection of benefits and rewards to help our employees thrive professionally and personally. We provide competitive compensation and a wide-range of benefits that support both employees and their families, helping them prepare for the future. In addition to highly competitive salaries, eligible employees are offered a bonus program, 401(k) with company match, employee stock purchase program; comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits, including robust wellbeing programs; disability and life insurance benefits; paid time off for vacation, holidays, and sick days; and much more.

Expected salary range of $189,000 to $210,000, varies based on experience, along with comprehensive benefits package that includes bonus and 401(k).

**Constellation is looking for a Plant Manager at our Geysers location in Middletown, California.**

Responsibilities:

**PRIMARY PURPOSE OF POSITION**

Manage and oversee the safe, efficient and reliable operation of fossil or hydro station(s). Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements, applicable industry technical standards and company policies. Operate the plant(s) in a manner that minimizes the cost of generation and maximizes profitability while maintaining the long-term viability of the station assets.

**PRIMARY DUTIES AND ACCOUNTABILITIES**

 

* Ensure standards are established and implemented to provide a safe work environment.
* Effectively manage all resources to ensure generation of electricity in a timely and reliable manner at the direction of the Power Team.
* Maintain a positive work environment and good employee relations. Provide guidance for employee development opportunities and timely feedback regarding performance.
* Serve as a change agent for business initiatives, while assuring the human element is understood and considered
* Manage the station O&M and capital budgets to minimize costs and maximize profitability while ensuring the long-term viability of the assets.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state and local regulatory requirements and maintain environmental stewardship.
* Maintain effective community relations to promote a positive image of the Company.
* Perform all other duties as assigned.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* BS in engineering or business
* Minimum of 10 years professional experience
* Minimum of 8 years power plant (or related) experience
* Minimum of 5 years supervisory/managerial experience
* Professional or technical level experience in a technical role at a power plant
* Operations
* At least 2 of the following: Corporate/Staff, Engineering, Maintenance, or Outage
* Leadership assessment required

 
Qualifications:

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

 

* Master's Degree in engineering, business or related field
* Multi-site experience
* Multi-departmental experience
* Collective bargaining experience

role.title: Senior Director Process Engineering
role.description:
**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

Position Summary

The Sr Director Process Engineering BDS CGT sets enterprise direction and senior technical governance for process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing within AbbVie Strategic Investment.

The role supports Strategic Investments through engineering leadership, technical expertise, standards development, technical governance and project execution support across multiple manufacturing sites, strategic investments and technology platforms.

The role supports engineering activities associated with new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing facility investments, new production capabilities, strategic capacity creation, advanced manufacturing platforms and new technology deployments across the Strategic Investment portfolio.

The role partners with Strategic Investments, manufacturing sites, operations, quality, EHS, validation / CQV and external engineering partners to deliver technically robust and business-aligned engineering solutions.

**Strategic Investment Context**

Strategic Investment provides engineering leadership, technical governance, standards development and project execution support across AbbVie’s Strategic Investments and strategic capital portfolio.

The organization supports new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing facilities, new platform deployments, strategic capacity creation, advanced biologics and CGT manufacturing capabilities and standards development for emerging technologies across Strategic Investments.

Strategic Investment roles are expected to promote common standards, transfer lessons learned across regions and sites, and enable consistent engineering delivery across strategic capital investments.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Investment Governance and Standards**

* Establish, maintain and deploy global engineering standards, technical practices and governance expectations for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery.
* Drive consistent application of technical standards, design principles, lessons learned and engineering playbooks across regions, sites and capital projects.
* Define enterprise standards, engineering requirements and technical guardrails for new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technologies, including requirements for consistent design, deployment, qualification, operation and scale-up across Strategic Investments.
* Ensure discipline strategies support AbbVie’s long-range Strategic Investment objectives, strategic investment programs and adoption of new technologies across future manufacturing platforms.
* Provide governance and escalation for technical decisions with material safety, quality, compliance, cost, schedule, operability or lifecycle impact.

**Strategic New Technology and Capital Investment Support**

* Provide engineering leadership for strategic capital investments, including new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy facility builds, technology platform deployments, new production capabilities, strategic capacity projects and lifecycle technology upgrades.
* Support front-end engineering, facility concept development, investment option evaluation, manufacturing capability assessments and site / platform planning activities for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy assets.
* Partner with Strategic Investments and project leadership to ensure technical assumptions, deliverables, risks and resource needs are integrated into capital program plans.
* Apply Strategic Investment lessons learned and standards to improve project quality, speed, reliability and readiness across the portfolio.

**Technical Leadership and Delivery**

* Lead or support technical decision-making for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery across multiple manufacturing sites, capital projects and technology platforms.
* Ensure engineering deliverables support safety, quality, compliance, operability, maintainability, reliability, sustainability and operational readiness.
* Coordinate technical input from project teams, site SMEs, external engineering partners, vendors and cross-functional stakeholders.
* Drive timely resolution of technical issues and ensure suitable escalation when decisions have broader project, network or business impact.

**Cross-Functional Integration**

* Partner with Strategic Investments, manufacturing operations, quality, validation / CQV, EHS, site engineering, MS&T, supply chain, finance and related engineering disciplines.
* Ensure discipline decisions are integrated with biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing strategy, network capacity, technology platform deployment, regulatory expectations and site handover needs.
* Facilitate collaboration across Strategic Investments, sites and project teams to avoid fragmented solutions and drive consistency across the strategic capital portfolio.
* Represent Strategic Investment in technical reviews, project forums and risk discussions relevant to assigned scope.

**Capability Building and Continuous Improvement**

* Share engineering best practices, lessons learned and technical knowledge across sites, regions and projects.
* Build capability through coaching, mentoring, technical review discipline and development of reusable engineering practices.
* Promote a culture of engineering excellence, safety, quality, reliability, collaboration, accountability and proactive risk management.
* Support continuous improvement of Strategic Investment standards, templates, knowledge management and project delivery approaches.

**Strategic Investment Leadership Expectations**

* Collaborate across Strategic Investments to identify, develop and deploy best practices, technical standards, lessons learned and capability-building initiatives.
* Promote consistency, quality, reliability, sustainability and project delivery performance across regions, sites and capital projects.
* Support long-range manufacturing strategy, strategic investment planning and Strategic Investment capability development.
