role.title: Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing (Contract Manufacturing)
role.description:
**Who we are**

With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility.

**What we need**

Symbotic is seeking a Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing to join our Strategic Sourcing team within our Supply Chain organization. Your role will be to lead our contract manufacturing strategy and develop a resilient, cost-competitive global manufacturing network for complex electromechanical products.

**What we do**

Our global procurement organization partners closely with the business to build category strategies that drive competitive advantage. We own strategic sourcing and supplier agreements end-to-end — from commercial and pricing structures through supplier relationship management — while our sourcing operations ensure disciplined execution at scale. Our scope spans the full lifecycle: procuring robotics, structural, and automation components at the core of our systems, sourcing third-party partners for installation and deployment, and ensuring robust aftersales support once systems are live — all in service of Symbotic's commitment to reimagining the supply chain and transforming the movement of goods through intelligent automation, while bringing unparalleled value to the customer. Every decision is grounded in a relentless focus on total cost of ownership, balancing speed and rigor to drive the best outcomes for the business.

**What you'll do**

* Lead Symbotic's contract manufacturing strategy, including selection, negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing management of global manufacturing partners.
* Own commercial relationships with key contract manufacturers and assembly suppliers, driving cost, quality, delivery, and capacity performance.
* Develop and execute sourcing strategies for complex electromechanical products, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing teams.
* Negotiate long-term supply agreements, manufacturing service agreements (MSAs), pricing, tooling, inventory, and capacity commitments.
* Drive annual cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, should-cost analysis, productivity programs, and supply base optimization.
* Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp activities to ensure suppliers meet schedule, quality, and cost objectives.
* Lead executive-level supplier business reviews and establish performance management scorecards and corrective action processes.
* Assess and mitigate supply chain risks related to capacity, geographic concentration, financial stability, and component availability.
* Partner with commodity sourcing teams across mechanical, electronics, motors, batteries, and other key categories to optimize total system cost.
* Develop manufacturing footprint strategies to support business growth, scalability, resiliency, and customer requirements.
* Manage significant annual spend and contribute to long-range supply chain, inventory, and working capital strategies.
* Build and mentor a high-performing sourcing organization as the business scales.

**What you'll need**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree or MBA is highly preferred.
* Minimum 8–10 years of strategic sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, or procurement experience in robotics, automation, industrial equipment, electronics, or other complex hardware industries.
* Minimum 3 years of people management experience leading and growing teams.
* Deep experience managing contract manufacturers or similar EMS/mechanical assembly providers.
* Proven track record negotiating complex commercial agreements and delivering measurable cost reductions.
* Experience supporting product launches, manufacturing transfers, and global production ramp-ups.
* Strong understanding of electromechanical systems, including mechanical assemblies, motors, electronics, batteries, and custom manufactured components.
* Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and effectively communicate with executive leadership and strategic suppliers.
* Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams and driving results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

**Our Environment**

* Up to 20% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ.
* Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued.

role.description:

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. role.title: Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing (Contract Manufacturing)
role.description:
Who we are 
 With its A.I.-powered robotic technology platform, Symbotic is changing the way consumer goods move through the supply chain. Intelligent software orchestrates advanced robots in a high-density, end-to-end system – reinventing warehouse automation for increased efficiency, speed and flexibility. 
 
 What we need 
 Symbotic is seeking a Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing to join our Strategic Sourcing team within our Supply Chain organization. Your role will be to lead our contract manufacturing strategy and develop a resilient, cost-competitive global manufacturing network for complex electromechanical products.

 What we do 
 Our global procurement organization partners closely with the business to build category strategies that drive competitive advantage. We own strategic sourcing and supplier agreements end-to-end — from commercial and pricing structures through supplier relationship management — while our sourcing operations ensure disciplined execution at scale. Our scope spans the full lifecycle: procuring robotics, structural, and automation components at the core of our systems, sourcing third-party partners for installation and deployment, and ensuring robust aftersales support once systems are live — all in service of Symbotic's commitment to reimagining the supply chain and transforming the movement of goods through intelligent automation, while bringing unparalleled value to the customer. Every decision is grounded in a relentless focus on total cost of ownership, balancing speed and rigor to drive the best outcomes for the business.

 What you'll do 
 Lead Symbotic's contract manufacturing strategy, including selection, negotiation, onboarding, and ongoing management of global manufacturing partners.
 Own commercial relationships with key contract manufacturers and assembly suppliers, driving cost, quality, delivery, and capacity performance.
 Develop and execute sourcing strategies for complex electromechanical products, partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing teams.
 Negotiate long-term supply agreements, manufacturing service agreements (MSAs), pricing, tooling, inventory, and capacity commitments.
 Drive annual cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, should-cost analysis, productivity programs, and supply base optimization.
 Support new product introduction (NPI) and production ramp activities to ensure suppliers meet schedule, quality, and cost objectives.
 Lead executive-level supplier business reviews and establish performance management scorecards and corrective action processes.
 Assess and mitigate supply chain risks related to capacity, geographic concentration, financial stability, and component availability.
 Partner with commodity sourcing teams across mechanical, electronics, motors, batteries, and other key categories to optimize total system cost.
 Develop manufacturing footprint strategies to support business growth, scalability, resiliency, and customer requirements.
 Manage significant annual spend and contribute to long-range supply chain, inventory, and working capital strategies.
 Build and mentor a high-performing sourcing organization as the business scales. 
 
 What you'll need 
 Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management , Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field; Master’s degree or MBA is highly preferred.   
 Minimum 8–10 years of strategic sourcing, supply chain, manufacturing, or procurement experience in robotics, automation, industrial equipment, electronics, or other complex hardware industries.
 Minimum 3 years of people management experience leading and growing teams.
 Deep experience managing contract manufacturers or similar EMS/mechanical assembly providers.
 Proven track record negotiating complex commercial agreements and delivering measurable cost reductions.
 Experience supporting product launches, manufacturing transfers, and global production ramp-ups.
 Strong understanding of electromechanical systems, including mechanical assemblies, motors, electronics, batteries, and custom manufactured components.
 Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and effectively communicate with executive leadership and strategic suppliers.
 Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams and driving results in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. 
 
 Our Environment 
 Up to 20% of travel may be required. Employees must have a valid driver's license and the ability to drive and/or fly to client locations and company HQ.
 Employees may be required to use a personal credit card for business travel expenses, which are reimbursed based on the program guidelines. Eligible employees may receive a corporate credit card based on role and travel requirements, but a personal credit card may be needed during onboarding until the corporate card is issued.

 Symbotic is an automation technology leader reimagining the supply chain with its end-to-end, AI-powered robotic and software platform. Symbotic reinvents the warehouse as a strategic asset for the world’s largest retail, wholesale, and food & beverage companies. Applying next-gen technology, high-density storage and machine learning to solve today's complex distribution challenges, Symbotic enables companies to move goods with unmatched speed, agility, accuracy and efficiency. As the backbone of commerce the Symbotic platform transforms the flow of goods and the economics of supply chain for its customers. For more information, visit  www.symbotic.com .
  
 We are a community of innovators, collaborators and pioneers who embrace our differences, because we know unique perspectives make us stronger and smarter. Every perspective matters. role.title: Senior Manager, Growth – Special Operations (SOCOM)
role.description:
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.




JOB OVERVIEW

Saronic is seeking a Business Development Manager to lead growth initiatives across the U.S. Special Operations community. This individual will be responsible for identifying, qualifying, capturing, and shaping opportunities that expand Saronic’s presence within USSOCOM, SOF Components, and adjacent mission organizations.

The ideal candidate possesses a deep understanding of Special Operations missions, DoD acquisition processes, and autonomous maritime technologies. They will leverage an established network across government, industry, and end users to develop strategic partnerships, influence requirements, and drive opportunities from early customer engagement through contract award.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Develop and execute the business development strategy for USSOCOM and related Special Operations organizations.

 - Build and maintain trusted relationships with key stakeholders across USSOCOM, TSOCs, SOF Components, Program Executive Offices, Program Managers, operational units, and acquisition organizations.

 - Identify, qualify, and mature new opportunities across autonomous maritime systems, unmanned surface vessels (USVs), maritime ISR, logistics, force protection, and expeditionary operations.

 - Develop and manage a qualified pipeline from early customer engagement through capture, proposal, negotiation, and award.

 - Influence customer requirements by maintaining regular engagement with operators, acquisition professionals, and mission planners.

 - Lead capture planning, competitive assessments, win strategies, and customer engagement activities for priority pursuits.

 - Partner with Engineering, Product Management, Government Affairs, and Program Management to align customer needs with Saronic’s product roadmap.

 - Represent Saronic at SOF industry conferences, experimentation events, demonstrations, exercises, and customer engagements.

 - Identify strategic partnerships with prime contractors, technology companies, and mission partners to strengthen competitive positioning.

 - Monitor acquisition strategies, funding opportunities, congressional priorities, and emerging SOF capability gaps to inform business strategy.

 - Support proposal development, pricing strategy, and contract negotiations for strategic opportunities.

 - Maintain accurate opportunity forecasting, pipeline reporting, and CRM data.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Political Science, International Relations, or a related field.

 - 8+ years of business development, capture, military, or government experience supporting the Department of Defense.

 - Demonstrated success winning and capturing DoD opportunities from identification through contract award.

 - Existing relationships across USSOCOM, SOF Components, Program Executive Offices, acquisition organizations, or the broader Special Operations enterprise.

 - Strong understanding of DoD and SOF acquisition processes, OTA agreements, FAR-based contracting, SBIR/STTR programs, and rapid acquisition pathways.

 - Knowledge of autonomous systems, unmanned maritime platforms, defense technology, or related capabilities.

 - Excellent executive communication, presentation, negotiation, and relationship management skills.

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced startup environment with minimal oversight.

 - Willingness to travel approximately 40–60%.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Former Special Operations military experience (e.g., SEAL, SWCC, MARSOC, Army Special Forces, Ranger Regiment, Air Force Special Warfare, or Coast Guard MSRT/MSST) or extensive experience supporting the SOF community.

 - Existing network across USSOCOM headquarters, SOF Components, TSOCs, PEO-SOF Warrior, SOFWERX, DIU, NavalX, DARPA, and other defense innovation organizations.

 - Experience with autonomous systems, unmanned surface vessels, maritime operations, ISR, C5ISR, or AI-enabled defense technologies.

 - Experience supporting demonstrations, exercises, experimentation campaigns, or operational user evaluations.




PHYSICAL DEMANDS

 - Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer

 - Occasional standing and walking within the office

 - Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment

 - Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports

 - Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies

 - Lifting and carrying items up to 20 pounds occasionally (e.g., office supplies, packages)




BENEFITS

Medical Insurance: Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services

Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents

Dental and Vision Insurance: Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care

Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents

Time Off: Generous PTO and Holidays

Parental Leave: Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents

Competitive Salary: Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses

Retirement Plan: 401(k) plan with company match

Stock Options: Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success

Life and Disability Insurance: Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

Pet Insurance: Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline

Additional Perks: Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

role.title: Head of Supply Chain (Robot Production)
role.description:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

You own the supply chain for a general-purpose robot going from prototype to production: every part in the bill of materials, from actuators, gears and motors to structures, PCBAs, harnesses, batteries and sensors, and every supplier and manufacturing partner behind them. You build it from the ground up, in the United States and abroad, and you build the team that runs it. The scale goes from tens of units to hundreds to thousands, and the supply base, partners and processes that got us to today will not be the ones that get us there. Building the next version is the job.

This is a role for someone who has done it before, in the trenches, and wants to do it again with a product that matters more than the last one. You will spend your weeks with suppliers, on the floor with our manufacturing partners, in design reviews with the engineers who are still changing the parts, and with the leadership team on the decisions that shape the company. Strategy and execution are the same job here.




WHY THIS ROLE

Few people get to decide how a new category of machine gets built. Eno is dexterous, wheeled and already working with real customers, built today with a supply base and partners that got us here. The next version of that supply chain, the one that takes us to volume, is yours to shape: what we make and what we buy, where in the world it comes from, which partners we grow with, and what the robot costs at scale. Those choices will be visible in every unit we ship for years.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Strategy. Set the supply chain strategy from pilot to volume: make versus buy, regional footprint, domestic content for regulated markets, single versus dual source by sub-system, and the order in which each piece moves as volume grows.

Partners. Own contract manufacturer and partner relationships at the executive level: selection, agreements, capacity commitments, cost and quality performance, and the transfer of sub-assemblies between regions and partners when the plan calls for it.

Cost. Own the cost roadmap: should-cost and total-cost models, the path from pilot cost to target cost, tooling and capital decisions, long-term agreements with pricing that steps down with volume; partner with Finance on working capital and with Legal on supplier agreements.

Supply base. Build the supplier base for the hard sub-systems: actuators, gears and motors, machined and cast structures, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two qualified sources for every critical part, in the regions the product and our customers require.

Risk. Run capacity and risk: capacity ahead of demand, lead-time and allocation strategy for constrained parts, tariff and trade exposure, geopolitical and single-point-of-failure risk, and a plan for each.

Team. Build and lead the organization: sourcing, supplier development, planning, supplier quality and logistics. Hire the leaders under you, hold a high bar, set the operating cadence and the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, purchase price variance, inventory, supplier quality) and the readout to the leadership team and the board.

Systems. Stand up what a scaled organization runs on, with Manufacturing Engineering and Platform: part numbering, BOM and change control, MRP and ERP, supplier portal, traceability. Lightweight first, then more.

Design. Be in the design conversation from the start: bring supplier capability and cost into the product early, and push the design toward what can be built at volume at the right price.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Built it before. You have led the supply chain organization for a complex electromechanical product from first builds through production at scale, and either built the supply base from scratch or moved it to a new geography. Robotics, electric vehicles, aerospace, consumer electronics or medical devices.

Leader of leaders. You have built a supply chain organization, hired its managers, and run it on numbers; you can still do the work yourself when the team is three people.

Commercial weight. You have negotiated with contract manufacturers and tier-one suppliers at the executive level and closed long-term agreements that held up under pressure.

Global. You have sourced across regions, including Asia and North America, and moved production between them.

Cost record. You can walk through a BOM cost-down from pilot to volume part by part, and you know where the money hides.

Technical. You read drawings and GD&T, you understand actuators, gearboxes, motors and PCBAs well enough to challenge an engineer constructively, and you are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and MRP.

Pace. You default to urgency, operate without a playbook, and are comfortable before the systems exist.

Experience. Typically 10 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or manufacturing operations for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and time in a company that was building it. Engineering degree preferred.




WHAT ELSE YOU NEED TO KNOW

On-site in the Bay Area. Travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 40%.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

role.title: Director, External Quality Management
role.description:
**Description:**

The Director, Quality – External Manufacturing leads the External Quality team responsible for quality oversight of Amneal's network of 50+ external manufacturers, including contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), contract packagers, contract testing laboratories, and API/critical material suppliers across oral solid dose, injectables, and complex products. The role ensures that products manufactured or tested externally meet Amneal's quality standards, approved regulatory filings, and applicable cGMP requirements, and that Amneal's Quality Unit retains full accountability for outsourced operations. Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Quality, the Director leads a team of External Quality Managers and QA Leads, each accountable for a defined set of partners / activities, and works closely with Supply Chain, Procurement, Research & Development, and Regulatory Affairs.

**Essential Functions:**

* External Quality Leadership & Network Oversight - Lead quality oversight of 50+ external manufacturers, contract laboratories, and business partners. Establish a risk-based oversight model that tiers partners by product criticality, dosage form, regulatory history, and performance, and sets audit frequency, on-site presence, and review depth accordingly. Serve as the senior Quality decisionmaker for external manufacturing issues, product impact assessments, and escalations. Represent External Quality in management review and Quality Council forums.
* People Leadership - Lead, coach, and develop a team of External Quality Managers and QA Leads; assign partner portfolios and balance workload across 50+ sites. Build team capability in auditing, investigation review, risk assessment, and regulatory requirements. Develop and maintain SOPs, tools, and standard work for external quality oversight. Foster a culture of quality ownership, independent challenge, transparency, and continuous improvement.
* Quality Agreements & Partner Qualification – Own the authoring, negotiation, approval, and periodic review of Quality Agreements. Lead quality due diligence, qualification, and approval of new partners; maintain the Approved Supplier List. Define and execute the CMO and contract laboratory audit program; ensure audit observations are tracked to effective closure. Lead quality disqualification and exit decisions for persistently non-compliant partners.
* Batch Disposition & Product Quality - Ensure timely, compliant review and disposition of externally manufactured batches against approved specifications and registered processes. Oversee review of executed batch records, CoAs, and release testing performed at contract laboratories. Ensure Annual Product Reviews incorporate complete and accurate CMO data and drive actions from trends. Oversee stability program commitments, OOS/OOT trending, and product quality complaints for externally manufactured products.
* Deviations, Investigations & CAPA - Ensure deviations, OOS/OOT results, and complaints at partner sites are investigated thoroughly and in a timely manner. Challenge root cause analyses for scientific rigor and identification of systemic contributors. Approve CAPAs and verify effectiveness; identify recurring issues across partners and drive network-wide preventive actions. Lead quality assessments for field alerts, recalls, and market actions involving external products.
Change Control & Regulatory Alignment - Govern partner-initiated and Amneal-initiated changes through change control, including product impact and regulatory reportability assessments. Partner with Regulatory Affairs to ensure changes are filed appropriately (CBE-0, CBE-30, PAS, annual report) and that partner operations remain aligned with approved ANDAs/NDAs. Provide quality oversight of technology transfers, site transfers, process validation, and new product launches at external sites. 

This position requires 30-40% travel both domestic and international.

 

**Education:**

* Bachelor's Degree (BA/BS) Chemistry, biology, Pharmacy, engineering or other technical fields - Required
Master's degree (MS/MA) Chemistry, biology, Pharmacy, engineering or other technical fields - Preferred 

**Experience:**

* 15 years or more in QA, QC, Compliance in pharmaceutical manufacturing company.
* 5 years or more in External / CMO quality oversight.
Must have experience managing others. 

**Specialized Knowledge:**

* Demonstrated quality oversight of a large, multi-site CMO network across dosage forms (oral solids, sterile injectables, and/or complex generics).
* Expert knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210/211, 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP, ICH Q7/Q9/Q10, and FDA expectations for Quality Agreements and outsourced manufacturing.
* Experience hosting or supporting FDA inspections and leading 483 / Warning Letter remediation.
Strong background in investigations, root cause analysis, CAPA, and change control. 

The salary range for this position ranges from $205,000 - $236,000 per year. In addition, Amneal offers a short-term incentive opportunity, such as a bonus or performance-based award as well as a long-term incentive award, such as restricted stock units, with this position within the first 12 months. Amneal ranges reflect the Company’s good faith estimate of what Amneal reasonably believes that it will pay for said position at the time of the posting. Individual compensation will ultimately be determined based on a variety of relevant factors, including but not limited to, qualifications, experience, geographic location and other relevant skills.
 
 
At the heart of our Total Rewards commitment is a comprehensive, flexible and competitive benefits program for eligible positions that enables you to choose the plans and coverage that meet your personal needs. This includes above-market, diverse and robust health and insurance benefits to meet the varied needs of our employees as well as a significant 401(k) matching contribution to help our employees save for retirement. We also promote employee well-being with programs that help you enjoy your career alongside life’s many other commitments and opportunities.

 

Amneal is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process or to participate in any part of the hiring process, please contact us at accommodations@amneal.com . Requests will be handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable laws.

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking an Executive Director, Manufacturing IT Planning & Strategy (Digital Transformation) to join our IOPS IT organization, leading the planning and governance behind our digital and automation transformation supporting GMP operations. Sitting within the Plan function of IOPS IT’s Plan-Build-Run operating model, you will set the direction, governance, and investment strategy that Build and Run teams deliver and sustain — partnering with corporate IT and cross-functional leaders across the enterprise to drive fast, reliable, and compliant technology decisions at scale. This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Troy, New York United States
* Work model: 8am - 4:30pm, onsite
* Travel percentage: 25% global to other manufacturing facilities
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Establish technology governance, portfolio management, and demand management anchored in enterprise architecture standards, driving business and technology transformation through full portfolio visibility and fast technology decisions.
* Lead large-scale IT and digital transformation programs, resolving constraints and redirecting priorities to deliver business outcomes.
* Successfully take modern, cutting-edge technologies from plan to implementation, with reliability and security built in.
* Deliver technology solutions in cGMP pharmaceutical or biotech manufacturing, aligning compliance, validation, and data integrity with every technology decision.
* Communicate technology strategy into funded investment plans and manage budgets with a clear view of long-term operating impact.
* Utilize interpersonal skills to collaborate across all organizational levels.
 

 

**This role requires:**

* Bachelor’s degree in IT or a related field and have 18+ years of experience in IT and business operations/transformations, including a cGMP biotechnology/pharmaceutical environment. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.
 

 
 

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

role.title: Director of Quality - Automotive Manufacturing
role.description:
"An Equal Opportunity Employer” It is the policy of North American Stamping Group to provide employment, training, promotion, and other conditions of Employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age or status as a qualified individual with a disability or other status protected by law.
 
 
GENERAL SUMMARY
 
The Director of Quality is responsible for oversight of Quality and APQP systems and operations. Responsibilities include development and improvement of the NASG Quality Management System, development of systems to ensure customer and NASG requirements are met during and after product launch and supporting plant quality and manufacturing teams to resolve concerns.
 
 
ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS
 
A. Development and ongoing improvement of NASG Quality Management System
 
B. Manage process to evaluate current state and develop plan to support department training and development of Quality teams in problem solving, improvement tools and communication methods
 
C. Serve as customer contact for Production quality, and represent NASG as required to resolve issues
 
D. Assist and support manufacturing plant quality teams with investigation and resolution of internal and external quality problems
 
E. Monitor / report / improve all NASG quality performance metrics
 
F. Participate in and support Feasibility reviews
 
G. Participate in and support Kick-Off meetings
 
H. Direct management of Quality Engineering teams
 
I. Indirect management of manufacturing plant quality teams
 
J. Monitor APQP process (ShopEdge) and ensure completion of APQP tasks
 
K. Support Internal / External / Customer audits as required
 
L. Establish and execute NASG Quality strategy plan for year over year continuous improvement for key department metrics
 
M. Continually evaluate department processes for adherence while identifying and executing improvement to process design to improve department efficiency and effectiveness
 
N. In addition to performing primary duties, the individual shall provide support where deemed necessary by Management
 
 
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS/REQUIREMENTS
 
 
**Education:** 

* Bachelor degree in metrology, industrial, mechanical, electrical or electronics engineering (Or relevant experience)
* Six Sigma Black Belt preferred

**Experience:** 

* 10 years manufacturing experience
* 5 years supervision / management
* 5 years in automotive manufacturing
* 5 – 10 years cumulative in Quality functions

**Personal/Technical Skills:** 

* Master level understanding of Control Plans, FMEA's, Flow Diagrams and In-Process Inspection
* Master level knowledge of GD&T, SPC, Gage R&R, and gage use
* APQP, PPAP, MSA, Core Tools
* Detail oriented and able to work with minimal supervision
* Strong leadership abilities
* Demonstrate and model Hands-on, involved, Go-See approach
* Highly organized
* Strong Interpersonal communication skills
* Will have the ability to work schedule that allows completion of the job on a daily basis

**Language Skills:** 

* Able to clearly communicate in verbal or written forms and act as a liaison between Production and Quality
* Ability to speak and write in the primary language of the NASG facility of employment

North American Stamping Group is a drug-free and smoke-free workplace.

role.description:
**Work Schedule**

Standard (Mon-Fri)

**Environmental Conditions**

Office

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in operations leadership in regulated manufacturing environments
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering, Chemistry, Biology, Business or related technical/scientific field
* Advanced training in continuous improvement methodologies (Six Sigma, Lean)
* Demonstrated P&L management and operational excellence experience at scale
* Strong working knowledge of cGMP, FDA, and other relevant quality/regulatory requirements
* Experience leading and developing large, multi-functional teams
* Experience implementing continuous improvement and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities
* Effective communication and influence skills across all organizational levels
* Ability to implement change and deliver results in matrix environments
* Experience with ERP systems and manufacturing technologies
* Strong project management capabilities
* Strategic mindset with ability to balance short and long-term priorities
* Experience in customer/client relationship management
* Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities
* Ability to travel 50-75% as required
* Change management and transformation experience
* Cross-functional collaboration and influence skills
* Financial planning and budget management expertise

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.

Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.

Manchester, CT United States | req34380

* Lead and inspire plant operations, overseeing production, maintenance, quality, safety, and financial performance to deliver exceptional results
* Drive operational excellence by developing and executing strategies that achieve production goals, reduce waste, enhance quality, and maximize efficiency
* Promote a world-class safety culture, ensuring compliance with all regulatory, environment and workplace safety standards while protecting employees and operations.
* Build and develop high-performing teams by fostering a culture of engagement, accountability, innovation, and continuous learning

* Exceptional leadership and communication skills with the ability to inspire, develop, and engage teams while building strong relationships across all levels of the organization
* Comprehensive understanding of manufacturing processes, equipment, and quality systems, coupled with a commitment to operational excellence
* Knowledge of safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements with a track record of maintaining compliance and promoting culture of workplace safety
* Results-oriented mindset with the ability to balance strategic thinking and hands-on leadership in a fast-paced manufacturing environment

Linde is a leading global industrial gases and engineering company with 2025 sales of $34 billion. We live our mission of making our world more productive every day by providing high-quality solutions, technologies and services which are making our customers more successful and helping to sustain, decarbonize and protect our planet.

role.title: Plant Manager B Shift
role.description:
The Plant Manager is responsible for coordinating, directing, leading, guiding, and managing areas of the plant consistent with company policies and procedures as well as with federal, state and local law. Will be accountable for the management and safety of employees, high quality products being produced, budgeting and the profitability of the facility. The Plant Manager develops processes that will maximize stewardship, safety, quality, culture, customer relations, and productivity. This role has direct supervisory responsibility for all operations management and hourly team members with an expanded dotted line responsibility for a variety of support groups when department heads are not present (i.e., Sanitation, Shipping, Maintenance & Engineering). Will work closely with Human Resources and production teams in hire and train staff.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**: This list is not intended to be all-inclusive and other duties may be assigned.

* Initiate and maintain a safe workplace in accordance with regulatory and plant policies by maintaining effective safety and ergonomic programs and proactively correcting deficiencies to meet company goals of an injury free workplace.
* Responsible for communicating necessary feedback updates, up through STF leadership that pertain to the shift's activities.
* Be an active member, leading and facilitating our Safety Committee.
* Implement and attain goals to reduce injuries and cost per claim of injuries.
* Responsible for team members for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of all shift operations; ensure all operating procedures are followed and correct and/or update when needed.
* Ensure employee safety training, assist in the identification of and correction of safety hazards and ergonomic issues.
* Ensure all staff and employees know and understand CCP's, HACCP and SSOP documents/plans.
* Maintain product failures and foreign material issues are kept at a minimum; continue efforts for improvement.
* Responsible for overseeing all plant activity within all departments of the shift including supporting areas.
* Serve as a contact person for vendors and suppliers.
* Initiate and modify as necessary methods of ensuring production goals are met, including product quality per food safety requirements and specifications, efficiency, hours, cost and safety to remain efficient and competitive.
* Develop and manage a system that tracks labor, product and packaging costs that result in a reduction to the budget.
* Carries out managerial/supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the companies policies and applicable laws.
* Responsible for plant labor, raw material utilization, yields, supplies and waste reduction to ensure they are being managed in the most efficient manner.
* Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, training employees, planning, directing and assigning work; appraising performance; rewarding and counseling employees when necessary to maintain a high standard of employee relations.
* Facilitate training and development sessions that develops the skills and education of company leaders.
* Develop and manage a strong productive working relationship with the UFCW, Local 2. Ensuring compliance with our collective bargaining agreement.

**QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS**: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the work environment, knowledge, skill, and/or ability required or preferred. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**: Bachelor's degree in a related field (agriculture, animal science or business) plus ten years of plant experience or the combination of education and experience that enables performance in all aspects of the position, including supervisory experience. Well-developed management skills utilizing sound management principles in leading a team of employees.

**COMMUNICATION SKILLS**: Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to write reports and business correspondence. Ability to effectively manage time and meet all specified deadlines.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**: Ability to read and interpret documents in the English language such as safety files, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Must be able to effectively communicate with USDA, production and management personnel.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**: Ability to apply mathematical applications to practical situations.

**REASONING ABILITY**: Ability to solve practical problems. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form.

**OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES**: Ability to use computers and all standard programs used by the industry and the ability to learn and effectively use any and all other computer programs that are or will be made available.

**BACKUP PERSONNEL**: In the absence of the Plant Manager, the Plant Superintendent will assume responsibilities for overseeing food safety and quality assurance programs.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
*Are you a passionate leader energized by driving continuous improvement?* ***Winnebago Motorhome is seeking a Plant Manager to join our team based in Forest City, IA.*** *The Plant Manager leads overall operations of a soft goods manufacturing facility (cut-and-sew, upholstery, foam, and textile assembly). This expert-level role owns safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people (SQDCP) performance, deploying lean manufacturing systems (5S, Standard Work, Visual Management, Kaizen) and ensuring compliance with relevant standards (RVIA, OSHA, NFPA 1192, ANSI methods as applicable). Responsibilities include strategic planning, capacity and labor management, production scheduling, quality systems oversight, supplier and materials coordination, cross-department alignment, and talent development to achieve world-class operational results.*

**Day to Day of the Role:**

* Own plant SQDCP performance; establish and drive KPIs and tiered daily management (Safety, OEE, FPY, on-time delivery, productivity, scrap, rework, etc).
* Lead daily Tier 1-3 process, Gemba walks, huddles, and visual management; drive corrective actions and sustainment.
* Implement and sustain lean systems: 5S, Standard Work, Kanban/pull systems, value stream mapping, line balancing, takt-time alignment, TPM. (Lean Six Sigma Blackbelt Preferred but not required)
* Ensure compliance with industry and regulatory requirements: Industry and lean best practices, RVIA, OSHA, EHS, NFPA 1192, and ANSI methods as applicable.
* Oversee master scheduling, capacity planning, labor planning, and materials flow to meet demand with optimal lead time and cost.
* Champion quality: PFMEA/Control Plans, incoming/in-process/final inspection, root cause analysis (8D, DMAIC), containment, and standardization.
* Optimize cutting, kitting, sewing, upholstery, and final assembly workflows; reduce WIP, increase throughput, and minimize waste.
* Manage budget, P&L elements, cost reduction, and productivity projects; implement make/buy and outsourcing strategies as needed.
* Build and mentor high-performing supervisors and hourly teams; certify skills; conduct performance reviews; drive cross-training and succession planning.
* Partner with Engineering on DFM/DFA; manage ECNs, prototypes, and ramp-to-rate.
* Own, develop, and mentor best practices for inventory and processes.
* Collaborate with Supply Chain on supplier performance, material availability, and packaging standards.
* Enforce safety culture: risk assessments (JSA), ergonomics, PPE, incident investigations, and compliance training.
* Lead continuous improvement events (Kaizen) and audits; maintain document control and training records.
* Coordinate with Customer Service/Program Management for priorities, promise dates, and escalations; communicate status and recovery plans.

**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field preferred.
* Associate’s degree with significant relevant experience will also be considered.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations.
* 7–10+ years of people management experience, including leading teams through change.
* Moderate to in-depth knowledge of Tools, Machines, or Equipment Required (Mechanical and digital measuring and inspection tools, tape, calipers, tension gauges, fabric weight/yardage tools, color/finish checks).
* ERP (D365) or similar modern Operations and Finance manufacturing software
* Basic office systems for analytics, drawings/specs, and work instructions.
* Practical understanding and ability to perform with Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, Word, NX & Team Center (or similar engineering software)

* Strong business and financial acumen to include critical daily KPI management

role.title: Director of Production - Grand Prix Plaza
role.description:
**Grand Prix Plaza, home of the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix,** is a world-class entertainment and event destination spanning approximately 39 acres in the heart of the Las Vegas Grand Prix circuit. The 300,000-square-foot facility features immersive Formula 1 attractions, premium hospitality experiences, event and meeting venues, retail, food and beverage offerings, and year-round activations that attract guests from across the globe. As both a daily operating entertainment venue and a critical component of one of the world's most recognized sporting events, Grand Prix Plaza requires a high-performing operational structure capable of delivering exceptional experiences while maintaining the highest standards of safety, service, and facility excellence.

**POSITION OVERVIEW**
=====================

The **Director of Production** serves as the leader responsible for all the experiences and production operations across Grand Prix Plaza. This position provides strategic leadership for Production, Guest Experience, Box Office, and Karting operations, ensuring all attractions, technical systems, guest interactions, and show elements consistently deliver a premium and memorable experience.

Working closely with the General Manager and cross-functional departments, the Director of Production drives operational strategy, financial performance, workforce development, guest satisfaction, and continuous innovation across the venue's immersive attractions and entertainment offerings. This role is responsible for ensuring all production and guest experience elements remain operationally ready to support daily business, private events, seasonal activations, and the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**
====================

* Develop and execute operational strategies that support organizational goals, business growth, and long-term venue objectives.
* Provides overall leadership and direction for Production, Guest Experience, Box Office, and Karting departments.
* Leads, develops, and mentors departmental leadership teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement.
* Establishes operational standards, guest service expectations, performance metrics, and departmental goals to drive exceptional guest satisfaction and revenue performance.
* Oversees annual operating budgets, capital planning, labor strategies, and financial performance for all production and guest-facing departments.
* Directs the planning, integration, and execution of attraction enhancements, technical upgrades, new experiences, venue activations, and special events.
* Provides executive oversight of attraction reliability, show quality, technical systems, and operational readiness across all guest-facing experiences.
* Manages key vendor relationships, production partners, service providers, and equipment suppliers to ensure performance, quality, and financial objectives are achieved.
* Partners with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to support venue-wide initiatives, operational readiness, and organizational goals.
* Ensures compliance with all applicable safety standards, operational procedures, regulatory requirements, and risk management practices associated with attractions, entertainment, and guest operations.
* Other responsibilities as assigned

**QUALIFICATIONS**
==================

* 9+ years of progressive leadership experience within entertainment venues, attractions, theme parks, sports venues, immersive experiences, or hospitality operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading multi-disciplinary teams across production, guest experience, attractions, entertainment, box office, or related operational functions.
* Proven experience managing operating budgets, labor planning, capital expenditures, and departmental financial performance.
* Strong knowledge of attraction operations, live entertainment production, technical systems, guest experience management, and venue operations.
* Experience overseeing third-party vendors, production contractors, service providers, and strategic partnerships.
* Knowledge of OSHA requirements, risk management practices, life safety standards, and operational compliance requirements.
* Experience supporting large-scale events, attraction launches, venue activations, or public-facing entertainment operations.
* Strong business knowledge with the ability to analyze operational metrics, guest feedback, revenue performance, and financial reporting.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, organizational, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

**WORK SCHEDULE:**

* This is a full-time position that works a flexible schedule including weekdays, weekends, evenings, and holidays.

**SEASONAL & EVENT-BASED RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* This role includes a seasonal period during which responsibilities extend beyond standard operations. During load-in and load-out of the Grand Prix Plaza facility, race week activations, and other special projects, this position may support non-traditional functions that fall outside a routine. Flexibility, cross-functional collaboration, and adaptability are essential and required during these high-impact times.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS**

* Physical ability to walk, stand, take stairs/elevators/escalators, and navigate the elements during the day and night
* May need to remain in a sitting or standing position for prolonged periods, and repeat motions that may include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers
* Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
* Ability to handle exposure to loud noises at live events, attractions, entertaining programs, and crowd
* Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at times.

**Other Duties:** Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Las Vegas Grand Prix, Inc. provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex (including pregnancy), parental status, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

role.title: Sr. Staff Solutions Architect – Manufacturing (R6252)
role.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


Shield AI is seeking a senior Solutions Architect – Manufacturing to serve as the functional and technical authority for Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP across Manufacturing, MRP/Supply Chain Planning, and the shop-floor-to-ERP technology stack. This role owns the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP capabilities, with deep, hands-on strength in MES, QMS, and PLM — ensuring plan, build, and quality processes operate as one coherent, well-architected system.
This is a hands-on, business-facing role. The Solutions Architect is expected to be the trusted advisor and go-to resource for Manufacturing and Quality business partners on any process change involving Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Planning or the MES, QMS, and PLM bolt-on applications — translating business need into a scalable, well-architected solution, and then configuring and implementing that solution directly for medium-complexity projects. For large, complex initiatives, this person leads solution design and partners with Shield AI’s implementation partner to deliver, while remaining the accountable architect and voice of the business throughout.
Beyond core ERP, this role holds full ownership of Shield AI’s manufacturing-adjacent bolt-on application landscape — including MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter) — and is responsible for how those systems integrate with Oracle Fusion ERP to form a coherent plan-to-build-to-quality operating model. This role partners closely with the other Solutions Architects for Supply Chain and Finance on shared MRP/planning signals, supplier quality matters tied to Procure-to-Pay and end-to-end integration with Finance/Accounting.

What you'll do: 
Solution Architecture & Business Partnership
Designs and delivers technical solutions, creates detailed solution designs, specific integration points, and selects appropriate tools and frameworks. Collaboration with developers and engineers to implement solutions, conducts technical reviews and resolves design challenges.
Documents architectures, provides technical guidance during development, and ensures solutions adhere to performance, security, and interoperability requirements. Prototypes new approaches and evaluates emerging technologies for project suitability.
Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for business partners across Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, and Engineering on process design and system capability questions.
Act as the lead advocate for Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders in all ERP, MES, QMS, and PLM-related discussions, ensuring their operational needs, constraints, and priorities are represented in solution design.
Become the go-to resource for any proposed Manufacturing or Quality process change, evaluating impact, feasibility, and fit within the Oracle Fusion ERP data model and integration landscape before implementation.
Translate business requirements into scalable solution designs that balance standard Oracle Fusion functionality against configuration, extension, or integration needs.
Maintain a working command of adjacent end-to-end flows (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) to ensure Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS designs do not create downstream conflicts or gaps.
Hands-On Configuration & Delivery
Directly configure Oracle Fusion Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning/MRP, Work Definitions, Quality Inspections, and related modules for medium-sized projects, enhancements, and break/fix work.
Build, test, and deploy configuration changes, including setup of Fusion functional areas, security, workflows, approval rules, and data structures related to manufacturing and planning processes.
Author functional design documents, configuration workbooks, test scripts, and process/procedure documentation to support changes made in the environment.
For large or highly complex initiatives, define solution architecture and requirements, then partner closely with the implementation partner to execute — remaining accountable for solution quality, business fit, and knowledge transfer.
Participate in and help lead workshops, fit-gap sessions, and design reviews with Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders and implementation partner teams.
MRP, MES & QMS Ownership
Own MRP and Supply Chain Planning configuration — planning parameters, supply/demand netting, exception messages, and planner workbench — ensuring plans translate cleanly into executable work orders.
Own the functional roadmap, configuration governance, and business alignment for:
– MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — work order execution, shop-floor data collection, routing/operation tracking
– QMS (Quality Management System) — inspections, non-conformance, corrective/preventive action (CAPA), supplier quality
– PLM – Teamcenter — engineering BOM, item master, and change management integration with Oracle Fusion
Ensure MES, QMS, and PLM remain architecturally aligned with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP, avoiding duplicate data ownership, conflicting BOM/routing data, or process gaps across systems.
Define and maintain the target integration model between MES, QMS, PLM, and Oracle Fusion ERP, including engineering-to-manufacturing BOM transfer and quality event-to-ERP disposition flows.
Partner with the Solutions Architect – Supply Chain on supplier-quality data flowing from Procure-to-Pay into QMS-driven supplier corrective action processes.
Integrations
Design and help implement integrations between Oracle Fusion ERP and MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter), including BOM/routing sync, work order status, and quality disposition data.
Define integration requirements, data mappings, and error-handling/reconciliation approaches in partnership with technical/integration teams.
Evaluate integration patterns (API, middleware, file-based) and recommend approaches appropriate to data volume, latency, and criticality, particularly for shop-floor/real-time data.
Support testing, cutover, and hypercare activities for integration-related changes.
Governance & Continuous Improvement
Maintain configuration standards, documentation, and change control discipline for the Manufacturing, MRP, MES, QMS, and PLM functional areas.
Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved data quality across planning, production, and quality cycles.
Stay current on Oracle Fusion quarterly releases relevant to Manufacturing and Planning, and assess/recommend adoption of new features.
Mentor junior functional/technical resources and contribute to a growing internal ERP center of excellence.
Required Qualifications:
12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise ERP systems, with significant depth in MRP/Supply Chain Planning, MES, and QMS functions.
Hands-on experience configuring Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (Manufacturing and Planning pillars); comfortable working directly in the application, not solely at a requirements level.
Experience across multiple full-lifecycle ERP implementations (Oracle Fusion required; prior experience with Oracle EBS, SAP, or other major ERP platforms is a plus).
Direct, hands-on experience with at least one MES platform and one QMS platform, including their integration into an ERP environment.
Working knowledge of Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes and how they interact with Manufacturing, MRP, and quality operations.
Demonstrated experience acting as a functional/solution architect — able to design solutions independently, not just execute configuration tasks handed down by others.
Experience partnering with or managing systems integrators/implementation partners on complex delivery efforts.
Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills; comfortable being the primary escalation point for Manufacturing and Quality process questions.
Working understanding of integration concepts and experience partnering on ERP-to-MES/QMS/PLM system integrations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing functional design documents, process documentation, and executive-level updates.
Preferred Qualifications:
Prior consulting background (Big 4, Oracle partner, or boutique Oracle Fusion implementation firm) strongly preferred.
Direct experience owning or integrating PLM (Teamcenter) with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Engineering data.
Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated/complex discrete manufacturing environments.
Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or similar middleware/integration platforms.
Oracle Fusion certifications in Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning, or Quality.
Experience operating in environments with export control, ITAR/CUI, or other regulated data-handling requirements.
AI & Agentic Automation Capabilities:
Shield AI is investing in Agentic AI to accelerate and automate manufacturing and quality operations. This role is expected to actively identify, design, and help implement AI-driven automation across Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS — not simply consume AI tools built by others.
Identify high-value candidates for Agentic AI automation within Manufacturing and Quality — e.g., planner workbench exception triage, shop-floor anomaly detection, quality non-conformance routing/CAPA drafting, and work order scheduling recommendations.
Design and configure AI agent workflows using Oracle’s embedded AI/ML and agentic capabilities (e.g., Oracle Fusion AI agents, OCI Generative AI, Redwood/AI-driven planning recommendations) as they become available across Fusion Manufacturing and Planning.
Partner with IT/data teams to define prompts, guardrails, data inputs, and approval/exception paths for AI agents acting on manufacturing and quality transactions, ensuring appropriate human-in-the-loop controls.
Evaluate and pilot third-party or custom Agentic AI tools (e.g., for predictive maintenance, quality defect pattern detection, MES data synthesis, or supply/demand sensing) and assess fit against the target architecture.
Use AI-assisted tools for day-to-day solution work — requirements analysis, test script generation, configuration documentation, and data mapping — to increase delivery speed and quality.
Bring or build fluency in prompt engineering and AI workflow design; prior hands-on experience with generative AI or agentic AI platforms (Oracle AI Agent Studio, OCI Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, UiPath/Automation Anywhere agentic features, or similar) is a strong plus.
Champion responsible AI adoption — data quality, auditability, and change management — when introducing agentic workflows into regulated, ITAR/CUI-sensitive environments.
Full-time regular employee offer package:
Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity
 
Temporary employee offer package:
Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)
 
Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.
 
###
 
Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.
