role.description:
MHI Ship Repair & Services is a major marine repair and conversion contractor serving the U.S. Navy, Military Sealift Command, Maritime Administration and Commercial ship owners and operators worldwide. Our shipyard is conveniently located in the Mid-Atlantic region at the port of Hampton Roads, Norfolk Virginia.

**JOB SUMMARY:** Manages the operations of all production trades to include Facilities and Gas Free. Responsible for ensuring that all projects are manned with competent, properly trained and certified personnel, and the work efforts are coordinated and executed in a cost-effective manner, safely, and on time. Provides leadership and guidance to Shop Superintendants and oversees the maintenance and improvement of all shop equipment and development of shop procedures.

**SUPERVISES:** All Shop Superintendents

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Primary oversight of all production departments to include Facilities and Gas Free. Responsible for making strategic and tactical decisions related to certain aspects of MHI's production business to include operation non-Program work
* Responsible for ensuring that all projects are manned with competent, properly trained and certified personnel, and that work efforts are prioritized, coordinated and efforts integrated between departments and executed safely, in a cost-effective manner and on time.
* Ensures performance is within the guidelines of the contracts, delivery orders are received and that all contractual requirements are within the scope of work for the specific market and are met for U.S. Navy, Government, private shipyard, and commercial projects.
* Holds daily production meetings with all trades and Project Managers. Communicate with all department heads to ensure that any manning, scheduling, tooling, and material issues are identified and resolved.
* Attend all SRA Production Meetings.
* Walks through all in plant vessels daily verifying all work in progress and identifying and resolving any issues as they arise.
* Provides leadership and guidance to Shop Superintendants and oversees the maintenance and improvement of all shop equipment and development of shop procedures.
* Reviews and proofreads specs.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Estimating as requested.
* May on occasion be required to manage a project.
* Performs other related duties as assigned by supervisor.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* College education and 15 years progressive experience in the maritime industry. (Apprenticeship and practical experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.) Prior management experience a must.
* Ability to estimate.
* Basic knowledge of all skilled trades, and ability to manage effectively.
* Ability to communicate effectively as a leader.

MHI Ship Repair & Services offers competitive wages and an excellent benefit package.

Affirmative Action/EOE Employer of protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

* Experience running large, complex location or multiple remote locations

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Position Overview**

Maltz Jupiter Theatre (MJT) is Florida's only LORT B+ regional theatre, with a 659-seat mainstage, the 198-seat Island Theatre, the Goldner Conservatory, the Wardrobe gift shop, VIP lounges and a growing campus. The Director of Operations becomes the single point of accountability for the building and the patron experience, from an air-conditioning issue, leaks to a sold-out opening night.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the day-to-day running of the Maltz Jupiter Theatre campus so that every performance, class, event and donor experience happens in a safe, clean, fully working building. This is a senior leadership role, not a hands-on trades role. The Director of Operations plans, assigns, follows up and is accountable for results, while maintenance staff, cleaners, House Managers and vendors execute the work.

The Director of Operations is responsible for the management, maintenance, safety and operational excellence of the Theatre's facilities, and develops and executes a long-term facilities plan for asset replacement, sustainability and risk management. This position reports to the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive.

**Key Responsibilities**

The Director of Operations is accountable for every area below. The work itself is executed by staff, volunteers and vendors whom the Director of Operations directs and follows up with.

1. Facilities and Building Systems

* Oversee the condition and performance of the entire Theatre including, but not limited to, the MainStage, Island Theatre, Goldner Conservatory, offices, lobbies, Wardrobe gift shop, Green Room Club Level, GR2 and future spaces such as the Scene.

* Oversee HVAC performance and response, including air-conditioning leaks, humidity, temperature complaints, and chiller and air-handler issues. Ensure root causes are repaired, not just the symptoms.

* Oversee roofing, plumbing, electrical, elevators, fire suppression, generators, non-theatrical lighting, doors and hardware, parking lot, landscaping and signage.

* Monitor moisture control and mold prevention, especially during dark periods, and coordinate professional remediation when needed.

* Build and execute a preventive maintenance calendar for all major systems, with service records, warranties, permits and equipment manuals kept current.

* Hold an annual facility condition review and recommend a multi-year capital repair and replacement plan to the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive and the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Maintain an asset inventory and forecast timely replacement of furniture, fixtures, carpeting, HVAC, lighting and equipment.

* Oversee environmental sustainability and energy efficiency initiatives.

2. Work Orders and Project Follow-Through

* Own the JotForm maintenance request system: Review each submission and ensure every request is logged, prioritized, assigned, tracked and closed.

* Review open requests daily and set response standards by urgency (for example, same-day for safety issues and leaks, 72 hours for routine repairs).

* Assign work to in-house maintenance and cleaning staff or the appropriate vendor, and confirm completion before a request is closed.

* Report weekly to leadership on open, overdue and completed work, and flag recurring problems.

* Manage small capital and renovation projects from scope through punch list, coordinating with contractors, designers and the Town as needed.

3. Vendors and Contracts

* Manage all building and operations vendors including, but not limited to, HVAC, janitorial supplies, pest control, elevator, fire and life safety, security monitoring, landscaping, waste and recycling, linens, bar and beverage suppliers, and others.

* Solicit bids, validate that contractors are licensed and insured, recommend vendors and negotiate service terms, with contracts executed through the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Hold vendors to service levels, track certificates of insurance and contract renewal dates.

* Approve vendor invoices for accuracy before they are provided to the Finance department for processing.

4. Front of House and Patron Experience

* Review incident and house reports after every performance.

* Ensure lobbies, restrooms, seating areas and accessible routes are clean, stocked and show-ready before doors open.

* Oversee ADA accommodations and assistive listening equipment in addition to the Front of House and Bar Manager, and serve as the escalation point for patron complaints about the facility or service.

* Coordinate with box office, development and marketing on opening nights, galas, donor events, the season announcement and community programs, as needed.

* Collaborate with Production on load-ins, load-outs and technical needs from a facilities perspective, and on scheduling building use among departments.

5. Bars, Concessions and Signature Experiences

* Supervise the Front of House and Bar Manger to ensure bar operations across the building are staffed, inventory is properly stocked, inventory counts are performed, cash handling with the Finance department, and liquor licensing and responsible-service compliance is maintained.

* Supervise the Building Facilities Manager who is responsible for room set ups and tear-downs for every event.

* Ensure the Front of House and Bar Manager delivers the operational side of Signature Experiences including, but not limited to, GR2, the Green Room Club Level Lounge, the future Scene, onstage seating packages and themed pre-show events, so the experience matches what was sold.

* Be available to fill in for the Front of House and Bar Manager in the event of an absence.

6. Volunteer Program (Indirect Oversight)

* Provide operational leadership for the Theatre’s 420 volunteers, working through the Volunteer Coordinator, who continues to recruit and schedule them.

* Ensure volunteers in operational roles (ushers, greeters, hospitality, event support) are trained in house procedures, safety and emergency protocols.

* Make sure staffing levels by performance and event match patron needs, and resolve conflicts between volunteer, staff and patron needs.

* Champion volunteer recognition alongside the Volunteer Coordinator.

7. Security, Access and Loss Prevention

* Oversee security systems including, but not limited to, alarms, access control, keys and building lock-up procedures.

* Work with the IT Manager on building security including cameras, access management, and workspace readiness (keys, access cards, phones and equipment) for new employee offices and visiting artists.

* Manage security staffing or contracted security for performances, galas and high-profile events.

* Investigate missing items, damage and building incidents. Maintain incident reports and coordinate with police and insurance as needed.

* Maintain the key and access register, issuing and revoking access as staff change.

* Manage and maintain the building-wide paging and communication systems.

8. Emergencies and On-Call Duty

* Serve as the primary on-call contact for the building 24/7, on a rotation with designated backups for nights off and vacations.

* Respond to alarms, leaks, power outages, break-ins and other after-hours events, and decide when to call vendors, police or fire.

* Oversee the Theatre’s emergency action plan as it relates to evacuation, severe weather and hurricane preparation and recovery, medical emergencies, active threat, and show-stop procedures.

* Run regular drills and training for staff, house managers and volunteers, and maintain emergency contact lists, evacuation plans, and first aid and AED readiness.

* Ensure the Producing Artistic Director/Chief Executive remains informed of any incident affecting safety, performances, donors or the press.

9. Safety and Compliance

* Serve as the Theatre's primary safety officer, ensuring the building meets fire code, life safety, OSHA, ADA, health department and occupancy requirements. Serve as lead for inspections with the fire marshal and the Town.

* Maintain safety data sheets, inspection logs, fire extinguisher and alarm testing records, and elevator certificates.

* Work with the Production department so front-of-house and building safety align with stage and backstage safety.

* Manage relationships with local emergency and law enforcement agencies.

* Partner with the Finance department on insurance renewals, claims and risk reviews.

10. Budget and Reporting

* Build and manage the operations, facilities, front-of-house and bar budgets, including annual and multi-year capital budgets, with the Director of Finance and Administration.

* Track spending against budget and identify potential savings in utilities, supplies and service contracts.

* Provide monthly operations reports to leadership and, when asked, to Board committees.

11. Staff Leadership and Cross-Department Coordination

* Hire, train, schedule, supervise and evaluate operations staff.

* Write and maintain standard operating procedures for building opening and closing, show days, events, rentals and emergencies.

* Lead a weekly operations meeting with production, box office, development, marketing, the Goldner Conservatory and the Volunteer Coordinator to review the week's calendar and building needs.

* Coordinate building use for rentals, community partners, Goldner Conservatory classes and camps, so every space is booked, set and turned over correctly.

12. Campus Growth

* Represent operations in planning for campus expansion, including visiting artist housing on the land across the street and new amenity spaces.

* Advise on maintainability, staffing and operating costs of new spaces before they open, and lead their move into day-to-day operation.

**Reporting Structure**

The Director of Operatins supervises the people who keep the building running and coordinates, without supervising, the people whose work depends on it.

**Direct reports**

Building Facilities Manager, Front of House Manager, contracted security

**Indirect / dotted-line**

Volunteer Coordinator (for operational volunteer roles); about 420 volunteers through the Coordinator, House Manager, House Attendants

**Key partners**

Director of Finance and Administration; Production and Technical Direction; Box Office; Development; Marketing; Goldner Conservatory

**External**

Building and service vendors, contractors, Town of Jupiter, fire marshal, police, insurance carriers

**QualificationsRequired**

* 5-7+ years of progressive experience in facilities, venue or operations management, with at least 3 years supervising staff and vendors.

* Experience running a performing arts center, theatre, arena, museum, hotel or similar public venue with large audiences.

* Working knowledge of HVAC, electrical, plumbing, life safety and building automation systems, enough to judge vendor recommendations and costs.

* Proven record of running a work-order or ticketing system and closing work reliably.

* Experience with project management, capital planning, and building and managing operating budgets and vendor contracts.

* Strong leadership, written and verbal communication, and organizational skills, with staff, board members, donors, patrons, visiting artists and contractors.

* Calm, decisive judgment in emergencies; comfortable being the person everyone calls.

* Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on problem solving, to be self-directed, and to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Outlook, Word and Excel, and online forms such as JotForm.

* Valid driver's license; ability to pass a background check; able to respond to the Theatre within about 30 minutes when on call.

* Professional conduct at all times, representing the Theatre positively to artists, partner organizations, vendors, donors, volunteers, patrons and Board members.

**Preferred**

* Bachelor's degree in facilities management, business, hospitality or arts administration, or equivalent experience.

* Certifications such as Facility Management Professional (FMP), Certified Facility Manager (CFM), OSHA 30, CPR/AED and first aid, and crowd management training.

* Experience with safety management and emergency preparedness protocols.

* Background in facilities management software or CMMS systems, and in LEED or sustainable facility practices.

* Front-of-house or hospitality leadership, including liquor service compliance.

* Experience with hurricane preparation and recovery in Florida.

* Experience working with volunteers in a nonprofit setting.

* Familiarity with theatre operations, production schedules and event logistics.

**Working Conditions**

* Schedule follows the Theatre and may include evenings, weekends and holidays, with a regular presence at performances and major events.

* On call 24/7 on a published rotation, including during hurricanes and other emergencies.

* Walks the full campus daily, climbs stairs and ladders, enters mechanical rooms and roof areas, and lifts up to 40 pounds occasionally.

Pay: $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

**Date Posted:**

2026-11-13

**Country:**

United States of America

**Location:**

US-CT-EAST HARTFORD-OBG ~ 400 Main St ~ BLDG OBG

**Position Role Type:**

Hybrid

**U.S. Citizen, U.S. Person, or Immigration Status Requirements:**

U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are authorized to access information under this program/contract.

**Security Clearance Type:**

None/Not Required

**Security Clearance Status:**

Not Required

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

 

Pratt & Whitney is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power systems and has been revolutionizing modern flight for over 100 years. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

**What You Will Do**:

We are in search of a **17/24K Industrial Manager, Production Chief** who will be managing, reviewing, and approving Engineering Change Industrialization. The 17/24K Industrial Manager, Production Chief will be key team member within our 17/24K EC Industrial Team of the 17/24K Production Chief Office.

 

Reporting to the Deputy Production Chief, 17/24K EC Industrialization Associate Director, the role will be focusing on program management, industrialization of engineering changes, business process development, and detailed analysis to support program needs.

The 17/24K Industrial Manager, Production Chief will be instrumental in the achievement of Program milestones through alignment of Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain organizational plans and initiatives to Program and Customer priorities and commitments.

 

* Deliver executive presentations and program reporting on deliveries, risks, and industrial initiatives.
* Support communications, cross-functional alignment, industrial risk identification, and risk mitigation efforts for 17/24K programs.
* Participate in GTF PIPTs on behalf of the 17/24K programs.
* Collaborate with Mod Center, GSC, and cross-functional leaders on planning and execution of critical industrial actions to rate readiness for our programs.
* Leading continuous improvement activities to improve key processes; coordinate, organize, and lead critical industrial initiatives for engineering changes to minimize disruption to OEM and MRO operations
* Support MIPT and IPMT meetings for key engineering changes; present and align industrial content for critical customers
* Track and realign block changes for 24k program
* Champion MRL progression and productivity tasks
* Serve as the primary liaison for the Production Chiefs, ensuring effective communication and smooth execution across the PCIR process
* Partner closely with CAT 1 supplier to maintain alignment and drive successful incorporation planning
* Role involves travel up to 10%

**Qualifications You Must Have**

* Bachelor's degree and minimum 8 years prior relevant experience in an engineering, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement or related environment OR a Master's degree and minimum 5 years experience in an engineering, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement or related environment
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
* Experience working in a fluctuating environment with constantly shifting priorities
* Demonstrated ability to critically assess industrial production schedules, qualification requirements and develop risk mitigations to drive successful program execution.

**Qualifications We Prefer**

* Experience using SAP
* Knowledge of the PCIR process
Working knowledge of continuous improvement principles (e.g. lean manufacturing, CORE, QCPC) 

 

**Learn More & Apply Now:**

Please ensure the role type defined below is appropriate for your needs before applying to this role. This position is classified as:

**Onsite:** Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.

***As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote.***

The salary range for this role is 107,500 USD - 204,500 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills.Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement.Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance.This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply.RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window.

*RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.*

postingQuotes:
Director of Quality Improvement & Corporate Compliance
Description:

**Help strengthen the quality, integrity, and impact of behavioral healthcare.**

Monadnock Family Services (MFS) is seeking an experienced, thoughtful, and collaborative **Director of Quality Improvement and Corporate Compliance** to provide organization-wide leadership for quality improvement, regulatory compliance, and organizational accountability.

This is an important opportunity for someone who believes quality improvement should be more than audits and reports. At MFS, this position will help turn data, feedback, and

* Training or experience in quality improvement methodologies such as PDSA, Lean, Six Sigma, or root cause analysis.

**What Success Looks Like**

Success in this role means building a quality and compliance program that is active, useful, and respected throughout the organization. The Director will help ensure that:

role.title: Director of Manufacturing Operations
role.description:
**About the Role**

* We are seeking an experienced, hands-on
 **Director of Manufacturing**
 to lead operations at an established U.S. manufacturing facility specializing in electrical equipment, industrial cabinets and enclosures, metal fabrication, and assembly.
* The ideal candidate will bring strong manufacturing leadership experience, preferably within electrical cabinet manufacturing, data and telecommunications cabinets, electrical enclosures, power distribution equipment, or related electromechanical assembly environments.
* This individual will oversee day-to-day plant operations, ensuring production targets, quality standards, safety requirements, and customer delivery commitments are consistently achieved.
* This is a critical leadership opportunity for a proven manufacturing professional who can improve operational performance, strengthen on-time delivery, implement process improvements, and develop a high-performing workforce.
* We are looking for a leader who is comfortable on the production floor, understands the complexities of fabrication and assembly operations, and can effectively manage production schedules, workforce productivity, and operational priorities.

**Salary Range: $180K - $230K + Yearly Bonus + Relocation package**

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Operational Leadership**

* Oversee daily manufacturing operations, including machining, metal fabrication, painting, electrical and mechanical assembly, warehousing, quality, and maintenance.
* Lead production involving electrical cabinets, data cabinets, industrial enclosures, and related electrical equipment.
* Manage manufacturing workflows from raw material processing and fabrication through finishing, component integration, assembly, inspection, and final shipment.
* Provide visible, hands-on leadership by working directly with production supervisors, manufacturing teams, and technical personnel.
* Coordinate production schedules, labor resources, materials, and equipment availability to meet customer demand and delivery commitments.
* Partner with domestic and international manufacturing teams to optimize production capacity and resource utilization.
* Identify production bottlenecks and implement solutions to improve throughput and on-time delivery.

**Manufacturing, Fabrication & Assembly**

* Oversee manufacturing processes involving sheet metal fabrication, machining, welding, painting, and industrial equipment assembly.
* Ensure efficient production and assembly of electrical cabinets, control enclosures, data cabinets, and related industrial products.
* Understand manufacturing processes involving electrical component installation, equipment integration, wiring, and mechanical assembly.
* Partner with engineering and production teams to address manufacturing challenges, improve product quality, and optimize assembly procedures.
* Ensure production teams follow engineering drawings, manufacturing specifications, quality procedures, and customer requirements.
* Identify opportunities to improve fabrication and assembly efficiency, reduce rework, and strengthen first-pass quality.

**Continuous Improvement & Operational Efficiency**

* Drive Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to improve productivity, reduce waste, and optimize plant performance.
* Develop and monitor operational KPIs covering safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost.
* Implement effective production planning, workflow management, and resource allocation processes.
* Utilize ERP systems, manufacturing data, and operational reporting to improve scheduling accuracy and decision-making.
* Build a flexible and accountable manufacturing organization capable of responding to changing customer demands and production requirements.

**Safety, Quality & Compliance**

* Promote a safety-first culture across all manufacturing departments.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, environmental, and applicable manufacturing safety standards.
* Maintain and strengthen ISO 9001 quality management processes and applicable environmental and occupational health and safety management systems.
* Work closely with quality and production teams to reduce defects, improve inspection procedures, and minimize customer complaints.
* Support facility improvements, equipment upgrades, and workplace safety initiatives.

**People Leadership & Culture:**

* Lead, coach, and develop production supervisors, manufacturing personnel, and operational support teams.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability throughout the organization.
* Partner with Human Resources to improve employee engagement, retention, training, and workforce development.
* Foster a collaborative, hands-on culture focused on safety, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and customer satisfaction.
* Build a strong leadership team capable of maintaining consistent production performance.

**Strategic & Financial Management:**

* Develop and execute plant operating strategies aligned with company objectives.
* Manage operating budgets, labor costs, manufacturing expenses, and capital improvement initiatives.
* Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, reduce production costs, and strengthen profitability.
* Collaborate with senior leadership and global manufacturing partners on production planning, resource allocation, and long-term operational improvements.

**Required Qualifications:**

* 10–15 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including significant responsibility for plant operations, production management, or manufacturing operations.
* Experience managing manufacturing environments involving electrical cabinets, data cabinets, telecommunications enclosures, electrical equipment, industrial enclosures, or related electromechanical products.
* Strong understanding of metal fabrication, machining, painting, mechanical assembly, and electrical equipment assembly processes.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing productivity, on-time delivery, quality performance, workplace safety, and employee retention.
* Proven experience overseeing multiple manufacturing departments and leading production supervisors and operational teams.
* Strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, ISO 9001, and OSHA requirements.
* Ability to interpret manufacturing workflows, understand engineering drawings, and work effectively with engineering and technical teams.
* Strong mechanical and technical aptitude with a hands-on approach to problem-solving.
* Experience with ERP systems, production scheduling, manufacturing KPIs, and operational reporting.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, and decision-making skills.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related discipline; MBA preferred.
* Direct experience manufacturing electrical distribution cabinets, switchboards, panelboards, control cabinets, or telecommunications/data enclosures.
* Familiarity with electrical component integration, wiring, industrial equipment assembly, and final product testing.
* Experience managing manufacturing operations involving sheet metal fabrication, CNC machining, welding, and industrial finishing processes.
* Experience working within a global manufacturing organization and collaborating with international teams.
* Previous success leading operational turnarounds, implementing Lean initiatives, or improving underperforming manufacturing facilities.

**Ideal Candidate Profile:**

* The successful candidate will be a hands-on manufacturing leader with a strong technical foundation and experience managing complex fabrication and assembly operations.
* We are particularly interested in candidates who have managed facilities producing electrical cabinets, data and telecommunications enclosures, industrial electrical equipment, or similar fabricated and assembled products.
* This individual must be comfortable working directly with production teams, addressing manufacturing challenges, improving operational efficiency, and building a strong culture of safety, quality, and accountability.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
ResourceTek is the Human Capital division of Barge Design Solutions, a multi-discipline Engineering and Architecture firm. We specialize in providing technical recruitment and staffing services to industry and government in all areas of Engineering, Information Technology, and a broad range of other technical disciplines.

In partnership with our client, a leading U.S. manufacturer of copper and aluminum building wire and cable, ResourceTek is seeking an experienced, solutions-driven
**Plant Manager**
to join the team at their facility located near
**Jackson, MS**
.

The right candidate will be responsible and accountable for making decisions that affect employee health & safety, employee relations, employee growth & development, facility profitability, quality of products, customer satisfaction, and local/regional community relationships. Develops manufacturing budgets and plans to meet production goals within budget.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

· Lead all aspects of the manufacturing operations and development activities of the plant to achieve short and long-term goals to meet customer and company expectations.

· Drive world-class processes in the areas of EH&S, developing a solid safety culture within the plant in order to achieve an accident-free work environment, providing prompt and effective action to eliminate unsafe acts or conditions as they become apparent.

· Propose and execute plant operational budgets, capital budgets, sales forecasts and resource requirements.

· Lead the manufacturing functions in the plant on all shifts to ensure on-time production and shipment of conforming products and materials. Including: planning the production flow, troubleshooting manufacturing issues, handling staffing issues, and monitoring production orders and schedules.

· Develop and implement sustainable manufacturing processes needed to manufacture high-quality products on time.

· Identify opportunities for improvement across the plant in relation to process, equipment, facilities and staffing and drive implementation in a spirit of continuous improvement.

· Maintain and control plant inventories to inventory plan to meet anticipated customer demands without excess investment.

· Responsible for the integrity of all the plant-related data and information.

· Continually monitor results achieved in relation to planned goals and undertake necessary corrective action to achieve the desired results.

· Drive the implementation and execution of robust quality systems to ensure product quality meets and exceeds customer expectations.

· Manage plant project list to set priorities and ensure they are completed in a timely manner.

· Develop and engage with all employees in order to develop a favorable employee relations environment and work with staff members on their personal growth and development goals to ensure employees feel encouraged and motivated to contribute at their full potential.

· Provide leadership for problem resolution to facilitate faster improvements and improved working relations.

**REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**

· Bachelor’s degree in business or engineering preferred

· 10+ years’ experience in manufacturing, including experience in a supervisory or managerial capacity, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

· 5+ years’ manufacturing experience in a process-based environment; wire and cable experience preferred.

· 5+ years manufacturing plant/general management experience

· Extensive and proven experience in Lean Manufacturing, strong track record of leading in a continuous improvement environment.

· Six Sigma / Lean Manufacturing Experience / Training

SKILLS & ABILITIES

· Strong leadership skills and presence

· Demonstrated history of hiring, retaining, and promoting team members

· Ability to build a safety-focused culture that is a great place to work

· Understand the financials of the plant and drive the necessary improvements to achieve and exceed financial and production targets

· Action and solution-oriented leader with strong sense of urgency

· Strong focus on understanding and meeting Customer needs

· Ability to manage multiple priorities

· Ability to build people’s capabilities – Coach and develop teams

· Results oriented with excellent organizational, problem solving, and interpersonal skills

· Seeks out information to understand root causes and drive effective decision-making

· Proven knowledge in budgeting, expense management, and capital equipment analysis

· Knowledge of plant manufacturing systems

· Demonstrated ability to lead people and get results through others

· Clear understanding of effective manufacturing practices in the areas of safety, quality, cost, productivity, and delivery

· Ability to effectively communicate verbally and in writing with customers and employees at all levels

· Computer proficiency (especially MS Office: Excel, PowerPoint, Word)

If you're looking for a stable career with an established manufacturer that values safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement, we encourage you to apply today!

Company offers a competitive salary with
**25% annual bonus**
and a comprehensive benefits package that includes tuition reimbursement, 401k/Roth with company match, and more. Equal Opportunity Employer.

role.title: Director of Engineering, Global Manufacturing Engineering & NPI
role.description:
The Director of Engineering leads Manufacturing Engineering, Process Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Test Engineering, Test Automation, NPI Engineering, and Customer TPM teams for a global data center rack manufacturing business. This role is responsible for engineering execution at the New Jersey manufacturing campus and for establishing global engineering standards, processes, and best practices across all manufacturing locations.
 
 
The Director drives manufacturing readiness, automation, operational excellence, quality, productivity, and successful new product introductions while partnering closely with customers and Platform Engineering. Platform Engineering retains ownership of product design, architecture, DFM approval, and Level 3 technical solutioning.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Manufacturing Engineering Leadership**

* Lead Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, Test Automation, NPI Engineering, Industrial Engineering, and Customer TPM organizations.
* Establish and deploy global engineering standards, SOPs, governance, and best practices.
* Develop engineering talent, succession plans, and organizational capability.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Own engineering performance for the New Jersey campus and drive global engineering consistency.
* Optimize manufacturing flows, capacity, labor efficiency, throughput, and cycle time.
* Deliver improvements in FPY, RTPY, DPPM, OEE, cost, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive KPI management systems and operational review rigor.

**Automation & Test Strategy**

* Define and execute factory automation and smart manufacturing roadmaps.
* Lead deployment of robotics, vision systems, automated assembly, digital manufacturing, and Industry 4.0 solutions.
* Own manufacturing test strategy, test automation, diagnostics, traceability, and test system scalability.

**New Product Introduction (NPI)**

* Own manufacturing readiness throughout all NPI phase gates.
* Ensure readiness of processes, tooling, automation, test systems, capacity, and staffing.
* Lead pilot builds, manufacturing validation, launch readiness reviews, and production ramps.
* Identify and mitigate manufacturing risks to schedule, quality, and scalability.

**Customer & Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Lead customer-facing TPM teams and serve as executive engineering interface for strategic customers.
* Partner with Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Customers, and Platform Engineering to achieve successful product launches.
* Align manufacturing capabilities with customer requirements and growth plans.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA, and SPC methodologies.
* Lead cost reduction, productivity, yield improvement, and waste elimination initiatives.
* Build a culture of accountability, standardization, and continuous improvement.

**Ownership & Interfaces**
**This Role Owns**

* Manufacturing Engineering
* Process Engineering
* Industrial Engineering
* Test Engineering
* Test Automation
* Manufacturing readiness
* Factory readiness
* SOPs and engineering standards
* FPY, RTPY, DPPM, productivity, throughput, and operational KPIs
* Manufacturing validation and production ramp execution
* Customer TPM organization

**Partner Organizations**
**Platform Engineering**

* Product architecture and design
* Product specifications and BOM ownership
* DFM/DFA approval
* Product validation and qualification
* Design changes and reliability engineering
* Level 3 debugging, root cause analysis, and technical solution development

**Customers**

* Product requirements
* Acceptance criteria
* Product roadmap priorities
* Qualification and approval requirements

**Key Metrics**

* First Pass Yield (FPY)
* Rolled Throughput Yield (RTPY)
* DPPM
* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ)
* On-Time Delivery (OTD)
* Productivity and labor efficiency
* Manufacturing cycle time
* Automation ROI
* NPI launch success
* Customer satisfaction
* Global standards adoption

**Qualifications**

* BS in Engineering required; MS/MBA preferred.
* 15+ years of manufacturing engineering leadership experience.
* Experience leading Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, Automation, and NPI organizations.
* Proven success in high-volume electronics, server, rack integration, or data center manufacturing environments.
* Strong customer-facing leadership skills.
* Demonstrated track record improving FPY, RTPY, quality, productivity, and operational performance.
* Lean Six Sigma and global manufacturing experience preferred.

**Ideal Candidate**
A strategic and hands-on engineering leader capable of building a world-class global manufacturing engineering organization that delivers scalable NPI execution, advanced automation, operational excellence, and industry-leading quality for hyperscale and enterprise data center infrastructure products.
 
 
**About ZT Systems**
At ZT Systems, a Sanmina Company, you’ll get to do work you are proud of alongside smart, passionate people. Every day, there are opportunities to collaborate with the best in the industry to design, build, and deliver impactful solutions to world-class customers. Along the way, you will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment that’s challenging, rewarding, and career-defining.
 
 
A culture built around our values we work hard and think fast. We view challenges as opportunities—to do better, push harder, and be faster than we were the day before. When we fail, we learn from it and move on together. And when we succeed, we use the momentum to go even further. We create value with everything we do, building the foundation of today—and transforming the future of tomorrow.
 
 
Join ZT Systems and help us build technology infrastructure that connects the world.
 
 
**What We Offer**
At ZT Systems, a Sanmina Company, we believe that investing in our people is key to our continued growth and innovation. When you join our team, you’ll gain access to a comprehensive and inclusive benefits package designed to support your well-being, financial security, and professional development—both now and in the future.
 
 
**Compensation & Financial Security**

* Competitive base salary
* Performance-based annual bonus eligibility
* 401(k) retirement savings plan
* Tuition reimbursement for eligible education programs

**Health & Wellness**

* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage with access to leading providers

-Mental health resources and employee wellness support programs-
 
 

* Company-paid life and disability insurance

**Time Away & Work-Life Balance**

* Paid time off (PTO) and company-paid holidays
* Parental leave and family care support programs

**Growth & Purpose**

* Structured training programs and on-the-job learning opportunities
* Matching gifts and volunteer programs to support causes you care about

These benefits are available to eligible employees and are designed to grow with you as your career evolves. Full benefits and eligibility varies by work location. Learn more about our benefits here.
 
 
ZT Group Int’l. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. ZT Systems provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
 
 
Please be aware that certain positions may require the applicant to either 1) be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C.
 
 

* 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C.
* 1158, or 2) be eligible to obtain an export control license or license exception from the Bureau of Industry and Science & U.S. Department of Commerce. All offers of employment will be conditional subject to the foregoing.

role.title: Senior Manager, Quality Assurance - GxP (GCP)
role.description:
PTC Therapeutics is a global commercial biopharmaceutical company. For over 25 years our team has been deeply committed to a unified purpose: Extending life’s moments for children and adults living with a rare disease.
 
 
At PTC, we cultivate an inclusive culture where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to join our team
**,**
fostering a strong sense of belonging.
 
 
Visit our website to learn more about our company and culture!
 
 
Site: www.ptcbio.com
 
 
**Job Description Summary**
The Senior Manager, Quality Assurance - GxP (GCP) is responsible for managing GxP Quality Assurance (QA) functions with an emphasis on Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance for development products. This involves engaging and collaborating with cross-functional internal and external teams to evaluate processes, procedures, and activities for adherence to relevant industry standards, regulatory guidelines, and company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) as appropriate.
 
 
The incumbent will support and/or conduct internal and external GCP audits of investigator sites, vendors, clinical study reports, investigator brochures, and submission documents, etc.
 
 
She/He will assist in inspection readiness activities.
 
 
She/He may manage direct reports.
 
 
The incumbent works cross-functionally with internal departments and external resources on GxP QA related issues.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Quality Assurance – GxP (GCP)supports adherence to relevant regulatory requirements and company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) as appropriate.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Job Description:**

* Partners with Clinical Development/Operations and actively participates in clinical study teams to ensure GCP compliance. Assists in identifying and communicating clinical trial-related risks and opportunities for process improvement. Reviews study-related documents and plans.
* Performs internal and external audits as assigned to ensure compliance with GXP regulations and guidelines.
* Communicates audit results to internal stakeholders and writes audit report.
* Assesses audit responses and ensures closure of corrective action preventative actions (CAPAs).
* Leads backroom activities during regulatory authority inspections and assists with GxP inspection readiness activities.
* Supports Quality Management System (QMS) including, but not be limited to, the following activities:
* QA review/approval of deviations, CAPAs and change controls.
* Drafts, reviews, and approves SOPs.
* May manage, coach, and mentor direct reports.
* Performs other tasks and assignments as needed and specified by management.

**Qualifications**
Bachelor’s degree in a scientific discipline and a minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in Quality Assurance or related role in a pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or related environment.
 
 

* Detailed knowledge and understanding of GCP regulations.
* Demonstrated experience leading and/or conducting QA audits.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing risk-based audit plans.
* Demonstrated ability to develop and foster positive, collaborative relationships with internal staff as well as with external, third-party vendors.
* Demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring direct reports.
* Experience supporting regulatory agency inspections.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively, as required, in a fast-paced, matrixed, team environment consisting of internal and external team members.
* Analytical thinker with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines.
* Excellent planning, organization, and time management skills including the ability to support and prioritize multiple projects.

**Special Knowledge Or Skills And/or Licenses Or Certificates Preferred.**

* Experience writing and reviewing SOPs.
* Clinical lab experience.
* Registered GxP Quality Assurance Certifications.
* Experience supporting regulatory agency (e.g., FDA, EMA, MHRA) inspections.
* Knowledge and experience in Good Laboratory Practice (GLP), Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), and/or Good Pharmacovigilance Practice (GVP) regulations.

*Travel requirements: Up to 30% (Domestic and International)*
*Expected Base Salary Range: $141,900 -$175,000. The base salary offered will be contingent on assessment of candidate education level, background, and experience relative to the requirements of the position they are being considered for, as well as review of internal equity.*
*In addition to base salary, PTC employees are also eligible for short- and long-term incentives. All eligible employees may also enroll in PTC’s medical, dental, vision, and retirement savings plans*
**EEO Statement**
**PTC Therapeutics is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from all individuals, regardless of race, color, national origin, gender, age, physical characteristics, social origin, disability, religion, family status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, disability, veteran status or any unlawful criterion under applicable law. We are committed to treating all applicants fairly and avoiding discrimination.**

role.title: Director of Quality
role.description:
*Reports To: SVP and General Manager, Business Operations*

**About Luminary Hospice:**
---------------------------

At Luminary Hospice, we are a mission-driven organization that empowers our team members to shape our culture in order to allow them to provide the highest quality support to patients and families throughout their entire end-of-life journey.

Our mission is to deliver personalized care that radiates compassion and preserves dignity for all that we are honored to serve on their end-of-life journey. We are centered on caring for the whole person – with expert medical care, pain management as well as emotional and spiritual support along with resources, information, and emotional support for families and caregivers.

### **About the role:**

The Director of Quality is responsible for leading, designing, and continuously improving the organization's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program. This role ensures compliance with all federal, state, and accrediting body requirements while driving a culture of safety, accountability, and high-quality patient care. The Director of Quality partners closely with clinical, operational, and executive leadership to translate quality data into meaningful improvements that enhance patient outcomes, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

This leader serves as the organization's subject-matter expert on quality, survey preparedness, and performance improvement, balancing regulatory rigor with practical, frontline-focused solutions.

**Job Responsibilities**

**Quality & Performance Improvement**

* Lead and oversee the organization's QAPI program, ensuring alignment with CMS Conditions of Participation, state regulations, and accreditation standards.

* Develop, implement, and monitor performance improvement initiatives based on data trends, adverse events, and regulatory requirements.

* Analyze quality metrics, patient outcomes, and incident reports to identify risks, root causes, and opportunities for improvement.

* Ensure corrective action plans are developed, implemented, and sustained across departments and markets. (Let's discuss with Nicole)

**Regulatory Compliance & Survey Readiness**

* Serve as the primary owner of regulatory readiness, including CMS, state surveys, and accrediting body reviews.

* Lead mock surveys, tracer activities, and ongoing readiness assessments to ensure continuous compliance.

* Coordinate survey responses, plans of correction, and follow-up activities in partnership with agency leadership.

* Stay current on regulatory changes and proactively educate leaders on impact and expectations.

**Patient Safety & Risk Management**

* Oversee patient safety initiatives, including incident reporting, investigations, and follow-up actions.

* Lead root cause analyses (RCAs) and failure mode assessments as needed.

* Partner with clinical leadership to reduce risk, prevent harm, and improve safety outcomes for patients and staff.

**Data, Reporting & Insights**

* Develop and maintain quality dashboards and reports for executive leadership, agency leaders, and governing bodies.

* Translate complex quality and compliance data into clear, actionable insights.

* Ensure accurate and timely reporting of required quality measures and outcomes.

**Leadership, Education & Collaboration**

* Partner with Executive Directors, Clinical Leaders, and Medical Directors to embed quality expectations into daily operations.

* Educate and coach leaders and frontline staff on quality standards, best practices, and regulatory requirements.

* Support a culture of transparency, continuous learning, and accountability.

* Participate in leadership meetings and provide strategic guidance on quality-related decisions.

**Job Qualifications**

* Registered Nurse (RN) with active, unrestricted license

* Minimum 5 years of hospice or home health experience

* Minimum 3 years in quality, compliance, or clinical leadership

* Strong knowledge of CMS Hospice Conditions of Participation

* Experience with surveys and regulatory audits

* Strong analytical and communication skills

**Preferred**

* Hospice or quality certification (CHPN, CPHQ, or similar)

* Experience with accreditation organizations (CHAP, ACHC, Joint Commission)

### **Physical Demands:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit or stand. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

### **Equal Employment Opportunity:**

Luminary Hospice is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We do not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. We are committed to providing a work environment free from discrimination and harassment, where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. All employment decisions at Luminary Hospice are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications.

### **Compensation and Benefits:**

Luminary Hospice offers a competitive compensation package, along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement savings options, and more. Our benefits are designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term financial goals.

role.title: Director Quality & Compliance
role.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

 

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

 

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) environment.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable. Direct leadership of quality teams is preferred.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

 

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

 

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected. 
 
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

role.title: Director, Quality Performance Operations
role.description:
**Company****:**
================

AHI agilon health, inc.

**Job Posting Location****:**
=============================

Remote - USA

**Job Title****:**
==================

Director, Quality Performance Operations

**Job Description****:**
========================

***Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, now or in the future.***

The Director, Quality Operations is a hands-on, results-driven operator responsible for disciplined, scalable execution across HEDIS, Stars, clinical quality programs, and the In-Home Assessment (IHA) program. Reporting to the Senior Director, Quality, this role provides operational leadership for the Quality Operations team and directly oversees the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations. The Director serves as the critical connection point between the centralized operations team and regional and market teams, between operations and technology, and alongside the Payor team with our health plan partners, ensuring priorities are clear, commitments are tracked, and work gets done. This role is built for a strong operator with a bias for action: someone who brings structure to complexity, holds teams and partners accountable, closes loops, and consistently delivers measurable improvement in quality results.

**Essential Job Function**s:

**1. Operational Leadership and Execution**

Lead the day-to-day operating model for enterprise quality programs, including HEDIS, Stars, ACO/MSSP quality initiatives, clinical quality programs, and the IHA program.

Execute priorities set by the Senior Director through annual operating plans, workstreams, milestones, accountabilities, and measurable outcomes.

Directly manage and develop the Senior Program Manager, Quality Operations, and provide leadership across the broader quality operations team.

Serve as the primary liaison between the centralized Quality Operations team and regional and market teams, ensuring enterprise priorities, workflows, and expectations are clearly communicated, adopted, and executed locally, and that market needs, barriers, and feedback are surfaced and resolved centrally.

Establish and run a disciplined operating cadence, including action-item tracking, issue logs, escalation paths, and KPI scorecards, so that commitments are owned, deadlines are met, and open items are driven to closure.

**2. IHA Program Oversig**ht

Own end-to-end operational oversight of the IHA program, including implementation planning, workflow design, market readiness, vendor coordination, KPI monitoring, and issue resolution.

Partner with market, clinical, analytics, coding, risk adjustment, and health plan teams to ensure IHA activities support quality and clinical objectives.

Monitor IHA program productivity, completion, quality, member experience, documentation, and downstream outcomes; implement corrective actions when results are below target.

Drive consistent IHA execution across regions and markets, holding vendors and internal partners accountable to targets and ensuring identified gaps and follow-up needs are closed.

**3. Quality Program Operation**s

Ensure operational readiness for HEDIS/Stars submissions, audits, roadmaps and health plan deliverables.

Coordinate enterprise and market-level quality calendars, dependencies, risks, and deliverables across cross-functional teams.

Drive continuous improvement by evaluating workflows, identifying root causes, and implementing scalable solutions.

**4. Technology Partnership and Prioritizatio**n

Serve as the liaison between Quality Operations and the Technology and Product teams, translating operational needs into clearly defined business requirements, use cases, and success measures.

Lead prioritization of quality-related technology requests and enhancements based on quality impact, operational risk, and timing; maintain a transparent backlog and roadmap in partnership with Technology.

Track delivery of technology work against committed timelines, coordinate user acceptance testing and rollout with operations and market users, and escalate risks or delays as needed.

**5. Health Plan Partnershi**p

Work alongside the Payor team to track, manage, and follow up on open health plan items, requests, and deliverables, ensuring clear ownership and timely resolution.

Attend and actively participate in health plan meetings, including Joint Operating Committees (JOCs) and quality working sessions, to build strong partnerships with health plan partners and drive quality results.

Lead operational discussions with health plans on quality programs, data exchange and supplemental data, gap closure, and quality results; ensure action items from health plan meetings are documented and completed.

Maintain a consolidated view of health plan quality commitments, programs, and incentive opportunities across markets to inform prioritization and resource planning.

**6. Stakeholder and Vendor Managemen**t

Build collaborative relationships with Regional Quality, Market, Payor, Clinical, Analytics, Coding, Risk Adjustment, Technology, Product, Finance, and other enterprise partners.

Lead operational discussions with vendors and external partners; monitor results against service levels, quality standards, and contractual commitments.

Support materials and deliverables for executive, Board, JOC, CQC, and other governance forums as requested.

**Other Job Functions:**

* Understand, adhere to, and implement the Company’s policies and procedures.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and mentoring to employees and team members.
* Support hiring, employee reviews, workforce planning, and development activities for the function.
* Demonstrate excellent communication, customer service, attention to detail, and accountability.
* Travel as required.
* Other duties as assigned.

**Required Qualifications:**

**Minimum Experience**

* Minimum of 9 years of applicable healthcare quality, clinical operations, or program operations experience, including at least 3 years of people management experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional quality programs in Medicare Advantage, value-based care, HEDIS/Stars, ACO/MSSP, or a comparable environment.
* Experience overseeing large-scale operational programs, vendors, KPI tracking, and process improvement; IHA or in-home clinical program experience strongly preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of Stars, HEDIS, CAHPS, CMS and NCQA requirements, quality measurement, and healthcare operations.
* Proven track record as a strong, hands-on operator who drives execution, holds teams and partners accountable, and delivers results in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
* Experience partnering directly with health plans (e.g., JOCs, quality program partnerships) and with technology teams on requirements and prioritization strongly preferred.

**2. Education/Licensure:**

Bachelor’s degree required in healthcare administration, public health, nursing, business, data analytics, or a related field; advanced degree preferred

**Skills and Abilities**:

1. Strong operator with a bias for action; able to take ambiguous problems, build a plan, and drive them to completion

2. Ability to manage multiple priorities, workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously with minimal supervision

3. Skilled at influencing and aligning cross-functional, regional, market, and external stakeholders without direct authority

4. Ability to translate operational needs into clear technology requirements and priorities

5. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills; uses data to monitor results and drive decisions

6. Exceptional attention to detail and follow-through; ensures open items are tracked and closed

7. Language Skills: Strong communication skills both written and verbal to work with multiple internal and external clients in a fast-paced environment

8. Mathematical Skills: Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

9. Reasoning Ability: Ability to apply principles of logical or scientific thinking to a wide range of intellectual and practical problems.

10. Computer Skills: Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); experience with project and work management tools preferred

**Essential Physical Functions**:

These are requirements normally expected to perform regular job duties. Incumbent must be able to successfully perform all the functions of the job with or without accommodation.

 
 
 
 

**Location****:**
=================

Remote - GA

**Pay Range****:**
==================

$129,700.00 - $162,100.00

Salary range shown is a guideline. Individual compensation packages can vary based on factors unique to each candidate, such as skill set, experience, and qualifications.

role.description:
We’re looking for talented professionals to join us in bringing smart money management and payment solutions to everyone’s fingertips.

This position is classified as structured hybrid, with an expectation of three (3) days per week working in the office and flexibility to work remotely on the remaining days. On-site expectations may evolve over time to support business needs, with clear communication provided in advance.

 > > > > > > > > > >

**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Position Summary**

The Director, Customer Support is a strategic leader responsible for overseeing Customer Support Learning & Development, Quality Assurance, Customer Experience Insights, and Root Cause Management across all customer contact channels. This role drives continuous improvement by ensuring frontline teams, business partners, and vendors have the knowledge, tools, coaching, and quality programs necessary to deliver exceptional customer experiences.

**What Does a Director, Customer Support Do?**

Leads the strategy and execution of Learning & Development, Quality Assurance, Customer Experience Insights, and Root Cause Analysis programs across customer support operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set the vision and strategy for Customer Support programs.
* Lead Learning & Development programs including onboarding, leadership development, and frontline capability building including program enhancements to processes, policies and procedures.
* Oversee quality assurance programs across voice, chat, email, social media, disputes, complaints, and escalations. This also includes oversight and management of the Coaching portal
* Oversight and execution of the root cause analysis program resulting in identification of initiatives to eliminate recurring customer issues and/or improve the overall customers experience
* Serve as the voice of the customer by translating feedback into actionable business improvements.
* Partner with Product, Technology, Compliance, Risk, and Operations leaders to improve customer outcomes.
* Lead managers and teams responsible for QA, L&D, knowledge management, and customer insights.
* Establish KPIs and reporting frameworks to measure effectiveness and drive continuous improvement.

**Success Measures**

* CSAT
* NPS
* Quality Assurance Scores
* Complaint Reduction
* Learning Effectiveness
* Root Cause Resolution
* First Contact Resolution

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
* 10+ years of leadership experience in customer support, quality, learning & development, or operational.
* 5+ years leading managers and cross-functional teams.
* Experience building scalable QA and L&D programs.
* Strong analytical and stakeholder management skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Financial services, fintech, banking, or payments experience.
* Experience managing BPO/vendor relationships.
* Lean, Six Sigma, Quality Management, or Organizational Development certifications.

**Leadership Competencies**

* Strategic Leadership
* Customer Centricity
* People Development
* Operational Excellence
* Cross-Functional Influence
* Innovation & Problem Solving
* Execution & Accountability

**POSITION TYPE**

Regular

**PAY RANGE**

The targeted full-time base salary for this position is $127,000 to $200,200 per year. The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.
