role.title: Manufacturing Operations Director
role.description:
The Figeac Aero Group has multiple locations across the world. Figeac Aero North America, located in Wichita, Kansas in the heart of the country, is a leading aerospace partner for detailed parts and sub-assemblies with specialization in saturation shot peening, shot peen forming, chemical processing, painting, assembly, non-destructive testing, and machining.

At Figeac Aero North America, we place a high value on our employees. Employees are given the opportunity to be a part of something special while achieving their career goals. We offer competitive compensation as a smaller company in addition to an attractive benefits package for qualified employees.

***Manufacturing Operations Director***

***Salary:*** *$90,000 - $120,000*

***Shift:*** *Monday to Friday 1st shift*

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Manages and directs all manufacturing and production activities including shift quality and quality of work
* Monitors overall plant performance for production and comply with all quality standards
* Familiarity with AS9100, NADCAP & ISO9001 standards & audits
* Works with multiple cross functional groups (Quality, Scheduling, Assembly, Procurement, Supply Chain, Facilities/Maintenance, etc.)
* Reviews production and operating reports and resolves operational/manufacturing problems to ensure minimum costs and prevent operational delays and to meet future growth.
* Uses problem-solving skills and analytical abilities to develop innovative and expedient solutions
* Applies Lean principles and production metrics to make informed decisions and drive continuous improvement processes
* Lead and motivate team members to achieve company/department goals while providing direction, development and leadership to production management team
* Provides training, problem solving, and interpersonal skills to diminish conflict and handle employee issues
* Works overtime and occasional weekend shifts as required to support production needs.
* Ensure ITAR/EAR restriction and regulations are followed

**Education/Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent and 5 years management experience in manufacturing environment; or 8+ years related management experience and training in a manufacturing environment 2
* 2+ years’ experience in aerospace industry
* CNC machining experience required
* Knowledge of NDT, paint, and chemical processing required
* Strong business acumen with proven leadership skills
* Full knowledge and adherence to ITAR/EAR restrictions and responsibilities

**Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Ability to act with integrity, professionalism and confidentiality
* Mandatory background in an aerospace or manufacturing environment required.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including interpersonal, negotiation & conflict resolution.
* Ability to prioritize tasks and to delegate them when appropriate.
* Expert in all Microsoft Office 365 applications and knowledge of ERP programs preferred
* Ability to prioritize tasks and to delegate them when appropriate.
* Self-motivated, innovative, practical, and adaptable
* Ability to speak, read, write, and understand English language
* Must be 18 years or older
* Must be a US citizen or legally authorized to work in the United States, not eligible for VISA sponsorship

**Working Conditions:**

* The essential duties job may require the ability to stoop; to reach; to stand,
* to walk and sit for extended periods of time;
* to push and/or pull objects weighing up to 30 pounds;
* to lift and carry objects weighing up to 15 pounds;
* to use finger dexterity to operate a computer and other office equipment and hand strength to grasp files and other objects;
* to perceive the attributes of objects by touch;
* to hear and verbally exchange ideas and information with the public, staff and others on the phone and in the office.
* Occasionally being on foot, bending, stooping, squatting, kneeling, climb stairs and kneeling and/or crouching to retrieve files and other items.
* Occasionally Lifting and carrying (with assistance) items weighing 20-50 lbs.

**Competitive Benefits:**

* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance with competitive rates
* Company paid life & AD&D insurance
* Corporate YMCA memberships
* Paid Time Off
* Generous 401(k) with company match
* Life Insurance, AD&D, Disability & Voluntary options
* Employee Assistance Plan

Figeac Aero North America is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

role.description:
The Figeac Aero Group has multiple locations across the world. Figeac Aero North America, located in Wichita, Kansas in the heart of the country, is a leading aerospace partner for detailed parts and sub-assemblies with specialization in saturation shot peening, shot peen forming, chemical processing, painting, assembly, non-destructive testing, and machining.

At Figeac Aero North America, we place a high value on our employees. Employees are given the opportunity to be a part of something special while achieving their career goals. We offer competitive compensation as a smaller company in addition to an attractive benefits package for qualified employees.

***Manufacturing Engineering Director***

***Salary****: $90,000 - $120,000*

**Experience:** 8+ years in Manufacturing Engineering discipline in Aerospace environment.

**Job Duties:**

* Responsible for coordinating and executing activities around the following: Leading technical teams in the improvement of current processes, transitioning new statements of work, being the focal point of communication between quality, operations, NC Programming and Planning.
* Monitor and enforce adherence to internal processes and standards to ensure a consistent product to the manufacturing floor.
* Collaborate with NC Programming, operations and Manufacturing Engineering on tool and fixture design.
* Review first part runs with Quality, Operations and NC Programming to verify a conforming part and acceptable manufacturing process.
* Mentoring and training of new Manufacturing Engineers/Planners.
* Interface with customer base to resolve engineering issues.
* Investigate and resolve manufacturing issues related to low profitability or excessive scrap.
* Engagement at the estimating stage on strategic packages to review engineering design and productivity concerns.
* Shop support and guidance on first article builds to ensure engineering compliance and manufacturing process design effectiveness.
* Provides planning, direction, and coordination for all technical activities while monitors performance to estimates, budgets and organization goals.
* Participates in developing organization and department goals and objectives.
* Manage and execute assigned projects to meet all project criteria on time and on budget.
* Transition Technical Phase of new work statements on time and achieve manufacturing targets.
* Be instrumental in reducing overall manufacturing costs of strategic work statements by reducing cycle times, setup, scrap, secondary operations content, raw material content and other process driven cost components.
* Enhance core competencies in complex machining and programming.
* Challenges others to develop as leaders while serving as a role model and mentor.
* Inspire coworkers to attain goals and pursue excellence.
* Recommend and implement process changes in order to improve cost, delivery, quality.
* Identifies opportunities for improvement and makes constructive suggestions for change.
* Analyze information and evaluate results to choose the best solution and solve problems.
* Leadership and Communications.
* Report progress and projects weekly to Leadership Team.
* Mitigate team conflict and communication problems.

**Education/Experience**

* A four-year Engineering degree and 8 years relative experience in an Aerospace Engineering discipline is required
* A minimum of 10 years’ experience in a Manufacturing Engineering discipline is preferred
* Extensive knowledge and experience in machining, inspection, tooling design, assembly, and lean manufacturing methodologies
* Familiarity with MRP systems and fundamentals
* Full knowledge and adherence to ITAR/EAR restrictions and responsibilities

**Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Ability to act with integrity, professionalism and confidentiality
* Mandatory background in an aerospace or manufacturing environment required.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including interpersonal, negotiation & conflict resolution.
* Ability to prioritize tasks and to delegate them when appropriate.
* Expert in all Microsoft Office 365 applications and knowledge of ERP programs preferred
* Ability to prioritize tasks and to delegate them when appropriate.
* Self-motivated, innovative, practical, and adaptable
* Ability to speak, read, write, and understand English language
* Must be 18 years or older
* Must be a US citizen or legally authorized to work in the United States, not eligible for VISA sponsorship

**Working Conditions:**

* This position is 100% onsite (Wichita KS)
* Monday to Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
* Some hours outside of office schedule may be required.
* Regular attendance is mandatory and must follow all work safety programs
* The essential duties job may require the ability to stoop; to reach; to stand, to walk and sit for extended periods of time; to push and/or pull objects weighing up to 30 pounds; to lift and carry objects weighing up to 15 pounds; to use finger dexterity to operate a computer and other office equipment and hand strength to grasp files and other objects; to perceive the attributes of objects by touch; to hear and verbally exchange ideas and information with the public, staff and others on the phone and in the office. Occasionally being on foot, bending, stooping, squatting, kneeling, climb stairs and kneeling and/or crouching to retrieve files and other items. Occasionally Lifting and carrying (with assistance) items weighing 20-50 lbs.

**Competitive Benefits:**

* Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance with competitive rates
* Company paid life & AD&D insurance
* Corporate YMCA memberships
* Paid Time Off
* Generous 401(k) with company match
* Life Insurance, AD&D, Disability & Voluntary options
* Employee Assistance Plan

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
POSITION TITLE: Plant Manager 
CLASSIFICATION: Exempt 
REPORTS TO: Plant Manager I 
SUPERVISES: Yes

POSITION PURPOSE: 
Responsible for overseeing and supervising the manufacturing and distribution departments by establishing, monitoring and enforcing policies and procedures to ensure that departments run smoothly and are aligned to quality standards. Creates and executes on strategies and policies for company growth. 
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND BASIC DUTIES: 

* Oversee and supervise the Manufacturing and Distribution departments.
* Provide for the timely manufacture and distribution of product against customer orders.
* Anticipates and tracks operational and tactical risks and providing strategic solutions.
* Plays a significant role in long-term planning, project status reporting, and implementing change control processes.
* Maintain average workdays to manufacture and ship all published catalog items.
* Maintain average workdays to manufacture and ship all custom manufactured items (RCC label)
* Provide monthly responses to budget variance.
* Provide for utilization planning by weekly reporting of the average Work-in-Process.
* Perform physical inventories of raw materials, packaging components, and finished goods.
* Provide for an appropriate balance of inventory to meet performance and financial objectives.
* Implement plant safety programs and ensure compliance with GMP.
* Confirm that appropriate work instructions are developed and maintained and followed throughout the business.
* Ensure that all ISO quality systems are followed.
* Provide compliance to ISO quality systems (i.e. Corrective Action)
* Oversee facilities and grounds maintenance.
* Oversees and reports weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual metrics.
* Identifies trends and assess opportunities to improve processes and execution.
* Completes reasonability testing and information validation prior to circulating findings and recommendations to key stakeholders.
* Solicits and responds to feedback while gaining commitment and support.
* Stays up to date on industry regulations, trends, and technology.
* Manage and supervise employees, resolve problems, and make recommendations for staffing and interviewing candidates for employment.
* Responsible for annual personnel reviews.
* Champions Functional Training Document (FTD) program through employee learning and development initiatives; standards of excellence & leader/employee accountability.
* Other Duties as assigned.
* Commitment to the organizations values; High Standards, Bias for Action, Teamwork, Customer

Obsession, Trust, Accountability, Innovation and Growth & Learning. 
Items covered in this job description are not all-inclusive of the expectations to perform this job 
satisfactorily. There may be times where management may require that you perform task not listed in this 
job description.

REQUIRED SKILLS: 

* Addressing operational concerns and issues, monitoring overall customer satisfaction.
* Developing and implementing operational procedures and policies.
* Analyzing training needs/requirements.
* Excellent interpersonal communication and organizing skills to coordinate project activities.
* Ability to communicate with others effectively.
* Ability to conduct research for special projects, respond timely inquiries, and present written/ oral briefings.
* Ability to work with details and time-sensitive issues.
* Good decision-making skills and response to high-pressure situations.
* Managing processes, developing standard.
* Tracking budget expenses, financial skills.
* Performance management.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: 

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry or Engineering-related discipline or a business-related area or equivalent work experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Minimum of eight (8) years manufacturing management experience supervising manufacturing employees.
* Minimum of two (2) years of recent overall project management experience.
* Knowledge of HazMat, ISO, Distribution and safety programs.
* Experience with Microsoft Office, including advanced Excel skills with the ability to manipulate spreadsheets, create pivot tables and summarize data from multiple sources
* Ability to meet deadlines
* Ability to work independently and with the team with strong follow through
* Strong communication skills, both written and verbal
* Accuracy and attention to detail
* A Project Management Professional (PMP) certified by the Project Management Institute (PMI) can be used in lieu of the educational requirements

WORK ENVIRONMENT: 
The physical environment may require the employee to work both inside and outside in heat/cold, wet/humid, and dry/arid conditions. This position may be working in the warehouse under various indoor environmental conditions, including supplemental heating in the winter months and without air-conditioning in the summer months. May be requested to work overtime and weekends. The position may occasionally be exposed to ruptured, leaking packages, some of which may contain Hazardous Materials. Where appropriate, proper safety equipment should be utilized and/or appropriate personnel notified. Frequently required to use personal protective equipment to prevent exposure to hazardous materials and chemicals. This job may require lifting of up to 50 pounds occasionally. 
INTENT AND FUNCTION OF JOB DESCRIPTIONS 
All descriptions have been reviewed to ensure that only essential functions and basic duties have been included. Peripheral tasks, only incidentally related to each position, have been excluded. 
Items covered in this job description are not all-inclusive of the expectations to perform this job 
satisfactorily. There may be times where management may require that you perform task not listed in this 
job description. 
Requirements, skills, and abilities included have been determined to be the minimal standards required to successfully perform the positions. In no instance, however, should the duties, responsibilities, and requirements delineated be interpreted as all-inclusive. Additional functions and requirements may be assigned by supervisors as deemed appropriate. 
In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, it is possible that requirements may be modified to reasonably accommodate disabled individuals. However, no accommodations will be made which may pose serious health or safety risks to the employee or others or which impose undue hardships on the organization. 
Job descriptions are not intended as and do not create employment contracts. The organization maintains its status as an at-will employer. Employees can be terminated for any reason not prohibited by law.

role.title: Cement Plant Manager
role.description:
The ideal candidate is a proven cement manufacturing leader with extensive experience managing plant operations, including production, maintenance and reliability, quality, engineering, process optimization, safety, environmental compliance, and capital projects. This individual will combine strong technical knowledge of cement manufacturing with business and financial acumen, including experience managing operating and capital budgets, improving equipment reliability and plant efficiency, and controlling manufacturing costs. We are looking for a visible, hands-on leader who develops strong teams, drives accountability, and has a demonstrated ability to improve safety, reliability, quality, production, and overall plant performance.
 
 
**Who we are:** 
GCC is a world-class company that produces, distributes and markets cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, and innovative products related to the construction industries in Mexico and the United States. We take pride in being a market leader with a culture of innovation, high performance and safety. GCC offers a very competitive benefits program including paid time off, medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability insurance plans, and a 401K.
 
 
**What you will do:** 
Directs, coordinates and administers all production, quality control, maintenance, engineering, purchasing and process control activities required in meeting the operations budget objectives and maintains alignment with the strategic plans of GCCA for the preservation of the plant's physical assets and to meet projected sales goals. Directs and coordinates activities to obtain optimum efficiency and economy of operations and maximize profits by performing the following duties personally or through subordinate managers and supervisors.
 
 

* Responsible for planning, directing, organizing and scheduling all manufacturing and quality control activities for the effective operation of the plant.
* Plans and direct the plant machinery and mobile equipment preventive maintenance program and all major maintenance projects and activities.
* Plans and directs the expenditures of the capital program.
* Directs the engineering program involving technical support to production and maintenance, operational cost studies, construction and environmental controls.
* Conducts final reviews of and approves all plant budget forecasts, standards, staffing schedules and capital programs.
* Directs the inventory control of all materials, parts and supplies needed to support the operational activities.
* Investigates kiln output to fuel consumption; finish grinding production to power consumption; equipment failures and effects of repair recommendations; expenditures and return on investment; studies manufacturing costs in relation to budget; initiates and reviews studies, analyzes data interpretations concerned with the production, engineering technical service, purchasing, employment costs and other operations support activities.
* Plans the annual operation and capital budgets; the overall manufacturing capabilities of the plant; and the manufacturing schedule.
* Develops long-range plans for plant operations, capital programs, and raw material reserves and personnel requirements.
* Establishes performance standards for the operational departments including all cost and man-hour standards; policy governing control of product quality standards; the maintenance, repairs and construction budgets; and the necessary quantity and quality levels of all raw materials and fuels used by the plant.
* Hires, counsels, and trains assigned personnel, set individual goals, evaluates performance, recommends salary adjustments, promotion or transfer, approves time-off, and accomplishes objectives through the qualities of strong leadership.
* Directs the efforts to maintain compliance with all city, county, state and federal regulations; maintains a cordial working relationship with the surrounding community.
* Cooperates with the Senior Staff of GCCA in advising of company policies and procedures, safety rules, disciplinary actions and grievance procedures.
* Coordinates activities of departments such as operating, quality control, engineering, and maintenance with GCCA planning, sales, process, or research and development, to effect operational efficiency and economy.
* Analyzes plant budget requests to identify areas in which reductions can be made, and allocates operating budget.
* Confers with administrative personnel and reviews activity, operating, and sales reports to determine changes in programs or operations required.
* Promotes organization in industry, manufacturing or trade associations, Chamber of Commerce and community charities and agencies.

**Experience & abilities you will need:** 

* Bachelor’s Degree in Chemical, Mechanical, or Electromechanical Engineering.
* Master’s in Business Administration.
* Ten years’ experience in cement processes and business practices in the cement industry as well as ten years’ experience in maintenance, production, and quality control management.

**You will love working here because:** 
At GCC, employees are our most important resource. As a part of the GCC family, you'll be welcomed into a culture that promotes the company vision and internal career growth. Our company vision is to have our customers recognize us as a business partner that generates the most value to their construction projects. We're a sustainable growing company, a great place to work and a solid investment for our shareholders. GCC is an enterprise with a global and sustainable approach. Our production is mainly devoted to the manufacture and sale of gray Portland cement, mortar, premixed concrete, concrete blocks, plaster, aggregates and other construction materials. Join the family!
 
 
An Equal Opportunity Employer
 
 
GCC does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability, genetic information or any other status protected by law or regulation. role.description:
**PLANT MANAGER**

**Icon Fixtures | Multi-Facility Manufacturing Operations | St. Louis Area (Hazelwood, MO)**

About Icon

Icon Fixtures designs and builds custom fixtures, millwork, and full environments for retail, restaurant, hospitality, banking, and museum clients across North America and internationally, from single-store orders to 100+ location rollouts. Our in-house production centers on custom wood cabinetry and architectural millwork, along with metal fabrication and solid surface components.

The Role

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on Plant Manager to lead manufacturing, warehouse, and assembly operations across three local facilities. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you will oversee approximately 30 employees through supervisors and team leaders, with significant room to grow the organization as we expand.

This is a role for a builder. The right leader will establish the scheduling systems, standards, and leadership structure that allow Icon to scale without sacrificing quality.

What You Will Do

* Lead manufacturing across all three facilities, including woodworking, cabinetry, millwork, metal, solid surface, finishing, and assembly.

* Build and own production schedules that reflect project deadlines, material availability, labor capacity, and equipment, and identify problems before they affect delivery.

* Run warehouse and assembly operations: receiving, inventory control, material flow between facilities, and preparation for shipment and installation.

* Coordinate material purchasing and production priorities with project management, engineering, and logistics.

* Develop supervisors and team leaders into a management team that runs daily operations independently; recruit, train, and retain skilled employees.

* Set and enforce quality standards against shop drawings and specifications, and reduce defects, rework, and waste.

* Manage labor costs, overtime, and operating budgets; track KPIs and report on performance, capacity, and staffing.

* Lead lean and continuous improvement initiatives, including facility layouts, workflows, and equipment utilization.

* Own safety and facilities: OSHA compliance, combustible dust and dust collection (NFPA 652/664), finishing and spray booth compliance, and preventive maintenance.

What You Bring

* 7+ years of manufacturing leadership, preferably in custom manufacturing, cabinetry, millwork, architectural woodworking, or commercial fixture production.

* Experience managing multiple departments or facilities and 30+ employees through supervisors and team leaders.

* Strong command of project-based production scheduling, labor planning, and manufacturing costs.

* Experience overseeing warehouse, inventory, material handling, and assembly operations.

* Ability to read and interpret shop drawings, production drawings, and specifications.

* Familiarity with ERP systems and production tracking tools.

* A proven record of developing people and building accountability.

Preferred Qualifications

* Retail store fixture manufacturing experience.

* Knowledge of CNC panel processing, edgebanding, and cabinet construction; familiarity with metal fabrication and solid surface.

* Experience implementing lean manufacturing.

* Experience scaling operations during periods of rapid growth.

What Success Looks Like

* Consistent, efficient operations across all three facilities.

* Projects delivered on schedule and within production budgets.

* Reliable schedules and predictable workflow.

* Reduced waste, rework, and unnecessary overtime.

* Strong department leaders and an accountable workforce.

* High standards of workmanship, quality, and workplace safety.

Why Icon

You will have significant influence over Icon’s manufacturing operations, workforce development, and future growth, with the opportunity to grow into a Director-level role. We are looking for a hands-on, results-oriented leader who understands custom manufacturing, develops people, and takes ownership of operational performance.

Pay: $105,000.00 - $140,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Relocation assistance
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

role.title: Power Plant Manager - Homer City
role.description:
Joining Kyuden Energy Partners means you’ll be joining a team in which employees are recognized as the backbone of the company. We offer a competitive benefits package that includes a 401K and provides a range of benefit options covering your wellness needs.
 
 
At Kyuden Energy Partners, diversity, respect, and inclusion are not simply initiatives, they are a commitment from the entire organization, treating everyone with respect, valuing people’s differences, and empowering everyone to have a voice.
 
 
Kyuden Energy Partners provides operations, maintenance, management, and power support services to the US Power Generation Industry across the United States. Our team is comprised of experts from diverse backgrounds of technical fields, including power operations, engineering, asset management, as well as finance, human resources, administration, safety and environmental. With this diverse background coupled with extensive years of employee experience, we provide exceptional operations, maintenance, management, and development expertise to a variety of power assets.
 
 
Kyuden Energy Partners Corporation (KEPC) has a career opportunity for a Power Plant Manager in Homer City, PA. The successful candidate will oversee all plant operations, maintenance, and facility functions, ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient operation while meeting performance, uptime, and client requirements.
 
 
Job Summary
 
The Plant Manager is responsible for directing all Operations and Maintenance (O&M) activities at the plant. The Plant Manager assures that an adequate supply of manpower, tools, equipment, and spare parts are always available to provide for the safe and efficient operation of the plant. The Plant Manager assures that the plant is operated in compliance with applicable safety, environmental, and power generating requirements.
 
 
The Plant Manager determines own practices and procedures, contributing to the development of new concepts, and performing duties independently with only general directions given. Decisions are made within policy constraints. The Plant Manager encounters new and varied work situations, extremely complex in nature. This is in conjunction with Kyuden Energy Partners Corporation (KEPC) and Owner policies and with the approval of the KEPC Chief Operating Officer or KEPC Director of Ops and the Owner's site representative.
 
 
The Plant Manager is accountable for the plant's long-range planning. The Plant Manager must effectively communicate information to the Director of Operations, Plant Supervisors, and client representatives relative to the overall operations of the plant. The Plant Manager must perform duties and ensure all plant personnel are performing duties in a safe manner resulting in no accidents, in compliance with all environmental permits at all times and in compliance with the applicable NERC Standards. The Plant Manager must perform duties, and ensure all plant personnel are performing duties, in such a way to result in an optimum cost-benefit ratio.
 
 
All employees have the responsibility to both the customer and their co-workers to do the job right the first time and to ensure the customer's needs are met.
 
 
Job Functions
 

* Responsible for ensuring that all plant personnel and plant objectives are aligned with client requirements.
* Administration and compliance with plant Safety, Operations, NERC, Maintenance, Administrative, Training, Chemistry and Environmental programs and ensure the safe, efficient, and reliable operation of the plant.
* Manage and oversee the performance of planned and unplanned plant outages.
* Implement training and qualification programs to assure that plant personnel are fully qualified to operate and maintain the facility and plant procedures are understood and properly followed by all plant personnel.
* Conduct periodic reviews of plant policies and procedures to ensure that they reflect current plant operating requirements.
* Direct the sourcing, screening, and hiring of new or replacement personnel as needed.
* Verify that the certification status of affected operation and maintenance personnel is maintained current.
* Provide leadership, coaching, mentoring, and development opportunities to plant personnel and ensure that the morale and motivation of plant personnel is always maintained at a high level.
* Develop a succession plan for key positions.
* Oversee the preparation of required client and utility reports, budgets, environmental compliance reports, etc.
* The Plant Manager supervises all site staff and has oversight responsibility for all contract work performed on behalf of the site (remote/on-site).
* The Plant Manager is the single point of contact between KEPC and the Owner on all matters pertaining to the operation and maintenance of the plant. The Plant Manager cooperates with other KEPC division managers as needed.
* The statements contained in this job description are not necessarily all inclusive; additional duties may be assigned, and requirements may vary from time to time.

Education and Experience – An equivalent combination of education, training, and experience will be considered.
 

* Bachelor of Science degree in engineering or equivalent field required.
* 10+ years of power plant or similar industry experience required.
* At least 10 years of experience supervising technical, supervisory, and administrative personnel.
* Must have 5 years’ experience in Gas Turbines or as a Power Plant Manager in another generation source.
* Strong leadership and motivational skills required.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities - which may be representative, but not all-inclusive of those commonly associated with this position.
 

* Must possess basic math skills, good verbal communications skills, and be proficient with the use of power and precision tools.
* Must be cooperative with those he/she contacts in this work and have the ability to work without direct supervision.
* Must know the hazards involved and the safety precautions to be practiced in the operation and maintenance of power plant equipment and machinery.
* Work within and insure strict adherence to all safety practices and procedures.
* Must be able to respond to audio alarms and variations of sound.

role.title: Sr. Manager - Continuous Improvement
role.description:
Lead continuous improvement at our Battle Creek, Michigan manufacturing facility, where your work will shape performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost and growth. As a key member of the plant leadership team, you will set the CI vision, advise site leaders on strategy and lead a team of continuous improvement professionals.

You will own the plant's management operating system and annual cost-out process while building the capabilities that sustain results. This role combines enterprise-level thinking with daily visibility on the plant floor, giving you the opportunity to turn data, Lean methods and cross-functional partnership into measurable operational gains.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set and execute the plant's continuous improvement strategy, creating the behaviors, systems and culture needed to achieve plant goals.
* Lead, coach and develop the salaried continuous improvement team while building Lean problem-solving capability across functions.
* Own the plant management operating system, annual cost-out process and A3 strategy documents, including daily, weekly and monthly performance tracking.
* Identify, scope and prioritize breakthrough and incremental improvement opportunities using plant data and operational metrics.
* Teach and model root-cause analysis, DMAIC, standard work, waste reduction, recurrence prevention and structured follow-up.
* Facilitate Kaizen events and cross-functional improvement efforts that strengthen safety, quality, delivery, cost, yield and equipment effectiveness.
* Maintain the plant continuous improvement project docket, track savings and communicate project status and results to operations leadership.
* Partner with operations, engineering and technical teams to implement sustainable solutions and share best practices across PCB facilities.
* Serve as a change leader who constructively challenges non-value-added work and helps teams navigate resistance to change.

**Why You'll Love This Role**

* A visible seat on the plant leadership team with direct influence on site strategy and operational performance.
* The opportunity to build CI capability across the organization and leave a clear handprint on how the plant works.
* Broad collaboration with operations, engineering and CI leaders across Post Consumer Brands.
* A role where big company resources meet a practical, hands-on plant environment.

**Location & Travel Requirements**

* This role is based at the Battle Creek, Michigan manufacturing facility.

**Education**

* A bachelor's degree in science, engineering, management or a related field is preferred.

**Required Qualifications**

* 5 or more years of related experience in a manufacturing environment.
* 3 or more years of successful leadership experience guiding teams that execute continuous improvement or Lean Six Sigma work.
* Demonstrated experience delivering measurable efficiency, effectiveness and financial benefits through continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience operating in a large manufacturing plant environment.
* Deep working knowledge of Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methods, including root-cause analysis, DMAIC, Kaizen and waste reduction.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional projects, use operational data to set priorities and sustain improvements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in food manufacturing.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.
* Experience in food or automotive manufacturing settings.
* Experience leading Black Belt-level or transformational cost-out initiatives.

**Success in This Role**

* Builds trust and strong working relationships across plant leadership, operations, engineering and frontline teams.
* Influences, coaches and develops others while setting clear expectations and maintaining accountability for results.
* Communicates a compelling improvement vision and translates complex problems into organized, practical action plans.
* Uses sound analytical and business judgment to solve complex problems and prioritize actions quickly.
* Leads change with candor, optimism and respect, including in environments where established ways of working may be challenged.
* Demonstrates a consistent commitment to a safe, respectful workplace.

**Ready to Make an Impact?**

If you are ready to lead transformational improvement, develop strong teams and help a large manufacturing operation perform at its best, bring your experience and big ambitions to Post Consumer Brands.

role.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Resource Planning & Materials
role.description:
**Ready to lead planning that delivers?**
-----------------------------------------

If building world-class planning systems for medical, aerospace, industrial, and scientific products sounds exciting, you’ll feel at home at Hirsh Precision. We blend software, advanced manufacturing techniques, and modern systems to improve lives—and we back it with a culture of integrity, quality, service, and excellence.

### **Your impact**

* Set the standard for MRP execution—from buy planning and material master governance to inventory control, warehousing, and logistics.
* Translate business objectives into aligned plans with Production, Engineering, Quality, and Finance.
* Elevate affordability and performance through continuous improvement.
* Grow a capable, engaged team through coaching, training, performance feedback, and recognition.
* Craft production schedules that balance on-time delivery with optimal capacity usage.
* Oversee shop orders, priorities, and work center load; course-correct as reality shifts.
* Partner with Operations, Purchasing, and Sales Operations to get ahead of constraints in materials, labor, and equipment.
* Be the go-to contact for schedule questions and escalations.
* Advance scheduling processes, tools, reports, and efficiency through iterative improvements.
* Safeguard data integrity in BPCS and deliver meaningful KPIs and performance metrics.
* Brief executive stakeholders with clear, actionable reporting.

### **What you bring**

#### **Education**

* Bachelor’s in Supply Chain, Business, Industrial Engineering, or related field
* APICS/ASCM CPIM certification

#### **Experience**

* 8–12 years in manufacturing planning, supply chain, or operations management
* 3+ years leading cross-functional or multi-disciplined teams

#### **Technical chops**

* Hands-on experience with mid/upper-tier ERP platforms
* Analytical strength with KPI dashboarding and data-governance know-how

#### **Leadership strengths**

* Persuasive communicator who influences at all levels
* Proven talent developer and mentor

#### **Core capabilities**

* Data-first problem solving
* Change leadership
* Continuous improvement orientation

#### **Bonus skills**

* Strategic execution—long-view thinking with roll-up-your-sleeves delivery
* Mentorship & team building—create high-performing teams and succession pathways
* Business acumen—turn data into cost savings and operational excellence
* Collaboration—excel in matrixed settings; promote knowledge sharing
* Innovation mindset—introduce tools, processes, and best practices to elevate PP&C

### **Tools & tech**

* ERP & MRP Systems
* ERP Software (BPCS for scheduling integrity and reporting)

### **Why Hirsh?**

You’ll shape how work flows through our factory—and how quickly life-improving products reach customers. We’ll give you the platform to experiment, iterate, and win together.

role.description:
**Date Posted:**

2026-11-16

**Country:**

United States of America

**Location:**

US-CA-EL SEGUNDO-E01 ~ 2000 E El Segundo Blvd ~ BLDG E01

**Position Role Type:**

Onsite

**U.S. Citizen, U.S. Person, or Immigration Status Requirements:**

The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance

**Security Clearance Type:**

DoD Clearance: Secret

**Security Clearance Status:**

Active and existing security clearance required after day 1

At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

Collins Aerospace is a leader in technologically advanced, intelligent solutions that help redefine the aerospace and defense industry. With a comprehensive portfolio and deep technical expertise, we help customers meet the demands of the global market. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

**Raytheon Company, Managed by Collins Aerospace**

We are seeking a dedicated professional to join our team as a Senior Manager, Program Quality Leader. This onsite role, based in El Segundo, CA will support Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) Avionics within Mission Systems. In this role, you will lead efforts and develop teams to effectively implement Quality & Mission Assurance (QMA) requirements across all program phases. You will serve as the primary Quality interface for customers, suppliers, and programs.

**What You Will Do**:

* Develop and lead a team of Program Quality Leads (PQLs) and Customer Quality Engineers (CQEs) to support program execution and deliverables.
* Engage with internal and external stakeholders to establish effective relationships and influence decision-making across multiple levels within a cross-functional environment at multiple sites.
* Ensure quality requirements are integrated into program estimates and proposals and oversee their consistent application.
* Lead and oversee the implementation of Quality & Mission Assurance (QMA) requirements across all phases of assigned programs.
* Serve as the primary QMA interface for customers, suppliers, and internal program teams, ensuring alignment with customer requirements and expectations.
* Drive strategic improvements to enhance quality processes, reduce defects, and improve overall program performance.
* Oversee the development and application of quality metrics to identify root causes and implement long-term corrective actions.
* Ensure compliance with industry and regulatory quality standards, including ISO 9001, AS9100, and AS9102.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including program management, operations, and engineering, to ensure process capability, product conformance, and on-time delivery.
* Manage customer interface activities, including interactions with Acquisitioned Customers and Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA).
* Support manufacturing processes by interpreting drawings, work instructions, and Bills of Materials (BOMs).
* Promote continuous improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency, reduce costs, and improve customer satisfaction.
* Must be willing and able to travel up to 10% of the time.

**Qualifications You Must Have**:

* Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and minimum 10 years of relevant experience, or an Advanced degree and minimum 7 years of relevant experience.
* Experience reviewing customer proposals and part orders for compliance risk to quality requirements, and establishing cost estimates for quality support.
* Experience leading teams in program management, quality management, operations management, or an engineering capacity.
* Experience as the direct interface to external customers.
* Experience with manufacturing processes, including quality systems and industry technical standards (ISO 9001 or AS9100), as well as interpreting drawings, work instructions, and Bills of Materials (BOMs).

**Qualifications We Prefer**

* Direct experience working with Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA).
* Certification in Customer Oriented Results and Excellence (CORE) or similar.
* American Society for Quality (ASQ) certification.
* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
* Experience leading initiatives that result in reduced operating costs, improved quality, and enhanced customer satisfaction.
* Experience with SAP (or similar ERP systems) and with Power Apps (or similar tools).

**What We Offer Benefits**

This position may offer relocation.

Some of our competitive benefits packages include:

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Three weeks of vacation for newly hired employees
* Generous 401(k) plan that includes employer matching funds and separate employer retirement contribution, including a Lifetime Income Strategy option
* Tuition reimbursement program
* Student Loan Repayment Program
* Life insurance and disability coverage
* Optional coverages you can buy pet insurance, home and auto insurance, additional life and accident insurance, critical illness insurance, group legal, ID theft protection
* Birth, adoption, parental leave benefits
* Ovia Health, fertility, and family planning
* Adoption Assistance
* Autism Benefit
* Employee Assistance Plan, including up to 10 free counseling sessions
* Healthy You Incentives, wellness rewards program
* Doctor on Demand, virtual doctor visits
* Bright Horizons, child and elder care services
* Teladoc Medical Experts, second opinion program
* And more!

**Learn More & Apply Now!**

Do you want to be a part of something bigger? A team whose impact stretches across the world, and even beyond? At Collins Aerospace, our Mission Systems team helps civilian, military and government customers complete their most complex missions — whatever and wherever they may be. Our customers depend on us for intelligent and secure communications, missionized systems for specialized aircraft and spacecraft and collaborative space solutions. By joining our team, you’ll have your own critical part to play in ensuring our customers succeed today while anticipating their needs for tomorrow. Are you up for the challenge? Join our mission today.

The next chapter of our future as an aerospace company is here, and we are excited about what this means for our employees and customers! Get onboard the Collins Aerospace Operations team and play a part in managing our innovative products from inception to delivery. The Operations team continues to grow and aims to strengthen the connection of Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain and Environment, Health & Safety (EH&S) across Collins Aerospace. In this dynamic environment, you will have the opportunity to network across our businesses and functions, all while improving the productivity, quality and efficiency of our operations worldwide.

* Please ensure the role type (defined below) is appropriate for your needs before applying to this role.
* **Onsite:** Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.

At Collins, the paths we pave together lead to limitless possibilities. And the bonds we form – with our customers and with each other - propel us all higher, again and again.

 

Apply now and be part of the team that’s redefining aerospace, every day.

#LI-JC4

***As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote.***

The salary range for this role is 145,600 USD - 276,800 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills.Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement.Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance.This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply.RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window.

*RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act.*

role.title: Director, Practice Operations Quincy and Middleton
role.description:
**About Tufts Medicine**

Tufts Medicine brings together the best of academic and community medicine to deliver exceptional, connected and accessible care. Comprised of Tufts Medical Center, the principal teaching hospital of Tufts University and the Tufts University School of Medicine, Lowell General Hospital, MelroseWakefield Hospital, Lawrence Memorial Hospital of Medford, Care at Home, and an integrated network of 2,300 physicians, we treat the most complex conditions, keep our communities healthy and bring research breakthroughs to life.

**Job Overview**

This position reports to the Vice President of the Community Practice Operations (South and West) & Network Integration and serves as a key leader within Ambulatory at Tufts Medicine. The role provides operational and strategic oversight across the South region and in alignment with Ambulatory within the broader Tufts network.

In addition, this leader will oversee the Tufts Medicine Multi-Specialty location in Quincy, as well as Middleton, including not only operations, but also growth within these practices. Operating within a collaborative leadership model and with a focus on service excellence in the ambulatory environment, this position is accountable for:

* Ensuring high-quality patient access and experience
* Driving financial performance and profitability
* Optimizing all revenue cycle processes
* Advancing strategic initiatives across the region and potentially across Ambulatory as a whole, when designated

This role plays a critical part in shaping the Tufts Medicine ambulatory strategy, enhancing operational effectiveness, and supporting the delivery and expansion of exceptional care within the community.

Location: Hybrid and at sites within the designated region (e.g., Quincy & Middleton)

**Job Description**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

1. Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare, or a related field or equivalent combination of education and experience such as Associate’s degree in business, healthcare, or a related field and two (2) years of relevant business experience or High School Diploma or GED and four (4) years of relevant business experience.

2. Seven (7) years of healthcare management or practice management experience working directly with physicians and practice members.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

1. Master’s degree in business, healthcare, or a related field.

2. Ten (10) years of healthcare management or practice management experience working directly with physicians and practice members.

**Duties and Responsibilities:** The duties and responsibilities listed below are intended to describe the general nature of work and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list. Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned.

1. Directs the practice operations managers in the day-to-day operations of their employed outpatient physician practices to ensure each practice is meeting optimal operational efficiency, fiscal stability and patient/employee satisfaction.

2. Collaborates with the practice operations managers in the implementation of best practice models in all areas of practices operations. Develops guidelines for prioritizing work activities, evaluating effectiveness and modifying activities as necessary.

3. Evaluates practice efficiency including all personnel (physicians, clinical and administrative support staff) utilizing accepted quality measures, productivity standards, skill mix comparisons, and patient satisfaction survey data. Implements new operational models and structures to reduce cost, improve efficiency and quality, and enhance services to patients.

4. Participates in the development of and oversees budgets for the practices. Reviews monthly P&L reports in detail, determines opportunities for improvements, and creates and implements action plans with practice operations managers as necessary.

5. Conducts monthly operations team meetings to review new policies and procedures, processes, quality measures, etc., and monthly one-on-one meetings with each practice manager at each practice location to provide individual support and leadership.

6. Initiates and maintains all policy and procedure manuals. Develops and implements standardized processes for practices to ensure consistency throughout the physician network. Works with practice operations managers to ensure practices meet required compliance and clinical competency thresholds.

7. Works collaboratively with the physician recruitment team on the provider enrollment onboarding activities related to new practice acquisitions or new employed providers. Works closely with the provider recruitment team, practice operations manager and provider(s) throughout the onboarding life cycle to ensure timeliness and deliverables are met for a seamless transition and successful implementation.

8. In collaboration with the Vice President of Physician Services, implements the transition plan for newly acquired physician practices. Acts as liaison to physicians, support staff, operations team, hospital departments, and hospital administration. Responsible for the human resources, payroll, finance, and purchasing components of the acquisitions.

9. Works collaboratively with representatives from the physician organizations to ensure that our practices and providers are achieving a high level of performance under managed risk contracts as we transition to a value-based model. Commitment to transformation and innovation in care delivery through the Practice of the Future work will also be a measure of success.

**Physical Requirements:**

1. Work environment: professional office environment with typical office requirements such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, etc.

2. Frequently required to speak, hear, communicate and exchange information.

3. Able to see and read computers displays, read fine print, and/or normal type size print and distinguish letters, numbers and symbols.

4. Occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

5. Ability to work in confined or open environments.

6. Ability to work independently or in a team environment.

7. Ability to travel to various locations both within the state and outside the state.

**Skills & Abilities:**

1. Demonstrates leadership style that emphasizes openness, visibility and connectivity.

2. Ability to convey the organization’s enthusiasm, confidence, goals, and mission and inspire those things in others.

3. Ability to connect with people in a meaningful way at all levels within the organization in keeping with the culture of the senior leadership team.

4. Demonstrates forward thinking and creativity with high ethical standards and an appropriate professional image while fostering collaboration and building consensus to achieve collective objectives.

5. Ability to make tough choices that serve the best interests of the organization. Proven creative problem-solving skills with the willingness to take the initiative in leading change as well as the ability to effectively manage change.

6. Ability to build consensus with strong negotiation, persuasion and communication skills to propose enhancements to operational processes to improve efficiency and/or effectiveness.

7. Demonstrates strong interpersonal skills necessary to engage effectively at all levels for effecting timely progress.

8. Ability to be an innovative problem solver with excellent critical thinking skills.

9. Demonstrates exemplary leadership and stakeholder management expertise.

10. Ability to hold self and others accountable to meet deadlines and achieve business goals.

**Job Profile Summary**

This role focuses on providing administrative and business support to the organization in order to achieve operational goals. In addition, this role focuses on performing the following Clinical Administration duties: Long-term strategic planning, determines strategic issues and opportunities that could affect practice success, prioritizes and tracks investments across practices, allocates resources and makes decisions regarding practice growth, and develops need to accomplish the practice's vision. A management role that supervises employees focusing on tactical, operational activities within a specified area, with the majority of time spent overseeing area of responsibility, planning, prioritizing and/or directing the responsibilities of employees. Goal achievement is typically accomplished through performance of direct and/or indirect reports. A role that directs a department or small unit that includes multiple teams led by managers and/or team Leaders. Responsibilities typically include: ownership of short to mid-term (1-3 years) execution of functional strategy and the operational direction of the Department, problems faced are often complex and require extensive investigation and analysis, and requires ability to influence others to accept practices and approaches, and ability to communicate and influence executive leadership.

At Tufts Medicine, we want every individual to feel valued for the skills and experience they bring. Our compensation philosophy is designed to offer fair, competitive pay that attracts, retains, and motivates highly talented individuals, while rewarding the important work you do every day.

The base pay ranges reflect the minimum qualifications for the role. Individual offers are determined using a comprehensive approach that considers relevant experience, certifications, education, skills, and internal equity to ensure compensation is fair, consistent, and aligned with our business goals.

Beyond base pay, Tufts Medicine provides a comprehensive Total Rewards package that supports your health, financial security, and career growth—one of the many ways we invest in you so you can thrive both at work and outside of it.

**Pay Range****:**

 
$134,525.66 - $171,524.44

*based on full-time equivalent*

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Director of Operations**

**Reports To:** VP of Operations

**Department:** Operations

**Location:** Beachwood, Ohio-primary location (Toledo, Nursing Home Programs, and Future Service Locations as needed)

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Position Summary**

The Director of Operations is responsible for supporting and executing enterprise operational oversight across multiple behavioral health service lines and locations. This role partners closely with the VP of Operations and executive leadership to ensure operational stability, scalability, compliance, staffing coordination, workflow management, and organizational performance across all assigned programs.

The Director of Operations serves as a key operational leader responsible for driving consistency, accountability, and operational execution across outpatient behavioral health programs, recovery support services, housing operations, nursing home partnerships, and future organizational growth initiatives.

This is a non-clinical leadership role. The Director of Operations does not provide clinical supervision or determine clinical level of care decisions, but works collaboratively with Clinical, Revenue Cycle, Housing, Intake, Human Resources, and Executive Leadership teams to ensure efficient and compliant operational performance across the enterprise.

This position requires the ability to exercise sound independent judgment, make operational decisions autonomously when appropriate, prioritize competing organizational needs, and respond effectively to rapidly changing operational demands across multiple service lines and locations.

This position is designed to support long-term operational leadership continuity across the organization. Responsibilities may expand or shift based on organizational structure, operational needs, leadership transitions, and enterprise growth initiatives.

**Essential Responsibilities**

* Enterprise Operational Oversight
* Support and oversee daily operational functions across multiple behavioral health programs and service locations
* Assist with operational oversight of outpatient behavioral health clinics, recovery support services, housing operations, nursing home partnerships, and future service expansions
* Ensure operational consistency, accountability, and workflow execution across enterprise locations
* Monitor operational performance, staffing needs, workflow barriers, and service delivery coordination
* Independently identify operational issues and implement timely solutions within the scope of organizational expectations
* Exercise independent decision-making related to operational workflow management, staffing coordination, scheduling adjustments, and day-to-day operational needs
* Assist with development and implementation of operational systems, policies, workflows, and accountability structures
* Identify operational inefficiencies and implement process improvement initiatives
* Support organizational scalability and stabilization efforts

**Staffing & Workflow Management**

* Oversee operational scheduling processes and staffing coordination across assigned programs
* Monitor staffing coverage, workflow efficiency, transportation coordination, and operational throughput
* Collaborate with department leaders regarding staffing support, scheduling concerns, and operational barriers
* Make operational decisions related to staffing coverage, workflow prioritization, and operational resource allocation when appropriate
* Ensure operational follow-up on workflow disruptions, scheduling gaps, cancellations, and staffing needs
* Support census oversight, operational capacity management, and throughput planning

**Interdepartmental Leadership**

* Partner collaboratively with Clinical, Housing, Revenue Cycle, Intake, Human Resources, Compliance, and Executive Leadership teams
* Support organizational alignment between operational and clinical departments
* Participate in leadership meetings, operational huddles, and enterprise planning initiatives
* Escalate operational concerns, risks, and barriers appropriately
* Assist with implementation of organizational initiatives, workflow changes, and operational directives
* Utilize critical thinking and independent judgment to support operational problem-solving and organizational decision-making

**Compliance & Accountability**

* Support operational compliance with company policies, workflows, regulatory standards, and organizational expectations
* Monitor operational accountability measures and ensure timely completion of assigned operational responsibilities
* Assist leadership with KPI tracking, operational reporting, and performance management initiatives
* Support implementation of corrective action plans related to operational performance concerns
* Maintain professionalism, confidentiality, and organizational integrity in all operational activities

**Leadership & Organizational Development**

* Assist with onboarding, orientation, and operational training initiatives for staff
* Provide operational leadership presence across enterprise locations
* Support leadership development and operational mentoring initiatives
* Assist with operational planning for organizational growth and expansion efforts
* Serve as a developing enterprise operational leader within the organization
* Demonstrate the ability to independently lead operational initiatives and maintain organizational continuity during leadership transitions or operational restructuring

**Qualifications**

* Minimum of 5 years of experience in healthcare operations, behavioral health operations, substance use disorder treatment, or healthcare leadership required
* Previous operational leadership or multi-site management experience preferred
* Strong understanding of operational workflow management, staffing coordination, and organizational accountability
* Demonstrated ability to make independent operational decisions in a fast-paced healthcare environment
* Ability to manage multiple priorities across multiple service lines and locations
* Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills required
* Experience working within multidisciplinary healthcare environments preferred
* Knowledge of behavioral health operations, recovery services, housing operations, or outpatient treatment environments preferred
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office, scheduling systems, reporting systems, and electronic health records preferred

**Core Competencies**

* Enterprise operational leadership
* Workflow optimization
* Organizational accountability
* Strategic problem-solving
* Ability to make independent decisions when needed
* Team collaboration
* Communication and conflict resolution
* Operational scalability
* Time management and prioritization
* Leadership development
* Adaptability and change management
* Ability to manage competing operational priorities in a fast-paced environment
* Professional judgment and critical thinking

**Physical & Travel Requirements**

* Ability to travel regularly between locations as needed
* Ability to work occasional evenings or weekends based on organizational needs
* Ability to move throughout facilities and remain stationary for extended periods as needed

**Organizational Structure Statement**

This position is intended to support long-term operational leadership continuity across the enterprise. The Director of Operations may assume expanded operational oversight responsibilities based on organizational structure, business needs, leadership transitions, and enterprise growth initiatives.

**Job Description**
-------------------

The Opportunity
 
 
The St. Jude Leadership Academy is building the systems, experiences and capabilities that help leaders across St. Jude grow their impact. We’re looking for a Director of Academy Operations who can help turn that vision into an enterprise-scale reality.

This is a role for a builder.

 
 

As the Academy’s primary operational leader and integrator, you’ll translate strategy into an integrated portfolio of work and create the infrastructure needed to move ideas from concept through implementation, evaluation and scale. You’ll work across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and institutional partners to connect priorities, clarify ownership and turn complex, cross-functional work into coordinated action.

You’ll also serve as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership, bringing visibility to priorities, tradeoffs, resources and execution risks while helping shape how the Academy delivers its work across St. Jude.

Because the Leadership Academy operates as a small, highly collaborative team, this isn’t a role where strategy gets handed off once the plan is built. You’ll move comfortably between enterprise-level thinking and hands-on execution, building the systems that allow a small team to have an outsized impact across St. Jude.

 
 

### **What You’ll Do**

As Director of Academy Operations, you will:

* **Turn strategy into execution.** Translate Leadership Academy priorities into an integrated portfolio, implementation roadmap and operating plan.
* **Lead complex work from idea to impact.** Guide cross-functional initiatives from concept and design through implementation, evaluation and scale.
* **Build the Academy’s operating infrastructure.** Establish governance, decision points, roles, handoffs, planning processes and operating rhythms that create clarity and accountability.
* **Connect work across St. Jude.** Build strong partnerships across Leadership Development, Culture Strategy and other institutional functions, bringing people and priorities together while maintaining clear roles and ownership.
* **See around corners.** Identify dependencies, duplication, capacity constraints, gaps and execution risks across the Academy’s portfolio and drive solutions.
* **Create visibility into impact.** Establish portfolio-level measures, dashboards and reporting that show progress, outcomes and organizational impact.
* **Help good ideas scale.** Develop practical approaches for moving promising concepts and pilots into sustainable institutional practices.
* **Lead operational and resource planning.** Oversee budgets, resources, technology, vendors, contracts and external partnerships that support the Academy’s work.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Apply human-centered design, agile and continuous-improvement approaches to strengthen programs, processes and operations.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor.** Help senior leadership navigate priorities, tradeoffs, sequencing, resource allocation and execution risk.
* **Communicate with influence.** Develop executive-level materials and clearly communicate progress, decisions, risks and recommendations to senior stakeholders.
* **Stay close to the work.** Remain directly involved in execution when needed, reflecting the hands-on, highly collaborative nature of the Academy team.
* **Develop people and teams.** Create clarity around goals and expectations while supporting performance, engagement, professional growth and meaningful career experiences.
 

 

### **What You Bring**

You are an experienced operations and program leader who knows how to take an ambitious vision and build the structure required to make it real. You are comfortable navigating complexity, influencing across organizational boundaries and leading work when accountability is shared across multiple teams.

You bring:

* A bachelor’s degree; an advanced degree is preferred.
* 10+ years of related professional experience.
* Significant experience leading complex enterprise programs, operations, transformation initiatives or similar work within a large organization.
* Demonstrated experience **building operating models, processes or organizational capabilities**, not simply administering established programs.
* A track record of translating strategic objectives into operational plans and driving those plans through execution.
* Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional work in environments where accountability and authority are distributed.
* Strong strategic program management, operational, analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
* The ability to move comfortably between enterprise-level strategy and detailed execution.
* Strong consulting, stakeholder-management and influencing skills, including experience partnering with senior leaders.
* Experience with budget planning, resource management, vendor relationships and contract negotiations.
* Experience with human-centered design, agile methods, continuous improvement or related approaches.
* Strong written, verbal and executive communication skills.
* Experience in leadership development, organizational development, talent, culture or another people-related function is preferred, but not required.

### **The Kind of Leader Who Will Thrive Here**

This role may be especially compelling if you:

* See complexity and instinctively begin creating clarity and structure.
* Get energy from **building something**, not simply maintaining what already exists.
* Can zoom out to see the enterprise picture and then zoom back in to make sure the details work.
* Know how to lead through influence when the people needed to accomplish the work don’t necessarily report to you.
* Are comfortable asking difficult questions about priorities, capacity, tradeoffs and risk.
* Enjoy turning promising ideas into repeatable, sustainable ways of working.
* Believe measurement should help people make better decisions, not simply create more reporting.
* Approach problems with curiosity and are willing to challenge established ways of working when there is a better path forward.
* Can advise senior leaders one moment and roll up your sleeves to solve an execution problem the next.
* Want to build systems that make it possible for other people to do exceptional work.
 

 
 

### **Key Capabilities**

Enterprise program leadership • Operational strategy • Portfolio management • Cross-functional integration • Systems thinking • Execution • Consultative problem solving • Stakeholder influence • Human-centered problem solving • Measurement and analytics • Continuous improvement • Organizational change

### **Why St. Jude**

At St. Jude, operational excellence ultimately serves a larger purpose. The work of the Leadership Academy helps equip leaders across the institution to lead people, navigate change and advance a mission unlike any other.

As **Director of Academy Operations**, you’ll have the opportunity to help shape not only what the Leadership Academy delivers, but how it works: building the infrastructure, partnerships and operating practices that allow a small team to create meaningful impact across St. Jude.

 
 

**Minimum Education and/or Training:**

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Master's degree preferred.
 

 

**Minimum Experience:**

* 10+ years related experience.
* Significant experience managing large teams and building systems and processes to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
* Experience translating strategic goals into operational goals and overseeing execution.
* Proven experience leading administration & operations management, driving execution, managing stakeholders, budget planning & resource mgmt.
* Prior experience in vendor contract negotiations and strategic vendor relationship management.
* Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role.
 

 

**Compensation**

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $125,840 - $238,160 per year for the role of Director of Operations: St. Jude Leadership Academy.

Explore our exceptional benefits!

 
 

We are committed to a human-centered hiring experience. Technology may support portions of our process, but recruiting decisions involve human review and engagement. Learn more about our approach to AI.

 
 

St. Jude is an Equal Opportunity Employer

 
 

**No Search Firms**

St. Jude Children's Research Hospital does not accept unsolicited assistance from search firms for employment opportunities. Please do not call or email. All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee or other representative at St. Jude via email, the internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written search agreement in place and approved by HR will result in no fee being paid in the event the candidate is hired by St. Jude.
