role.title: Sr. Staff Solutions Architect – Manufacturing (R6252)
role.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 

Shield AI is seeking a senior Solutions Architect – Manufacturing to serve as the functional and technical authority for Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP across Manufacturing, MRP/Supply Chain Planning, and the shop-floor-to-ERP technology stack. This role owns the design, configuration, and continuous improvement of Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP capabilities, with deep, hands-on strength in MES, QMS, and PLM — ensuring plan, build, and quality processes operate as one coherent, well-architected system.

This is a hands-on, business-facing role. The Solutions Architect is expected to be the trusted advisor and go-to resource for Manufacturing and Quality business partners on any process change involving Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Planning or the MES, QMS, and PLM bolt-on applications — translating business need into a scalable, well-architected solution, and then configuring and implementing that solution directly for medium-complexity projects. For large, complex initiatives, this person leads solution design and partners with Shield AI’s implementation partner to deliver, while remaining the accountable architect and voice of the business throughout.

Beyond core ERP, this role holds full ownership of Shield AI’s manufacturing-adjacent bolt-on application landscape — including MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter) — and is responsible for how those systems integrate with Oracle Fusion ERP to form a coherent plan-to-build-to-quality operating model. This role partners closely with the other Solutions Architects for Supply Chain and Finance on shared MRP/planning signals, supplier quality matters tied to Procure-to-Pay and end-to-end integration with Finance/Accounting.



What you'll do: 




SOLUTION ARCHITECTURE & BUSINESS PARTNERSHIP

 - Designs and delivers technical solutions, creates detailed solution designs, specific integration points, and selects appropriate tools and frameworks. Collaboration with developers and engineers to implement solutions, conducts technical reviews and resolves design challenges.

 - Documents architectures, provides technical guidance during development, and ensures solutions adhere to performance, security, and interoperability requirements. Prototypes new approaches and evaluates emerging technologies for project suitability.

 - Serve as the primary point of contact and trusted advisor for business partners across Manufacturing, Production Planning, Quality, and Engineering on process design and system capability questions.

 - Act as the lead advocate for Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders in all ERP, MES, QMS, and PLM-related discussions, ensuring their operational needs, constraints, and priorities are represented in solution design.

 - Become the go-to resource for any proposed Manufacturing or Quality process change, evaluating impact, feasibility, and fit within the Oracle Fusion ERP data model and integration landscape before implementation.

 - Translate business requirements into scalable solution designs that balance standard Oracle Fusion functionality against configuration, extension, or integration needs.

 - Maintain a working command of adjacent end-to-end flows (Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay) to ensure Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS designs do not create downstream conflicts or gaps.


HANDS-ON CONFIGURATION & DELIVERY

 - Directly configure Oracle Fusion Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning/MRP, Work Definitions, Quality Inspections, and related modules for medium-sized projects, enhancements, and break/fix work.

 - Build, test, and deploy configuration changes, including setup of Fusion functional areas, security, workflows, approval rules, and data structures related to manufacturing and planning processes.

 - Author functional design documents, configuration workbooks, test scripts, and process/procedure documentation to support changes made in the environment.

 - For large or highly complex initiatives, define solution architecture and requirements, then partner closely with the implementation partner to execute — remaining accountable for solution quality, business fit, and knowledge transfer.

 - Participate in and help lead workshops, fit-gap sessions, and design reviews with Manufacturing and Quality stakeholders and implementation partner teams.


MRP, MES & QMS OWNERSHIP

 - Own MRP and Supply Chain Planning configuration — planning parameters, supply/demand netting, exception messages, and planner workbench — ensuring plans translate cleanly into executable work orders.

 - Own the functional roadmap, configuration governance, and business alignment for:

–    MES (Manufacturing Execution System) — work order execution, shop-floor data collection, routing/operation tracking

–    QMS (Quality Management System) — inspections, non-conformance, corrective/preventive action (CAPA), supplier quality

–    PLM – Teamcenter — engineering BOM, item master, and change management integration with Oracle Fusion

 - Ensure MES, QMS, and PLM remain architecturally aligned with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing and MRP, avoiding duplicate data ownership, conflicting BOM/routing data, or process gaps across systems.

 - Define and maintain the target integration model between MES, QMS, PLM, and Oracle Fusion ERP, including engineering-to-manufacturing BOM transfer and quality event-to-ERP disposition flows.

 - Partner with the Solutions Architect – Supply Chain on supplier-quality data flowing from Procure-to-Pay into QMS-driven supplier corrective action processes.


INTEGRATIONS

 - Design and help implement integrations between Oracle Fusion ERP and MES, QMS, and PLM (Teamcenter), including BOM/routing sync, work order status, and quality disposition data.

 - Define integration requirements, data mappings, and error-handling/reconciliation approaches in partnership with technical/integration teams.

 - Evaluate integration patterns (API, middleware, file-based) and recommend approaches appropriate to data volume, latency, and criticality, particularly for shop-floor/real-time data.

 - Support testing, cutover, and hypercare activities for integration-related changes.


GOVERNANCE & CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

 - Maintain configuration standards, documentation, and change control discipline for the Manufacturing, MRP, MES, QMS, and PLM functional areas.

 - Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, and improved data quality across planning, production, and quality cycles.

 - Stay current on Oracle Fusion quarterly releases relevant to Manufacturing and Planning, and assess/recommend adoption of new features.

 - Mentor junior functional/technical resources and contribute to a growing internal ERP center of excellence.

Required Qualifications:

 - 12+ years of progressive experience in enterprise ERP systems, with significant depth in MRP/Supply Chain Planning, MES, and QMS functions.

 - Hands-on experience configuring Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP (Manufacturing and Planning pillars); comfortable working directly in the application, not solely at a requirements level.

 - Experience across multiple full-lifecycle ERP implementations (Oracle Fusion required; prior experience with Oracle EBS, SAP, or other major ERP platforms is a plus).

 - Direct, hands-on experience with at least one MES platform and one QMS platform, including their integration into an ERP environment.

 - Working knowledge of Order-to-Cash and Procure-to-Pay processes and how they interact with Manufacturing, MRP, and quality operations.

 - Demonstrated experience acting as a functional/solution architect — able to design solutions independently, not just execute configuration tasks handed down by others.

 - Experience partnering with or managing systems integrators/implementation partners on complex delivery efforts.

 - Strong business partnering and stakeholder management skills; comfortable being the primary escalation point for Manufacturing and Quality process questions.

 - Working understanding of integration concepts and experience partnering on ERP-to-MES/QMS/PLM system integrations.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing functional design documents, process documentation, and executive-level updates.

Preferred Qualifications:

 - Prior consulting background (Big 4, Oracle partner, or boutique Oracle Fusion implementation firm) strongly preferred.

 - Direct experience owning or integrating PLM (Teamcenter) with Oracle Fusion Manufacturing/Engineering data.

 - Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated/complex discrete manufacturing environments.

 - Familiarity with Oracle Integration Cloud (OIC) or similar middleware/integration platforms.

 - Oracle Fusion certifications in Manufacturing, Supply Chain Planning, or Quality.

 - Experience operating in environments with export control, ITAR/CUI, or other regulated data-handling requirements.

AI & Agentic Automation Capabilities:

 - Shield AI is investing in Agentic AI to accelerate and automate manufacturing and quality operations. This role is expected to actively identify, design, and help implement AI-driven automation across Manufacturing, MRP, MES, and QMS — not simply consume AI tools built by others.
 
 - Identify high-value candidates for Agentic AI automation within Manufacturing and Quality — e.g., planner workbench exception triage, shop-floor anomaly detection, quality non-conformance routing/CAPA drafting, and work order scheduling recommendations.
 
 - Design and configure AI agent workflows using Oracle’s embedded AI/ML and agentic capabilities (e.g., Oracle Fusion AI agents, OCI Generative AI, Redwood/AI-driven planning recommendations) as they become available across Fusion Manufacturing and Planning.
 
 - Partner with IT/data teams to define prompts, guardrails, data inputs, and approval/exception paths for AI agents acting on manufacturing and quality transactions, ensuring appropriate human-in-the-loop controls.
 
 - Evaluate and pilot third-party or custom Agentic AI tools (e.g., for predictive maintenance, quality defect pattern detection, MES data synthesis, or supply/demand sensing) and assess fit against the target architecture.
 
 - Use AI-assisted tools for day-to-day solution work — requirements analysis, test script generation, configuration documentation, and data mapping — to increase delivery speed and quality.
 
 - Bring or build fluency in prompt engineering and AI workflow design; prior hands-on experience with generative AI or agentic AI platforms (Oracle AI Agent Studio, OCI Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, UiPath/Automation Anywhere agentic features, or similar) is a strong plus.
 
 - Champion responsible AI adoption — data quality, auditability, and change management — when introducing agentic workflows into regulated, ITAR/CUI-sensitive environments.

role.title: Staff Engineer, Electromechanical Systems Advance Manufacturing - Ranger (R6547)
role.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

We are seeking a Staff Electromechanical Systems Advance Manufacturing Engineer to support the manufacturing and integration of complex motion-control and mechanically actuated systems across advanced aerospace and defense platforms. This role focuses on electromechanical assemblies involving actuators, hydraulics, pneumatics, motors, pumps, and integrated mechanical/electrical subsystems.

The ideal candidate thrives in fast-paced production environments and has experience developing robust manufacturing processes for highly integrated systems. 

What you'll do:

 - Lead manufacturing engineering efforts for electromechanical subsystems and assemblies 

 - Develop and optimize manufacturing processes, tooling, work instructions, and production flows for: 

 - Actuators 

 - Motors and drives 

 - Hydraulic systems 

 - Pneumatic systems 

 - Pumps and fluid systems 

 - Powertrain components 

 - Motion-control assemblies 

 - Partner with design engineering to improve manufacturability, reliability, testability, and producibility 

 - Drive root cause investigations and corrective actions for electromechanical manufacturing issues 

 - Develop work instructions, quality standards, and inspection methods  

 - Support supplier qualification, process validation, and production readiness reviews 

 - Lead DFM/DFA reviews and transition new products into manufacturing 

 - Support system integration, validation, and troubleshooting activities 

 - Define manufacturing standards, process controls, and acceptance criteria 

 - Support failure analysis and reliability improvement initiatives 

 - Collaborate with production, quality, supply chain, and test engineering teams 

 - Mentor junior manufacturing engineers 

Tools & skills:

 - MES & QMS systems, 3DEXPERIENCE / Teamcenter (PLM) systems, supplier manufacturing processes, 5S/visual management, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). 

Required qualifications:

 - 7+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in experience in electromechanical systems 

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechatronics, or related field 

 - Experience in prototype manufacturing in a startup or rapid-growth environment. 

 - Experience with:  

 - Actuators and motion systems  

 - Hydraulics and pneumatics  

 - Mechanical/electrical integration  

 - Precision mechanical assemblies 

 - Demonstrated ability to work in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment and adapt to changing priorities. 

 - Knowledge of manufacturing process development and production scaling  

 - Strong understanding of DFM/DFA principles  

 - Experience with root cause analysis and corrective action methodologies  

Preferred qualifications:

 - Aerospace, defense, robotics, or automotive industry experience  

 - Experience with servo systems and motor control assemblies  

 - Knowledge of GD&T and mechanical inspection methods  

 - Familiarity with lean manufacturing and production optimization 

 - Experience with ERP/MES systems and manufacturing data analysis 

 - Strong project management skills, including experience managing multiple priorities and deadlines 

 - Knowledge of quality standards, such as AS9100 or ISO 9001 

 - Proficiency in CAD software

role.title: Director of Industrialization
role.description:
About the Company 

 We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

 The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

 About the Job 

 Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.

 Panthalassa is moving from pilot production into volume manufacturing, and we are hiring a Director of Industrialization to stand up the production lines that get us there. You will own the manufacturing strategy, equipment definition, commissioning schedule, and production ramp for our new factories — the work that turns a proven pilot process and a rate target into a qualified, running line.

 This is the person who decides what we build with, how the line is configured, how long installation and commissioning will take, and how quickly the factory can climb to rate. Working with Pilot Manufacturing, you will translate product designs and proven pilot processes into a build strategy, then select and procure major capital equipment, sequence installation and qualification against a hard schedule, and define the ramp curve the rest of the business plans against.

 This role starts as an individual contributor and grows into a leadership role . For the first phase you will be doing the work yourself: building the models, writing the equipment specs, running the vendor evaluations, and standing in the building during commissioning. As the factories come online you will define, hire, and lead the industrialization and manufacturing engineering team that supports them. We are looking for someone who is genuinely happy in both modes and who wants to build the organization they will eventually run.

 You will report to the Vice President of Manufacturing and work most closely with the Director of Pilot Manufacturing, who owns the processes and product maturity you will be industrializing, and with the Plant Manager of each new facility, who owns the site once it is operating. You will also partner continuously with Pilot Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Technical Program Management, Digital Thread, Facilities, Finance, EHS, and Marine Operations.

 Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Responsibilities 

 Manufacturing Strategy and Industrialization Planning 

 
 Own the industrialization roadmap that takes each product and process from pilot production to qualified rate production.

 Build and maintain the manufacturing capacity and cost models that drive line decisions, including takt time, station balance, throughput, yield assumptions, unit cost, and capital intensity per unit of annual capacity.

 Partner with the Director of Pilot Manufacturing to define the build strategy for major structures and subsystems, including work breakdown, station sequencing, subassembly strategy, and heavy lift and transport requirements, bringing the rate-production perspective to processes proven in pilot.

 Partner with Supply Chain on make-versus-buy and internal-versus-contract-manufacturing decisions for major process steps, contributing the capacity, capital, process capability, and cycle-time analysis that informs them.

 Contribute manufacturing requirements to site selection and facility planning, including footprint, bay dimensions and door clearances, floor loading, crane and heavy lift capacity, laydown area, load-out access, and utility loads. Site selection is led by company leadership; you provide the manufacturing analysis and requirements that inform it.

 Develop facility layouts and material flow plans that support the target rate and future expansion.

 Provide manufacturability feedback to engineering, and drive design changes that reduce cost, cycle time, and process risk before they are locked in.

 
 Process, Tooling, and Equipment 

 
 Own the production equipment strategy and the major equipment list for each line, including welding and joining systems, automation and material handling, machining, coating, NDT and inspection, electronic rack assembly, panel wiring, hardware integration, and test infrastructure.

 Lead equipment specification, vendor evaluation, technical bid comparison, and selection in partnership with Pilot Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Quality.

 Define and manage the manufacturing capital plan, including budgets, phasing, long-lead-item strategy, and contingency, and present capital requests for approval.

 Transfer proven processes, work instructions, tooling, and training material out of pilot manufacturing and into the new lines, working with the Director of Pilot Manufacturing rather than reinventing what already works.

 Define tooling, fixture, and station design requirements and sequence their development against the installation schedule.

 Manage equipment vendors through design review, factory acceptance testing, delivery, installation, and site acceptance testing.

 
 Installation, Commissioning, and Qualification 

 
 Own the integrated installation and commissioning schedule for each line, from facility handover through equipment installation, utility tie-in, commissioning, process qualification, and first article.

 Define and drive the manufacturing critical path, including long-lead equipment, contractor sequencing, and dependencies on product and process readiness.

 Establish operational readiness criteria and lead readiness reviews with Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, and the incoming Plant Manager.

 Define the production system requirements the line needs at startup, including ERP, MES, and quality system needs, and partner with Digital Thread and enterprise systems teams on their delivery.

 Identify, track, and retire manufacturing schedule and technical risk with clear owners, mitigations, and escalation paths.

 
 Production Ramp 

 
 Define the manufacturing ramp curve for each line, including rate milestones, yield and learning-curve assumptions, labor ramp and training requirements, and staffing plan by station, in partnership with Technical Program Management and Production Planning.

 Set the readiness criteria that gate each step of the ramp and hold the line on them when schedule pressure builds.

 Establish the baseline process metrics, reporting cadence, and problem-solving mechanisms the Plant Manager will operate with.

 Lead a clean, documented handoff to the Plant Manager, and stay engaged as a partner through the ramp to rate.

 Capture lessons learned from each startup and apply them to the next line.

 
 Team Building and Organizational Development 

 
 Define the industrialization and manufacturing engineering org needed to support production at scale, including roles, sequencing of hires, and the split between central and site-based engineering.

 Recruit, hire, and develop that team, and set its technical standards, operating cadence, and priorities.

 Build the review mechanisms that keep industrialization work rigorous and visible, including design reviews, readiness reviews, and capital approval processes.

 Mentor engineers across manufacturing and grow bench strength for future factory startups.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 10+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, industrialization, or manufacturing operations, including time in a technical leadership role.

 Direct experience taking a product or process from prototype or pilot production through installation, qualification, and rate production.

 Demonstrated ownership of a manufacturing capital plan, including equipment specification, vendor selection, budgeting, and installation and commissioning schedules.

 Strong quantitative skills and fluency building capacity, cost, and ramp models that leadership can make decisions on.

 Experience defining and executing a production ramp, including realistic yield and learning-curve assumptions and the discipline to gate progress on readiness.

 Experience translating product designs into executable build strategies, process documentation, and station-level work content.

 Willingness to operate as a hands-on individual contributor now and build a team later, with genuine interest in both.

 Experience leading through influence across engineering, supply chain, quality, and site operations without direct authority over most of it.

 Clear written and verbal communication, and the judgment to know which decisions need a model, which need a conversation, and which need to be escalated.

 Comfort operating with incomplete information in a fast-moving environment where the product is still maturing.

 
 Desired Qualifications 

 
 Experience industrializing large welded steel structures, pressure-retaining assemblies, marine vessels, or comparable large-format fabricated hardware.

 Experience with waterfront manufacturing, shipyard or fabrication yard operations, or load-out and launch of large assemblies.

 Experience scaling from prototype or pilot production into volume manufacturing at a hardware startup.

 Experience hiring and building a manufacturing engineering or industrialization team from a small base.

 Experience selecting and deploying automation, robotic welding, or large-envelope machining and inspection systems.

 Familiarity with enterprise systems that support production, including PLM, ERP, MRP, MES, and QMS, and what they need to do at line startup.

 Experience with contract manufacturers, including qualification, technology transfer, and rate readiness.

 Experience in high-consequence or capital-intensive industries such as aerospace, defense, energy, shipbuilding, automotive, or advanced manufacturing.

 Working knowledge of facility and industrial infrastructure requirements for heavy manufacturing, including utilities, material handling, and layout and flow design.

 
 The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

 Skills and Competencies 

 
 High ownership and a bias toward delivery over analysis for its own sake.

 Ability to move between a spreadsheet model, a shop floor, and a leadership discussion in the same day.

 Rigor about assumptions, and willingness to state them plainly and revise them publicly.

 Ability to build trust quickly with plant leadership, trades, vendors, and contractors.

 Sound judgment about where to spend capital and where to spend ingenuity instead.

 Commitment to safety and quality as prerequisites for rate, not tradeoffs against it.

 
 Additional Requirements 

 
 This role requires regular on-site presence in Portland, Oregon, and at our pilot and contract manufacturing facility in Vancouver, Washington.

 Significant travel is expected, including to equipment vendors, contract manufacturers, candidate sites, and new facilities under construction. Travel will be heaviest during equipment procurement and startup phases and may include international travel.

 Comfort working across office, lab, fabrication, construction, and waterfront environments, with personal protective equipment required in designated areas.

 Ability to work extended or off-shift hours intermittently during commissioning, startup, and other time-critical operational windows.

 
 Compensation and Benefits 

 If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

 
 Cash compensation of $215,000 - $290,000.

 Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

 A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including:
 
 Flexible paid time off

 Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled)

 Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

 


 Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

 
 Location 

 This is an on-site position with expectation of regular presence in our Portland, Oregon facilities and at our Vancouver, Washington pilot manufacturing site. This position requires substantial domestic and international travel in support of equipment procurement, commissioning, and new facility startups.

 Exceptional remote candidates willing to spend at least 50% of their time in Portland are encouraged to apply.

role.title: Head of Quality
role.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Quality to lead quality as a function, alongside the Head of Manufacturing. You own the quality system, supplier quality across our supply base, product safety certifications, and the quality targets the company holds itself to. The quality engineers and the quality manager report to you, and you grow the team from there. You report to the CTO. As our operations organization grows, you and the Head of Manufacturing will report to the leader of that organization.
This is a building role. The first pieces, incoming inspection, supplier controls and failure analysis, are being put in place by the team you will lead. Your job is to turn them into a system that holds as production grows, a supplier base we can trust, and a quality record that customers and certifying bodies can verify. You have the authority to hold any shipment that is not right.

Requirements
You have led a quality function at a company that builds complex electromechanical hardware in volume
You have built or rebuilt a quality system and taken it through ISO 9001 or an equivalent certification
You have run supplier quality across a supply base, including suppliers overseas
You have taken a product through product safety certification
You have built and led a team of quality engineers and managers
You make decisions from data, and you can hold a shipment when the data says so
Nice to haves
Robotics, automation, vehicles, or capital equipment
Reliability engineering methods: life testing, failure rate analysis, design reviews
Building quality data and tooling that other teams use
Experience with manufacturing execution systems
Benefits
Fully employer-covered health insurance , so you’re protected without the premium.
A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.
Compensation
The base salary range for this role is $220,000 to $280,000, depending on experience.
As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.
Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

role.title: Head of Quality
role.description:
Your responsibilities
 
 
**Lead Quality Excellence in a Fast-Paced Manufacturing Environment**
We are seeking an experienced
**Head of Quality**
to lead our Quality organization and drive world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing the Quality Management System, developing quality strategies, leading customer and supplier quality initiatives, and driving continuous improvement throughout the organization.
 
 

* Lead and maintain the Quality Management System in compliance with IATF 16949 requirements.
* Develop and execute quality objectives, metrics, and improvement initiatives aligned with business goals.
* Manage customer and supplier quality activities, including audits, APQP, PPAP, launch readiness, corrective actions, and change management.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action efforts for internal and external quality issues.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance product quality, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Monitor and report key quality metrics, including scrap, rework, and overall quality performance.
* Partner with cross-functional teams to support production, new product launches, and supplier development.
* Build, develop, and lead high-performing quality teams.

**Success Competencies**
The Head of Quality embodies the following competencies:
 
 

* Manages Complexity: Making sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* Decision Quality: Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.
* Action Oriented: Taking on new opportunities and tough challenges with a sense of urgency, high energy and enthusiasm.
* Ensures Accountability: Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments.
* Drive Results: Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.
* Develops Talent: Developing people to meet both their career goals and the organization’s goals.
* Builds Effective Teams: Building strong-identity teams that apply their diverse skills and perspective to achieve common goals.
* Communicates Effectively: Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* Instills Trust: Gaining the confidence and trust of others though honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
* Manages Ambiguity: Operating effectively, even when things are not certain or the way forward is not clear.
* Being Resilient: Rebounding from setbacks and adversity when facing difficult situations.

**Supervisory Responsibility:**
Directly manages the Quality Department including the Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, Quality Planning, Quality Lab/ Gauging, Change and Series Management functions.
 
 
Your profile
 
 
**Qualifications:**
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.
 
 

* Education: A Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or a related technical field is required, experience in Quality functions within the automotive industry or related areas.
* Language: Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers, OEMs, or employees of organization.
* Technology: Microsoft Office Suite knowledge; SAP/ERP knowledge preferred. Knowledge of IATF 16949, APQP-PPAP, FMEA, MSA, 8D, Statistics, GD&T and mechanical manufacturing processes.
* Travel: Occasional travel, up to 10% including international

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 
 
Your benefits
 
 

* Annual Bonus Eligibility of 6% of your base salary!
* 10% Shift Premium, based on base wage
* Perfect Attendance Bonus; $2,600 Minimum Annual Potential!
* Performance Productivity Bonus, $2,600 Minimum Annual Potential!
* Paid Time Off (PTO)
* Supplier Discounts
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Paid Company Holidays
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription Drug Coverage
* Exclusive free medical services through our partnership with Marathon Health for employees and their dependents 3+ years of age.
* 401(K) Plan with 5% Company match!

**Company**
thyssenkrupp Dynamic Components is one of the world’s automotive industry leading partners for development and manufacturing of highly complex, state-of-the-art drivetrain technologies for both combustion engines and electric motors. Worldwide, 10 locations with 3,800 employees produce over 25 million drivetrain components per year. The product portfolio includes camshafts and cylinder head cover modules for the valve train as well as rotor shafts for battery electric vehicles.
 
 
Our electrical A/C compressor, designed for the natural refrigerant CO2, sets new standards in efficient and sustainable thermal management.
 
 
With precision and passion, we are enabling our customers in the automotive industry to achieve their emission and sustainability targets for more than 30 years.
 
 
thyssenkrupp Presta Dynamic Components is proud to be Certified by
**Great Place To Work**
. The prestigious award is based entirely on what current employees say about their experience working at thyssenkrupp Presta Dynamic Components. This year, 82% of employees said it’s a great place To Work – 25 points higher than the average U.S. company. Great Place To Work is the global authority on workplace culture, employee experience, and the leadership behaviors proven to deliver market-leading revenue, employee retention and increased innovation.
 
 
Contact
 
 
We only accept online applications submitted through the 'Apply Now' button on this job posting. You can find all current job openings on our career site at: https://jobs.thyssenkrupp.com/en Thank you for your interest in joining our team!

Job details:
 
**Plant Manager - St. Louis, MO**
This Jobot Job is hosted by: Madison Fincher
 
Are you a fit? Easy Apply now by clicking the "Easy Apply" button
 
and sending us your resume.
 
Salary: $120,000 - $150,000 per year
 
 
 
**A bit about us:**
Headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri with more than 1,200 employees and nearing $2B in revenue. A diversified construction company that partners with leading organizations throughout North America to build their most challenging and important projects.
 
 
Provides construction solutions to the automotive, commercial, civil, energy, food & beverage, healthcare, heavy industrial, industrial process, and water industries.
 
 
Our Values:
 
 
Working Safely
 
Valuing Diversity
 
Serving Humbly
 
Executing with Integrity
 
Solving Creatively
 
Engaging Fully
 
 
 
**Why join us?**
Profit-sharing plan, cash bonus programs and annual cost-of-living adjustments
 
Generous salary increases and per diems for qualified out-of-town assignments
 
Health, dental and vision insurance eligibility on day one
 
Paid parental leave
 
Continuing education reimbursement
 
Personalized career development and training programs
 
Minimum of 29 days of PTO (including holidays) for entry-level roles
 
Fitness center for St. Louis office-based team members
 
Gym membership reimbursement for project-based team members
 
Corporate office cafeteria access
 
Employee Resource Group (ERG) opportunities
 
Philanthropy opportunities
 
 
 
**Job Details**
The Plant Manager directs and manages all plant operations with overall responsibilities for production, maintenance, quality and other production-related activities as a part of a premier structural steel fabricator and erector.
 
 
Essential Responsibilities & Duties include the following; however, other duties may be assigned. The Company provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with a disability, unless doing so poses an undue hardship on the Company. To be a qualified individual, an employee must be able to perform each of the essential functions of his or her job with or without a reasonable accommodation.
 
 
Directs and manages Responsible for labor relations and managing union issues associated with craft labor.
 
Manages capital asset maintenance.
 
Establishes and monitors overall plant performance for production and quality standards.
 
Controls and minimizes repair expenses.
 
Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment; replaces or makes adjustments to plant facilities and equipment when necessary.
 
Provides leadership and training to accomplish Company goals and objectives.
 
Implements and maintains preventative maintenance programs.
 
Incorporates shop floor organization and plant cleanliness among plant personnel.
 
Manages and directs non-supervisory administrative or union employees and is responsible for the overall direction and management of these employees.
 
Travels to Company and subsidiary offices; offsite client, subcontractor, and supplier meetings; and other locations across North America to fulfill the essential duties of the role as required.
 
Exhibits regular and reliable attendance in person as required by the Supervisor, Company guidelines, and/or project and office obligations.
 
Education and Experience
 
 
Bachelor's degree and 5 years’ plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
 
 
Experience managing in a union environment required.
 
Working knowledge of budgets and financials statements required.
 
Background with manufacturing methods, process improvement programs and procedures required.

role.title: Head of Plant Production Engineering
role.description:
Your Contribution
 
 
The Head of Plant Production Engineering is responsible for leading all Production Engineering activities associated with customer projects, product acquisitions, new product launches, industrialization, and production readiness within the plant. This position serves as the plant's primary owner for Production Engineering processes, ensuring successful execution of the Product Development Process (PDP) from acquisition through Start of Production (SOP) and ramp-up. The role provides leadership to Production Engineers, drives standardization and deployment of manufacturing concepts, ensures manufacturability of product designs, manages capital investments, and represents Operations within project core teams. The Plant Head of Production Engineering ensures project launches meet safety, quality, delivery, cost, and operational performance objectives.
 
 

* Lead, develop, coach, & manage the plant Production Engineering organization.
* Build organizational capability to support current and future product launches.
* Own industrialization activities for all customer projects within the plant. Ensure successful execution of product launches from acquisition and business transfer through SOP and stabilization.
* Lead development of manufacturing concepts, production processes, line layouts, and assembly strategies.
* Ensure product designs are manufacturable and meet operational standards.
* Coordinate launch readiness across Manufacturing Engineering, Tooling Engineering, Quality, Logistics, Purchasing, and Operations Support acquisition reviews and participate in PAC, PRC, and pre-development activities.
* Ensure implementation of Design-for-Manufacturing principles throughout project development. Ensure compliance with MAHLE PDP milestones, gates, deliverables, and timing requirements. Oversee completion of all Production Engineering deliverables throughout all quality gates.
* Monitor project status, risks, cost performance, capacity requirements, and launch readiness. Lead escalation activities when project risks threaten timing, quality, or cost objectives. Review project dashboards and launch metrics with plant leadership and program teams.
* Approve and govern: Manufacturing concepts, Process flows, Plant layouts, Assembly concepts, Material flow strategies, Value stream integration.
* Ensure application of Lean Manufacturing and Manufacturing Optimization Process (MOP) methodologies in alignment with Operations Excellence Manager.
* Drive takt-time analysis, line balancing, ergonomic studies, and capacity planning. Validate cycle times using MTM or equivalent engineering methods. Ensure implementation of standardized manufacturing processes across the region.
* Ensure development, completion, and approval of Process FMEA (P-FMEA), Control Plans, Special Characteristics, Process Capability Studies, Validation Plans. Support flawless launch activities and manufacturing risk reduction. Lead readiness reviews for installation checks, internal process approval, internal run at rate, customer run at rate, PPAP readiness. Ensure production systems consistently achieve quality and operational KPI’s.
* Lead capital expenditure planning and approval activities. Validate business cases and investment requirements. Ensure optimal utilization of existing equipment before requesting new capital. Support supplier selection through PDC and SDC processes. Approve manufacturing equipment specifications. Participate in procurement and acceptance of production equipment, tooling, fixtures, and test systems.
* Chair Production Engineering project meetings, and lead the plant Production Engineering Extended Team, ensuring effective communication between Project Core Teams and Plant Extended Teams.

**Your Experience & Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s Degree required, B.S. in Engineering, or related technical discipline required. Master’s Degree preferred.
* 8+ years’ experience in manufacturing, launch, industrialization, or production engineering.
* 5+ years’ progressive leadership responsibility regarding engineering or manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success in leading complex product launches and PDP projects.
* Experience in an automotive manufacturing facility required; high volume, medium to large campus experience preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge in IATF16949, ISO14001 and 45001 Audits and processes.
* Excellent diagnostic abilities / root cause analysis required; Lean Six Sigma and Black Belt certification strongly preferred.

Our Offer
 
 
We will provide a collaborative environment working on exciting assignments, along with ongoing personal & career development opportunities. We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every single requirement. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles! After receiving your online application, the interview process will typically be, a screening call followed by Personal Interview(s).
 
 
For more information about MAHLE and what a career with us looks like for you, click here. and to learn more about our foundation owned technology group click here.
 
 
#DiversityMatters with our inclusive culture, we welcome applications from all social, religious & ethnical backgrounds, disabilities both mental and physical, identities (gender) and neurodivergent people.
 
 
MAHLE is not currently hiring individuals for this position who now or in the future require sponsorship for employment based non-immigrant and immigrant visas. However, as a global company, MAHLE offers many job opportunities outside of the U.S. which can be found through our employment website www.jobs.mahle.com
 
 
MAHLE Jobs & Career | Jobs With Opportunity to Advance MAHLE Careers
 
 
Find your job at MAHLE. Get to know this leading international supplier to the automotive industry as an employer. Shape the future, with us.
 
 
**Do you have any questions?**
SHEILA.HOOVER@MAHLE.COM

role.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
role.description:
**Job Description**
The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.
 
 
Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.
 
 
**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**
In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:
 
 
Be Curious
 
 

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots
 
 

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High
 
 

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast
 
 

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More
 
 

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations
 
 

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

Additional Information
 
 
Benefits:
 
 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

role.title: Director of Quality
role.description:
**About Us:**

BW Design Group is a fully integrated architecture, engineering, construction, system integration, and consulting firm committed to helping our clients realize their most critical goals from Strategy to Commercialization. As the only firm born from a manufacturing technology company to become an independent and fully integrated firm, we combine deep domain expertise in the manufacturing environment with an approach that is built to serve the dynamic needs of our clients. Rooted in our distinct culture of Truly Human Leadership, we cultivate the leaders who will define tomorrow and partner with our clients in the food & beverage, life sciences, industrial, and advanced technology industries to build the future of manufacturing and technology. 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world. 
 

**Job Description:**

**Who You’ll Work With**

At BW Design Group, you'll collaborate with experienced leaders, technical specialists, and subject matter experts to solve complex challenges for some of the world's leading companies. You'll join a growing team of more than 2000 professionals across nearly 50 U.S. offices where you'll be empowered to make an impact, develop your expertise, and grow your career.

As Director, Quality for our Boston office, you will join our Regulatory Compliance Practice, leading the local quality team while serving as a trusted quality subject matter expert, industry thought leader, and client lead for life science clients across New England.

**What You’ll Do**

This role balances hands-on, billable project/service delivery with growing our Boston team, client relationships, and reputation in the industry.

* Lead a team of quality professionals and interface with clients
* Train, mentor, and recruit talent, championing the career growth of early-career professionals through Individual Development Plans and on-the-job coaching.
* Serve as the firm’s local quality SME across QMS maturity, supplier quality, CAPA and deviations, audit and inspection readiness, remediation, and product development, and advise clients on evolving regulatory guidance.
* Lead delivery of multiple concurrent projects, owning scope, budget, schedule, quality, risk, and client satisfaction.
* Drive thought leadership through publications, white papers, and industry conference presentations, and contribute to firmwide quality standards and best practices.
* Maintain a personal billable utilization target of approximately 60–70% while managing team staffing and utilization to meet billable hours goals.
Develop scopes, estimates, and proposals, and expand engagements with new and existing clients through your industry network. 

**What You’ll Bring**

* A minimum of fifteen years of increasing responsibility in quality services and project management for life sciences, biotech, medical device, or other FDA regulated projects.
* A minimum of five years of people leadership experience, including hiring, coaching, and developing quality professionals.
* Proven success in a consulting or professional services environment, including meeting billable utilization goals and leading client relationships
* Experience leading quality teams across capital project handover, QMS establishment, quality audits, root cause and deviation resolution, and remediation planning.
* Working knowledge of quality regulations for medical device, pharmaceuticals, biologics, C&GT, and aseptic/sterile manufacturing (21 CFR Parts 11, 210/211, and 820; ISO 13485; EU GMP), along with cGMP, good documentation practices, and risk management tools (ICH Q9, FMEA, PFMEA/DFMEA).
* Recognized industry expertise and thought leadership through publications, presentations, or professional associations such as ISPE, PDA, or ASQ; a Boston/New England life science network is preferred.
* Strong communication and technical writing skills, with experience developing proposals and estimates is preferred.
* A willingness to travel regionally to client sites throughout the Boston/New England area, as well as for company sponsored meetings, training, and industry events.
A Bachelor of Science in engineering or a related technical degree; an advanced degree or ASQ certification is preferred. 

 

Our culture and commitment to our people is what sets us apart. We foster an environment of mutual respect, integrity, and unconditional interest in the individual and collective success of our professionals. Our model and entrepreneurial mindset offer a rewarding, challenging, and highly flexible path.

 

As Director of Quality, you will build a meaningful and fulfilling career with the support of professional development resources and mentorships including our First Year Experience program, Individual Development Plans, and Career Path resources and tools. You will be surrounded by exceptional talent who will support your development as both a world-class professional and a highly effective leader.

 

*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*

Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify. 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments. 
 

**Company:**

Design Group

role.title: VP, Regional Manufacturing
role.description:
Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.

**Compensation:** $185,048 - $248,596. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.

**Location:** Dallas, TX

**Benefits of working for Primo Brands:**

**Health Benefits:**

Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA)

**Retirement/Investing:**

401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

**Insurance:**

Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment

**Other great benefits:**

Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.

The Regional Vice President (RVP), Manufacturing is responsible for leading the end-to-end manufacturing operations across a multi-site regional network within Primo Brands. This executive leader drives safety, quality, production, cost, service, people, and continuous improvement performance across factories while ensuring alignment with enterprise Supply Chain strategies and business objectives.

The RVP, Manufacturing partners closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Procurement, Planning, HR, and Finance leaders to deliver operational excellence, optimize manufacturing capacity, develop organizational capability, and support long-term business growth. The role is accountable for creating a high-performance culture that prioritizes safety, quality, associate engagement, customer service, and productivity improvements.

The Regional Vice President, Manufacturing reports to the Senior Vice President, Manufacturing Operations.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Compliance Leadership**

* Lead a culture where safety is the first priority and operational decisions reflect a zero-harm mindset.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive accountability for safety performance, incident reduction, risk mitigation, and compliance excellence.
* Serve as a visible champion for workplace safety and associate well-being.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead manufacturing performance across multiple factories, ensuring consistent execution against operational objectives.
* Deliver production plans that support customer demand, service expectations, and inventory requirements.
* Drive schedule attainment, throughput, asset utilization, and manufacturing reliability.
* Optimize regional manufacturing capacity and network performance.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems and operational governance routines.

**Food Safety & Quality**

* Champion food safety and quality excellence across all facilities.
* Ensure manufacturing sites maintain compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company standards.

role.description:
If you’re reading this on your way from 5am spin class to festival fast-pass, you’re CELSIUS®— an everyday hustler with the essential energy to aim high, and go the extra mile wherever your goals take you.

Joyful by design, sunny by nature, and unapologetically bold. If your bestie has you saved in their phone as “Icon,” you’re ALANI NU® — confident, colorful, and bringing main-character energy to every moment.

SoCal in your soul, attitude in your stride. If gravity doesn’t stop you and “impossible” sounds more like “dare you,” you’re ROCKSTAR®— a born rebel, raising the bar with mind-body energy and zero compromise.

-

Together, we’re Celsius Holdings, Inc.— a global CPG company united by three powerhouse brands and one incredibly talented team.

At Celsius, we pride ourselves on empowering our people. Every employee has a stake in our success. We create a collaborative culture built on inclusivity, innovation, and a belief that great ideas can come from anywhere.

And we’re on our way to building something bigger: a category where energy isn’t just consumed, it’s lived—where performance meets personality, brand becomes community, and every can crack sparks a statement.

**This is the future of modern energy. This is Celsius.**

Ready to take your career to the next level? Join our team and redefine what it means to be energized.

**Position Overview**
---------------------

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. This role requires strong business judgment, operational discipline, technical understanding, and the ability to build an accountable, collaborative culture focused on safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, and continuous improvement.

**On-Site:** Based full-time in Charlotte, NC at Big Beverages manufacturing facility

**Travel Requirements:** Up to 25% domestic travel

**People Management Responsibilities:** Yes

**Reports To:** VP of Manufacturing

**Role Type:** Full-Time

 **Requirements** 

* **Experience:** 7-10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in high-speed beverage filling/canning, food, or consumer packaged goods operations, including at least 3–5 years leading a plant or multi-department operation with full responsibility for production performance and hourly teams.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Food Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* Experience leading high-volume, automated manufacturing operations and managing production, maintenance, engineering, quality, safety, and continuous improvement functions.
* Working knowledge of FSSC 22000, ISO 22000 principles, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, food defense, food fraud prevention, traceability, prerequisite programs, CAPA systems, and audit readiness.
* Demonstrated success improving OEE, schedule attainment, throughput, labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, quality, cost performance, and equipment reliability through disciplined operating systems.
* Experience managing budgets, labor planning, capital projects, business cases, and plant-level financial performance.
* Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Experience using ERP/MRP, MES, maintenance-management, and manufacturing-performance systems to make data-driven decisions.
* Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work onsite at the manufacturing facility and support a flexible schedule based on operational needs.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Food Science, or a related field.
* PCQI, HACCP, FSSC 22000, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification or training.
* Hands-on experience with high-speed carbonated beverage filling and canning lines, including syrup batching/blending, water treatment, carbonation, fillers, can seamers and double-seam integrity, can warmers/pasteurizers, CIP sanitation, and end-of-line packaging and palletizing.
* Experience with plant start-ups, expansions, new line installations, automation, commissioning, scale-up, or major capital investments.
* Experience supporting a rapidly growing consumer brand or publicly traded company.
* Experience working with labor relations or represented manufacturing environments.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and consistent production of high-quality canned beverages from production scheduling through finished-goods handoff.
* Develop and execute the plant operating strategy in alignment with CELSIUS business objectives, demand forecasts, customer requirements, and long-term growth plans.
* Own production planning, capacity, staffing, schedule attainment, changeovers, line utilization, labor efficiency, and daily operating execution.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, warehouse, and support functions.
* Drive key operating metrics, including safety, OEE, throughput, yield, scrap, waste, downtime, labor productivity, cost per unit, on-time production, and schedule attainment.
* Establish and sustain leader standard work, tiered accountability, visual management, root-cause problem solving, standard work, and continuous-improvement routines.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering on preventive and predictive maintenance, equipment reliability, automation, capital priorities, commissioning, line expansions, and new technology implementation.
* Coordinate with Warehousing, Logistics, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Customer Service to maintain material availability, protect product integrity, and ensure accurate and timely finished-goods handoff.
* Maintain compliance with applicable safety, environmental, food-contact, quality, food-safety, and regulatory requirements, including FSSC 22000, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, and customer standards.
* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities.
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality.
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing.
* Lead audit readiness and support certification, surveillance, recertification, customer, regulatory, internal, and third-party audits.
* Maintain a strong safety culture through employee engagement, training, audits, risk assessments, safety observations, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, and corrective-action plans.
* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce.
* Build leadership capability through coaching, performance management, individual development plans, skills matrices, cross-training, succession planning, and consistent leader standard work.
* Lead labor planning and workforce optimization in response to production volumes, seasonality, new product requirements, and business growth.
* Manage the plant operating budget, labor costs, maintenance spending, capital expenditures, and other controllable expenses.
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actions needed to improve plant performance.
* Communicate plant performance, operating priorities, business risks, resource needs, and improvement plans clearly to plant and executive leadership.
* Contribute to network and growth planning, including capacity, new product introductions, and line additions, in partnership with corporate Operations and Supply Chain.
* Build strong working relationships with corporate brand, R&D/innovation, Quality, and Supply Chain partners, as well as co-pack customers and key suppliers where applicable.
* Promote a culture consistent with CELSIUS values, including ownership, agility, grit, commercial thinking, collaboration, positive influence, and a bias for action.
* Provide site-wide leadership that translates company goals into plant priorities, targets, and daily execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.
* Leadership Expectations
* Lead with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
* Make thoughtful, timely decisions in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
* Balance immediate production needs with long-term operational excellence.
* Build trust across plant, corporate, commercial, and cross-functional teams.
* Develop people and create a culture where employees are engaged, respected, and empowered to perform at their best.
* Use facts, data, and business judgment to solve problems and make decisions.
* Maintain high standards for safety, food safety, quality, compliance, and operational execution.
* Be comfortable operating in a high-growth consumer products environment where priorities may change quickly.

### **Physical Demands and Work Environment**

This role is based on the manufacturing floor and in plant offices. The work environment includes high-speed automated equipment, elevated noise levels requiring hearing protection, wet floors, temperature variation, and forklift traffic. Required PPE (such as safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety footwear) must be worn in production areas, and all plant safety, GMP, and food-safety rules must be followed. The role regularly requires standing and walking for extended periods and climbing stairs and platforms, and occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

 **Benefits** 

* Comprehensive Medical, Dental & Vision benefits
* Long- and short-term disability
* Life insurance
* 10 Vacation days per year, subject to accrual policy
* 11 Company paid holidays
* 401(k) with Company match
* Identity theft and legal services

*The base salary range for this position is dependent on experience and location. The final offer will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, and qualifications. This position may be eligible for other compensation, including bonuses and Restricted Stock Units (subject to company plans).*

*We promptly review all applications. Highly qualified candidates will be contacted for interviews.*

*CELSIUS Holdings, Inc. celebrates diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all applicants without regard to race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability status, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. If you require accommodations during the application process, please reach out to* *careers@celsius.com**.*

*The above information has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job.*
