**Job Description**
**Director Operations for Drug Product**
Do you aspire to secure a critical role in the production of biologics-based medicines? Are you excited to lead dynamic teams in a state-of-the-art facility that brings transformative biotech treatments to patients globally? We invite you to become a part of our journey as the Director Operations for Drug Product. This role offers you the chance to contribute to the site's development and wield technical leadership to ensure successful GMP manufacturing.
 
 
**Principle Roles & Responsibilities / Accountabilities**

* The Director, Operations – Drug Product plays a critical part in strategic project realization of the Wilmington Biotech facility, a new hi-potent facility in our company's Biologic manufacturing network, ensuring that site’s mission and objectives are effectively achieved, consistent with our company's requirements to ensure compliance, safety and reliable supply to our customers.
* As a key member of the Site Leadership Team, you'll have the opportunity to shape site and organizational strategies, overseeing drug product manufacturing for commercial and new product introductions.
* Be part of facility start-up to manufacture high-potent products, eg antibody drug conjugates (ADCs)
* You will work collaboratively with cross-functional teams to streamline technology transfers and commercial approvals, meanwhile nurturing and empowering your operations team.
* You'll get to foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement, leading or supporting various site functional and cross-functional structures for departmental alignment.
* Tackling resource constraints and needs, you will champion operational and technical excellence for efficient production and implement Lean principles for process optimization.
* Upholding our Manufacturing Division Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, you will manage relevant quality topics, and ensure permanent inspection readiness.
* You will oversee financial forecasts and workload for departmental cost improvements, aligning with capital and expense targets while contributing to sustainability and cost reduction initiatives.
* You will have the chance to leverage digital tools for operational efficiency and informed decision-making, keeping pace with emerging digital technologies relevant to manufacturing processes.
* You will be accountable for achieving onsite Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), monitoring and striving to improve performance metrics related to hiring, uptime, training, change controls, investigations, CAPAs, yield, volume, production cadence, operational availability, and more.

**Qualification And Experience**
**Required Experience and Skills:**

* A degree or equivalent in Engineering, Science, Technical, or other relevant fields: Bachelor’s degree + 12 years industry experience Or Masters + 10 years Or PhD + 8 years
* 6 or more years demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring high-performing cross function teams.
* Demonstrated experience in a biotech/vaccines/pharma manufacturing site, project, or other relevant roles, specifically drug product sterile manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing clinical and commercial products.
* Understanding of cGMP requirements for commercial high-potent ADC manufacturing of drug product

**Preferred Experience And Skills**

* Sterile manufacturing leadership & operations, with preferred multi-product experience.
* A leader who inspires, coaches, and fosters a high-performance organizational culture.
* A continuous learner who cultivates a culture of ongoing development within your team.
* An innovative thinker with excellent decision-making and problem-solving skills.
* Experienced in leading highly effective cross-functional teams with a passion for shaping the future of our organization.
* Capable of influencing and building relationships across organizational layers, as well as externally with partners.

#ADC #ADC2026

Adaptability, Adaptability, Business Agility, Continuous Development, Cross-Functional Project Management, Customer Delivery, Data Analysis, Decision Making, Lean Manufacturing, Manufacturing, Manufacturing Quality Control, Manufacturing Technologies, Operations Management, Organizational Leadership, People Leadership, Performance Metrics, Process Improvements, Process Optimization, Product Compliance, Production Scheduling, Quality Compliance, Quality Control Management, Quality Control Systems, Quality Management, Regulatory Compliance {+ 7 more}

For our client, we are seeking a Director of Manufacturing and Quality to join the team of a leader in the Consumer Technology space.
 
 
This leader will own the global manufacturing strategy and quality execution for a hardware-driven business operating across design, production, and supply chain partners. The role will be central to scaling high-volume manufacturing, improving operational efficiency, and ensuring product quality from early design through full production. You will work closely with engineering, contract manufacturers, and cross-functional partners to strengthen launch readiness, vendor accountability, and long-term quality performance.
 
 
Location: Sunnyvale, CA
 
 
Compensation: $200,000 – $250,000 annually
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Architect and execute the global manufacturing strategy, including optimization of production facilities
* Drive NPI handoffs from design to high-volume manufacturing with robust playbooks
* Optimize production capacity and efficiency through innovative layout and automation designs
* Manage technical execution at tier-1 contract manufacturers and oversee vendor accountability
* Own and improve the global Quality Management System across all sites and partners
* Implement early design quality practices to mitigate manufacturing issues through the lifecycle
* Lead global failure analysis and corrective action processes to maintain product quality

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of leadership experience in hardware manufacturing operations, NPI, and quality engineering in high-tech industries
* Direct experience establishing and scaling overseas manufacturing facilities, particularly in Asia
* Deep understanding of electrical fabrication and mechanical processes
* Expertise in advanced quality methodologies such as Six Sigma and Lean Manufacturing
* Bachelor's degree in a technical field; an MS or MBA is a plus

**Benefits**

* 100% premium coverage for Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
* Equity options available in the form of stock options
* 401(k) match to support retirement savings
* Reimbursement for work-from-home hardware expenses

role.title: Southwest Regional Director of Production and Logistics
role.description:
About PopUp Bagels

 

PopUp Bagels is not just a bagel company—we’re a cultural movement. Our stores are small, our vibes are loud, and our energy is contagious. From signature neon and iconic bullhorns to our “Not Famous but Known” mirror, we’ve reimagined not just how a bagel is created, but how it’s enjoyed: Grip, Rip and Dip! With a cult-like following, massive social presence, and unparalleled collaborations with top companies, partners and Brand Ambassadors PopUp Bagels is defining a new food lifestyle brand.

 

We keep things simple, but we do them really, really well. And our customers agree.

 

The Role

 

We're looking for a Regional Director to lead operations at our Nevada cream cheese production facility. This facility will play an important role in supporting PopUp's continued growth and our ability to deliver the products our customers love.

 

This is a senior operational leadership role responsible for overseeing the day-to-day performance of the facility, from the moment raw materials come through the door to the second finished goods ship out to shops around the country.

 

Here's what makes this role different from other operations roles: we're building something big, and we're building quickly. With established production facilities and operating procedures already in place, the right person for this role will know how to take proven processes, put them into practice, and continue improving them as we grow.

 

We're looking for a problem-solver who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and find solutions, a leader who earns trust on the floor just as easily as they collaborate with senior leadership, and someone who can translate operational expectations into consistent, measurable results.

 

This role serves as a key connection between the Nevada production facility and our broader operations leadership team. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, develop our people, and contribute to the continued evolution of our production processes as PopUp expands.

 

If you're a driven leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, values collaboration, and takes pride in building strong teams and efficient operations, this could be the role for you.

 

What You'll Do:

 

Run the Facility. You'll provide day-to-day operational leadership and oversight across Cream Cheese and Schmear production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, and Equipment Maintenance Working closely with the President of Operations and other facility leaders, you'll implement and maintain established SOPs, manage production schedules, drive throughput targets, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how we operate. You'll be responsible for addressing operational challenges, escalating significant issues when appropriate, and ensuring the facility consistently meets established performance, quality, and safety expectations.

 

Lead People Who Make an Impact. Building a strong team culture is at the core of this role. You'll recruit, develop, and retain a workforce that makes a genuine impact at PopUp Bagels. You'll coach and support your management team, reinforce established training programs, and identify opportunities to strengthen employee development as the operation grows. You'll create an environment where accountability and recognition go hand in hand. Our hourly workforce is the backbone of this operation, and how you show up for them defines everything.

 

Manage the Numbers. You'll be accountable for facility-level operational performance, including production costs, labor efficiency, waste reduction, and budget adherence. You'll partner closely with the President of Operations, Finance, and Accounting on budgeting, forecasting, and period-end reporting, and regularly communicate facility performance, challenges, and opportunities to senior leadership. You'll identify ways to improve efficiency and control costs without compromising quality, safety, or people, while supporting broader capital planning and investment decisions.

 

Drive Supply Chain Alignment. Work directly with our VP of Supply Chain to align production schedules with material availability. You'll oversee raw material procurement planning, inventory controls, and warehouse operations, ensuring established FIFO and food safety standards are consistently followed. You'll collaborate with Supply Chain and other production facilities to support inventory accuracy, product availability, and efficient distribution.

 

Lead Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance. Champion a food-safety-first culture across every part of the facility. You'll ensure consistent execution of established food safety programs and compliance with applicable FDA regulations, FSMA requirements, HACCP plans, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC), as applicable. You'll partner with Quality Assurance and the President of Operations to maintain rigorous in-process and finished product quality standards, address compliance concerns, and implement corrective actions when something doesn't meet the bar.

 

Collaborate Across the Company. You'll represent Nevada facility operations in company-wide leadership meetings and collaborate with Distribution & Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and corporate leadership. You'll translate what's happening on the floor into meaningful operational insights, communicate opportunities for improvement, and ensure company priorities and decisions are effectively implemented at the facility level.

 

Who You Are and What You Bring

 

     We're looking for a leader who is genuinely:

 

A scrappy problem-solver. When something breaks at 7am or a key ingredient is backordered, you find a way. You're resourceful, calm under pressure, and put in the time to figure it out. You know when to make decisions, when to collaborate, and when to escalate an issue.

 

A trust-builder. Your team respects you because you've worked to build trust, not because of your title. You're on the floor, you know people's names, and you follow through on what you say.

 

A galvanizing leader. You provide clear direction, get buy-in, and bring your team along with energy and conviction. People want to work hard for you because they know you'll do the same for them.

 

Equally at home in a leadership meeting and a production room. You can review financial and operational performance in the morning and troubleshoot a production issue in the afternoon. You don't ask your team to do what you're not willing to do yourself.

 

Built for growth and continuous improvement. PopUp is growing fast, and our processes will continue to evolve. You appreciate the value of established systems and standards, but you're also comfortable identifying opportunities to make them better. You know how to balance consistency with adaptability as the business scales.

 

       You bring:

 

 
* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Master's degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
 
* 8–10+ years of progressive plant or manufacturing operations leadership experience, including demonstrated responsibility for facility performance, team leadership, and operational budgets.
 
* Experience leading operations in fast-paced manufacturing environments, preferably within growing or multi-site organizations.
 
* Proven track record of leading high-performing, cross-functional manufacturing teams.
 
* Prior food and beverage industry experience strongly preferred; dairy, cream cheese, spreads, or related refrigerated food production experience is a significant plus.
 
* Familiarity with food safety regulatory frameworks, including FSMA, HACCP, GMP, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC, AIB).
 
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, cost analysis, labor efficiency, and operational performance reporting.
 
* Working knowledge of production cost drivers, manufacturing KPIs, and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Production Excellence, or equivalent).
 
* Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining standardized operating procedures, production processes, and operational controls.
 
* Experience partnering with corporate Finance, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and Distribution teams.
 
* Availability and willingness to be on-call on weekends and off-hours to respond to facility disruptions or emergencies.
 
* Experience supporting capital improvement projects and operational efficiency initiatives.
 
* A history of building positive, rewarding workplace cultures for hourly workforces.
 

 

Physical Requirements

 

The following physical requirements are representative of those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with qualifying disabilities.

 

 
* Ability to walk, stand, and move throughout a production facility for extended periods during daily floor presence and inspections.
 
* Must be able to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures, including refrigerated dairy production and storage areas, moderate to loud noise levels, and exposure to dairy ingredients and food-grade cleaning agents.
 
* Occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds may be required.
 
* Must be able to wear required PPE, including hair nets, beard nets, gloves, and safety footwear when on the production floor.
 
* Ability to use standard office equipment (computer, monitor, phone, conferencing technology) for extended periods.
 
* Occasional travel to corporate offices, other production facilities, or external meetings (estimated up to 30%).
 

 

PopUp Bagels is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

 

We do not discriminate based on race, age, ancestry, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, pregnancy, childbirth or related condition, unemployment status, gender identity or expression, transgender status, marital status, domestic violence or sexual violence victim status, national origin, citizenship, disability, covered veteran and/or military status, genetic information, familial status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, and local law. PopUp Bagels conducts pre-employment screenings in compliance with local, state, and federal laws, and utilizes E-Verify to confirm U.S. employment eligibility.

 

The duties of this position may change from time to time. PopUp Bagels reserves the right to add or delete duties and responsibilities at its discretion. This posting describes the general nature and level of work expected and is not intended to be all-inclusive.

role.title: Sr. Manager, Operations
role.description:
**Position Summary**
The Senior Operations Manager leads the machining department (approximately 60 employees) through supervisors and technical specialists. The role is accountable for safety, quality, on-time delivery, capacity utilization, productivity, and margins in a high-mix, low-volume precision CNC environment.
 
 
This is a people-and-business leadership position focused on removing barriers, driving continuous improvement, and partnering with the General Manager and Business Development to support profitable growth. Hands-on machining or CNC programming is not required.
 
 
**Key Accountabilities**

* Safety & Quality: Maintain a safety-first culture. Partner with Quality to uphold ISO standards, reduce nonconformances, and lower cost of poor quality through root-cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Operational Performance & Capacity: Direct production through supervisors across milling, turning, and secondary operations. Improve throughput by reducing bottlenecks, setup times, downtime, and waste. Optimize capacity planning, staffing, sequencing, and preventive maintenance.
* Delivery & Customer Execution: Own on-time delivery from order release through shipment. Ensure realistic schedules, visible priorities, and proactive recovery plans. Coordinate cross-functionally with Planning, Quality, Purchasing, and Shipping.
* Financial & Margin Management: Partner with Finance and the General Manager to protect and improve gross margin through labor productivity, material yield, scrap reduction, and disciplined cost control. Monitor job costs and provide reliable data for quoting, make/buy decisions, and capital recommendations.
* Systems & Continuous Improvement: Drive adoption, accuracy, and continuous improvement of ERP/MRP and shop-floor systems. Apply Lean tools (5S/6S, standard work, SMED, value-stream mapping, Kaizen) where they deliver measurable results. Develop practical performance dashboards and management reviews.
* People Leadership & Culture: Develop supervisors, team leads, and production personnel through coaching, clear expectations, and empowerment. Build engagement, retention, skills development, and succession. Foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Growth Partnership: Support Business Development with capacity assessments, customer meetings, and opportunity qualification to profitably fill available machine capacity.

**Key Performance Measures**

* Safety performance
* On-time delivery and schedule adherence
* Throughput, labor productivity, setup time, and unplanned downtime
* Capacity utilization and available capacity for new work
* Gross margin, job-cost variance, and scrap/rework costs
* ERP/MRP data accuracy and timely reporting
* Employee engagement, retention, and internal development
* Nonconformance trends and cost of quality

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience leading manufacturing teams or operations departments, preferably in CNC machining, high-mix/low-volume contract manufacturing, or precision manufacturing. Hands-on machinist or programming experience is not required.
* Demonstrated improvements in productivity, on-time delivery, profitability, and operational performance, supported by measurable results.
* Experience implementing or improving ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, job costing, and KPI reporting.
* Strong people leadership, coaching, business acumen, change management, and cross-functional communication skills.
* Practical understanding of capacity, cost drivers, scheduling, Lean methods, and ISO-based quality systems.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or business preferred; equivalent relevant leadership experience will be considered.

**Role Alignment**
This role manages the machining department through its supervisors and technical staff, with accountability for people development, operational performance, and continuous improvement. The Senior Operations Manager partners with the General Manager on business priorities, financial objectives, and capital recommendations, and with Business Development on customer relationships and growth.
 
 
The position does not require personally operating or programming CNC equipment. Final authority for pricing, hiring, capital spending, and related decisions will be defined by company leadership.
 
 
**Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled**
This employer participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. If E-Verify cannot confirm that you are authorized to work, this employer is required to give you written instructions and an opportunity to contact Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) so you can begin to resolve the issue before the employer can take any action against you, including terminating your employment. Employers can only use E-Verify once you have accepted a job offer and completed the Form I-9.

role.title: Sr Director - Advanced Manufacturing Engineer - NPI
role.description:
**Job Description**
Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
 
 
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
 
 
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Deliver NPI program objectives including product producibility, design-to-cost (DTC) targets, production readiness, and customer quality.
* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
 
 
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
This position is incentive eligible.
 
 
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
 
 
**POSTING TIMELINE**
The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.
 
 
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At
**Honeywell Aerospace**
(NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.
 
 
Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.
 
 
Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.
 
 
Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.
 
 
Honeywell Aerospace Products And Services Are Found On Aircraft Across Commercial Aviation, Defense And Space. We Operate Through Three Business Areas
 
 
Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft
 
 
Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying
 
 
Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board
 
 
With approximately 58,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, we are also advancing systems for autonomous and supersonic platforms — bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com
 
 
Join Honeywell Aerospace! Our aerospace innovations bring people together, make the world safer and more secure, and help humankind reach for the stars. Now we’re shaping aviation’s future with sustainable aviation fuels, smarter cockpits, ultra-efficient engines, smart airports, flying taxis and much more.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Salary:**
$180,000 - $220,000 annually

**Location:**
Onsite - Fremont, CA

**Job Summary:**

The Director of Operations will be responsible for overseeing and optimizing the company's operational processes to ensure efficiency, productivity, and the highest quality of service. This role involves strategic planning, management of operational teams, and implementation of best practices to support the company's goals and growth. The Director of Operations will work closely with senior leadership to align operational strategies with organizational objectives.

**Duties/Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Planning and Implementation**

* Develop and implement operational strategies that align with the company’s overall goals and objectives.
* Analyze operational performance and make recommendations for improvements.
* Ensure the effective execution of the company’s strategic initiatives.

**Team Management**

* Lead, mentor, and manage the operations team, including setting performance goals and conducting regular evaluations.
* Foster a positive and productive work environment that encourages team collaboration and professional development.

**Process Optimization**

* Identify opportunities for process improvements and efficiency gains across various departments.
* Implement best practices and standard operating procedures to enhance productivity and service quality.

**Financial Oversight**

* Develop and manage the operations budget, ensuring cost-effectiveness and alignment with financial targets.
* Monitor financial performance and report on key metrics related to operational efficiency and profitability.

**Quality Management**

* Oversee the quality management system to ensure adherence to industry standards and regulatory requirements.
* Address and resolve operational issues and customer complaints in a timely manner.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Work closely with other departments such as PM, Quality, and Engineering to ensure cohesive operational support and alignment.
* Coordinate with external partners, customers and vendors as needed.

**Data Analysis and Reporting**

* Utilize data analytics to track performance, identify trends, and make informed decisions.
* Prepare and present reports on operational performance to senior management.

**Compliance and Risk Management**

* Ensure that all operational activities comply with company policies, industry regulations, and legal requirements.
* Develop and implement risk management strategies to mitigate potential operational risks

**Skills/Competencies**

* Expertise in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Strong knowledge of production planning, supply chain management, and quality assurance.
* Excellent leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
* Proficiency in ERP systems and manufacturing software.

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related field (MBA or advanced degree preferred).
* Minimum of 7 years of experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 10+ years in a leadership role.
* Proven track record of driving operational improvements and achieving production goals.

**Our company does not guarantee immigration sponsorship. We may offer immigration sponsorship for employees in select critical roles. Any sponsorship will be subject to internal review and approval based on employee performance, current immigration law and business needs.**

role.title: DIRECTOR OF HEALTHCARE QUALITY
role.description:
**JOB SUMMARY:** Within the framework of the objectives and policies established by the Board of Directors of Franklin Primary Health Center, Inc., organizes and coordinates activities related to Healthcare Quality among all Franklin Primary Health Center’s clinical departments including Primary Care, Oral Health, Behavioral Health, Ryan White program, laboratory, performance improvement, etc. Plans and coordinates performance improvement activities in collaboration with the Deputy Director of Healthcare Quality Chief Medical Officer, Director of Nursing, Deputy Chief Operations Officer, Director of Behavioral Health, and Performance Improvement Manager. Participates in planning and policy formulation, with particular reference to the role, functions, and operations of the Center's clinical quality and performance improvement activities.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Coordinate and monitor clinical quality activities through the initiation of a clinical quality work plan that encompasses all clinical areas. Reports quarterly on the progress of the work plan to Chief Medical Officer. Coordinates an annual evaluation and update of the quality work plan.
* Works as a liaison between Franklin and other entities in matters pertaining to clinical quality and performance.
* Assists the Chief Medical Officer by working with all areas of clinical services to improve efficiency, communication and collaboration.
* Ensures compliance to accreditation standards, other regulatory standards, quality and initiatives.
* Coordinates the peer review process.
* Provides quality indicator analysis for the physician’s quality incentive program.
* Monitors and keeps abreast of any changes or trends in the healthcare quality area.
* Addresses through the appropriate channels any potential risk and safety issues identified through clinical quality activities.
* Publishes and monitors standards of care for the providers and the nursing department.
* Monitors the provision of quality patient care through the Chief Medical Officer and the Director of Nursing with data from Azara and EHR.
* Evaluates all clinical services and consults with Chief Medical Officer and Quality Committee.
* Supervises the Performance Improvement functions of the Performance Improvement Department.
* Develops and implements standards, goals and initiatives for the Performance Improvement department in coordination with the Deputy Director of Healthcare Quality, Performance Improvement Manager and Chief Medical Officer.
* Responsible for developing, administering, and managing the Center’s performance improvement plan.
* Provides educational support to all FPHC departments with regard to performance improvement
* Monitors and ensures Joint Commission, NCQA and OSV standards of compliance on an ongoing basis, maintaining a constant state of readiness for survey
* Reviews all clinical indicators on a regular basis including but not limited to UDS Quality Measures and makes recommendations as needed to ensure the department’s performance improvement activities are effective.
* Review Performance data presented by PI committee and identify opportunities for improvement and presents findings quarterly to Senior Management.
* Actively participates and/or facilitates committees such as: Performance Improvement, Safety and Infection Control.
* Other duties at the discretion of the Chief Medical Officer.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Maintains current Alabama Nursing License and board certification. Remains abreast of current employee health practices and guidelines through continuing education classes, journals and professional organizations.
* Attends continuing education classes/webinars related to infection control practices, monitoring and surveillance of infectious disease processes within the organization.
* Attends seminars and continuing education related to Healthcare Quality trends and initiatives.
* Maintains webinars confidentiality.
* Observes and supports Center policies.
* Is prompt and efficient with minimal absences.

**CUSTOMER SATISFACTION REQUIREMENTS:** Must provide the very best customer satisfaction to staff, visitors, guests, and patients at all time in a professional and courteous manner. Provide assistance in resolving customers’ problems relating to employee services. Coordinates efforts and interfaces with other departments to resolve complaints and patient care deficiencies.

**PERFORMANCE STANDARDS:** Performance will be evaluated by the Chief Medical Officer annually wherein an overall satisfactory rating is considered as a minimum acceptable level of performance.

**HEALTH AND SAFETY REQUIREMENTS:** The health and safety requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.

* Must adhere to safety regulations, personnel policies and procedures.
* Safety and Hazard Communication training update is required annually.
* Knowledgeable of OSHA and CLIA requirements to assure compliance.
* Maintain yearly health maintenance by obtaining TB skin testing and completion of the hepatitis series.

**PRIVACY RULE COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS:**

* Adheres to Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA Privacy Rule) policies and procedures.
* Must successfully complete Privacy Rule compliance training annually or as revisions are made to the policies and procedures.
* Must comply with Privacy Rule guidelines by learning to protect FPHC patient’s medical privacy.
* Must comply with Privacy Rule guidelines by appropriately maintaining our patient information in compliance with national standards.
* Must comply with Privacy Rule guidelines by providing appropriate security of FPHC patient records.

**PROTECTED HEALTH INFORMATION (PHI) ACCESS: RESTRICTED-** For purposes of HIPAA Compliance, there are 4 workforce categories, which define the level of access to PHI that is granted to the incumbent. This position is classified as **PRIMARY PROVIDERS** and therefore granted **UNRESTRICED access**- for the purpose of providing patient care; **RESTRICTED** access for other uses and disclosures, to be defined according to the purpose for which use or disclosure is intended. Use and disclosure must be in accordance with applicable privacy policies and procedures.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE: Minimum of Bachelor’s Degree and 5 years’ experience working with Quality Management (QM) in a healthcare setting or 5 or more years’ demonstrated management and supervisory skills in a healthcare setting. Possess strong managerial, administrative, and effective communication skills. Nursing licensed and/or certified professional healthcare quality (CPHQ) in the state of Alabama preferred.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Demonstrated clinical competence. Demonstrate appropriate conduct, grooming and sound judgment. Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively and communicate effectively. Good health and consistent attendance. Membership and participation in AL Board of Nursing Association. Possess the ability to delegate duties effectively and efficiently. Ability to read, analyze and interpret clinical data, quality measures, and governmental regulations. Possess ability to write professional reports, letters and procedural manuals. Ability to present information and respond to questions from diverse professional and community groups effectively.

CERTIFICATION, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS: State of Alabama Registered Nurses License; CPR certification; Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) certification preferred

**PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS:** Requires working under stressful conditions or working irregular hours. Must be able to express ideas clearly and concisely; and exercise balanced judgment in evaluating situations and making decisions. Possess strong oral and written communication skills. Knowledge of the professional nursing theory and practice to direct, give, and evaluate patient care processes for the department. Knowledge

role.title: Director of Quality and Accreditation
role.description:
Overview:

Join the Cedar Crest leadership team as the Director of Quality! Situated on over 30 acres in the beautiful rolling hills of Central Texas, Cedar Crest provides innovative behavioral health and substance abuse treatment for children, adolescents, and adults. Our private campus includes walking trails, picnic areas, outdoor swimming pool, full-size gym, and state-of-the-art exercise equipment; providing opportunities for leisure, therapeutic recreation, and team building skills. Cedar Crest provides a full continuum of care including adolescent residential, inpatient, outpatient, and partial hospitalization/intense outpatient treatments.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Quality and Accreditation to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
 + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
 + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
 + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
 + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
 + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
 + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
 + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
 + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
 + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
 + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
 - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
 - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
 - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
 + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
 + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
 + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
 + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
 + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
 + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
 + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
 + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
 + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
 + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
 + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
 + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
 + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
 + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
 + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
 + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
 + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
 + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
 + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
 - Changes in policies/procedures,
 - Staffing and assignment changes,
 - Additional education or training for staff,
 - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

**ADDITIONAL REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS:**

***While this job description is intended to be*** ***an accurate*** ***reflection of the requirements of the job, management reserves the right to add or remove duties from*** ***par******ticular jobs*** ***when circumstances*** 
***(******e.g.*** ***emergencies, changes in workload, rush jobs or technological developments) dictate.***

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants for employment regardless of an individual’s characteristics protected by applicable state, federal and local laws.

role.title: Director of ICF & Quality Enhancement
role.description:
**Position Summary:** The **Director of ICF & Quality Enhancement** provides direction and hands-on leadership to ensure the effective delivery of assigned programs and services. The Director of ICF & Quality Enhancement is responsible for all activities pertaining to the program’s licensure, human rights, personnel, and contract management obligations for the Fort Lauderdale campus. The Director of ICF & Quality Enhancement will evaluate ASC programs/services, including, but not limited to, the development, implementation, data collection, and analysis of program/services, as well as developing staff training programs, to ensure a standard of quality that serves the organization’s mission to improve the lives of persons supported in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations including licensing requirements which include nursing and nutrition.

**Areas of Responsibility:** 
***A. Program Management (FTL ICF, Nursing and Nutrition): Ensures the delivery of high-quality programs and services in compliance with all federal, state, funding, and city regulations, certifications, and licensing requirements, ASC’s best practices.***

* Provides effective and inspiring leadership, as well as stewardship, of ASC by being actively involved in all programs and services.
* Provides programmatic leadership and input to the CEO for strategic planning purposes.
* Ensure that all program activities operate consistently and ethically within the mission and values of ASC.
* Ensures FTL ICF maintains a safe environment to minimize employee and resident accidents/injuries and unnecessary expenditures.
* Ensures the optimal physical condition of the ICF is appropriately maintained (e.g., furnishings, appliances, grounds, etc.); verifies tickets are submitted in a timely manner to the Maintenance department; follows up with the Facilities Supervisor on outstanding issues, as necessary.
* Ensures Emergency Management Guidelines are followed including, but not limited to timely completion of drills, documentation of drills, maintaining an adequate inventory of emergency supplies, etc.
* Implements and leads a continuous quality improvement process throughout the program and service areas, focusing on systems and process improvement.
* Conducts regular site inspections and regularly attends program meetings to maintain an awareness of day-to-day efforts and needs.
* Arranges, prepares for and participates in all audits and surveys.
* Evaluates programs based upon internal management audits, external survey and audit findings, and specific monitoring data and subsequent analysis; develops new programs as needs emerge.
* Complete all required reports for funding agencies.
* Provide reports on the programmatic status of each program at regularly scheduled meetings;
* Informs the CEO of any programmatic, individual or organizational crisis, or eminent need.
* Submits program updates to the CEO for reporting to the Board; Presents at Board and/or Executive Committee meetings upon request.
* Prepares and submits annual budgets for the department to the CEO for review and approval, manages effectively within these budgets.
* Execute contracts for services and secures CEO and/or Board of Directors’ approval as necessary.
* Assumes responsibility for major projects related to programs and services.
* Conducts home walkthroughs; Ensures the environment is home-like, safe, sanitary, and has adequate supplies to permit service and program delivery to all residents.
* Assures resident’s rights, wishes, desires, and individual needs are met through delivery and Programming.
* Maintains up-to-date knowledge of State and Federal regulations and ensures compliance with rules and regulations.
* Participates in the State, Federal, and quality assurance survey process.
* Ensures the delivery of high-quality nursing care in compliance with established health management and pharmacology procedures.
* Provides oversight to the nutritional department to ensure the delivery of high-quality services to the individuals and program participants.
* Ensure that kitchen and dining room facilities are maintained in compliance with expected standards for the safety and welfare of the residents and the employees.

***B. Quality Assurance and Enhancement (FTL & PPC - ICF, Nursing and Nutrition): Ensures the delivery of high-quality programs and services in compliance with all federal, state, funding, and city regulations, certifications, and licensing requirements, ASC’s best practices.***

* Implements and leads a continuous quality improvement process throughout the program and service areas, focusing on systems and process improvement.
* Periodically reviews services being offered and develops new programs as needs emerge.
* Establish tracking and compliance measures as per contract and/or funding agreement.
* Arranges, prepares and participates in all audits and surveys ensuring the organization is “survey ready.”
* Conducts evaluations of ASC ICF programs/services to ensure overall quality, consistency, compliance with all regulatory requirements, and ASC’s mission and vision
* ***FTL only*** - Prepares and submits annual budgets for each department to the CEO for review and approval, manages effectively within these budgets.
* ***FTL only*** - Assumes responsibility for major projects related to programs and services.
* Implements and manages a system of evaluation services that provides professional development, guidance, education/training and support of ASC staff.
* Maintains up-to-date knowledge of State and Federal regulations and ensures compliance with rules and regulations.
* Develops a monitoring schedule for both campuses with flexibility to provide immediate assistance as requested
* Ensure that the facilities are maintained in compliance with expected standards for the safety and welfare of the residents.

***C. Agency Leadership & Supervisory Duties***

* Establishes and maintains a leadership role within the Agency through implementation of the Annual Plan and timely response to issues and problems and facilitation of crisis circumstances.
* Consults with program leaders regarding the development and/or implementation of Agency Programs and Best Practices; Reviews and updates program-related best practices on an annual basis.
* Reviews and reports progress towards completion of Agency program objectives and goals through meetings and individual conferences.
* Partners with the CEO to represent ASC with external constituency groups, including community, governmental, and private organizations.
* Recruits, trains, and supervises direct reports; Oversees the recruitment, hiring, training, and management of all program staff.
* Defines, clarifies and holds staff accountable to established standards of behavior consistent with ASC’s policies.
* Ensures qualitative interactions between staff and residents.
 + Ensures employees receive timely feedback on their performance.
 + Consults with HR on termination decisions; Participates in the grievance process as required.
 + Ensures rewards and disciplinary actions for staff supervised.
* Assists staff in the development and implementation of coaching and training skills.
 + In-Service training as required.
 + Ensures that management meetings and trainings are held monthly.
 + Attends In-Service training and CEO meetings
 + Develop feedback methods after teaching.
* Ensuring communication with staff about residents’ progress, needs, wishes, and desires is being conducted by Directors and Residential Managers
* Payroll
 + Reviews staff timecards biweekly with Residential Managers to ensure proper clocking in and out, reducing overtime and payroll errors.
 + Monitor overtime report and make required adjustments to reduce costs but ensure we are staying in compliance with the appropriate ratios.
* On Call 24/7; Responds to emergencies appropriately following established procedures.

***D. Executes professional responsibilities effectively and efficiently.***

* Participates in Leadership Meetings to unify departments and programs which will ultimately benefit the Center and the people served.
* Maintains, as needed, consultations with all Circle of Support (COS) members regarding residents’ concerns and/or programs and activities.
* Review minutes of Individual Care Plans (ICP), quarterly reports and attends sampling of meetings throughout the year.
* Receives, reviews, and completes ICP packets for distribution.
* Ensures annual meeting schedule is completed and sent to COS.
* Ensures skill maintenance procedures and check-off sheets are created and forwarded to Records Managers.
* Is responsible for FTL Management monthly meetings and follow-up.
* Provides expertise and input into Homes as requested.
* Compliance with Department of Professional Regulation and Health Department compliance issues.
 + Assists in preparing and implementing plans for quality improvements as needed

**MINIMUM EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:**

* Master’s Degree in human services or a related field; Master’s degree in business administration or related field, accepted
* 7 years of related professional-level experience including five years of senior leadership experience supervising seasoned staff operating multiple human services programs.
* Knowledge of developmental and intellectual disabilities and three years of experience providing direct care to intellectually and/or developmentally disabled individuals.
* Strong relationship builder and communicator with experience leading diverse work teams, developing an organization-wide strategy for program excellence, engaging community partners, and partnering with a CEO and board of directors.
* Personal qualities of integrity, credibility, and commitment to ASC’s mission.
* Demonstrated resourcefulness in setting priorities and guiding people and systems.
* Ability to adapt quickly to unexpected changes, deadlines or business demands and to make sound business judgments independently and under pressure.
* Reliable transportation; Current Florida Motor Vehicle license and automobile insurance with good driving record.
* Ability to travel regularly to provide on-site leadership for multiple operating units and programs.
* Working knowledge of AHCA regulations.
* Computer literate (Microsoft Office and/or Google Workspace).
* Must possess excellent administrative and organizational skills.

**WORKING CONDITIONS:** Standard office environment with moderate noise levels. Variable schedule includes regular business hours, evening and weekends. Regular local travel for meetings, conferences, and events is required. Position is categorized as essential personnel for the purpose of providing disaster services.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:** ASC is in full compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and does not discriminate with regard to applicants or employees with disabilities and will attempt to make reasonable accommodations when necessary. The following are abilities and physical requirements for this position at ASC: 
a. Able to lift 50 lbs. safely and appropriately utilizing standard orientation techniques. 
b. May be exposed to short, intermittent, and/or prolonged periods of sitting, standing, and/or squatting in the performance of job duties. 
c. Must be able to hear see, and communicate effectively in writing, using the English language, with or without reasonable accommodation.
 
d. Ability to work cooperatively with all levels of staff, exercising effective problem-solving, reasoning, and critical thinking skills. 
e. May be required to accomplish job duties using various types of equipment/supplies to include, but not limited to, pens, pencils, calculators, computer keyboards, telephone, etc. 
f. A moderately sedentary position requiring computer and telephone work.

role.title: Director of Quality Control
role.description:
Direct Biologics is a market leading innovator and science-based cGMP manufacturer of regenerative biologic products. Direct Biologics is hiring a hands-on QC leader for our Poway, CA testing laboratory in the greater San Diego area. You will lead a team of analysts to execute release and stability testing for a late-stage extracellular vesicle biologics program as part of a broader multi-product pipeline, and prepare the QC function for commercial operations.

We are currently looking for a Director of QC, responsible for:

* Responsible for strategy and execution of late-stage to commercial cGMP testing laboratory readiness, owning key decisions in method transfer, validation, and life-cycle management.
* Drives phase-appropriate regulatory and compliance initiatives for a portfolio of cell therapy extracellular vesicle products (early clinical through commercial stages). Presents plans to senior leadership and leads QC workstream for inspection readiness.
* Leads interactions with health authorities related to internal and outsource testing programs, including in-process, characterization, drug substance and drug product release, and stability.
* This working leadership position requires hands-on participation in routine and non-routine testing activities. The individual must maintain their own training and qualification, work independently at the laboratory bench, execute test methods, troubleshoot problems, perform investigations, and write reports when needed to meet business and regulatory commitments.
* Collaborates with R&D and Analytical Development team to introduce method lifecycle improvements and new technologies to the QC laboratory.
* Accountable for timely execution and documentation of routine laboratory tests. Ensures the on-time closure of sampling plans, protocols, laboratory investigations, CAPAs, change control records, and other QMS commitments.
* Develops and communicates departmental resourcing plans to serve broad company goals, including personnel, budget, and timelines. Adjusts plans and priorities according to executive leadership resourcing decisions.
* Leads Quality Control operations:
* + Hire, onboard, train, qualify, and assist professional development of QC team members.
* + Ensure timely execution of STAT and release testing.
* + Manage stability sample inventory and pull schedule, coordinating sample transit with cGMP warehouse, outsource sample submission, and timely internal testing.
* + Ensure timely purchase and qualification of supplies, materials, and equipment.
* + Maintain equipment use, calibration, maintenance, and cleaning records and coordinate related activities.
* + Communicate testing timeframes, expected start/finish dates, and testing outcomes to internal and external stakeholders.
* + Author/approve policies, procedures, and work instructions for accuracy and compliance.
* + Author/approve ROA, COA, trend reports, and stability reports.
* Responsible for QC data/records to ensure content adheres to established cGMP quality standards.
* + Maintain risk register, support internal and mock audits, and show steady compliance progress in collaboration with QA team members.
* + Collaborate with IT to ensure data Integrity and storage of original source data in accordance with part 11 requirements.
* Ensure strict adherence to EPA, OSHA, and FAA safety and clean environmental guidelines.
* Occasional travel by air and/or car may be required to participate in on-site vendor activities, such as method transfer, vendor meetings, and vendor quality audits.
* Excels in a fast-paced environment. Independently prioritizes activity based on importance and urgency, manages time well, anticipates challenges, and delivers progress in line with program goals.
* Strong attention to detail and related understanding of CFR, compendial, and other regulatory requirements.

 
 
**Requirements**

**Skill Requirements:**

* Top expert in preparing cGMP clinical stage testing laboratories for commercial launch, with evidence of leading a QC readiness workstream for a late-stage or commercial biologic product.
* Extensive knowledge of domestic and global compliance requirements for commercial release testing programs.
* Recent hands-on experience with one or more of the following: human cell culture techniques, cell-based potency assays, protein assays (plate based ELISAs, immunostaining-based assays, fluorescence microscopy), quantitative PCR, RNA and protein isolation and quantification methods.
* Familiarity with cGMP Quality Control testing, qualification, and validation of analytical test methods with internal and outsourced contexts.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills in cross-functional team setting.
* Must be highly flexible to respond to urgent needs and directional changes in a start-up environment but also have the attention to detail required to execute studies that will be reviewed by the FDA and other regulatory authorities.
* Lead GMP QC investigations and provide solutions to issues including OOS, deviations and/or CAPA.
* Ability to maintain lab equipment including qualification and calibration.
* Knowledgeable about statistical modeling for quality control applications.
* Technical understanding and working knowledge of contemporary molecular biology, cell biology, microbiology and/or biochemistry.
* Track record leading efficient and cost-effective QC operations while maintaining scientific rigor and GMP compliance. Demonstrated ability to optimize resources, streamline processes, and overcome challenges in a lean operating model.

**Qualifications Requirements:**

* Advanced degree in analytical chemistry, biotechnology, cell and molecular biology, biochemistry, or other related field is preferred.
* Minimum of 8 years biotech based-work experience in cell culture, biochemical, or molecular biology GMP QC testing. Experience with late-stage advanced therapy products is preferred.
* Prior experience with cGMP release testing of drug products is required.
* Prior experience managing and developing GMP laboratory staff, leading investigations, and overseeing outsourced testing is required.
* Past experience interacting with health authorities during laboratory inspections.

 
**Benefits** 

* Health Care Plan (Medical, Dental & Vision)
* Company 401k match up to 4%
* Paid Time Off (Vacation & Sick)
* Holidays
* Stock Option

role.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**POSITION TITLE:**

**Director of Quality and Population Health**

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

The Director of Quality and Population Health leads CHCFC’s Quality Improvement and Population Health programs, with accountability for program planning, implementation, and evaluation. The Director works across departments to improve patient outcomes, access, and health equity; leads measurable improvement initiatives; and oversees quality reporting. The position directly supervises Population Health staff and independently manages program priorities and follow-through within plans approved by the Chief Medical Officer.

**REPORTS TO:**

Chief Medical Officer

**FLSA STATUS:**

Exempt

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Lead Quality Improvement and Performance Management**

* Develops quality and population health priorities and the annual Performance Management Plan in collaboration with the Quality Council and other leaders for Chief Medical Officer approval; leads implementation and evaluates progress toward established goals.
* Leads monthly Performance Management meetings; establishes reporting expectations with Quality Champions, reviews measures, and ensures improvement plans have clear owners, timelines, and follow-through.
* Coaches teams in practical improvement methods, including setting measurable goals, testing workflow changes, and evaluating whether changes improve results.
* Provides staff training and presents clear reports and recommendations to leadership and relevant committees; independently addresses routine program barriers and escalates unresolved issues, resource needs, and major decisions to the Chief Medical Officer.

**2. Manage Population Health Programs and Staff**

* Recruits, hires, orients, supervises, and evaluates Population Health staff; establishes priorities, monitors workloads, and supports staff development and accountability.
* Oversees outreach, patient registries, and workflows that support preventive care, chronic disease management, and closure of care gaps.
* Coordinates with Medical, Behavioral Health, Nursing, Operations, and other teams to integrate population health activities into daily workflows and reduce avoidable duplication.
* Uses population data to identify disparities and barriers to care and works with teams to improve outreach and access for underserved patients.

**3. Oversee Quality Data and Reporting**

* Oversees a calendar of quality reporting requirements, measure definitions, data sources, responsible staff, and deadlines; follows up with contributors to ensure timely, accurate completion of program deliverables.
* Works with IT and other data partners to develop and validate reports, registries, and dashboards; investigates discrepancies and supports consistent data collection and documentation.
* Analyzes trends and presents actionable findings to support priorities, resource decisions, and evaluation of improvement efforts.
* Shares responsibility for annual Uniform Data System (UDS) reporting with IT, Finance, and other designated contributors; coordinates the quality and clinical measures within the Director’s scope, supports validation, and completes assigned reporting deliverables.
* Coordinates other assigned HRSA, payer, accountable care organization, and program quality reporting with the appropriate organizational leads.

**4. Lead PCMH Activities and Cross Department Collaboration**

* Serves as the primary coordinator for Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH) recognition and ongoing reporting, maintains documentation and timelines, and works with departments to meet applicable requirements.
* Leads improvement work across departments in collaboration with clinical and operational leaders; translates quality priorities into feasible workflows, establishes shared responsibilities and timelines, and evaluates whether improvements are sustained.
* Participates in relevant meetings, training, and professional development and performs other duties as assigned, consistent with the position’s responsibilities and qualifications.

**REQUIRED SKILLS, EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in public health, health administration, a related field, or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. A master’s degree in a related field is preferred. Clinical training or licensure is not required.

**Experience**

* Minimum of three years of relevant experience in healthcare quality improvement, population health, or healthcare performance management, with demonstrated success independently leading improvement initiatives and managing program deliverables.
* Experience collecting, validating, analyzing, and presenting healthcare performance data.
* Supervisory or substantial cross-department team leadership experience required; direct staff supervision experience preferred.
* Experience in an FQHC, community health center, or other setting serving diverse and underserved populations preferred.
* Familiarity with PCMH, UDS, and value-based care quality measures preferred.

**Skills**

* Practical knowledge of continuous quality improvement methods and ability to help teams turn data into measurable improvements.
* Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and reporting deadlines.
* Proficiency with Excel and Microsoft Office; ability to use electronic health records, registries, and reporting tools. Familiarity with Epic preferred.
* Clear written and verbal communication, effective staff coaching, and collaborative leadership across departments.
* Ability to work respectfully with culturally, racially, ethnically, and gender diverse staff and patients and apply an equity perspective to quality and population health work.
* Sound judgment, integrity, and ability to maintain confidentiality and comply with CHCFC privacy and information security policies.

**Physical Demands:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of this position, with or without reasonable accommodation. Duties primarily involve sitting, computer use, reviewing electronic records and reports, and communicating with staff and leadership. The role also involves attending meetings and moving between work areas or CHCFC locations as needed.

**Working Conditions:**

Work is primarily performed in an office or health center setting, with travel between CHCFC locations as needed. Work arrangements are determined by organizational needs and CHCFC policies. Secure access to patient and organizational information is required, and confidential work must be conducted in a private setting using approved systems.

**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement:**

CHCFC is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any protected status under federal or state law. CHCFC is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace.

**Disclaimer:**

This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not intended to be an exhaustive list. It does not constitute an employment contract. Duties and responsibilities may be modified based on organizational needs.
