role.title: Director of Quality-Cleveland Medical Center
role.description:
**A Brief Overview**

The Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for clinical quality, patient safety, regulatory readiness, accreditation compliance, and organizational policy management across a large, complex medical center. The Director establishes priorities, ensures alignment across clinical and operational functions, and partners with physician, nursing, operational, and administrative executives to advance high reliability, continuous improvement, regulatory excellence, and patient-centered care. This position has accountability for the design, execution, and sustained performance of quality improvement, patient safety, accreditation, policy governance, performance measurement, and regulatory compliance programs. The Director translates organizational strategy into medical center-wide priorities, evaluates performance and risk, directs corrective action, and provides executive leaders with recommendations needed to achieve organizational goals and external standards.

**What You Will Do**

* **Quality and Performance Improvement**
 + Establish and lead the organization's quality, safety, accreditation, and policy strategy in alignment with organizational strategy and medical center priorities.
 + Set the performance improvement agenda and direct organization-wide and departmental initiatives, including prioritization, resource allocation, accountability, and sustainability of results.
 + Establish performance expectations and governance for key quality indicators, publicly reported measures, regulatory metrics, and improvement commitments; intervene when performance or compliance is at risk.
 + Facilitate data-driven improvement efforts using Lean, Six Sigma, PDSA, and other improvement methodologies.
 + Own the integrity, interpretation, and executive communication of quality dashboards, scorecards, and performance reporting, including recommendations for action and escalation.
 + Partner with physician and nursing leaders to improve clinical outcomes, reliability, equity, and patient experience.
 + Exercise decision-making authority within the assigned portfolio and escalate material quality, safety, regulatory, or accreditation risks to executive leadership and appropriate governance bodies.
 + Define accountability structures for leaders responsible for performance improvement plans and verify that corrective actions produce sustained results.
* **Patient Safety**
 + Provide leadership for the patient safety program and establish expectations for a culture of safety, high reliability, transparency, learning, and accountability
 + In partnership with Risk and clinical loss control, monitor serious safety events, near misses, and highreliability metrics. Collaborate with risk management, infection prevention, and operational leaders on safety priorities.
 + Integrate patient safety, infection prevention, clinical risk, quality improvement, and regulatory priorities to reduce duplication, close gaps, and promote consistent practices across care settings.
 + Support implementation of evidence-based practices to reduce preventable harm.
* **Accreditation and Regulatory Compliance**
 + Provide oversight of Joint Commission, DNV, CMS, state, and specialty accreditation readiness, partnering with the designated accreditation leader who directs day-to-day readiness activities to include establishing priorities, assigning corrective actions, and escalating unresolved compliance risks.
 + Oversee organizational responses to survey findings and regulatory deficiencies, including corrective action governance, evidence submission, validation of sustained compliance, and executive escalation; monitor regulatory changes and communicate implications to leadership; and partner with operational leaders to address gaps and sustain compliance.
* **Policy Management and Governance**
 + Ensure policies remain current, evidence-based, and aligned with regulatory requirements.
 + Coordinate policy review cycles and approvals with clinical, operational, legal, compliance, and executive stakeholders.
 + Evaluate policy compliance trends and identify improvement opportunities.
 + Resolve or escalate cross-functional policy conflicts and ensure accountable leaders address material gaps in policy implementation or adherence.
 + Maintain oversight of organizational policy standards and publication processes. Consistent with UH policy governance structures, accreditation, compliance, legal, quality, and operational leaders collaborate to ensure policy adherence and regulatory alignment.
* **Academic Mission Support**
 + Collaborate with medical school leadership, residency and fellowship programs, and research leadership to integrate quality, safety, and regulatory expectations into organizational programs.
 + Support quality and safety education for medical students, residents, fellows, and faculty.
* **Leadership and Operations**
 + Establish departmental goals, operating plans, budgets, staffing models, and resource priorities; monitor financial and operational performance and adjust plans as organizational needs change.
 + Build leadership capability and succession plans for quality, safety, accreditation, regulatory, policy, and performance improvement professionals; hold direct reports accountable for measurable outcomes.
 + Serve as the quality and safety advisor to executive, physician, nursing, and operational leadership, providing independent evaluation of performance, risk, regulatory exposure, and improvement priorities.
 + Present quality, safety, accreditation, regulatory, and policy performance to governing boards, executive committees, and medical staff leadership; recommend decisions, investments, and corrective actions.
 + Chair or lead multidisciplinary governance committees focused on quality, accreditation, safety, regulatory compliance, and policy, with authority to establish agendas, assign accountability, and escalate unresolved issues.
 + Negotiate priorities and resource needs across competing operational demands while protecting regulatory compliance, patient safety, and organizational performance.
 + Represent the medical center in organization-wide councils and, as assigned, with external regulators, accrediting organizations, professional associations, and community partners.

**Additional Responsibilities**

* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Complies with all policies and standards.
* For specific duties and responsibilities, refer to documentation provided by the department during orientation.
* Must abide by all requirements to safely and securely maintain Protected Health Information (PHI) for our patients. Annual training, the UH Code of Conduct and UH policies and procedures are in place to address appropriate use of PHI in the workplace.

**Education Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree in Healthcare Administration, Nursing, Public Health, Business Administration, or related field (Required)
* Master's Degree in Healthcare Administration, Nursing, Public Health, Business Administration, or related field Preferred (Preferred)

**Experience Qualifications**

* 8+ years of experience in healthcare quality, patient safety, accreditation, regulatory, and clinical leadership experience with several years in people management capacity[ (Required)
* Experience within an academic medical center, integrated delivery system, or large healthcare organization. (Required)

**Skills and Abilities**

* Experience with Joint Commission/DNV survey leadership. (Preferred proficiency)
* Experience overseeing policy governance. (Preferred proficiency)
* Experience leading multidisciplinary teams, influencing senior and executive leaders, managing organizational change, and sustaining measurable results across complex operations. (Preferred proficiency)
* Experience presenting to governing boards, executive committees, medical staff leadership, or comparable senior governance groups. (Preferred proficiency)
* Experience managing budgets, staffing plans, and resource allocation for a complex function or department. (Preferred proficiency)

**Licenses and Certifications**

* Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ) (Preferred)
* Certified Professional in Patient Safety (CPPS) (Preferred)
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent (Preferred)
* Healthcare accreditation or regulatory certification (Preferred)

**Physical Demands**

* Standing - Occasionally
* Walking - Occasionally
* Sitting - Constantly
* Lifting - Rarely (up to 20 lbs)
* Carrying - Rarely (up to 20 lbs)
* Pushing - Rarely (up to 20 lbs)

* Climbing - Rarely (up to 20 lbs)

* Reaching - Rarely
* Handling - Occasionally
* Grasping - Occasionally
* Feeling - Rarely
* Talking - Constantly
* Hearing - Constantly
* Repetitive Motions - Frequently
* Eye/Hand/Foot Coordination - Frequently

role.title: Director of Quality and Accreditation
role.description:
Overview:

**Valley Behavioral Health** is seeking an experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to join our team!

Offering the highest quality of treatment in the area, **Valley Behavioral Health** focuses on providing their patients with the tools and knowledge needed to live happy, healthy lives. Regardless of the level of care, patients receive personalized treatment by a multi-disciplinary team of therapists, social workers, psychiatrists, psychiatric nurses, and other caring mental health professionals.

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced **Director of Quality and Accreditation** to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
 + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
 + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
 + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
 + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
 + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
 + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
 + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
 + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.
* Regulatory preparedness – implement sustainable survey preparation and ongoing monitoring processes, including facility-wide auditing and early-issue identification, to maximize achievement of zero- or standard-level survey outcomes.
 + Facility-wide support – collaborate with other departments to sustainably implement best-practices in regulatory/accreditation compliance as evidenced by measurable results with regard to survey outcomes, patient safety metrics, patient experience results, HBIPS, etc.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in regulatory planning strategy for all standards for all relevant regulatory and accrediting bodies at the local, state, and federal level.
 + Develop and maintain proficiency in the functionality and auditing within electronic platforms such as electronic patient observations and the electronic medical record, as applicable.
 + Lead Root-Cause Analyses and conduct timely and regular evaluation of serious incidents, complaints, grievances and related investigations to:
 - Identification of events, trends and patterns that may affect client health, safety and or treatment efficacy,
 - Committee evaluation findings and recommendations submitted to agency management for corrective action,
 - Implemented actions, outcomes, trends analyzed over time
 + Develop corrective action plans for the resolution of areas of regulatory vulnerability or those which could compromise patient safety in collaboration with other facility leaders.
 + Ensure proper reporting of violations or potential violations to duly authorized enforcement agencies as appropriate and/or required.
 + Ensure proper reporting of incidents and adverse clinical outcomes to duly authorized enforcement agencies or regulatory agencies as appropriate and/or required.
 + In conjunction with assigned corporate Division Quality Director, initiate and lead communications with regulatory agencies as appropriate.
 + Develop sustainable performance improvement practices through analysis of data and prioritization of efforts to improve survey readiness and consistency of care delivery using expected best-practices.
 + Ensure multidisciplinary ownership of best-practices in self-monitoring, auditing, and process improvement, escalating opportunities for improved engagement to the facility CEO as appropriate.
 + Ensures strategic and operational implementation of regulatory requirements, guidelines, and standards of federal, state, and local licensing agencies, accrediting and certifying organizations.
 + Collaborates with Division and Corporate entities and external parties to ensure strategic quality and patient safety initiatives are fully executed at the facility level. Facilitates effective communication with facility and division leadership regarding key clinical performance improvement activities and initiatives.
 + Serves as a technical advisor, educator and internal consultant to all hospital management, staff, and physicians on the use of performance improvement tools and techniques, analytical techniques, and statistical applications.
 + Ensure facility compliance with policies and applicable standards as required by regulatory/accrediting bodies.
 + Facility leader and subject matter expert on high reliability principles and strategies to achieve zero harm.

* Clinical program excellence – assess fidelity and identify root-causes for gaps/lapses in fidelity to Acadia standards. Support other departments in developing and implementing remediation and improvement plans to achieve fidelity to Acadia’s expected practices, including all elements of treatment program implementation.
* + Develop, review, and educate on internal clinical procedures and appropriate use of outcome evaluation tools and the associated results – including patient experience data and other quality scorecard metrics – to ensure continuous quality improvement and ongoing compliance with federal, state, and third-party regulatory requirements.
 + Translate standards, requirements, and policies into terms or processes meaningful to the facility.
* Leadership – serve as a visible, engaged, and dynamic member of the facility leadership team.
 + Chairs the monthly Quality Council
 + Complete safety rounds, participate in leadership rounding, and submit results/corrective actions to Acadia corporate office.
 + Review incident/safety concerns with the leadership team to identify systemic issues and facilitate the development of corrective actions.
 + Lead and facilitate Root Cause Analyses into all serious and/or sentinel events.
 + Invest in the facility staff through engagement in hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient operations.
 + Oversees the Culture of Safety Survey and follow-up action planning and sustainment processes.
 + Identification of problems or potential problems to prevent risks to patients and staff. Proposes corrective steps that may include, but are not limited to:
 - Changes in policies/procedures,
 - Staffing and assignment changes,
 - Additional education or training for staff,
 - Addition or deletion of services

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s Degree in Human Services or nursing required. Master’s degree in behavioral health/risk discipline, Registered Nurse preferred.
* Two or more years of experience in a Quality, Clinical, or PI role required.
* One or more years of management experience preferred.
* Experience with CARF, DEA, Joint Commission, or CMS surveys, as required by service line(s) supported

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Current licensure appropriate for the degree held required.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.

**ADDITIONAL REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS:**

***(******e.g.*** ***emergencies, changes in workload, rush jobs or technological developments) dictate.***

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants for employment regardless of an individual’s characteristics protected by applicable state, federal and local laws.

role.title: Site Quality Director
role.description:
**Why Us?**

At Par Health, we believe great healthcare is built on getting the essentials right. We’re looking for passionate, talented individuals who share our commitment to improving lives. With a global workforce, we lead with pride and purpose—prioritizing quality and safety while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and teamwork. Elevating the Essentials isn’t just our tagline, it’s the higher standard we live by every day.

**Job Description Summary**

The Site Quality Director is responsible for ensuring cGMP compliance and product quality at the Raleigh, NC facility while supporting broader site quality initiatives aligned with company objectives. This role provides strategic leadership in the development, implementation, and oversight of the site quality systems to ensure that all manufacturing, testing, packaging, storage, and distribution activities meet regulatory standards and deliver the highest product quality. The Site Quality Director leads and mentors quality teams, oversees daily quality operations, and serves as a key partner to site leadership by providing guidance on quality and compliance across the organization.

**Job Description**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* **Manages all aspects of Site Quality System including but not limited to: CAPA, exceptions, document management, complaint investigation handling, change control, supplier quality, OOS investigations, stability programs, and regulatory inspection readiness.**
* **Support a quality program which instils personal accountability for accuracy, consistency, and completeness for all operations**
* **Provides direction and leadership for the successful execution of quality activities, such as:**
* **Ensures health authority inspection (FDA, EU, Health Canada and others) readiness through development of compliance enhancement plans, internal audit program, and industry intelligence.**
* **Customer complaint investigation, including interaction with customers and resolution of critical issues.**
* **Manages the supplier quality program to fulfill regulatory and site needs.**
* **Conducts and/or administers new employee, ongoing, and directed training on GMP topics to ensure compliance to regulations. Manages site training compliance program.**
* **CAPA program to effectively identify and correct problems that impact product quality or compliance.**
* **Validation activities for new, altered, or modified equipment, facilities, or manufacturing processes.**
* **Customer audit process (approximately 50/yr.) to include preparation, hosting, and responding to issues noted – also, utilize input from customer audits and a continuous improvement tool.**
* **Documents management and label control to fulfill regulatory and business needs**
* **Stability program for both API products manufactured at the site.**
* **Approves highly technical investigations involving product impact.**
* **Sets direction and policies for cGMP compliance activities.**
* **Schedules employees through subordinates, performance appraisals, and performance management of team members.**
* **Budgets and adherence for areas of functional responsibility.**
* **Directly interacting with key customers relating to technical issues, potential non-compliance activities, or service issues impacted by quality/compliance.**
* **Resolution of critical quality issues that could impact production, customer service, quality, or compliance.**
* **Interprets regulatory guidance to determine site course of action for compliance.**
* **Technical expert in multiple quality functional areas, such as validation, product investigations, quality systems, and establishing compliance plans, etc.**

**DEPARTMENT** **SPECIFIC/NON-ESSENTIAL** **FUNCTIONS:**

* **Other duties as assigned with or without accommodation.**
* **Participates in a certified 5S Workplace System to ensure good housekeeping and organization.**

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:**

**BS Chemistry, Engineering, Life Science or related.**

**Experience:**

**7-10 years leadership experience in a chemical or pharmaceutical manufacturing environment, preferably specific to Quality and/or manufacturing related functions.**

**Preferred** **Skills/Qualifications:**

* **Working knowledge of chemical, pharmaceutical or bio-pharmaceutical manufacturing.**
* **Must have knowledge and understanding of applicable global regulations, GMP and compendial requirements.**
* **Must have thorough knowledge and understanding of QA regulations as they apply to this type of facility.**
* **Experience in driving improvements in quality systems and quality performance is preferred.**
* **Certification as a Six Sigma Black or Green Belt and/or as a Certified Quality Engineer is considered a plus.**
* **Must have high technical ability and excellent** **interpersonal/communication** **skills. Requires excellent oral and written skills and good negotiation skills to effectively communicate and influence the outcome of quality related plans, programs, and activities throughout the business unit.**
* **Must have the ability and experience to drive cost reduction while continuously improving performance, as well as the ability to lead employees in making these changes.**

**RELATIONSHIP WITH OTHERS/ SCOPE:**

* **This position reports to the Interim Head of Quality, Generics.**
* **This position will have frequent communication and working relationships with departments and plant managers.**
* **Interacts with internal Staff (Department and Plant Managers) on all Site management issues. Advises Staff on compliance issues. Report on overall performance and critical quality issues to Corporate Quality. Interacts with Corporate Quality personnel, R&D, and quality and managers within the organization. Works with Commercial team on customer issues. External contacts include regulatory authorities, state, federal and international (FDA, OSHA, EPA, NCDENR), suppliers, customers and community contacts.**
* **Financial responsibilities include managing multi-million payroll and operating budgets. Also recommends major purchases and capital expenditures that are necessary to maintain operations of QC laboratory and to maintain or improve the site’s GMP compliance and performance.**

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

* **70% Office Environment** 
 **30% Laboratory and Plant environment including exposure to raw materials and finished products**
* **Must be willing and able to wear PPE including hard-hat, steel-toed shoes, safety glasses, and any other devices or equipment as specified for the position.**
* **Some travel is required, both domestically and internationally.**

**DISCLAIMER:**

**The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this** **classification.** **They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of employees assigned to this position.**

**EEO Statement:**

We comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws prohibiting discrimination and harassment, and provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or genetic information, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

role.title: Director of Manufacturing
role.description:
**Job Summary**

The Director of Manufacturing will provide strategic and operational leadership across manufacturing operations, ensuring production performance, scalability, operational excellence, cost efficiency, and quality. This role is responsible for developing manufacturing strategies, leading cross-functional teams, and aligning operations with business growth and organizational objectives.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with organizational goals.
* Lead manufacturing operations, production, and operational support functions.
* Establish operational KPIs and drive accountability across manufacturing teams.
* Improve production capacity, throughput, efficiency, quality, and cost performance.
* Lead continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
* Develop and implement workforce planning and organizational strategies.
* Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and leadership.
* Support new product introduction, process transfers, and manufacturing scale-up.
* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, quality, and safety requirements.
* Develop management teams and succession planning.
* Identify opportunities for automation, technology implementation, and process innovation.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, or related field.
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience.
* 5+ years of senior manufacturing leadership experience.
* Proven experience managing complex manufacturing operations.
* Strong background in operational excellence, Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement.
* Experience managing budgets, KPIs, production capacity, and large teams.
* Experience in medical devices, biotech, aerospace, electronics, or advanced manufacturing preferred.

role.description:
Job Description
 
 
The Executive Director, Organization & Talent Partner (OTP), Manufacturing Division, reports to the Vice President, Human Resources, Manufacturing Division and serves as the senior strategic organization and talent advisor to senior leaders and their leadership teams within the Global Biologics Operating Unit and the Global Science Engineering and Commercialization organization.
 
 
Operating with a divisional as well as an enterprise mindset, the leader architects the long-term view that connects priorities and business needs into organizational capability planning solutions that help ensure these organizations have the structures, capabilities, leadership, talent pipelines and ways of working needed to deliver their priorities.
 
 
The role operates across complex scientific, pipeline, workforce, geographic and organizational priorities; co-creates strategy; frames organization and workforce choices; and establishes governance and ways of working across multiple leadership interfaces.
 
 
The Executive Director leads a team of two Organization & Talent Partners. Operating with an enterprise mindset, the role connects priorities across Manufacturing, partnering with Talent Enablement and commissioning the right expertise from Centers of Excellence (COEs), Enterprise Team HR (ETHR) and HR Solutions & Operations to bring strategy into execution. As a people leader, the role is accountable for the direction, development, performance and effective deployment of a direct and indirect team of HR professionals.
 
 
**Primary Responsibilities:** 
Shape the agenda
 
 

* Understand, anticipate and translate business strategy into the long-term organization and talent agenda​
* Lead organization capability planning so structures, roles and capabilities are ready for where the business is going​
* Drive strategic workforce planning linked to business direction and transformation
* Bring an enterprise perspective to leadership and business planning, connecting organization, workforce and talent implications across leadership teams and the broader enterprise.

Develop the organization and its leaders
 
 

* Enable talent development strategy, including succession and leadership development for critical populations​
* Coach senior leaders to improve organizational effectiveness, leadership impact and talent decisions​
* Support transformational efforts from an organization and talent perspective​
* Act as steward in organizational effectiveness, driving stronger collaboration across functions and clarity in interfaces, so priorities connect rather than compete

Leverage the HR operating model to bring strategy into execution
 
 

* Be accountable for the strategy and execution of macro-level organizational change and transformation and ensure the right partnerships are activated to deliver successful execution​.
* Engage with TELs, COEs, ETHR, HR Solutions & Operations and other partners to deliver the highest-value business priorities, leveraging expertise and capacity where they reside. Across these partnerships, provide context on business priorities and dynamics, connect organization and talent priorities across divisions and countries
* Seek to understand local nuances and considerations when defining organization and talent strategy and execution plans​

​
 
 
**Experience, capabilities and leadership characteristics:** 
The successful candidate will bring deep strategic HR experience in a large, complex organization and a record of shaping outcomes through influence. The role requires the following capabilities and leadership characteristics:
 
 

* Business savviness: bring the depth of advanced business understanding needed to build differentiated talent strategies and workforce plans leaders will trust​.
* Organization development and effectiveness: diagnose how well the organization is working and take action to close the gaps and strengthen effectiveness, using the OCP playbook and OD team resources​.
* Talent growth and senior-leader coaching: anticipate talent and capability gaps in critical populations well before they become urgent, and shape the succession and development plans that close them​.
* Influence and executive communication: effectively frame and communicate complex or sensitive issues clearly and confidently to stakeholders and partners to ensure effective action is taken, ​and align senior stakeholders without relying on formal authority.
* Change catalyst leadership: drive the organizational and cultural shifts your strategy requires, championing new approaches and helping people move through resistance to get there​.
* Networking, partnerships: effectively navigate the organization, delivering through trusted partnerships across the HR Operating Model.
* People leadership: ​Demonstrated success as a people leader, ability to build an inclusive, high-performing OTP team with clear direction and shared accountability.
* Systems Thinking: see the organization as a connected system — deep understanding of he interdependencies between businesses, functions and regions, and read data and signals across them to find the patterns that shape the org and talent agenda​.

**Education:** 

* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline required

**Required Experience and Skills:** 

* Minimum of twelve (12) years of progressive HR or closely related business experience, including significant strategic HR partnership experience in a complex, global environment.
* Demonstrated experience advising and coaching senior executives and leadership teams.
* Demonstrated broad-reaching experience in strategic workforce planning, organization capability planning, organization design and development, talent and succession.
* Experience supporting a pharmaceutical, life sciences, manufacturing, or other science-based organization.
* Proven ability to influence senior leaders, manage high-risk and sensitive matters, and coordinate outcomes across organizational boundaries. Ability to commission work through a networked operating model. Broad global perspective and the ability to lead with cultural sensitivity across a matrixed, global organization
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, business judgment and analytical capability.
* Demonstrated people leadership experience, including leading, coaching and developing experienced HR professionals and building a high-performing, inclusive team.

**Required Skills:** 
Change Management, Executive Coaching, Organizational Capability, Organizational Design, Strategic Human Resources Leadership, Strategic Workforce Planning, Succession Planning
 
 
**Preferred Skills:** 
Commercialization, Manufacturing

role.title: Senior Director, Brand Strategy - PFG Manufacturing
role.description:
**Job Description:**

**We Deliver the Goods:**

* Competitive pay and benefits, including Day 1 Health & Wellness Benefits, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, 401K Employer Matching, Education Assistance, Paid Time Off, and much more
* Growth opportunities performing essential work to support America’s food distribution system
* Safe and inclusive working environment, including culture of rewards, recognition, and respect

**Position Purpose** 
 
The Sr Director, PFG Manufacturing Brand Strategy owns and is accountable for Manufacturing brand strategies, growth initiatives, and works with the Vice President of Sales to shape the Division’s commercial strategy. This role leads the development and execution of long-range brand strategies that support Manufacturing revenue, margin, customer growth, market expansion, and business performance objectives. The position partners with Sales, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Manufacturing leadership to establish commercial priorities, align customer commitments with production capabilities, evaluate market opportunities, and drive strategies that strengthen customer relationships and profitable growth. This role provides strategic direction, decision support through insights, and executive-level leadership to guide commercial planning, brand awareness, pricing strategy, demand planning, and long-term business performance. 
 
**Major Functional Responsibilities**

* Leads the development and execution of brand strategies that support Manufacturing revenue, margin, customer growth, and market expansion objectives.
* Partners with Manufacturing, Operations, Finance, Marketing, and Sales leadership to align sales plans, customer commitments, pricing actions, and production capabilities.
* Analyzes market trends, customer needs, competitive activity, sales performance, and financial results to identify opportunities, risks, and recommended actions.
* Builds and maintains effective relationships with key customers and internal business partners to support customer retention, growth, and service execution
* Owns pricing governance, promotional strategy, contract opportunity evaluation, customer profitability planning, and revenue optimization initiatives for Manufacturing.
* Identifies new customer, channel, product, and market opportunities that support Manufacturing growth and business strategy.
* Provides direction, coaching, and support to assigned associates and cross-functional resources to ensure priorities, timelines, and deliverables are met.
* Leads executive-level business reviews by presenting commercial strategy, business performance insights, growth priorities, pricing decisions, and recommended actions that guide Manufacturing leadership planning.
* Establishes and monitors sales strategy initiatives, commercial KPIs, pricing performance, growth metrics, and corrective action plans to drive accountability for Manufacturing business results.
* Performs other duties as assigned

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree - Business or related stuty
* 8+ years of progressive experience in brand and commercial strategy, sales operations, commercial planning, business development, using insights to generate actions, revenue planning, or related commercial functions
* Strong knowledge of brand strategy, commercial planning, data insights, customer planning, and business performance analysis.
* Ability to analyze market, customer, financial, and operational data and translate findings into practical business recommendations.
* Ability to partner effectively with sales, operations, manufacturing, finance, marketing, and leadership teams.
* Ability to lead projects, influence stakeholders, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in a fast-paced business environment.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, CRM tools, sales reporting systems, financial analysis tools, and related business applications.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present information to leadership and business partners.
* Works on complex business issues involving sales performance, customer needs, pricing, margin, and market conditions. Problems require analysis, cross-functional input, and practical recommendations. Problem/task resolution timeframe is typically three to twelve months.
* Works under general direction. Exercises judgment within established policies, practices, and business objectives. Receives guidance on overall priorities and strategic direction from the Manufacturing VP, Sales & Marketing.
* Decisions and recommendations may impact revenue growth, margin performance, customer relationships, production planning, service execution, and Manufacturing business results.
* Regularly interacts with Sales, Operations, Finance, Marketing, Manufacturing, and executive leadership. May interact with customers, suppliers, and external business partners related to sales strategy and growth initiatives.
* Supports sales revenue, margin, pricing, forecasting, and customer profitability objectives for Manufacturing. Provides recommendations that influence revenue growth and business performance. Does not have direct P&L ownership unless assigned by business leadership

**Company description**

Start-to-finish manufacturing, packing, and distribution of best-in-class, grab-and-go items to drive growth to a customer’s bottom line — this is the dynamic and delicious world of PFG Manufacturing. With the latest array of in-house manufactured food, snack, and beverage offerings, customers can choose products from a family of name brands or create their own custom-made, private label products to stand out in the market.

**Awards and Accolades**

Performance Food Group and/or its subsidiaries (individually or collectively, the "Company") provides equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all applicants and employees, regardless of race, color, national origin, sex, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable local, state and federal laws and regulations. Please click on the following links to review: (1) our EEO Policy; (2) the "EEO is the Law" poster and supplement; and (3) the Pay Transparency Policy Statement.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
Description:

**About Us**

Family-owned and operated since 1970, we are an industry-leading gas distributor founded on unparalleled customer service. Our industrial, medical, food, and specialty gas products support a variety of industries that work daily to improve the world we live in, and our ongoing commitment to serve spans the southwestern United States with 16 locations across California and Arizona. Discover the most interesting industry you’ve never heard of!

**Position Overview**

The Plant Manager oversees the daily operations on the plant floor while enhancing production and revenue. You will manage scheduling, supervise daily operating reports, and boost production by providing leadership and developing strategic plans.

**Essential Functions**

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

* Lead, manage, and develop plant employees to ensure they possess the necessary capabilities and culture to maintain effective operations. This includes establishing direction, gaining commitment, delegating responsibilities, and building organizational capabilities
* Ensure all staff members adhere to OSHA general standards related to manufacturing facility safety protocols
* Responsible for maintaining the facility, including understanding and explaining basic mechanical theory to direct reports, coordinating with vendors, and projecting and establishing preventative maintenance programs and schedules while directing the maintenance staff to ensure all equipment is properly maintained and operational
* Workforce Planning/Scheduling
* Ensure our products meet or exceed quality control standards using specified SOP testing methods
* Manage notable projects and improvements as directed
* Create a work environment that ensures the safety and health of employees, the community, and the environment
* Focus on continuously improving the competitiveness of operations
* Recognize customer commitment and drive activities for ongoing quality improvement
* In conjunction with senior group management, establish and oversee activities to meet short- and long-term plant goals
* Improve efficiency and capacity through capital expenditure improvements in processes and procedures and through both formal and informal continuous improvement activities
* Conduct monthly safety meetings as needed
* Other duties as assigned

Requirements:

* 5 years of experience in production management
* Ability to operate or willingness to train for forklift operation
* Production/distribution experience required; industrial gas industry or equivalent experience preferred
* In-depth knowledge of cylinder gases and processes of each
* Knowledge of all regulatory agencies including, but not limited to, FDA, DOT, OSHA, and EPA
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills; ability to communicate effectively with customers, employees, and management
* Ability to lift 50 pounds and stand for extended periods
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft applications, TIMS CU

**Supervisory Responsibility**

Manages direct reports

**Physical Demands**

The physical demands described here represent those that an employee must meet to perform the essential functions of this job successfully.

While performing this job, the employee must stand for long periods, talk, hear, and use hands and fingers to operate a computer and telephone, reach, stoop, and kneel. This person must be able to lift, carry, or set down 50+ pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision requirements due to computer work.

**Travel**

No travel is expected for this position

**Position Type and Expected Hours of Work**

This is a full-time, exempt, and on-site position. Typical days and hours of work are Monday through Friday, and range from 6:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

**Compensation and Benefits**

* Individual and company performance-based quarterly bonuses as outlined in our plan documents
* Annual performance-based merits
* Comprehensive benefits package:
 + Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
 + Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
 + Voluntary accident coverage, hospitalization plans, Employee Assistance Programs (EAP’s), Wellness platform access
 + 401(k) + company match
* 7 company-paid holidays
* 3 weeks of paid time off (PTO) earned on an accrual basis
* Professional development opportunities and ongoing training
* Healthy work/life balance and a collaborative and inclusive company culture

The compensation range reflects WestAir’s good-faith estimate for the base compensation expected at the time of posting. Compensation offered will be determined by the job-related factors, including skills, experience, qualifications, education, and geographic location.

This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. An employee may perform other related duties as negotiated to meet the organization’s ongoing needs.

WestAir Gases and Equipment, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

role.title: Director, Facility Operations
role.description:
**Director, Facility Operations** 
The 3-time WNBA Champions Los Angeles Sparks are seeking an innovative, strategic, and revenue-driven **Director, Facility Operations**. This executive will be responsible for working with both in-house employees and 3rd party vendors, and will oversee the day-to-day upkeep and operation of the Los Angeles Sparks’ Training Facility.

**PRINCIPAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Oversee the operation of building systems and equipment, including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, hydro, and food service equipment and direct the work of personnel associated with the systems and building engineering.
* Serve at the primary point of contact for building maintenance, repairs, and facilities-related service requests across all organizational spaces, including offices and venues.
* Assist in the development and implementation of a computerized work order management system to enable occupants to submit service requests, track progress, and support the prioritization and scheduling of maintenance and repair activities.
* Serve as point of contact for local utilities (ex. Southern California Edison for building power).
* Serve as the primary building point of contact for the Fire Marshal, coordinate and attend required inspections, maintain all necessary fire and life safety records and documentation, and schedule and oversee required annual, quarterly, and other periodic testing of building safety systems in accordance with applicable codes and jurisdictional requirements.
* Build and maintain budgets for annual preventative maintenance costs.
* Develop and maintain appropriate inventory levels of supplies, materials, and repair parts based on facility and venue needs, ensuring materials are readily available to support maintenance and repair activities, and maintain accurate inventory records.
* Develop and oversee annual and preventive maintenance schedules for all facilities and building systems; establish and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for facility operations, maintenance, and emergency response; and identify, engage, and manage third-party vendors to support venue operations, including establishing clear emergency response protocols and service expectation.
* Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, supply usage, labor, and associated costs to track facility performance, identify maintenance trends, and inform the development of a long-term asset management and replacement program Develop service contract requirements, scope of work, performance standards, and service-level expectations for third-party vendors to ensure facility maintenance and operational needs are clearly defined and consistently met.
* Oversee and direct housekeeping services and cleaning services for back of house spaces, player spaces, and office spaces.
* Demonstrate knowledge of professional sports hardwood court cleaning practices and maintenance requirements to ensure the playing surface meets the standards and operational needs of a professional sports team.
* Oversee and coordinate specialty window cleaning and other specialized cleaning services, ensuring work is performed safely, effectively, and in accordance with facility standards.
* Build and maintain strong working relationships with team personnel to understand facility-related needs and requests, coordinate service delivery, and ensure clear, timely, and consistent communication.
* Working alongside Food Service team and associated personnel, coordinate repairs to equipment essential to food and beverage operations as needed.
* Working alongside team trainers, schedule servicing hydrotherapy equipment as required.
* Oversee and direct the work of landscaping team to ensure trees and plants (indoor and outdoor) are maintained.
* Collect and maintain accurate records to track venue assets, with an ability to identify faulty equipment, or make recommendations based on anticipated lifecycle for asset replacement.
* Track warranties of building assets.
* Conduct frequent physical inspections of building and external grounds to ensure the highest industry standards are met in Maintenance, System Operations, identifying and communicating any potential safety concerns, and areas requiring follow-up attention.
* Other duties, as assigned, related to the upkeep, maintenance and operation of the Sparks’ Training Facility.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in facility maintenance, building systems management, and facilities oversight, including supervisory or managerial responsibilities. Experience in a professional sports or large-scale venue environment is strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated knowledge of building systems and facility maintenance, including HVAC systems (air- and water-cooled systems, humidity control, and ventilation), fire and life safety systems, electrical systems, plumbing, and exterior grounds maintenance. Ability to oversee preventive maintenance, troubleshoot facility issues, and coordinate specialized contractors to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient building operations.
* Experience leading maintenance personnel and managing third-party service providers, with the ability to establish maintenance standards, oversee service delivery, and ensure facilities meet the operational requirements of a professional sports organization.
* Understanding of basketball schedules and basic team operations.
* Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects simultaneously, working efficiently, to meet deadlines, with an excellent eye for detail.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, computer and communication skills, as well as analytical skills.
* A proven ability to think critically and set priorities.
* Innovative thinker with success in developing and implementing new ideas and programs.
* Ability to anticipate and resolve problems and conflicts.
* Available to respond to emergencies 24/7.
* Ability to maintain a high level of Professionalism in all circumstances.
Ability to work frequent irregular and long hours, weekends, evenings and all full-stadium events through completion and departure of public and team personnel as appropriate. 

**Compensation commensurate with experience; minimum starting salary at $105,000 annually.**

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the employee in this position. It is not intended to provide an exhaustive list of responsibilities. The incumbent is expected to perform other duties necessary for the effective operation of the department and organization.

We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and employment process. Please contact Human Resources to request an accommodation.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Plant Manager**
=================

**Company:** North Point Technology Consulting 
**Work Location:** Fort Wayne, Indiana, USA 
**Employment Type:** Full-Time / Contract 
**Work Arrangement:** On-Site

### **Job Overview**

North Point Technology Consulting is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead a high-volume automotive driveline manufacturing plant in Fort Wayne, Indiana.

This leader owns the full plant P&L and organizes, leads, and manages every functional area of the facility, driving lean manufacturing and a Toyota Production System based operating system while building a motivated, high-performing workforce.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Own the full plant P&L, including strategy, policies, processes, and systems.
* Lead manufacturing and assembly operations, finance (budget, cost control, capital), supply chain and inventory, EHS, labor relations, and engineering and facilities.
* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement in cost, quality, productivity, and operational excellence.
* Lead metrics and reporting, program management, and product launches.
* Build and develop a motivated workforce that meets or exceeds performance standards.
* Communicate effectively at all levels and with customers, suppliers, and the community.
* Influence business unit and executive leadership on strategy and long-range improvement plans.

### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or 4+ years of applicable experience, with 12+ years of manufacturing experience.
* Experience working in a unionized environment.
* Proven ability to set and execute long-term operational strategy tied to efficiency, cost, and quality.
* Deep understanding of manufacturing systems, lean principles, and continuous improvement.
* Strong budgeting, cost analysis, and financial metrics skills.
* Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop diverse teams with a focus on safety and accountability.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior plant manager or operations director experience in automotive or heavy manufacturing.

### **About North Point Technology Consulting**

North Point Technology Consulting provides specialized engineering and technology professionals to support manufacturing automation, MES implementations, ERP systems, and industrial technology operations across the United States and internationally.

North Point Technology is **THE BEST** place to work for curious-minded engineers motivated to support our country's most crucial missions! We focus on long term projects, leveraging the latest technology in support of innovative solutions to solve our customer's most difficult problems.

At North Point Technology, EMPLOYEES come first! We value our employees by providing excellent compensation, benefits, and a flexible work-life balance. We strive for a close-knit and open atmosphere where the owners are always directly available to our team members.

**Come join us!** **Apply with North Point Technology today!**

*For positions requiring a federal security clearance, your clearance level must be clearly identified on your resume.*

role.title: Director of Operations - Commercial Laundry
role.description:
**LEAD OPERATIONS. DEVELOP PEOPLE. DRIVE RESULTS.**

Century Linen and Uniform is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Operations to lead and oversee operations across five commercial laundry and uniform rental facilities throughout New York State and Massachusetts.

This is a key leadership position responsible for driving operational excellence, improving financial performance, developing strong management teams, and ensuring consistency and accountability across all facilities.

The ideal candidate is a strategic and hands-on leader who understands how to manage a multi-location operation, develop General Managers, improve productivity, control costs, and build a culture of performance and accountability.

**WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR**

**Multi-Plant Leadership**

* Provide overall operational leadership and direction to five commercial laundry facilities.
* Lead, coach, and hold General Managers accountable for facility performance and results.
* Establish consistent operating standards, procedures, and expectations across all locations.
* Conduct regular facility visits to evaluate performance, identify opportunities, and address operational challenges.

**Financial and Operational Performance**

* Oversee operational budgets, expenses, labor costs, overtime, and profitability.
* Partner with Finance to monitor financial results, identify variances, and implement corrective actions.
* Drive cost-control initiatives, productivity improvements, and operational efficiencies.
* Ensure each facility meets established financial and operational objectives.

**Production and Productivity**

* Oversee production performance, workflow, scheduling, labor utilization, and capacity planning.
* Monitor productivity, quality, rewash, linen loss, and production efficiency.
* Identify bottlenecks and implement improvements to maximize throughput and resource utilization.
* Ensure production operations support customer demand and service commitments.

**Customer Service and Service Delivery**

* Ensure consistent service quality, accuracy, and on-time delivery.
* Partner with Sales, Customer Service, and Transportation to resolve operational issues.
* Establish accountability for customer complaints, service failures, shortages, and recurring quality concerns.

**Leadership and Employee Development**

* Recruit, develop, coach, and evaluate General Managers and key operational leaders.
* Establish clear performance expectations, measurable goals, and accountability standards.
* Address performance concerns and leadership gaps promptly.
* Build a culture of ownership, teamwork, communication, and continuous improvement.

**Maintenance, Engineering, and Safety**

* Partner with Engineering and Maintenance leadership to improve equipment reliability and reduce downtime.
* Support preventive maintenance programs, capital projects, and facility improvements.
* Promote a safe working environment and ensure compliance with applicable safety and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Human Resources and plant leadership on employee relations, workforce planning, and labor matters.

**Transportation and Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Partner with Transportation leadership to improve routing, fleet utilization, delivery performance, and operating efficiency.
* Work collaboratively with Finance, Human Resources, Sales, Engineering, Customer Service, and other departments.
* Provide regular operational updates, performance reports, and recommendations to executive leadership.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**

The Director of Operations will be accountable for measurable improvements in:

* Plant profitability and performance against budget.
* Labor costs, overtime, and productivity.
* Pounds processed per labor hour and production efficiency.
* Customer service, on-time delivery, and quality.
* Rewash, shortages, and linen loss.
* Equipment reliability and downtime.
* Workplace safety and compliance.
* Staffing, employee retention, and General Manager performance.
* Execution of operational improvement initiatives.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

**Education and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, Industrial Management, or a related field preferred. Equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* Minimum of 7–10 years of progressive operations management experience.
* Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple facilities, locations, or business units.
* Experience leading and developing General Managers, Plant Managers, or senior operational leaders.
* Commercial laundry, textile rental, manufacturing, distribution, or other labor-intensive industrial experience strongly preferred.
* Experience managing budgets, analyzing financial results, and improving operational profitability.
* Experience working in a unionized environment and interpreting collective bargaining agreements preferred.

**Leadership Qualities**

* Strong leadership and people-development skills.
* Ability to lead through others rather than micromanage.
* High level of accountability and the ability to hold others accountable.
* Strong financial and analytical abilities.
* Strategic thinking and sound business judgment.
* Effective communication and relationship-building skills.
* Decisive problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
* Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
* Ability to implement change and drive continuous improvement.

**TRAVEL AND TRANSPORTATION REQUIREMENTS**

* This position requires frequent travel, potentially up to 90% of working time, among the company's five facilities throughout New York State and Massachusetts.
* Travel may include overnight stays, early morning departures, evening returns, weekends, and schedule adjustments based on operational needs.
* The employee is responsible for independently arranging reliable transportation to and from all assigned work locations and required reporting locations.
* The employee must be able to report to all assigned locations at the times and schedules required by the position.
* Company-provided bus transportation, if available, is offered as a convenience only and is not guaranteed. Bus service is subject to designated routes, schedules, and availability and may not accommodate the travel requirements or working hours of this position.
* Employees in this position may not rely on company-provided transportation as their sole means of commuting or traveling to required work locations.

This position requires regular presence in both office and industrial laundry environments, including production floors, maintenance areas, and loading docks. The employee must be comfortable working in environments with elevated temperatures, humidity, noise, moving equipment, industrial chemicals, and other conditions commonly found in commercial laundry facilities.

role.title: Director Facility Operations
role.description:
Overview:

**Maple Heights Behavioral Health Hospital** | **Onsite in Fort Wayne, Indiana**

Join Maple Heights Behavioral Health Hospital, a modern 120-bed behavioral health hospital serving adolescents, adults, and seniors in Fort Wayne, Indiana. Our purpose-built campus provides a full continuum of behavioral healthcare services, including inpatient treatment, partial hospitalization (PHP), and intensive outpatient programming (IOP), all delivered in a safe, therapeutic, and patient-centered environment.

As the Director of Facility Operations, you will oversee the physical plant, facilities maintenance, safety, security, environmental services, and regulatory compliance across our approximately 80,000-square-foot hospital campus. This leadership role is critical to ensuring a safe, efficient, and welcoming environment for patients, visitors, and staff while supporting the hospital's mission of delivering exceptional behavioral healthcare.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

Responsible for the overall maintenance of the buildings, grounds, fixtures, and equipment of the facility. Areas of responsibility may include two or more of the following areas/departments: safety, security, maintenance, facilities, materials management, and housekeeping.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Oversee general building maintenance including plumbing, carpentry, painting, roofing, minor repairs, and electrical work.
* Ensure preventative maintenance is completed on all equipment.
* Ensure the facility is in a sanitary, attractive, safe, orderly condition and in compliance with all regulatory standards and accreditation requirements.
* Ensure the facility maintains compliance with all regulatory standards (i.e., NFPA, OSHA, etc.) and accreditation requirements (i.e., CMS, TJC, etc).
* Provide staff management including hiring, development, training, performance management, and communication to ensure effective and efficient department operation.
* Ensure proper operations and maintenance of water systems, emergency electrical systems, sewage systems, primary electrical systems, telephone systems, fire alarm systems, and heating and cooling systems.
* Develop facility maintenance plans, timetables for completion ,and recommendations for maintenance projects.
* Serve as project manager for small-scale, short-duration projects.
* Respond to facility fire and disaster situations immediately and assist per emergency plans.
* Coordinate outside service vendors/contractors and maintenance staff to complete projects as assigned/necessary.

**OTHER FUNCTIONS:**

* Perform other functions and tasks as assigned.

 
Qualifications:

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS**

* High School Diploma required.

Bachelor’s degree or higher level of education in Business or technical field preferred.

* Five or more years’ of Healthcare experience involving construction/maintenance preferred.
* Ten or more years’ construction/maintenance/Healthcare supervisory experience preferred.

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* Valid state driver's license, where required in a facility.
* CPR and de-escalation/restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility.
* Valid Certified Healthcare Facility Manager (CHFM) will be preffered.

**ADDITIONAL REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS:**

While this job description is intended to be an accurate reflection of the requirements of the job, management reserves the right to add or remove duties from particular jobs when circumstances (e.g. emergencies, changes in workload, rush jobs or technological developments) dictate.

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all applicants for employment regardless of an individual’s characteristics protected by applicable state, federal and local laws.

role.description:
To thrive as a Plant Quality Manager, you are a strategic quality leader who is passionate about driving continuous improvement, developing high performing teams, and ensuring world class product and process quality. You will lead plant quality systems, champion quality initiatives, and partner with cross functional teams to build a culture of excellence, accountability, and operational success. We are looking for someone who combines strong technical expertise with exceptional leadership skills to help elevate quality performance across the organization!

In this role, you will oversee plant quality programs, analyze key quality metrics, identify improvement opportunities, and lead quality focused initiatives that support business objectives. You will collaborate closely with Operations, Engineering, Purchasing, R&D, and Corporate Quality teams to resolve quality challenges, strengthen processes, and drive sustainable results. We value leaders who inspire teams, foster professional development, and proactively create solutions that enhance quality, efficiency, and customer satisfaction. Together, we strive for continuous improvement, and we believe quality is everyone's responsibility.

**Here’s what we’re looking for:**

 

* High School Diploma required; Bachelor's degree preferred in Quality, Engineering, Management, or a related technical/scientific field.
* 5+ years of progressive experience in quality management, quality engineering, or manufacturing quality leadership, with a proven track record of leading plant-level quality systems, driving continuous improvement initiatives, and successfully managing cross-functional quality programs in a manufacturing environment.
* Experience in batch chemical manufacturing and managing Quality Control (QC) laboratory operations, with a strong understanding of quality testing processes, laboratory compliance, and manufacturing quality standards.
* Experience using statistical analysis and problem-solving tools to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Demonstrated leadership ability with experience coaching, developing, and managing high-performing teams.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to build effective partnerships across multiple functions.
* Experience managing budgets, resources, and quality performance metrics in a manufacturing environment.
* ASQ Certified Quality Manager (CQM) and/or Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) certification preferred.

**Here’s what we offer you:**

 

* Accrue 15 paid days of vacation time off the first year plus sick days.
* Competitive salary + performance-based incentives.
* 401(k) retirement plan with 4% match. Annual retirement profit sharing payments.
* Competitive health plans for individuals and families.

role.description:
**Location:**

1

Mercy Retirement & Care Center

1

3431 Foothill Blvd

11

Oakland CA 94601

1

**Mercy Retirement and Care center**

**Oakland, CA**

 

***The shift for this role pays $90,000 to $100,000 DOE***

Do you thrive in an environment where meaningful work happens every day? Do you want to make a difference in the lives of older adults?

 

**Mercy Retirement & Care Center** has been at the forefront of senior care for more than 150 years. Situated on our lush campus in Oakland, we provide assisted living, memory care, skilled nursing and rehabilitation services to meet a variety of healthcare needs. We provide exceptional, person-centered care that enhances the quality of life for our residents.

 

Our **Culture of Excellence** is built on a foundation of respect, integrity, and a commitment to the well-being of both our residents and our team members. We foster a collaborative and supportive environment where innovation and compassion drive everything we do.

This position is responsible for the supervision and administration of security services, maintenance operations, and ground management, in addition to overseeing capital improvements. Ensures a secure and welcoming atmosphere for residents, staff, volunteers, and visitors, this position provides management, technical expertise, life safety reviews, and quality assurance initiatives to guarantee customer satisfaction and adherence to regulatory standards related to the physical plant maintenance and appearance as well as a dedication to maintaining our World Class **Culture of Excellence.**

 

**Our Plant Ops Director:**

* Oversees preventative maintenance of systems, buildings, and grounds. Manage contracts with external experts and contractors, as necessary.
* Manages capital projects, which includes handling project bids, selecting and overseeing contractors, and managing purchases and expenditures within the allocated budgets. Ensure that project status reports and related documentation are submitted promptly.
* Supervises maintenance operations, including an organized system for tracking work orders. Promotes the efficient use of resources, with a focus on energy conservation.
* Conducts quality assurance inspections as needed to uphold high service standards. Engages in various Quality Improvement programs and committees, either personally or by designating appropriate facility personnel.
* Actively participates in and supports the Work Safety committee.
* Performs safety reviews of the campus; ensures compliance with regulations concerning buildings, systems, and disaster response protocols.
* Oversee security services for the community.
* Understands the essential role of security, establishes necessary protocols and procedures, and secures personnel to ensure the safety of both residents and team members.
* Develops job descriptions; recruits-hire, trains, schedules, supervises, and advises personnel in relevant departments. Assesses performance, suggests promotions and salary adjustments, and implements progressive disciplinary measures for Plant team members.
* Acts as an integral member of the management team.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
 

 

**What you need to succeed:**

* High School Diploma required; with some college coursework preferred. Contractor’s license is preferred but is not a requirement.
* Minimum of 6 years’ related experience in facilities management, construction, engineering, property management and maintenance, at least 3 years in health care or retirement community environment.
* An advanced understanding of building codes, life safety regulations, and Cal-OSHA standards is required, along with journeyman-level expertise in HVAC/boiler systems, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical equipment.
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills in the English language.
* A valid driver's license is required, along with strong leadership and supervisory skills.
* Familiarity with safety policies and procedures is also essential.
* Committed to delivering high-quality and professional interactions with residents, volunteers, and staff members.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly in Office 365, including Microsoft Word, Excel, and email software, is expected.
* Capable of demonstrating adaptability, informed decisions under pressure, and effectively prioritizing tasks and projects.
* Completion of a background check and drug screening. Pre employment screenings may also include a physical, TB test, and fingerprinting per state/local guidelines.
 

 

**Physical Requirements:**

* May involve lifting, pushing, pulling, up to 75lbs, and transporting equipment, and candidates may encounter challenging environmental conditions, such as dirt, noise, heights, and confined spaces, necessitating caution for safety.
* To ensure the health and safety of both our team members and residents, Elder Care Alliance may mandate that team members receive vaccinations, engage in daily screenings, undergo surveillance testing, and utilize face coverings along with other personal protective equipment (PPE) in accordance with regulatory guidelines to mitigate the transmission of infectious diseases.
* Essential abilities for the safe execution of duties include good vision and hearing; full mobility on steps and ladders; adequate dexterity and mobility in both arms (or mechanical alternatives) to operate hand and power tools, gauges, and valves safely.
* Physical requirements can be accommodated with mechanical aids/devices.
