role.title: Sr. Director, Process Engineering
role.description:
R3 Lithium operates North America's first commercial scale lithium carbonate recovery facility, located in Covington, Georgia. Using a lithium-first extraction process, the company recovers, refines, and returns lithium carbonate from recycled black mass into the battery supply chain for energy storage systems, defense applications, and electric vehicles. Founded in 2026 and privately held, R3 Lithium is headquartered at 9176 Industrial Drive NE, Covington, Georgia. For more information, visit www.r3lithium.com

R3 Lithium is seeking a highly experienced **Lead Discipline Process Engineer** to provide technical leadership for process design, process optimization, and operational excellence across lithium processing and manufacturing operations. This position serves as the subject matter expert for process engineering and is responsible for leading process design activities, supporting project execution, troubleshooting operational challenges, and driving continuous improvement initiatives that enhance safety, reliability, quality, and production performance.

The successful candidate will play a key leadership role in the development, commissioning, and optimization of lithium processing facilities while collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering, operations, maintenance, and project teams.

**Required Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, Process Engineering, or related engineering discipline required.
* Master's degree preferred.

**Experience**

* Minimum **15+ years of progressively responsible process engineering experience** in lithium, chemical processing, mining, hydrometallurgical, battery materials, refining, or industrial manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading process engineering activities for large capital projects and operating facilities.
* Experience supporting facility commissioning, start-up, troubleshooting, and process optimization.
* Strong understanding of process simulation, process control, mass and energy balances, and industrial process design.
* Proven leadership experience mentoring engineers and leading multidisciplinary technical teams.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Process Engineering Leadership**

* Serve as the technical lead and discipline authority for all process engineering activities.
* Develop and oversee process engineering standards, specifications, and best practices.
* Provide technical leadership and mentorship to process engineers and project teams.
* Review and approve engineering deliverables to ensure technical accuracy and compliance with design requirements.

**Process Design & Project Execution**

* Lead process design efforts including:
* + Process Flow Diagrams (PFDs)
 + Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs)
 + Heat and Material Balances
 + Equipment Sizing and Specification
 + Process Control Philosophies
 + Process Hazard Analyses (PHA/HAZOP)
* Support feasibility studies, front-end engineering design (FEED), detailed engineering, commissioning, and startup activities.
* Participate in technology evaluations, vendor selection, and equipment procurement activities.
* Support capital project planning, budgeting, scheduling, and execution.

**Process Optimization & Operational Excellence**

* Identify and implement opportunities to improve production efficiency, recovery rates, throughput, product quality, and operating costs.
* Lead root cause investigations and corrective action programs for process-related issues.
* Utilize process data analytics to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
* Develop performance metrics and monitor process key performance indicators (KPIs).

**Safety, Environmental & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure process designs and operating practices comply with applicable safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
* Lead participation in HAZOP studies, Management of Change (MOC), and risk assessments.
* Promote a strong safety culture and operational discipline throughout the organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with lithium extraction, lithium conversion, lithium salts production, hydrometallurgical processing, or battery materials manufacturing.
* Experience with Aspen HYSYS, Aspen Plus, MATLAB, or other process modeling software.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.
* Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
* Experience supporting greenfield facility development and startup activities.

**Core Competencies**

* Process Design & Engineering
* Hydrometallurgical Processing
* Chemical Plant Operations
* Process Simulation & Modeling
* Capital Project Execution
* Process Safety Management (PSM)
* Root Cause Analysis
* Commissioning & Startup
* Continuous Improvement
* Team Leadership & Mentorship
* Technical Risk Assessment
* Cross-Functional Collaboration

**Key Performance Indicators**

* Plant Throughput & Capacity Utilization
* Process Recovery Rates
* Yield Improvement
* Operating Cost Reduction
* Process Reliability & Uptime
* Safety Performance Metrics
* Environmental Compliance
* Successful Capital Project Delivery
* Process Improvement Savings
* Engineering Quality and Execution

role.title: Vice President of Continuous Improvement & Lean
role.description:
Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.

Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.

The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.

**Job Responsibilities:**
-------------------------

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).

role.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations (Nights) - Site Based, Redmond, WA
role.description:
**Job Title:** Sr. Manager, Manufacturing Operations

**Location:** Redmond, WA

**Reports To:** Director, Manufacturing Operations

**Shift:** Nights

**About Us:**

At Just-Evotec, we believe that curiosity is the spark that drives innovation and success. As a forward-thinking team, we thrive on challenging the status quo, learning from each other, and pushing the boundaries of what’s possible. We're on a mission to create a place where curiosity isn't just encouraged, it’s celebrated.

Are you someone who asks questions, seeks answers, and isn't afraid to go deeper? #BeCUREious with us and see where your curiosity can take you!

**The Role:**

We’re looking for a passionate and curious Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations to join our team. If you’re excited by new challenges, solving complex problems, and learning every step of the way, you might just be the perfect fit. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to drive impactful projects, collaborate with bright minds, and explore uncharted territories.

As a Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations**,** you'll have the freedom to ask the hard questions, think outside the box, and find creative solutions that push us forward. It’s a role where your curiosity will fuel both your personal growth and the success of the team.

**What You’ll Do:**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for night-shift GMP manufacturing operations, including upstream and downstream biologics manufacturing activities.
* Ensure manufacturing operations are executed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with approved procedures, batch records, and production schedules.
* Establish clear shift priorities, communicate expectations, and ensure effective allocation of personnel and resources.
* Monitor manufacturing performance, identify emerging risks, and take proactive action to prevent delays, deviations, and disruptions.
* Ensure equipment, materials, personnel, and documentation are ready to support scheduled manufacturing activities.
* Lead real-time troubleshooting and operational decision-making, engaging appropriate technical and support functions as required.
* Maintain operational continuity across shift transitions through effective communication, documentation, and handovers.
* Own night-shift execution performance and drive consistent, predictable manufacturing outcomes.

**Who You Are:**

* Master’s degree and 6 years of Manufacturing or Operations experience; or
* Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of Manufacturing Leadership experience
* Proven knowledge of cGMP requirements to ensure compliance
* Significant experience in operations required for the manufacture of biotherapeutics
* Proven record of accomplishment managing, supervising and developing staff
* Candidate must possess strong focus on quality and attention to detail
* Excellent communication with senior leadership
* In-depth knowledge of biotech equipment, operations, and engineering principles
* Recognized technical mastery of disposable manufacturing technologies at commercial scale
* Change control, NC/CAPA, and deviations
* Fundamental understanding and basic operation of process automation (DeltaV)
* Experienced in technology and/or process transfer for late stage clinical manufacturing or commercial qualification campaigns; commercial campaign support
* Application of knowledge and expertise to solve complex technical problems; may apply novel approach that provides significant technology advancement

**Why Join Us:**

* **Growth Opportunities**: We’re a company that believes in continuous learning and development. Whether it’s professional courses, mentorship, or new projects, we’ll help you grow.
* **Inclusive Culture**: We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone’s voice is valued, and curiosity is encouraged.
* **Innovative Projects**: You’ll have the chance to work on groundbreaking initiatives and cutting-edge technology in an atmosphere where your curiosity is the key to success.
* **A Place for Big Ideas**: We don’t just talk about thinking outside the box, we throw the box away. If you’ve got ideas, we want to hear them.

**Are You Still Curious?**

If you’ve read this far, then chances are you’ve got a curious mind, just like us. So, what are you waiting for? Take the leap and apply today. We can’t wait to see where your curiosity leads you and how it will shape the future of Just-Evotec.

Let your curiosity guide your career #BeCUREious and explore the endless possibilities at Just Evotec Biologics!

The base pay range for this non-exempt position at commencement of employment is expected to be $130,000 to $155,000 annually. Base salary offered may vary depending on individual's skills, experience and competitive market value. Additional total rewards include discretionary annual bonus, comprehensive benefits to include Medical, Dental and Vision, short-term and long-term disability, company paid basic life insurance, 401k company match, flexible work, generous paid time off and paid holiday, wellness and transportation benefits. Evotec (US) Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, gender, age, disability, genetic information, gender expression, gender identity, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, or veteran status.

role.title: Senior Manager Operational Area Quality (Hybrid)
role.description:
**Job Description**

**General/Position Summary**

 

The Quality Assurance Senior Operational Manager is recognized as an expert internally in the principles and application of quality assurance and compliance. The Quality Snr Manager will provide QA support of manufacturing operations, analytical laboratory operations and materials management for the external manufacture of Cell & Genetic Therapeutic programs. This role will drive, review & support activities related to product disposition including review of batch data, batch records, deviations, in-process data, EM data, QC release testing and other quality systems documentation.

 

**Key Duties & Responsibilities**

* Responsible for quality support of Vertex Cell and Gene Therapy manufacturing operations across all phases of development, support of analytical laboratory, materials management and manufacturing operations.

* Responsible for GMP batch disposition activities including review and approval of batch records, deviations, in-process data, EM data, QC release testing, materials review board and other quality activities as applicable to determine acceptability of product disposition.

* Partner with External CDMOs

* Provide QA support of change controls, process and OOS investigations, and associated CAPAs.

* Responsible for approval of COAs and product labelling.

* Support review and approval of manufacturing documents such as technical and analytical protocols/reports

* Support technical transfer, and process performance qualification activities.

* Responsible for identifying compliance risks and gaps for GMP processes and supporting implementation of mitigating controls

* Support audit and inspection readiness activities.

* Act as a trusted advisor by providing compliance guidance through collaborative review and partnering with business stakeholders and contract manufacturers.

* Support the vendor management process including the creation and review of Quality Agreements with suppliers.

* Assist with addressing product complaints

* Maintain periodic batch record metrics and assists department with routine/quarterly Quality System data review metrics and reporting

* Execute improvements to QA operations procedure.

* Participate/ lead Cell & Genetic Program and Quality projects and drive continuous improvement activities.

 

**Required Education Level**

* Bachelor's degree in a biotech/ Lifesciences field.

* Preferred Master's degree or relevant comparable background.

 

**Required Experience**

8+ years of relevant industry experience such as manufacturing, quality assurance, and/or quality control in biotechnology/regulated pharmaceutical environment.

 

**Required Knowledge/Skills**

* Demonstrated experience providing QA support to GMP manufacturing operation
* Experience successfully leading event investigations, Root Cause Analysis and CAPA
* Experience with network-based applications such as Oracle, TrackWise, Veeva
* In-depth knowledge of both the conceptual and practical application of cGMPs in a pharmaceutical setting; Biotech/Cell & Gene GMP regulations and applicability. (e.g. EU, FDA, ICH, USP, etc. or other industry best practices ex. ISPE, WHO, etc.)
* Knowledge in Cell technology, aseptic manufacturing technology, analytical assays, cell & genetic therapies/Biologics processing, fill/finish and testing.
* Professional membership or equivalent in relevant societies, network of knowledge in cell and gene therapy industry.
* Ability to evaluate quality matters and make decisions utilizing risk-based approach
Ability to independently lead cross-functional teams, and effectively communicate with business stakeholders. 

 

**Other Requirements**

Up to 15% Travel may be required 

 
 

At Vertex, we embrace continuous learning and encourage employees to stay informed on advances in AI, technology, automation, and industry trends. We seek talent who bring an external perspective, demonstrate curiosity and sound judgment, and thoughtfully adopt new capabilities that improve decision-making, drive innovation, increase efficiency, and help deliver better outcomes for patients.

**Pay Range:**

$133,800 - $200,600

**Disclosure Statement:**

The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations. From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more.

**Flex Designation:**

Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible

**Flex Eligibility Status:**

In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as:
 
1. **Hybrid** : work remotely up to two days per week; **or select** 
2. **On-Site** : work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility.

Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time.

#LI-Hybrid

**Company Information**

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation.

Vertex is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, or any characteristic protected under applicable law. Vertex is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. Vertex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law.

Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should make a request to the recruiter or hiring manager, or contact Talent Acquisition at ApplicationAssistance@vrtx.com

role.title: Sr. Manager, Assembly, Integration & Test, Project Sunrise - Orbital Data Centers
role.description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Advanced Concepts and Enterprise Engineering (ACE), supporting Blue Origin’s mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. The team fosters innovation and drives engineering workflows of the future, shared solutions and standards, simplicity and lower costs, and manufacturable design.

**About the Program**
---------------------

Project Sunrise is designing and building orbital data centers — spacecraft that run AI compute workloads on 100% solar power in orbit. This is a first-of-kind program at the intersection of spacecraft engineering and hyperscale GPU infrastructure, housed within Blue Origin. We are building the team from scratch and need people who can operate at the frontier of both domains.

 

**About the Role**
------------------

his is a leadership role with technical depth: you will manage and develop people, and also own integration and test technical content yourself, alongside senior individual contributors who report to you. You have led spacecraft integration and test through qualification and into production, and you want to do it again with a new kind of payload, a tighter schedule, and a team you get to shape from the start. You will work side by side with Manufacturing, Systems Engineering (verification), the technical leads for the spacecraft bus, compute system, software, and operations. You will represent Assembly, Integration & Test in Program leadership forums and reviews.

 

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Build and lead the Assembly, Integration & Test organization: hire and develop integration and test engineers, technicians, and automation and test data specialists, set clear ownership, and scale the team as the program moves from qualification to production

* Own the integration and test schedule and facility resource allocation: sequence qualification and acceptance campaigns, balance competing demands for chambers, shakers, and test benches, and surface schedule risk early

* Own test anomaly resolution: set the process for stopping safely, preserving evidence, finding root cause, and dispositioning nonconformances, and close anomalies with the design and systems teams

* Plan facilities and equipment: define the space, power, cleanroom, environmental test, and ground support equipment needs, and make build, buy, or lease decisions on schedule

* Drive the design the production flow from first-article integration through repeatable acceptance, with defined stations, handoffs, and test gates that Manufacturing and Operations can run

* Drive test automation: set the architecture for electrical ground support and automated test equipment, and deliver more than 80% automated acceptance testing

* Own the test data and digital thread: make sure results are captured, stored, and traceable to requirements, configuration, and hardware serial numbers, and that they flow to engineering, quality, and operations

* Work with Systems Engineering to implement the verification plan: make sure test configurations, procedures, and readiness reviews support requirement closure, and give test feasibility feedback into requirements and design

* Partner with the spacecraft bus, compute system, and software teams so designs can be integrated and tested, building test access, telemetry, and interface needs into the design early

* Manage relationships with suppliers and external test houses: define scope, schedule, and acceptance criteria, and bring the program's integration and test standards to supplier reviews

* Support the production readiness maturity checklist with objective evidence from integration and test

* Set the safety culture on the factory floor and in the test cell, including hazardous operations review and safe handling, and build a team that stops work without hesitation when something looks wrong

 

**Required Qualifications**
---------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related technical field; master's degree preferred

* 12+ years of spacecraft integration and test, or comparably complex hardware test, experience, including ownership of spacecraft-level qualification or acceptance testing

* Prior experience leading and developing engineers and technicians as a manager, lead, or chief test engineer

* Demonstrated experience running a test schedule and test facilities for flight hardware, including environmental test (vibration, thermal vacuum, EMI/EMC) and the resource trade-offs that come with it

* Experience resolving test anomalies and nonconformances on flight hardware through root cause and closure

* Experience with test automation, including electrical ground support equipment and automated test equipment, and with test data management and traceability

* Experience establishing or substantially improving integration and test processes, facilities, or tools in a fast-moving environment

* Ability to make and defend sound technical decisions with incomplete information, and to communicate clearly with engineers, executives, suppliers, and customers

 

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Experience taking a spacecraft from first-article integration to production-rate acceptance testing, including converting manual procedures to automated test

* Experience with high-power or high-heat-flux spacecraft, or with high-density electronics, HPC, or GPU hardware in demanding environments

* Experience planning and commissioning new test facilities or major environmental test equipment

* Experience managing external test houses or test suppliers, including scope, schedule, and quality oversight

* Hands-on experience with digital engineering and manufacturing execution or test data systems, including linking test results to configuration and requirements

* Experience on commercial or rapid-development programs, and judgment in tailoring heritage standards to what a program actually needs

* Experience supporting launch site operations or on-orbit commissioning

 

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

* U.S. citizenship or permanent residency required (ITAR)

* Travel may be required up to 15% of the time but may change based on project needs.

* Relocation assistance available.

 

Base Pay Range for:

VA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15
CO applicants is $157,318.00 - $220,244.85
WA applicants is $171,093.00 - $239,529.15

**Other site ranges may differ**

 

**Culture Statement**

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 

**Export Control Regulations**

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 

**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical 

 

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details. 

 

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws.

 

**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**

Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com . Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

role.title: Sr Manager, Quality Assurance Engineering (Hybrid - Acton, MA)
role.description:
Job Summary

This Senior Manager, Quality Engineering role is a key leadership position responsible for overseeing Insulet’s global Design Transfer Quality Engineering team and ensuring new and modified Omnipod products and manufacturing processes are successfully transferred, validated, and sustained in compliance with FDA and ISO quality standards. The position leads a team of Quality Engineers supporting product launches, manufacturing expansion, process validation, risk management, CAPA, and continuous improvement initiatives across global manufacturing sites. The ideal candidate brings extensive medical device quality experience, deep expertise in design transfer, process validation, and regulatory compliance, along with proven people leadership skills. Success in this role requires partnering across Manufacturing, Operations, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, and Quality organizations to drive quality strategy, support global growth initiatives, and maintain high standards in a complex, high-volume regulated manufacturing environment.



The Senior Manager, Quality Engineering leads Insulet's global Design Transfer Quality Engineering team, ensuring new and changed Omnipod products and manufacturing processes are successfully transferred to production, validated and sustained in compliance with the Insulet Quality System, FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485 and ISO 14971. The Sr. Quality Engineering Manager leads a team of Quality Engineers to support design transfer, capacity expansion, and process controls across Insulet's manufacturing sites. The Senior Manager establishes quality strategy, owns key QMS procedures and metrics, represents Quality throughout major design transfer and global expansion initiatives, and partners closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, R&D, Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders. The ideal candidate is an experienced medical device quality leader who builds strong teams, makes sound risk-based decisions and drives continuous improvement in a highly regulated, high-volume manufacturing environment at a global scale.

 

Responsibilities:

· Lead, coach and develop a team of Quality Engineers; set priorities, manage workload and resourcing, conduct performance reviews and development plans, and lead hiring.

· Serve as Quality lead for the design transfer of new products and product design changes, ensuring quality deliverables (e.g. Project Quality Plans, Design Transfer Plans, Product Launch Plans) are created and properly executed through each phase gate.

· Serve as global process owner for Production & Process Controls and Design Transfer including procedure continuous improvement, performance monitoring of KPIs, and development of new or expanded processes to support Insulet’s growing production capacity.

· Support manufacturing process validation, equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) and Test Method Validation for new manufacturing lines, capacity expansion, site transfers and equipment upgrades; review and approve plans, protocols and reports.

· Drive process risk management across all sites, including pFMEA governance and integration of nonconformance and production data into risk management.

· Lead remediation and compliance initiatives and provide Quality oversight of CAPAs, investigations, quality events and nonconformances, ensuring effective root cause analysis and verification of effectiveness.

· Partner with global manufacturing sites and contract manufacturers to deploy harmonized quality and process improvements.

· Provide Quality leadership for enterprise systems and digital initiatives (e.g. SAP, MES, eDHR, eQMS).

· Prepare and present quality metrics and project status for operations leadership, QMS process owner forums, and management review.

· Support internal and external audits as a subject matter expert, maintain inspection readiness, and serve as the escalation point for cross-functional quality questions from Operations, Engineering and Supply Chain.

Education and Experience:

• BS degree in engineering, a technical or scientific discipline; and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Master's degree in engineering or technical or scientific discipline preferred.

• Minimum 10 years' experience in Medical Device Quality Assurance.

• 3-5 years' experience managing people, including leading engineers and technical staff.

• In-depth knowledge of FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 and ISO 14971.

• Demonstrated experience leading design transfer and process validation for high-volume manufacturing of single-use products, preferably on automated manufacturing equipment.

• Experience with process risk management (pFMEA), CAPA, nonconformance and change control processes; QMS process ownership experience preferred.

• Experience with statistical methods (e.g. statistical process control, sampling plans, Test Method Validation, gauge R&R, and capability).

• Experience working with global manufacturing sites and contract manufacturers.

• Experience with eQMS/PLM, ERP and data visualization tools, as well as word processing, spreadsheet and database programs.

 

Skills/Competencies:

• Proven ability to build, lead and develop high-performing teams, including effective delegation and succession planning.

• Strategic thinking with the ability to organize, judge and balance priorities across multiple complex projects.

• Sound, risk-based decision making in a highly regulated environment.

• Strong verbal (including presentation) and written communication skills, with the ability to influence and present to executive leadership.

• Effective collaboration and communication with individuals at multiple levels and across functions, sites and geographies.

• Strong problem solving / root cause analysis skills.

• Ability to generate and maintain organized and accurate records, and to follow up with task owners to close out open items.

 

Other Expectations:

· Flexibility to work across multiple time zones, outside of normal working hours.

· Travel (International) – 10%

*NOTE: This position is eligible for hybrid working arrangements (requires on-site work from an Insulet office). #LI-Hybrid*

Additional Information:



Compensation & Benefits:

For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $138,700.00 - $208,000.00

This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation.

We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Medical, dental, and vision insurance
• 401(k) with company match
• Paid time off (PTO)
• And additional employee wellness programs

Application Details:
This job posting will remain open until the position is filled.
To apply, please visit the Insulet Careers site and submit your application online.

Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.
 
 
We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!

At Insulet Corporation all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

role.title: Senior Manager, Operations - Quality
role.description:
**About the role:**
===================

This is a hands-on role with both strategic and executional scope. You will build and lead quality assurance and quality control standards across Operations, set the sampling, validation, and escalation practices the organization runs on, and partner closely with the Senior Manager, Operations - Payer Ops, the Human-in-the-Loop Operations leader, Product, and Engineering. You will report to the Head of Operations and help define the company's AI/Human QA strategy as Adonis scales.

**What you'll do:**
===================

**Own the Quality Program across Operations**
---------------------------------------------

* Define and own QA/QC standards, sampling methodologies, audit practices, and validation processes across AI agent outputs, human-executed work, and vendor-delivered operations.
* Develop & present quarterly plans and operating metrics; communicate progress and trade-offs; surface risks early + Work closely with the Head of Operations on strategic projects
* Lead quality assurance for payer workflows and agent outcomes, including new payer activations on the voice channel.
* Lead the development and implementation of a near-real-time QA Dashboard to provide visibility into quality, identify performance gaps, and track improvement over time.
* Partner with the operations team and external vendors to ensure work consistently meets Adonis's accuracy, operational, and compliance standards.
* Partner closely with the operations team to align on quality standards, remediation priorities, and operational performance.
* Collaborate with Product, Engineering, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to address quality gaps, improve workflows, and support strategic initiatives.
* Serve as the quality subject matter expert across Operations, ensuring quality considerations are incorporated into new workflows, product launches, and operational changes.

**Turn quality findings into operational and product improvements**
-------------------------------------------------------------------

* Translate and present quality trends and findings into actionable recommendations for Product, Engineering, and Operations, driving improvements from identification through implementation and validation.
* Leverage AI, automation, and internal tooling to increase the efficiency, accuracy, and scalability of QA/QC processes.
* Establish quality thresholds and escalation criteria for uncertain, complex, or high-impact outcomes.

**Build and lead a high-performing quality function**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Build and scale the Quality function, establishing clear goals, ownership, processes, and performance metrics.
* Lead, coach, and develop onshore and offshore team members, as the function grows.
* Develop and maintain SOPs, playbooks, training materials, and quality guidelines to support operational consistency and continuous improvement.

**Who you are:**
================

* 6+ years of experience
* Experience in healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM) is required, with practical understanding of payer, claims, or related revenue-cycle workflows.
* Experience building or leading quality assurance, quality control, or quality programs in a technology-enabled operations environment.
* Experience coaching a team and creating clarity across multiple workstreams.
* Experience defining operating standards, evaluating results, investigating failures, and ensuring corrective actions are effective.
* Strong cross-functional communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Product, Engineering, customer-facing teams, and operational partners.
* Comfort moving between strategic planning and hands-on operational detail in a fast-changing environment.
* An AI-forward mindset and practical experience applying AI, automation, or intelligent tooling to improve quality and operational performance, with sound judgment about when human review is needed.

The base salary range for this position is $140,000 to $180,000. Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. In addition to base salary, we also offer competitive equity and benefits packages.

**About Adonis**
================

Adonis is the leading AI orchestration platform for healthcare revenue cycle management (RCM), purpose-built for healthcare organizations seeking to transform their revenue operations. Traditional RCM processes often struggle with inefficiencies, costing providers up to 15% or more of their potential revenue. Through advanced automation, data science, and AI Agents, Adonis helps revenue teams detect vulnerabilities, optimize workflows, and deploy precise solutions that drive reliable and scalable financial outcomes.

Adonis is headquartered in New York City and has raised over $95M in funding, including a recent $40M Series C round led by Quadrille Capital with continued support from existing investors such as General Catalyst and Bling Capital. This funding supports our mission to restore sanity to RCM and equip provider groups and health systems with AI-driven revenue cycle operations at scale.

**Compensation Philosophy**
===========================

Actual base pay will depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Adonis determines compensation based on each candidate’s experience and qualifications relative to peers, and most new hires fall near the middle of the range. In addition to base salary, you’ll receive meaningful equity and great benefits.

**Perks at Adonis**
===================

* Competitive equity packages
* Employer-paid medical insurance
* Employer-paid dental insurance
* Employer-paid vision insurance
* Employer-funded HSA
* Parental leave
* Commuter benefits
* Office lunches every day
* Office snacks
* Generous PTO
* Located in 3 World Trade Center with easy access to all trains and the PATH, and amazing views of the city

Adonis is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive culture that celebrates authenticity to win as one. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, citizenship or immigration status, or any other legally protected characteristics.

At Adonis, we fully comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). We are dedicated to embracing challenges and creating an accessible, inclusive workplace for all individuals.

Compensation Range: $140K - $180K

role.title: Sr. Director, Infrastructure and Operations
role.description:
**J****ob Title:** Sr. Director, Infrastructure and Operations

**Group:** Information Technology

**Location:** Hybrid

**Reports To**: Chief Information Officer

ASME is seeking a **Sr. Director, Infrastructure and Operations** to join our IT group. The Sr. Director will lead the strategy, architecture, engineering, and operations of ASME's infrastructure, telecommunications, networks, help desk, and related security capabilities.

This role will ensure secure, reliable, scalable, and cost-effective technology services while advancing DevOps practices, business continuity, disaster recovery, and responsible implementation of artificial intelligence across ASME's technology stack.

The position partners closely with Architecture and Applications, Security, the Project Management Office, and business leaders to support current operations and future enterprise needs.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the strategy, architecture, engineering, and day-to-day operations of ASME infrastructure, cloud, network, telecommunications, endpoint, help desk, and production platforms.
* Lead major infrastructure initiatives, establish policies and standards, strengthen cross-functional and vendor partnerships, and coach and develop a high-performing, customer-focused Technology team.
* Design and implement secure, compliant, reliable, scalable, and cost-effective infrastructure systems that integrate effectively with current applications and meet enterprise requirements.
* Determine current and future infrastructure needs, develop capital and expense budgets, and oversee vendors, service-level agreements, and key performance indicators.
* Build and continuously improve DevOps practices, methodologies, and tools that support continuous integration and continuous delivery.
* Direct business continuity, disaster recovery, institutional risk management, infrastructure documentation, and compliance with applicable security and data requirements, including PCI-DSS.
* Identify and implement emerging AI capabilities for Infrastructure and Operations, including AIOps, AI-enabled platform engineering, AI agents, and automation platforms, with appropriate governance, monitoring, security, lifecycle management, and risk controls.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in information technology or a related field, or equivalent additional experience; master's degree is a plus.
* Minimum of 8 years of relevant technical and leadership experience in infrastructure and operations.
* Extensive experience designing, implementing, and managing infrastructure, cloud, network, telecommunications, endpoint, virtualization, storage, recovery, and support environments, including Microsoft Azure.
* Experience with endpoint management and asset lifecycle solutions such as Microsoft Intune, PDQ, or Jamf, and with secure network architecture and protocols such as SASE; Cato experience is highly preferred.
* Demonstrated leadership experience in security, crisis management, business continuity, disaster recovery, risk management, and technology compliance.
* Experience applying project management frameworks to large-scale technology initiatives and communicating complex technical topics clearly to senior and executive leaders.
* Experience with emerging AI technologies, including Microsoft Copilot and private large language models, and the ability to build strong internal and external relationships.
* Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing technical teams.
* Demonstrated ability to establish clear standards, strengthen accountability, and build a customer-focused culture of operational excellence.
* Demonstrated success leading organizational change and operational improvement initiatives.

**Work Arrangement**

This role is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement and will be based in either our New York or New Jersey office locations, subject to ASME's hybrid-work policies and business requirements. Periodic business travel will be required, including but not limited to ASME Offices which are currently located in NYC, NJ, DC, TX.

**Compensation and Benefits**

The New York Metro annual base salary range for this position is $210,000–$225,000 per year. The actual compensation offered will be determined based on factors including qualifications, experience, skills, geographic location, and internal equity.

This position will also be eligible to participate in ASME's annual incentive bonus program, subject to the applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements.

Additionally, ASME offers eligible employees a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage; health savings and flexible spending account options; life and disability insurance; a 401(k) retirement plan; paid vacation and safe and sick leave; paid holidays; parental leave; employee assistance and wellness programs; and professional-development opportunities. Eligibility and benefit levels vary based on employment status and the terms of the applicable plans. For additional information, please visit ASME's Benefits page.

**About ASME**

ASME helps the global engineering community develop solutions to real-world challenges. Founded in 1880 as The American Society of Mechanical Engineers, ASME is a nonprofit professional organization that enables collaboration, knowledge sharing, and skill development across all engineering disciplines, while promoting the vital role of the engineer in society. ASME codes and standards, publications, conferences, continuing education, and professional development programs provide a foundation for advancing technical knowledge and a safer world. From college students and early-career engineers to project managers, corporate executives, researchers, and academic leaders, ASME's members are as diverse as the engineering community itself.

ASME is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. At ASME, we nurture an inclusive environment, and we encourage, support, and celebrate diversity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, gender identity & expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, citizenship status, disability, or protected veteran, military status, or any other basis protected by law.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity policy pertains to every aspect of an individual’s relationship with the organization, including but not limited to recruitment, hiring, compensation, benefits, training and development, promotion, programs, and all other terms and conditions of employment.

Only those candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted.

role.title: Director, FP&A - Enterprise Operations
role.description:
Company Overview:

**Why Choose Us?**
------------------

Novolex is a leading manufacturer of food, beverage, and specialty packaging that supports multiple industries including foodservice, restaurant delivery and carryout, food processing, grocery and retail, and industrial sectors. Novolex manufacturing and sourcing expertise spans a diverse range of substrates including resin, paper, molded fiber, aluminum and more. We provide customers a broad array of stock and customized solutions with 120 product categories, 250 brands and over 39,000 SKUs.

**Our Sustainability Commitment**
---------------------------------

The Novolex sustainability vision is built upon three pillars: our products, our operations and our people. Each is critically important to our growth and future as a business. These pillars form the foundation of our company-wide commitment to sustainability, helping us achieve our ambitious goals through our wide-ranging initiatives.

Job Description:

The Director of Financial Planning & Analysis is a key leadership role responsible for financial planning, forecasting, reporting and analysis used to identify risks and opportunities across the business. The successful candidate will build strategic partnerships across business units and functional teams that will lead to improved processes and transparency around key operating metrics. This is a key member of the Enterprise Operations function, who will support senior leaders, including COO and Operations staff, to drive organizational transformation and ensure company financial objectives are met

**How You’ll Perform the Role**

 

* Oversee and coordinate monthly finance processes, resulting in added visibility and a clear understanding of business trends and overall financial outlook
* Oversee and directly guide annual Enterprise Operations budgeting process
* Responsible for management reporting, ensuring desired level of accuracy and timeliness is met
* Lead Capital Expenditure process, driving strong financial governance, and ensure effectiveness of capital deployment in generating favorable business outcomes
* Develop and implement tools and/or processes to establish forecasting, budgeting, reporting within function.
* Identify appropriate KPIs and reporting across the different levels of the organization to measure productivity, capital expenditure, and other operational metrics
* Conduct ad-hoc analyses with the ability to clearly summarize and present findings to executive leadership team members
* Partner across Operations, Engineering, Accounting and all necessary functions to drive business results and assure connectivity
* Connect with BU CFOs, Operations VPs, and Operations Finance to assure efficiencies and align processes

**What We Need From You**

 

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or related Business field
* 10+ years of experience
* Experience leading teams both directly, indirectly, and leading projects cross-functionally

* Excellent business partnership skills with a record of collaborating across functions and levels within an organization to accomplish team goals
* Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
* Strategic thinking, ability to simplify the complex, make/drive decisions, and adapt to changing environment

* Proven analytical and financial skills, demonstrated strong economic thinking
* Clearly understand integrated financial systems and the Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Access, Word, PowerPoint)
* Travel approximately 10% or less

#LI-Hybrid

Company Benefits:

**What You'll Get From Us**
---------------------------

### **Benefits**

With safety as our top priority and a commitment to employee well-being an important focus, we offer comprehensive and competitive benefits that include medical, dental and vision insurance as well as a variety of other well-being resources focused on mental, physical and financial health. Specific benefits and well-being programs may vary depending on where you work.

### **Community Engagement**

At Novolex, giving back to the local communities that support us is important. Our Focused Giving Program prioritizes support for organizations whose missions promote sustainability initiatives or address food and hunger needs. We also encourage facility level support of activities in the communities where our employees live and work.

### **Training and Development**

We offer constant opportunities for advancement. From skills development to advanced education programs, training and development programs and courses are available through MyLearning. Programs include company and industry training curricula, support for formal education through the Tuition Reimbursement Program (Non-Union), and a Learning Management System that supports and enhances employee skills at all levels of the organization.

Novolex is committed to providing equal employment opportunity in all employment practices, including but not limited to selection, hiring, promotion, transfer, and compensation to all qualified applicants and employees without regard to age, race, color, national origin, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, handicap or disability, genetics, citizenship status, service member or veteran status, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law. Any individual who, because of his or her disability, needs an accommodation in connection with an aspect of the Company's application process should contact myHRservices@novolex.com.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
Description:

**Job Title:** Director of Campus Operations

**Department:** Facilities

**Reports To:** Executive Director of Administration

**Direct Reports:** Assistant Director of Campus Operations

**FLSA Status:** Exempt

**Prepared By:** Human Resources

**Prepared Date:** November 11, 2026

**OUR MISSION**

The mission of Eastern Star Church is to form followers of Jesus to love God, love people, and live to serve. Guided by our vision of Growing People to Love Like Jesus, we are committed to creating environments that support worship, discipleship, community engagement, and service.

**YOUR ROLE IN OUR MISSION**

Under the direction of the Executive Director of Administration, the **Director of Campus Operations** provides strategic leadership, oversight, and accountability for campus operations and facilities across Eastern Star Church and its affiliated organizations, including JEWEL Human Services.

This role is responsible for establishing operational standards, ensuring effective stewardship of facilities and resources, and leading the development and performance of the operations team. Through direct supervision of the Assistant Director of Operations and other assigned leaders, the Director ensures that campus operations are safe, efficient, consistent, and aligned with organizational priorities.

The Director serves as a key partner in advancing the ministry’s mission and strategic plan by ensuring that our facilities and physical environments support worship, discipleship, community outreach, and an exceptional experience for all who enter. The position emphasizes strategic planning, leadership development, financial accountability, and continuous improvement while delegating day-to-day operational execution to the Assistant Director of Operations.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for campus operations and facilities across Eastern Star Church and its affiliated properties, under the direction of the Executive Director of Administration.
* Establish operational standards and performance expectations to ensure all facilities are safe, functional, well-maintained, and reflective of a culture of excellence and stewardship, holding the Assistant Director of Operations accountable for daily implementation.
* Develop and recommend long-term facilities strategies, including capital improvements, renovations, and expansion planning, in alignment with organizational priorities and the direction of the Executive Director of Administration.
* Provide leadership and oversight for facilities-related capital projects, ensuring appropriate planning, budgeting, resource allocation, and accountability for successful completion within approved timelines and budgets.
* Lead, coach, and develop the Assistant Director of Operations and other assigned direct reports, establishing clear expectations, delegated responsibilities, performance measures, and opportunities for professional growth.
* Establish and maintain consistent operational policies, facility standards, and accountability measures across all campuses and affiliated properties, ensuring effective implementation through the Assistant Director of Operations.
* Partner with executive leadership, Campus Pastors, ministry leaders, and production and creative teams to align campus operations, facility resources, and operational priorities with worship services, programs, events, and organizational needs.
* Provide strategic oversight of vendor relationships, contracts, and service providers, ensuring quality, compliance, cost-effectiveness, and accountability, while delegating routine vendor coordination and service management to the Assistant Director of Operations.
* Develop, manage, and monitor facilities and operations budgets in partnership with Finance and the Executive Director of Administration, ensuring responsible stewardship of resources, financial accountability, and timely identification of budget variances.
* Establish and oversee safety, security, emergency preparedness, and risk management standards, ensuring regulatory compliance and holding operational leadership accountable for implementing and maintaining required procedures.
* Lead the development and continuous improvement of operational systems, processes, technology, and workflows that strengthen efficiency, consistency, communication, and accountability across all campus operations.
* Establish campus experience and operational readiness standards to ensure facilities consistently provide safe, welcoming, functional, and well-prepared environments that support ministry effectiveness and reflect the mission of Eastern Star Church.
* Establish and monitor departmental performance goals and key performance indicators, evaluating operational effectiveness, preventive maintenance performance, campus readiness, service delivery, and resource utilization.
* Provide regular operational reports to the Executive Director of Administration, including departmental performance, budget status, capital project progress, operational risks, and recommendations for continuous improvement.
* Collaborate with the Executive Director of Administration to establish departmental priorities, evaluate organizational needs, recommend resource allocations, and support the implementation of organizational strategic initiatives.
* Carry out all responsibilities with excellence, integrity, trust, professionalism, and the utmost confidentiality.

Perform other duties as assigned

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Demonstrated alignment with the mission, vision, and values of the ministry.
* Proven ability to lead large-scale operations and facilities across multiple sites.
* Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence across departments.
* Active member of Eastern Star Church within three months of starting in the role
* Attend at least one weekly Sunday service.
* Active in a Ministry within three months of starting in the role.
* Complete FFI 101 series or is currently enrolled in class.
* Consistent giver as an opportunity to show God Owns It All by giving back to Him the first of what He gives to us.
* Please refer to the Eastern Star Church Discipleship Policy for additional details.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of leadership experience in operations, facilities, or multi-site management
* Experience leading large-scale projects, capital improvements, renovations, multi-site operations and vendor relationships.
* Strong financial and budget management experience.
* A combination of relevant experience and demonstrated leadership may be considered in place of formal education requirements.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS**

* Relevant facilities, operations, or project management certifications (preferred but not required).

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* This role requires regular travel between multiple campus and organizational locations.
* Must be available to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays as required for church services, events, emergencies, and operational needs.
* Work is performed in a combination of office, campus, event, and facilities environments.
* Must be able to stand, walk, climb stairs, inspect facilities, and move throughout campus locations for extended periods of time.
* Must be able to effectively communicate in meetings, public settings, and operational environments.
* Must be able to occasionally lift and transport materials or equipment up to 25 pounds.
* Requires the ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively in fast-paced and high-demand environments

role.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53235
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring an Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence for our highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and discipline. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Associate Director/Director of Operational Excellence runs our site MDI (managing for daily improvements) OpEx, continuous improvement programs, and all site PMO operations owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio while coordinating cross-functional projects. They build the operating rhythm that turns discrete functions into one aligned site team as the site scales to six suites, and owns the site’s strategy, execution, and culture discipline planning. Lead executive-level investigations and special initiatives as project/program lead, absorbing crisis response so operational leaders can stay focused on daily management.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Run site MDI including ownership of the Tier 6 site critical issue forum, ensuring cross-functional blockers are surfaced and resolved quickly

* Establish and sustain the site's cadence of daily, weekly, and monthly forums so issues are raised and resolved at the right level

* Lead OpEx and continuous improvement programs, building and prioritizing a CI project pipeline and delivering realized savings

* Lead all site PMO activities, owning the site project register and deciding how work is staffed and prioritized across the project portfolio, coordinating cross-functional projects and site initiatives and driving on-time delivery

* Own site strategy, execution, and rigor planning for culture translating strategic priorities into a disciplined, trackable execution plan across the site

* Own MDI and all standard work initiatives site-wide, ensuring consistent methodology and application across every function and suite

* Own site-wide implementation of lean principles building and driving the phased adoption roadmap across leadership, suites, and functions, from initial leadership alignment through daily floor-level practice

* Own site business analytics building and maintaining the reporting, dashboards, and KPI infrastructure that drive MDI, CI prioritization, and Site Leadership Team decision-making

* Co-lead the monthly finance/business review with finance operations, reconciling cost and capital needs against the site's financial plan

* Coach leaders and teams in Lean and problem-solving methods and build an OpEx culture across the site

* Embed MDI and OpEx practices as suites come online so new suites start up with the site's operating standards

* Partner with manufacturing, quality, technical services, technical operations, supply chain, and Finance as a member of the site leadership team

* Embed the digital and connected plant model in site MDI, using real-time data and digital tools for daily management and escalation

* Own the site's multi-year operational efficiency roadmap, driving leaner operations and delivering year-over-year efficiency gains

* Build, coach, and retain a high-performing OpEx team; establish high standards for performance management and accountability; perform other duties as required

* Own a gross margin improvement program and goal for this function, contributing to the site's overall margin performance

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

* Own these function's OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary party responsible for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function
 

 

**This role requires:**

* B.S in engineering, life sciences, business or related technical field
* MBA & PMP certification preferred

* + Associate Director: 10+ years of operational excellence, continuous improvement, or manufacturing operations or biopharmaceuticals including 5+ years of progressive leadership

* + Director: 12+ years in operational excellence, continuous improvement, or manufacturing operations or biopharmaceuticals including 7+ years of progressive leadership

* + Level will be determined based on experience

* Previous people leadership/supervisory experience

Does this sound like you? Apply now to take your first step towards living the Regeneron Way! We are committed to building a workplace with an inclusive culture. Regeneron is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion or belief (or lack thereof), sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, civil status, pregnancy or parental status, age, disability, nationality, citizenship status, ethnic or national origin, membership of the Traveler community, familial status, genetic information, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. Where required, we will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with known disabilities or chronic illnesses during the recruitment process, unless such accommodation would impose undue hardship.

Where necessary, we disclose salary ranges for roles in all countries in which we operate. The final offer will be determined within the relevant range based on the country of employment, specific role level, and your skills and experience. In some countries, collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) may apply and influence certain elements of pay or benefits. Regeneron offers a competitive and comprehensive total rewards package which may include, depending on country and role: annual bonuses or other incentive plans, equity awards, pension or retirement benefits, 401(k) company match, health and wellness programs, fitness centers, insurance benefits (e.g. medical, dental, vision, life and disability), paid time off, and family support benefits. For additional information about Regeneron benefits in the U.S., please visit https://careers.regeneron.com/en/working-at-regeneron/total-rewards/. For other locations, additional information will be provided during the recruitment process. If you have any questions, please speak with your recruiter.

 
 

Please be advised that at Regeneron, we believe we do our best work when we are together. For that reason, many roles are required to be performed on‑site. Please speak with your recruiter and hiring manager for more information about on‑site expectations for your role and location.

 
 

As part of the recruitment process, certain background checks may be conducted in accordance with the laws of the country where the position is based. The purpose of such checks is to verify certain information prior to the commencement of employment such as identity, right to work and educational qualifications.

 
 

For jobs in Canada: this posting is for an existing position.

role.title: Director of Warehouse Operations
role.description:
**Director of Warehouse Operations**

**Your Leadership. Our Foundation.**

At **Cash Depot**, you’re not just joining a company, you’re becoming part of a family.

As a nationwide leader in ATM management and financial transaction processing, we’ve built our reputation on innovation, exceptional customer service, and strong partnerships. As we continue expanding our footprint and evolving our solutions, we’re seeking a strategic, hands-on operations leader to oversee the teams that keep our ATM equipment and components ready to support our customers.

When you join Cash Depot, you’re stepping into an organization where your ideas matter, your leadership is valued, and your impact is visible across the business. This is an opportunity to lead four teams, improve how our operations run, and build a high-performing warehouse organization focused on efficiency, quality, and long-term success.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive compensation package
* **Profit Sharing Bonus Program**
* **Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision benefits**
* **Company-paid Life Insurance**
* **Company-paid Short-Term Disability (STD)**
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off and holidays
* Monday through Friday daytime schedule
* Leadership visibility with a direct reporting line to the COO
* Opportunity to shape how our operations grow and improve
* Stable, growing organization with nationwide operations

**Position Summary**

The **Director of Warehouse Operations** provides strategic leadership, direction, and oversight for Cash Depot’s Inventory and Warehousing, ATM Parts Repair, ATM Set-Up and Refurbishment, and Purchasing departments.

Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director is accountable for operational efficiency, inventory accuracy, cost management, quality control, productivity, and the timely availability of ATM equipment and components to support company operations and customer commitments.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Leadership & Cost Management**

* Manage departmental budgets and identify opportunities to reduce operating costs.
* Improve productivity and eliminate inefficiencies across warehouse, repair, refurbishment, and purchasing functions.
* Analyze operational data to identify bottlenecks and opportunities for improvement.
* Increase throughput, quality, and profitability across all areas of responsibility.

**Inventory, Repair & Equipment Readiness**

* Improve inventory accuracy, availability, and inventory turns.
* Improve repair turnaround times and reduce replacement costs.
* Ensure ATM equipment is set up, refurbished, and deployment-ready on schedule.
* Maintain quality standards that support company operations and customer commitments.

**Purchasing & Vendor Management**

* Improve vendor pricing, procurement efficiency, and cost controls.
* Ensure timely availability of ATM equipment, parts, and components.
* Build productive vendor relationships that support quality and reliability.

**Team Development & Accountability**

* Lead, develop, and hold accountable four department leaders: the Warehouse Manager, Purchasing Manager, Parts Repair Lead, and Setup/Refurb Lead.
* Set clear performance standards and expectations across all four departments.
* Build and foster high-performing teams aligned with Cash Depot’s culture and values.
* Operate within corporate policy guidelines and business practices.

**Requirements**

* 3–5 years of operations management experience preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze data and identify operational bottlenecks or opportunities.
* Deep understanding of service delivery principles and customer satisfaction.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite or other relevant systems.

**Skills & Qualifications**

* Strong ability to lead and inspire teams.
* Excellent communication skills to collaborate with teams, customers, and leadership.
* Results-oriented with a demonstrated sense of urgency.
* Strong problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.
* Ability to adapt to change in the workplace or in assigned duties.
* Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

**Why Cash Depot?**

This is an opportunity to join a growing national organization in a highly visible leadership role. As Director of Warehouse Operations, you’ll lead the teams that keep Cash Depot’s ATM equipment moving, shape how our operations run, and directly influence the service we deliver to customers across the country.

**Join Cash Depot and lead the operations that power our next chapter of growth.**
