role.title: Regional Director of Operations
role.description:
Advance your career as a Regional Director of Operations (CDM - Certified Dietary Manager) in Illinois, supporting environmental services and food service operations within our healthcare facilities. If you're passionate about mentoring teams and driving excellence across multiple locations, we invite you to apply today.

**As a Regional Director of Operations - Dietary and Environmental Services, you will...** Oversee all assigned facilities, ensuring leadership and guidance in operations, finances, human resources and client relationships, while providing direct supervision to the facility Food Service Directors and Environmental Services Directors. **Must live in the state of Illinois and have previous Healthcare Dietary experience.**

***Key Responsibilities:***

* Actively support and apply all company and facility policies and procedures to ensure the highest quality of service is being provided to our customers at the lowest possible cost.
* Work with Corporate and/or onsite dietitians to ensure that all federal and state requirements are being achieved.
* Cultivate and maintain business partnerships with clients by developing a broad knowledge and understanding of clients’ and their customers’ needs and expectations, including:
* Establish and maintain internal Quality Assurance and Assessment processes in each assigned facility, including inspections, annual client satisfaction surveys, keep the company and its facilities on the cutting edge of our industry.
* Actively participate in food service-related committees within assigned facilities (if applicable), or otherwise be involved in and visible at special events within each assigned facility, to demonstrate the company’s team approach and commitment to the clients
* Plan and develop each unit’s operational budgets and demonstrate an understanding of the company’s financial objectives for each unit. Financial responsibilities include:
* Review financial results weekly and monthly and make necessary adjustments to improve operational performance.
* Develop a weekly financial plan to include sales, menu and production records, food purchases, inventory, and labor productivity to assist each unit in achieving its budget targets.
* Educate Food Service Directors and Environmental Service Directors for each facility in P&L process (where applicable) and review month-end results for each facility.
* Ensure all established accounting practices and timelines are consistently adhered to.
* Provides assistance as needed, with new business bids, rebids for current clients/customers, and the development of new programs, including:
* Renegotiate contract terms and/or fee/pricing increases with client, when necessary.
* Manage transition of new business accounts.
* Conduct audits and evaluate each facility’s performance in the areas of food production, menu and recipe standards, sanitation, uniforms, purchasing, inventories, safety, payroll, human resources compliance and record keeping.
* Demonstrate working knowledge of operational, accounting and human resources policies and procedures (i.e. new hire process, payroll, etc.).
* Ensure all human resources and safety practices and policies are intact and adhered to.
* Hold facility Directors and employees accountable for behavior and performance, following Corrective Action guidelines when necessary.
* Conduct training and development needs assessment of Food Service Directors and arrange necessary training, including the areas of food and cost productions, customer services, team building, time management, human resources skills, etc.
* Communicate with and assist in developing goals and objectives for each Food Service Director. Meet with Directors on an individual basis to assess goals and areas of opportunity.
* Support Directors in conducting training and development needs assessment of employees and assist in arranging appropriate training sessions/tools.
* Ensure companies systems are followed and in compliance daily

**Regional Food Service Director Minimum Requirements:**

* High School diploma (required)
* Certified Dietary Manager (required)
* Multi-site Dietary Operations experience (required)
* Ability to travel within your region frequently (required)
* Minimum 2-5 years’ experience coordinating food service operations
* Bachelor’s degree in culinary arts or related field (preferred, but not required)
* Demonstrated ability to lead and guide teams.
* Strong initiative.
* Strong ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
* Ability to maintain confidentiality of records and information.
* Skill in the use of operating basic office equipment.

**Why Join Our Team?**

Whether you’re looking for a **challenge or opportunity for growth as a Certified Dietary Manager** this provides the chance to build your leadership skills in the Healthcare Dietary sector in Environmental Services and Dietary operations, while doing work that truly matters!

role.title: Director of Quality & Training
role.description:
**Additional Information** 
**Job Number**26150788 
**Job Category**Procurement, Purchasing, and Quality Assurance 
**Location**500 Channelside Drive, TAMPA FL 33602, United States 
**Schedule**Full Time 
**Located Remotely?**N 
**Position Type** Management 
**Pay Range:** $75,000-$93,000 annually 
**Bonus Eligible:** Y

**JOB SUMMARY**

Responsible for communicating the concept of Total Quality Management through advising, coaching, training, and facilitating. Position works with direct reports, General Managers, and other staff to develop and implement quality assurance strategies. The position is responsible for ensuring that quality processes meet company’s mission and brand standards, target customer needs, ensure employee satisfaction, and focus on continuous improvement at the property level. .

**CANDIDATE PROFILE**

**Education and Experience**

* 2-year degree from an accredited university in Business Administration, Hotel and Restaurant Management, or related major; 4 years experience in the guest services, front desk, housekeeping, sales and marketing, management operations, or related professional area.

OR

* 4-year bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Hotel and Restaurant Management, or related major; 2 years experience in the guest services, front desk, housekeeping, sales and marketing, management operations, or related professional area.

**CORE WORK ACTIVITIES**

**Managing Quality Assurance Goals**

* Coaches managers on adopting the Total Quality Management leadership style.

* Makes and executes the necessary decisions to keep property moving forward toward achievement of goals.

* Directs property quality efforts to address critical customer requirements.

* Facilitates process improvement teams, assuring use of the systematic processes, and improvement is achievable and measurable.

**Leading Quality Assurance Team**

* Trains team members and managers on problem solving, process improvement and strategic planning techniques

* Develops systems to enable employees to understand guest satisfaction results.

* Communicates a clear and consistent message regarding departmental goals to produce desired results.

* Coaches managers on adopting the Total Quality Management leadership style.

* Educates new employees on the foundations of the quality processes, how to use quality tools and their role in continuous improvement.

* Familiarizes employees with the daily quality production reports and how to spot trends in their work areas and initiate root cause analysis.

**Managing Quality Tools**

* Ensures that management practices at all levels are aligned with quality tools.

* Uses data collection methods to compile, display, track, and analyze defect trends.

* Demonstrates and communicates key drivers of guest satisfaction for the brand’s target customer.

* Analyzes issues and identifies trends.

**Managing the Guest Experience**

* Reviews guest feedback with leadership team and ensures appropriate corrective action is taken.

* Responds to and handles guest problems and complaints.

* Stays visible and interfaces with customers on a regular basis to obtain feedback on quality of product, service levels and overall satisfaction.

* Creates an atmosphere in all properties that meets or exceeds guest expectations.

**Managing and Conducting Human Resources Activities**

* Facilitates the development of creative solutions to overcome obstacles and ensures implementation to continually improve guest satisfaction results.

* Ensures employees are treated fairly and equitably.

* Ensures that regular, ongoing communication is happening in quality assurance.

* Fosters employee commitment to providing excellent service, participates in daily stand-up meetings and models desired service behaviors in all interactions with guests and employees.

* Incorporates guest satisfaction as a component of staff/operations meetings with an emphasis on generating innovative ways to continually improve results.

* Sets goals and expectations for direct reports using the performance review process and holds staff accountable for successful performance.

* Solicits employee feedback, utilizes an “open door policy” and reviews employee satisfaction results to identify and address employee problems or concerns.

* Ensures property policies are administered fairly and consistently, disciplinary procedures and documentation are completed according to Standard and Local Operating Procedures (SOPs and LSOPs) and supports the Peer Review Process.

* Conducts annual performance appraisal with direct reports according to Standard Operating Procedures.

* Champions change, ensures brand and regional business initiatives are implemented and communicates follow-up actions to team as necessary.

*At Marriott International, we are dedicated to being an equal opportunity employer, welcoming all and providing access to opportunity. We actively foster an environment where the unique backgrounds of our associates are valued and celebrated. Our greatest strength lies in the rich blend of culture, talent, and experiences of our associates. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis, including disability, veteran status, or other basis protected by applicable law.*

role.title: Director, Global Supply Chain Center of Excellence – Chemical Manufacturing
role.description:
**The Opportunity:**
--------------------

**Position purpose**

 
 

Lead the global Supply Chain Center of Excellence across three pillars: Planning Excellence & Governance; Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement; and Data, Systems & Digital Enablement.

 
 

Strengthen supply chain performance by establishing consistent planning practices, delivering actionable analysis and measurable improvements, and enabling reliable data and effective planning technology. Partner with regional supply chain leaders to build capabilities and sustain improvements while regional teams retain operational supply and inventory accountability.

 
 

**How you will thrive and create an impact**

 

**Planning Excellence & Governance**

* Establish global planning standards, business rules, decision rights, and exception thresholds.
* Define planning horizons, freeze rules, and handoffs between master supply planning, site scheduling, materials planning, and regional supply planning.
* Own S&OE/S&OP process design, calendars, review standards, and escalation methods.
* Establish Plan for Every Part (PFEP) standards and review methods for finished goods, raw materials, and packaging.
* Assess planning-process adoption and effectiveness, identify gaps, and lead improvements with regional owners.
* Build planner capabilities through training, coaching, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.

**Analytics, Optimization & Value Improvement**

* Establish common KPIs, dashboards, and performance-analysis methods across regions.
* Lead capacity scenarios and inventory modeling to support supply, working-capital, and investment decisions.
* Develop inventory policies, safety-stock methods, and replenishment recommendations with regional teams.
* Partner with Manufacturing and regional planning teams to improve capacity utilization, campaign planning, and planning parameters.
* Identify and quantify value leakage, including excess inventory, expiry, write-offs, premium freight, and avoidable expediting.
* Develop prioritized improvement initiatives with clear business cases, accountable execution owners, and milestones.
* Track corrective actions and validate realized benefits with Finance, distinguishing recurring savings, cash release, and cost avoidance.

**Data, Systems & Digital Enablement**

* Establish master-data standards, business ownership, validation controls, and data-quality remediation processes.
* Prioritize SAP planning gaps and configuration issues and lead business resolution with IT.
* Lead the business workstream for planning system implementation and SAP integration, including requirements, data readiness, testing, and deployment readiness.
* Advance reporting and workflow automation to improve planning productivity and exception management.
* Develop AI-enabled reporting, exception insights, and commentary with appropriate validation and accountable business review.
* Lead planner training, system adoption, and post-implementation improvement.
* Maintain a technology roadmap aligned with planning needs and measurable business outcomes.

**Leadership and cross-functional alignment**

* Set a balanced CoE roadmap across the three pillars, prioritizing resources against business needs.
* Lead and develop the CoE team with clear responsibilities and performance expectations.
* Partner with regional supply chain leaders, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Quality, Finance, and IT to implement improvements.
* Communicate progress, risks, benefits, and decisions required to supply chain leadership.
 

 

**Measures of success**

 
 

**Planning excellence**

* Adoption and effectiveness of planning standards, PFEP reviews, and S&OE/S&OP processes.
* Improved planning discipline, handoffs, and planner capability.

**Analytics and improvement**

* Quality and use of analysis in business decisions.
* Inventory and capacity improvements delivered with regional teams.
* Reduction in value leakage and Finance-validated benefits.

**Data and digital enablement**

* Planning-data accuracy and closure of critical data issues.
* Delivery and adoption of SAP, Netstock, and automation improvements.
* Measurable improvements in planning productivity and decision support.
 

 

**What we're looking for**

 
 

**Required**

* Typically 10 or more years of progressive supply chain experience, including team leadership and cross-functional improvement.
* Strong knowledge of master planning, capacity planning, inventory management, PFEP, and S&OE/S&OP.
* Demonstrated experience establishing planning governance and delivering measurable operational improvements.
* Proven leadership of teams and large, complex transformation programs across multiple sites or regions.
* Strong track record leading planning-system implementations, organizational change, training, and sustained adoption.
* Deep SAP planning expertise, including master-data governance and configuration, sufficient to guide business design and challenge technical solutions.
* Strong analytical judgment, with experience directing BI reporting, dashboards, and optimization initiatives to improve business performance.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, establish planning governance, and deliver measurable operational and financial results.

 

**Preferred**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or equivalent relevant experience.
* Chemicals or batch/process manufacturing experience.
* Experience leading a global-scale CoE or planning transformation.
* SAP and Netstock or comparable planning-platform experience.
* ASCM/APICS certification, Lean Six Sigma qualification, or an advanced degree.

 

**Disclaimer:**

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required of employees assigned to this position. Avantor is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

**Why Avantor?**

**Dare to go further in your career.** Join our global team of 14,000+ associates whose passion for discovery and determination to overcome challenges relentlessly advances life-changing science.
 
 
**The work we do changes people's lives for the better.** It brings new patient treatments and therapies to market, giving a cancer survivor the chance to walk his daughter down the aisle. It enables medical devices that help a little boy hear his mom's voice for the first time. Outcomes such as these create unlimited opportunities for you to contribute your talents, learn new skills and grow your career at Avantor.
 
 
We are committed to helping you on this journey through our diverse, equitable and inclusive culture which includes learning experiences to support your career growth and success. At Avantor, dare to go further and see how the impact of your contributions set science in motion to create a better world. **Apply today!**

**Pay Transparency:**

The expected pre-tax pay for this position is

$139,500.00 - $235,175.00

Actual pay may differ depending on relevant factors such as prior experience and geographic location.

**EEO Statement:**

We are an Equal Employment/Affirmative Action employer and VEVRAA Federal Contractor. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state/province, or local law.

Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

For more information about equal employment opportunity protections, please view the Know Your Rights poster.

**Privacy Policy:**

We will use the personal information that you have submitted to us in order to consider your application for the relevant role.

Your privacy is important to us. Please click here for our Privacy Policy which explains the purposes for which we will use your personal information and the ways in which we will handle and retain your information. It also explains the rights you have in relation to your information, and how to contact us with any queries or requests.

**3rd Party Non-Solicitation Policy:**

By submitting candidates without having been formally assigned on and contracted for a specific job requisition by Avantor, or by failing to comply with the Avantor recruitment process, you forfeit any fee on the submitted candidates, regardless of your usual terms and conditions. Avantor works with a preferred supplier list and will take the initiative to engage with recruitment agencies based on its needs and will not be accepting any form of solicitation.

Avantor offers a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, and vision coverage, wellness programs, health savings and flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with company match, and an employee stock purchase program. Employees also receive 11 paid holidays, accrue 18 PTO days annually, are eligible for volunteer time off and 6 weeks of 100% paid parental leave (except in states that offer paid family leave). These benefits may not apply to employees covered by a collective bargaining agreement or those subject to other eligibility rules.

role.title: Operations Director
role.description:
Amphenol Communications Solutions (ACS), a division of Amphenol Corporation, is a world leader in interconnect solutions for Communications, Mobile, RF, Optics, and Commercial electronics markets. Amphenol Corporation is one of the world’s largest designers and manufacturers of electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors and interconnect systems, antennas, sensors and sensor-based products and coaxial and high-speed specialty cable. ACS has an expansive global presence in research and development, manufacturing, and sales. We design and manufacture a wide range of innovative connectors as well as cable assemblies for diverse applications including server, storage, data center, mobile, RF, networking, industrial, business equipment, and automotive.

Amphenol's High Speed IO Connectors and OverPass Solutions Business Unit is a market leader in high-speed, high-bandwidth interconnect solutions used in servers, storage, networking equipment, and data center infrastructure. Our products enable reliable, low-loss data transmission in some of the world's most advanced IT and Datacom platforms, helping power the technology behind leading Tier 1 OEMs. With global design, sales, and manufacturing teams, we are growing quickly and continuing to invest in our people and products. This role is a chance to make a real impact as part of a collaborative, fast-moving team within Amphenol's decentralized culture, where ideas are heard, initiative is encouraged, and teams are empowered to make decisions with clear accountability.

**Position: Operations Director**

**Location: USA, Remote**

***Must have multi-site global and electrical manufacturingexperience***

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operations Leadership**

* Lead new product introductions from concept to full-scale production
* Oversee global plant operations and standardize processes
* Ensure effective resource allocation and EHS best practices
* Manage critical operational issues and crisis response

**Strategy & Capacity**

* Develop and execute 3-year operational and capacity plans
* Lead expansion initiatives, new site development, and capital projects
* Forecast demand and optimize global resource utilization

**Financial Management**

* Oversee global budgets and P&L performance
* Drive cost reduction and operational efficiency
* Identify risks and implement mitigation strategies

**Performance & Reporting**

* Define and monitor KPIs (quality, delivery, productivity)
* Use data insights to improve performance and on-time delivery
* Report results and recommendations to leadership

**Collaboration & Quality**

* Partner cross-functionally to meet customer and business needs
* Ensure compliance with ISO standards and global regulations
* Maintain strong supplier quality systems and audit readiness

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years in manufacturing management (electronics or mechanical preferred)
* Degree in Engineering or related field
* Experience building and scaling manufacturing operations
* Knowledge of ISO 9001/14001, Lean, Six Sigma, 5S
* Strong leadership, analytical, and communication skills
* Willingness to travel globally (50%+); Mandarin is an asset

Amphenol Corporation is proud of our reputation as an excellent employer. Our focus is to provide the highest level of support and responsiveness to both our employees and our customers, the world's largest technology companies. Amphenol Corporation offers the opportunity for career growth within a global organization. We believe that Amphenol Corporation is unique in that every employee, regardless of his or her position, has the ability to positively impact the business.

Amphenol is an “Equal Opportunity Employer” - Minority/Female/Disabled/Veteran/Sexual Orientation/Gender Identity/National Origin. For additional company information please visit our website at https://www.amphenol-cs.com/

role.description:
About Us :

Signature HealthCARE of Elizabethtown is a 112-bed facility offering short-term rehabilitative care as well as long-term care. It is our mission as a family-based organization to revolutionize the healthcare industry through a culture of resident centered healthcare services, personalized spirituality, and real quality of life initiatives.

About Signature :

**Signature HealthCARE** is a family-based healthcare company offering integrated services across multiple states. Our continuum of care includes skilled nursing, rehabilitation, assisted and memory care, and home-based services supported by innovative technologies like telehealth and Care.ai-enabled solutions.

We are committed to advancing person-directed care and quality outcomes. Many of our facilities continue to receive high performance ratings and accreditations. As an award-winning organization recognized over the years by national outlets such as *U.S. News & World Report*, we take pride in fostering compassionate care environments and being an employer of choice in the healthcare industry.

Additional Details:

**Signature HEALTHCARE of Elizabethtown**

**NOW Hiring!!**

**Plant Director - Full time 8 hr days>(M-F w/some Weekend Rotation)**

**Benefits in 30 days!!**

**Required Experienced in Maintenance> Plumbing/ Dry-Wall/Painting, If you have this experience We want to talk to you. Come Join our TEAM!!**

How you Will make a Difference:

**Our Plant Operations Directors make a difference in the lives of our stakeholders and residents by ensuring our facilities, equipment, and utilities are in good working order and that property grounds are maintained in accordance with facility policies and state and federal regulations.**

What you Need to make a Difference:

* High school diploma or GED required or equivalent related work experience.
* Practical knowledge of day-to-day maintenance and facility physical plant upkeep.
* One (1) to two (2) years management/supervisory experience required.

Our exceptional Benefits Package and Signature Perks include the following and more! (if applicable):

**Live with Purpose at Signature HealthCARE**

Our exceptional benefits and Signature Perks are designed to support your health, wealth, and well-being, including:

* Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage
* First Stop Health Virtual Healthcare
* 401(k) & Roth 401(k)
* Company-Paid & Voluntary Life Insurance
* Health Savings Account (HSA) & Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Paid Time Off (PTO) & Holiday Incentive Pay
* Tuition Reimbursement & Tuition Discounts with Select Universities
* Student Debt Assistance (eligible SNF RNs & LPNs)
* Uniform Allowance
* Partner Perks Discount Program
* Perfect Attendance Program
* Pay Advance & Next Day Pay
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Support Beyond Benefits with VitalLink and the Signature Inspire Foundation

At Signature HealthCARE, our team members are empowered—not just encouraged—to use their talents and abilities to solve problems. 
Our culture is built on three pillars: Learning, Spirituality, and Intra-preneurship.

Each pillar has dedicated initiatives that strengthen our culture and create opportunities for growth.

**Come see what the revolution is all about!**

*Signature HealthCARE is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace for all applicants and stakeholders.*

Pay Range: USD $23.97 - USD $26.46 /Hr. Hashtag : #LI-MS1

role.title: Plant Manager-Northeast Water Treatment Plant
role.description:
**Job Summary**
---------------

Provides leadership and management for treatment plant operations, process control, regulatory compliance, laboratory activities, preventive and corrective maintenance coordination, safety programs, emergency preparedness, employee development, budget administration, inventory control, contractor activities, and facility improvement projects. Evaluates plant performance and treatment processes, establishes operational priorities, develops and implements procedures, and directs corrective actions necessary to maintain treatment quality, regulatory compliance, equipment reliability, and continuity of operations.

**Essential Functions**
-----------------------

• Recognizes and fulfills the professional and ethical obligations associated with an FDEP treatment operator license. Ensures licensed duties and treatment operations are performed in accordance with FDEP requirements, applicable federal, state, and local laws and standards, permit conditions, County policies, established operating procedures, and safety requirements. Exercises professional judgment in a manner that protects public health, employee safety, water quality, environmental quality, and the integrity of the County's treatment operations.
 
• Plans, directs, manages, and evaluates the operations and activities of an assigned water or wastewater treatment facility to ensure safe, reliable, efficient, and regulatory-compliant operations. Establishes facility priorities, coordinates personnel and resources, evaluates operational performance, and provides overall management and technical direction for treatment processes, maintenance activities, laboratory functions, safety programs, regulatory compliance, and facility support activities.
 
• Supervises, directs, develops, and evaluates assigned employees; coordinates daily work activities; organizes, prioritizes, and assigns work; monitors work in progress and completed work; addresses employee concerns and performance matters; provides coaching, counseling, training, and technical expertise; completes employee performance evaluations; and administers personnel responsibilities consistent with County policies and delegated authority.
 
• Directs and evaluates water treatment processes and equipment applicable to the assigned facility, including pumping, chemical treatment and disinfection, filtration, membrane and reverse osmosis systems, biological treatment, aeration, clarification, sludge and solids handling, storage, wells, and related treatment equipment. Ensures treatment processes are operated and adjusted as necessary to maintain treatment performance, water quality, regulatory compliance, equipment reliability, and continuity of operations.
 
• Evaluates plant performance through SCADA systems, computerized controls, laboratory and process-control results, instrumentation, gauges, meters, alarms, flow conditions, chemical feed rates, equipment performance, treatment loading, and operational trends. Directs appropriate operational adjustments and corrective actions and provides technical direction for complex treatment-process, equipment, mechanical, instrumentation, chemical-feed, and operational problems.
 
• Evaluates laboratory and process-control activities associated with the assigned facility. Ensures required water samples are collected and analyzed in accordance with applicable requirements; reviews laboratory and quality-control results; evaluates treatment trends and compliance data; and directs operational adjustments or additional investigation when results indicate abnormal treatment conditions or potential compliance concerns.
 
• Maintains responsibility for the professional and ethical performance of licensed treatment plant operations within the assigned facility. Ensures operational and regulatory records are accurate, complete, and truthful; reinforces the professional and ethical obligations associated with FDEP licensure; and ensures actual or potential regulatory violations, treatment failures, permit exceedances, unsafe conditions, or environmental concerns are appropriately evaluated, documented, reported, and addressed.
 
• Directs facility safety activities and ensures adherence to established safety procedures and requirements. Monitors workplace conditions and use of required personal protective equipment; ensures appropriate Job Safety Analyses and hazard assessments are completed; supports safety training, inspections, incident investigations, and corrective actions; and takes appropriate action to address unsafe conditions or practices.
 
• Directs and coordinates preventive and corrective maintenance activities involving treatment equipment, instrumentation, buildings, grounds, and other facility assets. Establishes operational and maintenance priorities; coordinates work orders, equipment shutdowns and start-ups, equipment isolation, contractor activities, and return-to-service requirements; and ensures maintenance activities are coordinated to minimize disruption to treatment operations.
 
• Consults with Division management and other appropriate officials regarding development and administration of the facility’s operating budget in accordance with County procedures. Evaluates operational needs, develops budget recommendations, monitors expenditures within approved limits, and supports operating and capital budget development.
 
• Develops and implements short- and long-term operational plans, goals, and objectives for the assigned treatment facility; evaluates plant performance, operational efficiency, treatment processes, procedures, staffing, and resource utilization; identifies opportunities to improve safety, reliability, regulatory compliance, treatment performance, and operational efficiency; and implements appropriate improvements.
 
• Develops, evaluates, updates, and implements standard operating procedures, treatment-process protocols, safety requirements, security procedures, emergency-response plans, disaster-preparedness plans, and other facility programs necessary to support effective and compliant plant operations.
 
• Performs and oversees administrative activities associated with facility operations. Prepares, reviews, approves, or authorizes operational reports, records, purchases, work orders, payroll information, schedules, overtime, specifications, solicitations, procurement documentation, and other administrative materials within delegated authority.
 
• Coordinates capital improvements, construction projects, facility modifications, and contracted services affecting the assigned treatment facility. Provides operational and technical input during planning and design; reviews proposals and project documents; participates in project and bid meetings as appropriate; coordinates construction activities with engineering personnel and contractors; and ensures continuity of treatment operations during construction, expansion, commissioning, and start-up activities.
 
• Directs and monitors facility inventory and asset-management activities. Ensures adequate availability of chemicals, equipment, parts, tools, safety materials, laboratory supplies, and other operational resources; reviews anticipated needs; authorizes or initiates purchases and requisitions within delegated authority; assists with specifications and procurement activities; and ensures appropriate inventory and asset records are maintained.
 
• Responds to complaints, questions, and concerns regarding facility operations or related matters; researches operational issues, coordinates appropriate follow-up, and initiates or directs problem resolution within assigned authority. Performs public-information and community-outreach functions related to the assigned treatment facility. Provides information regarding treatment operations.
 
• Serves as the primary management-level operational contact for the assigned facility and maintains availability consistent with the requirements of a continuous-operation treatment facility. Responds to all significant conditions requiring management-level direction or decision-making.
 
• Follows and ensures compliance with established safety and emergency-response requirements. Recognizes when a conditions exceeds the Plant Manager's delegated authority or technical scope and promptly coordinates with or seeks assistance from Division or Department management, engineering, maintenance, regulatory agencies, emergency-management personnel, legal or risk-management personnel, or other appropriate specialized resources.

**Minimum Qualifications**
--------------------------

-Vocational/technical degree required.
 
-Seven (7) years of related experience.
 
-Candidates without a degree should possess one (1) additional year of related experience.
 
-Fingerprinting/background screening required.
 
 
LICENSES/CERTIFICATES
 
-Must possess and maintain the Florida Department of Environmental Protection (FDEP) Drinking Water Treatment Operator License required for the assigned facility and position, as applicable.
 
-Driver’s License with any applicable endorsement(s) to drive a county vehicle as provided in CMA 5805.
 
-Maintains all required professional licenses and certifications in good standing and complies with applicable continuing-education and renewal requirements.

**Supplemental information**
----------------------------

Salary offers above the minimum pay grade may be considered based on qualifications.
 
Essential Employees may be required to work during an undeclared or declared emergency. The County’s Administrative Office will determine who will be required to work on an incident-by-incident basis.
 
This job posting is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of responsibilities, skills, or working conditions associated with the position.

***Collier County is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any status protected by applicable law. In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, reasonable accommodations are available to qualified individuals with disabilities. Veterans’ Preference is provided to eligible applicants in accordance with Florida law.***

role.title: Senior Manager, Quality Management
role.description:
L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.

L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

***Job Title: Senior Manager, Quality Management***

***Job Code: 48086***

***Job Location:*** ***Camden, AR***

***Job Schedule:*** ***4/10: Employees work 10 hours per day, 4 days a week***

**Job Description:**

L3Harris Technologies is seeking an experienced **Senior Quality Manager** to lead quality assurance operations and drive excellence across our defense programs. This strategic leadership role is responsible for ensuring the highest standards of quality, compliance, and customer satisfaction while managing quality teams and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. The Senior Quality Manager will serve as a key liaison between customers, regulatory agencies, and internal stakeholders to maintain L3Harris's reputation for delivering mission-critical solutions that meet the most stringent quality requirements.

The **Senior Quality Manager** provides executive-level oversight of quality management systems, processes, and personnel across assigned business units or programs. This role requires a seasoned quality professional who can balance strategic planning with hands-on problem-solving in a fast-paced aerospace and defense environment.

In this capacity, you will direct all aspects of quality assurance including manufacturing quality, inspection operations, and quality engineering. You will be accountable for maintaining AS9100 and ISO 9001 certifications, ensuring compliance with FAA and DoD regulations, and meeting contractual quality requirements for complex defense systems and aerospace products.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate proven expertise in leading cross-functional teams, managing customer quality relationships, and implementing data-driven quality improvement initiatives. You will work closely with Program Management, Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain leadership to embed quality throughout the product lifecycle—from design and development through production, delivery, and field support.

This position demands strong technical knowledge of aerospace/defense manufacturing processes, exceptional leadership skills, and the ability to influence at all organizational levels.

The ideal candidate will drive cultural change, mentor quality professionals, and establish L3Harris as a quality leader in the defense industry.

**Essential Functions:**

* Quality Leadership & Management
* Quality System Development & Compliance
* Product Quality & Inspection Operations
* Nonconformance Management & Problem Resolution
* Risk Management & Process Improvement
* Customer & Stakeholder Interface
* Documentation & Records Management
* Quality Cost Management

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of 12 years prior relevant experience. Graduate Degree with a minimum of 10 years prior relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 16 years of prior relevant experience.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

* Demonstrated experience managing quality operations.
* Proven track record leading Material Review Board (MRB) activities and nonconformance resolution.
* Hands-on experience with AS9100, ISO 9001, and other aerospace quality management system standards.
* Background in document control systems and configuration management practices.
* Experience interfacing with government customers (DoD, NASA, FAA) and managing customer quality requirements.
* Knowledge of inspection methods, precision measurement, and calibration systems for aerospace components.
* Experience with quality cost management and budget administration

role.title: Senior Manager - Level 1 Operations
role.description:
Pico fuels the global capital markets community by providing exceptional market data services and customized managed infrastructure solutions. As financial industry experts at the center of markets and technology, we help our clients efficiently scale their business and quickly access markets. From infrastructure to connectivity, we support our clients through the full trading lifecycle. We are a global company headquartered in New York, with offices in Chicago, London, Singapore, Hong Kong and Tokyo.

**Role Description**

Pico powers the global capital markets community with high-performance market data services and tailored managed infrastructure solutions. As financial industry experts at the intersection of markets and technology, we help clients scale efficiently and access markets quickly. From infrastructure to connectivity, we support our clients across the full trading lifecycle. Pico is headquartered in New York, with offices in Chicago, London, Dublin, Madrid, Krakow, Singapore, Hong Kong, South Korea, and Tokyo.

 

**Title:** Senior Manager, Level 1 Operations

 

**About the Role**

Pico is looking for a Senior Manager, Level 1 Operations to lead its global Level 1 technical operations function supporting financial markets infrastructure. The role combines accountability for operational performance, technical capability, people development and the quality of incident response and client communication.

Pico operates mission-critical, low-latency technology supporting banks, hedge funds, asset managers, broker-dealers and other financial market participants. The Level 1 team sits at the front line of that environment and is responsible for rapid detection, triage, communication and escalation of service-impacting issues.

This is not a traditional service desk management role.

The Senior Manager, Level 1 Operations will be accountable for developing a technically strong, customer-focused operations function capable of taking meaningful ownership of incidents from the moment they are detected or reported. Alongside operational delivery, the role will drive improvements to tooling and processes and develop talent across the team. The team is expected to conduct effective first-line diagnosis across network, connectivity, server and platform domains, establish technical direction during the early stages of an incident and engage the appropriate Level 2 or engineering teams with clear evidence and context. The successful candidate will combine people leadership, strong technical judgement, incident management and excellent client communication. They will be comfortable leading critical incidents involving senior internal stakeholders, clients, carriers and technology partners while maintaining calm, structure and urgency.

 

**Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Leadership**

* Own the day-to-day operational performance of the global Level 1 team.
* Ensure operational queues and monitoring are actively managed and that nothing falls between shifts, regions or technical teams.
* Establish and track service management performance metrics covering response and triage times, escalation quality, queue health, shift-handover quality and client communication.
* Agree targets with Operations Management, review trends across shifts and regions, and use the findings to drive corrective action.
* Drive a prioritised roadmap for Level 1 tooling improvements, working with technical teams to improve monitoring, alert quality, workflow automation and operational visibility.
* Own continuous improvement of Level 1 processes, including triage, escalation, shift handovers, runbooks and knowledge management. Use incident reviews, service data and feedback from regional leads to prioritise changes, embed adoption and verify their effectiveness.

 

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Lead, coach and develop the Level 1 Operations Engineers, working with the regional leads in AMRS, APAC and EMEA to translate global priorities into regional delivery and maintain consistent technical, behavioural and service standards.
* Work with regional leads to translate global priorities into clear local responsibilities, delegate operational ownership and review delivery against agreed standards across shifts and regions.
* Conduct regular 1:1s, performance reviews and career development discussions.
* Develop future technical authorities, technical specialists and team leaders from within Level 1.

**Incident Management**

* Act as the senior point of escalation for the Level 1 team and the regional leads in AMRS, APAC and EMEA when incidents, operational risks or service issues require senior direction, cross-region coordination or decisions beyond regional authority. Take ownership of the escalation and coordinate the appropriate technical and management response.
* Lead real-time technical triage across network, platform, server and connectivity domains.
* Direct incident bridges involving clients, senior stakeholders, Network Operations, Platform Operations, engineering teams, carriers and third-party providers.
* Ensure incidents are correctly prioritised and escalated based on technical and customer impact.
* Drive improvements in MTTR, first-line diagnosis and incident quality.

 

**Client & Stakeholder Management**

* Ensure consistently high standards of client communication throughout incidents and service requests.
* Communicate confidently with senior client and internal stakeholders during high-pressure situations.
* Ensure updates are technically accurate, concise, timely and appropriate for the audience.
* Work closely with Operations Management and technical teams to ensure a consistent service narrative.
* Reinforce a customer-centric rather than ticket-centric approach throughout the team.

 

**Experience and Qualifications**

 

**Essential**

* 10+ years' experience in technical operations, infrastructure support, network operations, production support or a comparable mission-critical environment.
* Demonstrable experience managing or leading technical operations/support engineers within a 24x7 or follow the sun environment, including coordinating delivery across regions and working with regional or shift leads to maintain consistent service standards.
* Strong understanding of ITIL processes or related frameworks for incident management.
* Experience leading significant incidents and technical bridges.
* Strong analytical and troubleshooting ability with the technical judgement to assess first-line diagnosis across network, connectivity, server and platform domains, challenge assumptions and recognise when specialist escalation is required.
* Experience establishing KPIs and improving operational performance.
* Excellent written and verbal communication.
* Confidence communicating directly with senior client and internal stakeholders.
* Demonstrable ownership mentality and ability to operate effectively under pressure.

 

**Highly Desirable**

* Experience in financial services, fintech, electronic trading or low-latency infrastructure.
* Previous experience in a telecommunications or managed service provider environment.
* Experience with monitoring and infrastructure management tooling.
* Experience with Salesforce, Jira, SolarWinds Orion, or Device42.
* ITIL certification or similar service management qualification.
* Strong networking fundamentals, particularly TCP/IP, routing, switching and BGP at a CCNA level or higher.
* Good working knowledge of Linux/Unix.

 

**Working Arrangements**

This is an office-based position with a minimum of two days office attendance per week. Occasional travel may be required, but it is not expected to be regular or frequent. The core business hours to be covered by the role are 09:00 – 18:00, Monday to Friday. The role holder will be expected to work the hours necessary to perform this role, recognizing it supports multiple jurisdictions/geographies including (but not limited to) EMEA, AMRS, and APAC. Out-of-hours escalation arrangements and availability expectations will be agreed and communicated explicitly; the team's 24/7 coverage does not imply continuous personal availability.

 

**IMPORTANT DATA PRIVACY INFORMATION:**

This position is available with Pico Services Inc. The controller of your personal data will be Pico Services Inc.

For further information on what personal data we collect, how we will process your personal data and your rights with respect to your personal data please read our Pico Job Candidate Privacy Notice, View Here.

Be a part of Pico Family

Pico is an equal opportunity employer. Pico does not discriminate on the basis of a candidate's age, race, gender, color, religion, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, or other non-merit factors. All employment decisions at Pico are based on business needs, job requirements and qualifications. If you require any assistance or accommodations to be made for the recruitment process, please inform us when you submit your online application.

role.title: Deputy Director of Strategic Operations and Transformation (Austin)
role.description:
**Description**
---------------

The Texas Workforce Commission (TWC) is seeking a Deputy Director of Strategic Operations and Transformation to support the Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) Division. This position is based out of the TWC office located at 1117 Trinity Street, Austin, TX. This role performs highly advanced (senior-level) managerial work providing direction and guidance in strategic operations, organizational transformation, and implementation of division-wide initiatives.

Work involves developing and executing comprehensive change management strategies that align with agency goals and improve service delivery across regions. This role is responsible not only for designing change initiatives, but also for ensuring effective implementation, adoption, and long-term sustainability through structured project management, stakeholder engagement, and continuous feedback loops.

The Deputy Director leads large-scale transformation efforts by establishing priorities, developing policies and procedures, and creating performance measures to assess progress and outcomes. This position works closely with leadership, regional staff, and stakeholders to strengthen alignment, reduce operational gaps, and ensure initiatives are informed by field insight and practical application.

This position supervises the work of others and operates under minimal supervision with extensive latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment.

TWC is not considering applications from individuals who require sponsorship for an employment visa, now or in the future, for this position. This includes, but is not limited to, individuals currently on H-1B, F-1 (OPT/CPT), or H-4 visas. You must be a Texas resident to work for the Texas Workforce Commission or willing to relocate to Texas.

EXAMPLES OF WORK PERFORMED: 

* Develops and implements comprehensive change management strategies that align with organizational goals and improve service delivery outcomes.
* Leads implementation of division-wide initiatives, ensuring alignment, consistency, and measurable adoption across the division.
* Establishes project governance structures, timelines, and accountability measures to support successful execution of strategic initiatives.
* Directs and evaluates program activities and business functions related to change management and transformation efforts.
* Develops and maintains feedback mechanisms (e.g., communities of practice, listening sessions, stakeholder engagement processes) to inform continuous improvement and strengthen connection between state and field operations.
* Partners with leadership to translate strategy into operational practice and sustain long-term change.
* Leads the development and use of data systems, performance metrics, and key indicators to monitor implementation, measure adoption, and drive continuous improvement.
* Identifies and mitigates risks and resistance to change through proactive communication, coaching, and stakeholder engagement.
* Develop policies, procedures, and standardized practices to support consistency and efficiency across the division.
* Oversee and/or prepares budgets related to change initiatives, ensuring appropriate use of resources and compliance with funding requirements.
* Represents the agency at business meetings, legislative sessions, conferences, and stakeholder engagements to communicate and advance strategic initiatives.
* Supervises staff, including assigning work, evaluating performance, and supporting professional development.
* Performs related work as assigned.

YOU QUALIFY WITH: 

* Six years of full-time experience in the oversight and direction of an agency program; or in strategic planning and policy development and implementation, three years of which must have been in an administrative management or supervisory capacity.
* Relevant academic credits may be applied toward experience qualifications for this position.

YOU ARE A GREAT FIT WITH: 

* Graduation from an accredited four-year college or university.
* Demonstrated experience leading large-scale organizational change initiatives across multiple regions or programs.
* Experience implementing management frameworks (e.g., Prosci ADKAR®, Kotter’s 8-Step Process, Lean, or similar methodologies).
* Strong project management experience, including oversight of multiple concurrent initiatives with defined timelines, deliverables, and outcomes.
* Experience developing feedback loops and engagement strategies to incorporate field or stakeholder input into program design and implementation.
* Certification in change management or project management (e.g., CCMP, PMP, Lean) preferred.

 
Knowledge of: 

* Principles and practices of public administration and management.
* Change management methodologies, tools, and implementation strategies.
* Project management principles, including planning, execution, and performance monitoring.
* Federal and state laws, regulations, and policies applicable to state Vocational Rehabilitation (VR) programs.

 
Ability to: 

* Direct and organize complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Translate strategic priorities into operational implementation.
* Establish measurable goals and evaluate outcomes.
* Identify problems, evaluate alternatives, and implement effective solutions.
* Engage, influence, and communicate effectively with stakeholders at all levels.
* Analyze data and use insights to guide decision-making and continuous improvement.
* Develop and implement policies, procedures, and standardized practices.
* Plan, assign, and supervise the work of others.

YOU GAIN: 

* A Family Friendly Certified Workplace
* Competitive salary: $12,500.00/month
* Defined Retirement Benefit Plan
* Optional 401(k) and 457 accounts
* Medical Insurance
* Paid time off, including time for vacation, sick and family care leave
* Additional benefits for active employees can be found at https://www.ers.texas.gov/Active-Employees/Health-Benefits

Duty involves up to 25% travel within the state of Texas.

VETERANS: 
Use your military skills to qualify for this position or other jobs! Go to www.texasskillstowork.com to translate your military work experience and training courses into civilian job terms, qualifications, and skill sets. Also, you can compare this position to military occupations (MOS) at the Texas State Auditor's Office by pasting this link into your browser: https://hr.sao.texas.gov/Compensation/MilitaryCrosswalk/MOSC\_ProgramManagement.pdf

HOW TO APPLY: 
To be considered, please complete a State of Texas Application for Employment and apply online at www.workintexas.com or on Taleo (Job Search). TWC is not considering applications from individuals who require sponsorship for an employment visa, now or in the future, for this position. This includes, but is not limited to, individuals currently on H-1B, F-1 (OPT/CPT), or H-4 visas. You must be a Texas resident to work for the Texas Workforce Commission or willing to relocate to Texas. In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire. A position utilizing this classification will be designated as security sensitive according to the Texas Labor Code, Section 301.042.

role.title: RN Director of Quality & Safety
role.description:
**Employment Type:** 
Full time
 
 
**Shift:** 
Day Shift
 
 
**Description:** 
The Eddy’s continuing care network, including a wide range of services—from nursing homes, assisted living, independent living, memory care, home health, hospice, PACE, infusion pharmacy to durable medical equipment—has an exciting and rewarding opportunity for a RN Director of Quality& Safety to work with teams across our network
 
 
Key responsibilities related to quality improvement include but are not limited to:
 
 

* Supporting the development of QAPI plans, goals and metrics
* Supporting and preparing reports for three Divisional QAPI Committees (Community-Based Services, Nursing Homes, and Senior Living)
* Gathering and presenting quality and safety data to the Board Quality& Safety Committee across all service lines
* Representing The Eddy Continuing Care services in a wide range of quality-related meetings
* Overall education and support of leaders across the network in continuously improving quality and outcomes

**Key responsibilities related to Safety include:** 

* Educating and support colleagues
* Facilitating meetings and the work of Safety Champions at each location
* Representing The Eddy Continuing Care Network in a wide range of Safety& Risk Management related meetings
* Preparing a wide range of reports summarizing safety/risk management related data across all service lines and development of presentations

**Education:** 

* BSN Required; MSN preferred

**Experience:** 

* Quality improvement, safety/risk management.
* Experience working in at least one continuing care service line a plus but not required (nursing homes, assisted living, independent living, memory care, home health, hospice, PACE).
* Requires expertise in using a wide range of software programs (EPIC and PCC Electronic Medical Records, MIDAS, etc.)
* Preparing concise SBARs summarizing incidents
* PowerPoint, Excel and other programs in the presentation of quality and safety data/trends, etc.

**Pay Range:** 
$116,480-$153,795.20
 
Pay is based on experience, skills, and education. Exempt positions under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) will be paid within the base salary equivalent of the stated hourly rates. The pay range may also vary within the stated range based on location.
 
 
Our Commitment
 
 
Rooted in our Mission and Core Values, we honor the dignity of every person and recognize the unique perspectives, experiences, and talents each colleague brings. By finding common ground and embracing our differences, we grow stronger together and deliver more compassionate, person-centered care. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by federal, state, or local law.

role.title: Regional Healthcare Operations Director
role.description:
Do you enjoy creating structure, improving efficiency, and helping organizations grow without sacrificing the patient experience? **Minimally Invasive Procedure Specialists** in Highlands Ranch, CO is seeking a **full-time Regional Healthcare Operations Director** to lead operational excellence across our expanding network of locations. If you're looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a significant impact and help shape the future of a growing healthcare organization, submit your application today!

As our Regional Healthcare Operations Director, you'll earn a competitive annual salary of **$120,000 - $150,000**. We're also proud to offer a **comprehensive benefits package**, including:

* Health, dental, and vision
* Paid time off (PTO)
* An employee assistance program
* A companymatched 401(k) plan
* HSA/FSA
* Life insurance
* Uniforms
* Short-/long-term disability coverage

**THE TYPE OF REGIONAL HEALTHCARE OPERATIONS DIRECTOR WE'RE LOOKING FOR**

We're searching for someone who can meet the following qualifications:

* Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience
* 7+ years of progressive operations leadership within a physician practice, ambulatory surgery center (ASC), or office-based lab (OBL)
* 3+ years of experience managing managers
* Experience leading procedural or surgical specialties such as interventional radiology, vascular, cardiology, or orthopedics
* Working knowledge of front-end revenue cycle operations, prior authorization, and payer requirements
* Proven experience developing staffing models, KPIs, and budgets
* Familiarity with HIPAA, OSHA, and outpatient survey-readiness standards

Extensive leadership experience within physician practices, ambulatory surgery centers, or office-based laboratories and a proven ability to lead leaders while driving operational excellence are preferred.

**WHAT IT'S LIKE TO BE OUR REGIONAL HEALTHCARE OPERATIONS DIRECTOR**

In this full-time role, you'll oversee daily operations across all MIPS locations, ensuring procedure days run efficiently, schedules align with patient demand, and every site delivers a seamless experience. You'll partner with clinic managers and departmental leaders to develop teams, improve workflows, maintain compliance, and drive performance. You'll also play a key role in launching new locations, standardizing best practices, managing resources, and helping the organization scale successfully while maintaining operational excellence.

**ABOUT OUR COMPANY**

Our team at Minimally Invasive Procedure Specialists comprises world-renowned vascular specialists and healthcare support staff who are passionate about making a real difference in others' lives. With over four decades of combined experience and armed with cutting-edge technology, our clinic provides precise treatment for complex vascular and chronic conditions, including pelvic venous disorders, POTS, long COVID, and fibroids.

We are a beacon of hope for our patients, and we take pride in helping to improve their quality of life. If you are passionate about providing exceptional care in a progressive, supportive atmosphere and are looking to be at the forefront of healthcare innovation, we invite you to join us!

Great organizations are built by great leaders. If you're ready to guide teams, improve performance, and help drive continued growth, this could be the perfect opportunity for you! Our initial application process is fast, simple, and mobile-friendly. Apply today!

====================================================================================

Hope Plumbing, Heating, and Cooling is a locally owned Indianapolis home services company known for great customer service and for developing outstanding people. **Reasons to Join Hope:**
-------------------------

* Competitive compensation based on experience.
* Company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision insurance.
* Long-term and short-term disability and life insurance.
* Company-sponsored PTO and paid holidays.
* Company-sponsored 401(k) retirement plan.
* Maternity/Paternity Leave.
* Ongoing leadership training and development.
* Fun company-wide events for you and your family!

* Develop strategies to improve revenue, close rates, average ticket, technician productivity, and operational efficiency.
* Conduct regular leadership meetings and performance reviews.
* Build a strong leadership pipeline through coaching, mentoring, and succession planning.
* Ensure managers maintain high standards for customer satisfaction, safety, quality, and operational performance.
* Partner with the General Manager to align departmental goals with company-wide objectives.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

* Seven (7)+ years of leadership experience in home services, retail, or a multi-department service organization.
* Three (3)+ years of experience directly managing managers or department leaders.
* Proven ability to lead through others and develop high-performing management teams.
* Experience with P&L ownership, budgeting, revenue growth, and profitability.
* Strong understanding of KPIs, financial reporting, and data-driven decision-making.
* Proven ability to improve operational performance and hold leaders accountable.
* Excellent leadership, communication, coaching, and strategic planning skills.
* Valid driver's license with a driving record that meets company insurance requirements.
* Plumbing, HVAC, or home services leadership experience preferred.
* ServiceTitan and/or Rilla experience a plus.
* Plumbing trade background is not required.

**Apply today and help shape the future of Hope Plumbing, Heating & Cooling!**

role.title: Executive Director, Research Administration Transformation & Operational Excellence
role.description:
Discover Your Career at Emory University: Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community. Description:

The Executive Director for Research Administration Transformation & Operational Excellence provides executive strategic and operational leadership for the Office of Research Administration's (ORA) enterprise-wide transformation portfolio.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

* Leads an enterprise-wide transformation portfolio spanning research administration functions across schools, units, and Emory Healthcare, requiring university-wide change leadership and executive influence.
* Partners with Artificial Intelligence & Digital Strategy (AI & DS) to implement a broad portfolio that includes enterprise technology implementation (including the Insight grants management system), organizational redesign, shared services transformation, operational performance improvement, artificial intelligence and emerging technology strategy, and research administration training and professional development.
* Directs implementation, ongoing maintenance, and optimization of enterprise systems and tools, including Insight and LegalSifter, and ensures that technology investments support the future-state operating model.
* Co-leads implementation and ongoing review of future-state operating model, including organizational design, workflow refinement, shared services transformation, and operational performance.
* Exercises decision-making authority over implementation, configuration alignment, workflow and business process design, user acceptance, vendor management, future-state operating model alignment, and continuous refinement across pre-award, post-award, agreements, effort reporting, personnel, and compliance modules.
* Manages vendor performance (including Huron), monitors project milestones, and reports status, risks, decisions, and outcomes to the Vice President and Steering Committee.
* Holds executive accountability for realization of transformation outcomes, including organizational effectiveness, service excellence, operational efficiency, adoption, and sustained performance improvement.
* Partners with AI & DS to implement technology programs and enabling capabilities required for responsible AI success. This includes project management, development and evaluation of workflows, tool evaluation, implementation, governance, workforce readiness, and adoption. Manages technology evaluation, implementation, and security coordination in partnership with Emory OIT and Information Security.
* Serves as ORA's operational technologies (Insight, SciShield, Huron, etc.) liaison to central technology and governance bodies.
* Provides subject matter expertise to the Learning and Organizational Development team for the design and deployment of a scalable, role-based training ecosystem that includes Insight and Compass system training, process-compliance content, change enablement, and professional development for ORA and school-based research administration staff.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

* Bachelor's degree in business administration, public administration, health administration, or a related field from an accredited institution and eight years of progressively responsible professional experience in related research administration experience, including a minimum of five years of experience in a management role with direct supervisory responsibility.
* Master's degree (MBA, MPA, MHA, MS, or related discipline) strongly preferred.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

* Master's degree or doctoral degree in a relevant field.
* Experience with Huron's Insight platform at an R1 university or academic medical center in a project leadership or system administration capacity.
* Direct, client-side experience supporting or co-leading a management consulting engagement (EY, Huron Consulting, Deloitte, or equivalent) in a research or academic operations context.
* Experience building or leading a training, learning and development, or organizational capability function in a higher education or healthcare research environment.
* Knowledge of AI governance frameworks, responsible AI principles, and federal data security and research security requirements.
* Demonstrated experience with process improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or equivalent); certification preferred.
* Professional certification in one or more of the following: research administration (CRA or CPRA), project management (PMP), or change management (Prosci ADKAR / CCMP).
* Experience in a centralized or shared services research administration environment, particularly at an institution transitioning from a decentralized model.
* Familiarity with Emory University's systems, culture, and governance structure, or comparable experience at an AAU or Carnegie R1 institution.

NOTE: Position tasks are generally required to be performed in-person at an Emory University location. Remote work from home day options may be granted at department discretion. Emory reserves the right to change remote work status with notice to employee.

#LI-MR1

Additional Details: Emory is an equal opportunity employer, and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by state or federal law. Emory University does not discriminate in admissions, educational programs, or employment, including recruitment, hiring, promotions, transfers, discipline, terminations, wage and salary administration, benefits, and training. Students, faculty, and staff are assured of participation in university programs and in the use of facilities without such discrimination. Emory University complies with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the Vietnam Era Veteran's Readjustment Assistance Act, and applicable executive orders, federal and state regulations regarding nondiscrimination, equal opportunity, and affirmative action (for protected veterans and individuals with disabilities). Inquiries regarding this policy should be directed to the Emory University Department of Equity and Civil Rights Compliance, 201 Dowman Drive, Administration Building, Atlanta, GA 30322. Telephone: 404-727-9867 (V) | 404-712-2049 (TDD).
 
 
Emory University is committed to ensuring equal access and providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities upon request. To request this document in an alternate format or to seek a reasonable accommodation, please contact the Department of Accessibility Services at accessibility@emory.edu or call 404-727-9877 (Voice) | 404-712-2049 (TDD). We kindly ask that requests be made at least seven business days in advance to allow adequate time for coordination.

role.title: Vice President of Quality
role.description:
VP of Quality – Structural Steel & Bridge Fabrication

**Confidential Fabricator**

The cost of poor quality rarely sits in one department.

Production loses hours to repairs.

Project managers spend time chasing answers.

Shipping loses its window.

And the customer remembers who had to explain the delay.

That’s when quality becomes a leadership issue.

A large-scale structural steel and bridge fabricator is hiring a
**VP of Quality**
to set the quality strategy and make it work across engineering, fabrication and project delivery.

You’ll set expectations with department leaders, use data on rework and audit findings to decide where to act first, and build a quality team that can support the business as it grows.

You’ll need the technical credibility to challenge a welding or inspection decision and the judgment to know when a recurring issue calls for investment, a process change or clearer ownership.

**What they’re looking for**

* Senior quality leadership in structural steel, bridge fabrication or comparable heavy welded fabrication
* Experience owning a quality management system and leading quality managers or inspection teams
* Strong knowledge of AWS D1.1, AWS D1.5 and AISC certification requirements
* Evidence of measurable improvements in rework, delivery performance or customer outcomes
* Confidence representing the business with customers, auditors and third-party inspectors

**Why it’s worth a conversation**

* Executive influence over how quality decisions are made across the business
* State-of-the-art facility: 2000+ tonnes a month
* Complex steel and bridge work where those decisions have a real impact on cost and delivery
* Scope to shape the quality team, systems and standards as the business grows

If you’ve changed how a fabrication business manages quality, I’d like to hear what you changed and what improved.

**Apply on LinkedIn or message me directly for a confidential conversation.**
