role.title: Director of Operations, North America
role.description:
Director of Operations, North America

**About Us:**

We are committed to finding smart solutions that enable an intelligent and seamless world. Our success as a world-class leader in technology has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. Our innovative sensing, connectivity, and motion solutions offer a diverse range of products across diversified end markets including transportation, medical, aerospace and defense, and industrial. We are at the forefront of supporting innovating life-changing technology, focusing on quality to keep people safe, healthy, and happy.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director, North America provides strategic and operational leadership for the regional manufacturing network, ensuring safe, compliant, cost-effective, and customer-focused execution across assigned sites. This position requires a hands-on, execution-focused leader who can standardize operating processes, improve performance variability across sites, coach plant leadership teams, and convert strategic business priorities into measurable operational and financial results. This role is accountable for safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, capital execution, and people development across the North America plants.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the North America manufacturing operations network, establishing clear priorities, standard work, operating cadences, and performance expectations across assigned sites.
* Own regional operational performance and operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, and employee engagement metrics.
* Partner with business unit leadership, plant managers, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial teams to align operating plans with customer demand and business objectives.
* Establish and reinforce standardized operating processes across the region while allowing appropriate site-level flexibility based on product, customer, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive a disciplined daily, weekly, and monthly management system to review performance, identify gaps, assign accountability, and ensure timely corrective actions.
* Translate operational actions into financial outcomes by improving margin performance, controlling costs, optimizing resources, and partnering with finance on budgeting and forecasting.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and development for plant managers and site leadership teams, building a strong succession pipeline and culture of accountability.
* Champion a zero-harm safety culture and ensure compliance with company EHS standards and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Ensure customer requirements are met or exceeded, including on-time delivery, responsiveness, quality performance, and timely resolution of escalations.
* Lead continuous improvement and Lean deployment across the region, including visual management, standard work, 5S, value stream improvement, structured problem solving, and waste reduction.
* Reduce performance variability between sites by deploying common metrics, operating reviews, best-practice sharing, and targeted improvement plans.
* Drive structural cost improvement through labor efficiency, material yield, scrap reduction, inventory optimization, manufacturing productivity, and capacity utilization.
* Review and approve capital project proposals, support business cases, and ensure approved capital expenditures are implemented on time, on budget, and with expected returns.
* Support digital manufacturing, automation, data transparency, and ERP-enabled process improvements where they improve operational control, productivity, and decision-making.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment, facilities, and processes are maintained and utilized effectively to produce high-quality products at competitive cost.
* Maintain strong governance of quality management systems, audit readiness, corrective actions, and certification requirements applicable to assigned sites.
* Support new product introductions, transfers, footprint changes, and capacity expansion projects through disciplined planning and cross-functional execution.
* Establish strong communication routines with site and regional teams to reinforce priorities, escalate risks, and ensure alignment on business-critical actions.
* Ensure compliance with corporate policies, business unit procedures, internal controls, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

**Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong multi-site manufacturing leadership experience with demonstrated ability to deliver results through plant leadership teams.
* Deep knowledge of Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, visual management, standard work, and daily management systems.
* Strong business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, P&L management, productivity analysis, labor planning, capital investment justification, and margin improvement.
* Demonstrated ability to standardize processes across sites while adapting execution to local operating realities and customer requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across operations, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial functions.
* Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to engage shop-floor teams, plant leadership, executives, and customers.
* Ability to prioritize competing objectives, manage risk, lead through change, and make timely decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of building high-performing teams, developing leaders, improving retention, and creating succession plans for critical operations roles.
* High integrity, sound judgment, and commitment to safety, quality, compliance, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related field required; master’s degree or MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 12 to 15 years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including leadership of complex plant operations.
* Minimum of 5 years of multi-site operations leadership experience preferred, with accountability for regional performance across multiple plants or business units.
* Experience leading manufacturing operations in North America, including cross-border or multi-country operating environments, preferred.
* Experience with P&L ownership, operating budgets, capital planning, productivity programs, operational KPI management, and financial performance improvement required.
* Demonstrated experience with Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or equivalent continuous improvement systems required; certification preferred.
* Experience with ERP systems, manufacturing data, automation initiatives, and digital operations tools preferred.
* Experience in automotive, electronics, sensors, mechatronics, industrial manufacturing, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
* Bilingual English/Spanish capability preferred, particularly for roles supporting Mexico operations.

**Physical Demands**

* Must follow applicable safety requirements while visiting manufacturing areas, including use of required personal protective equipment.
* Ability to work several hours at a computer and participate in meetings across multiple time zones.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed, approximately 35% to 50% depending on business requirements.

**Working Environment**

* Plant, office, and travel-based environment across North America manufacturing locations.

**Join Us**

At CTS, one of the ways we recognize the value of our employees is through our comprehensive benefits program. Highlights of our benefits program for full-time employees include:

* Health Benefits
* 401K
* Paid Time Off
* Holiday Pay
* Employee Assistance Program
* Paid Parental Leave
* Pet Insurance
* Tuition Reimbursement

The expected annual salary range for this position is $150-200K.

This position is eligible for variable pay, issued as a monetary bonus or in another form.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. CTS considers a variety of factors when setting base salary rates including, without limitation, a candidate’s skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

Ready to shape the future? Apply now to join a world leader in sensing and connectivity.

**United States EEO Statement**

CTS Corporation is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer who complies with all applicable federal, state and local employment laws. In order to provide equal employment and advancement opportunities to all individuals, employment decisions at CTS Corporation will be based on merit, qualifications, and abilities. It has been and shall continue to be both the official policy and the commitment of CTS Corporation to further equal employment opportunities for all persons regardless of, among other characteristics, race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, genetic information, status as a protected veteran or status as a qualified individual with a disability, or any other characteristics protected by applicable Federal, State or Local law.

ADA accommodation statement: If you require reasonable accommodation in the application process, call Human Resources at 630.577.8811. All other applications must be submitted online.

**United States Additional Considerations**

It is unlawful in all states where the Company operates, including Massachusetts, to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates applicable laws may be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. The Company does not require a lie detector test as a condition of employment nor continued employment.

Applicants must have valid work authorization that does not now and/or will not in the future require sponsorship of a visa for employment authorization in the United States.

No agencies, please. We do not accept any unsolicited resumes and are not looking to engage an agency. We receive inquiries from agencies daily. Do not direct any inquiries or emails to hiring managers. It is not our standard practice to utilize agencies; we are a federal contractor and need to comply with the same process for all.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
Cenveo is a leading North American manufacturer of envelopes with over 100 years of experience and approximately 30 billion envelopes manufactured annually. We are committed to safety, quality, and operational excellence.

We are hiring immediately for an experienced Plant Manager for its envelope manufacturing facility in Chicago, IL. The position will report into the Site-Leader/General Manager.

Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, Cenveo provides competitive pay and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager directs the manufacturing, maintenance, warehousing and distribution operations of a facility to achieve business goals including safety, quality, and production (including efficiency and profitability). They ensure compliance with all government regulations and corporate policies. Additionally, the Plant Manager serves as a liaison between the manufacturing facility and its clients, the Sales department, and other groups.

**Key Responsibilities** (\*Essential Functions)

*These are functions a qualified incumbent or applicant must be able to perform with or without reasonable accommodation.*

* Through direct action and the management of others, ensure the safe, productive, and profitable daily operations of an envelope manufacturing facility.
* Effectively use financial, & other, reports to monitor and improve facility performance on a variety of business related metrics. Prepare similar reports as required.
* Select, train, and develop subordinates necessary to conduct facility operations.
* Direct the plant supervision team in the enforcement and consistent application of policies, and plant rules which may include the terms of a collective bargaining agreement.
* Monitor, train and communicate safety and quality programs and ensure compliance with company policies and government regulations.
* Ensure the efficient and effective purchasing and utilization of all materials and services.
* Collaborate with sales to improve or modify existing products as needed, and to aid in new product development.
* Visit customer facilities, or host customer visits to the Cenveo facility to aid in sales, customer relations, or the resolution of problem situations.
* Monitor new trends and developments in business and manufacturing.
* Represent the company and facility in community relations functions.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Perform other duties as assigned based on business needs.

**Pay / Other**

* Salaried Pay Range: $120,000 – 140,000 annually
* Schedule: Monday – Friday; Saturdays required during peak production/business needs.

**Other (Non-Essential) Functions**

Includes functions which are normally performed by persons holding this title. However, these functions may be reassigned to other employees as part of a "Reasonable Accommodation" under the ADA.

* Other duties and assignments as required.

**Job Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree preferred. Will consider experience in lieu of Bachelor's degree, emphasis on Manufacturing, Industrial Management, or similar preferred.
* Comprehensive experience in manufacturing, along with advanced knowledge in multiple related disciplines and processes is required.
* Experience in envelope, printing or packaging is highly preferred.
* Extensive experience Environmental, Health, & Safety.
* Six Sigma / Lean Manufacturing experience preferred.
* Managing teams or projects is preferred.
* Strong PC skills including Microsoft Office and internet research
* Strong interpersonal verbal and written communication
* Ability to work independently and with others, demonstrate analytical abilities, and be a strong and versatile leader.
* Must be a self-starter and thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
* Ability to perform work, and resolve problems, that are complex and varied in nature.

**Physical Requirements & Environmental Conditions**

* Requires the ability to move throughout a manufacturing facility on a regular basis, including frequent walking of the production floor, climbing stairs, and navigating operational areas.
* Frequent exposure to manufacturing environment with one or more unpleasant or hazardous conditions including but not limited to dust, dirt, high noise levels, chemicals, etc.
* Ability to communicate effectively, hear, distinguish colors
* May occasionally reach, bend, grasp, carry, and lift and/or move objects weighing up to 50 pounds; manual dexterity as needed to perform job duties.
* Occasional travel may be required based on business needs.

**Employee Benefits**

* Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
* 401(k) Retirement Plan
* Paid Holidays
* Vacation / Paid Sick Leave
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Employee Referral Bonus Program
* Other Company Sponsored Benefits

**CENVEO IS AN EEO EMPLOYER**

Requirements:

* The minimum education requirement is some college coursework or Associate's degree. Bachelor's degree is highly preferred.
* Typically possesses 10 years of related work experience, with at least 5 years' experience in managing teams or projects. Requires advanced technical and business knowledge in multiple disciplines and processes.
* Extensive experience Environmental, Health, & Safety experience.
* Comprehensive experience in manufacturing is required. Experience in envelope, printing or packaging is highly preferred.
* Experience in Six Sigma or Lean Manufacturing is preferred, but not required.
* Strong PC skills including Microsoft Office, Internet and Hagen.
* Excellent written/verbal communication skills.
* Excellent organizational skills.
* Must be able to work well with individuals at all levels within the organization.
* Must be a self-starter and must be able to thrive in a fast-paced, deadline driven environment.
* Proven ability to perform work that is complex and varied in nature. Defines and discerns key aspects of problem and develops an integrated solution within a broad technical and business context of significant impact. May provide guidance/training to more junior staff.
* This position requires contact with employees, management, sales, account teams, call center, production staff, customer and vendors.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
This position will oversee production to enable plant productivity and maintenance and the delivery of quality products to customers in an efficient manner, performs various manual tasks in the pits as required. Production activities and coordinates projects. Maintains quality control and ensures the project is going smoothly and according to schedule.

**Essentials Functions**

* Full and complete working knowledge and understanding of all equipment.
* Promotes and supports safety culture and ensures compliance with safety rules and regulations.
* Manages the plant’s production function while maintaining working relationships with other departments to ensure smooth operation.
* Reviews sales forecast and schedules production to ascertain and meet production quantity and quality requirements.
* Review production and operating reports, and resolve operational, manufacturing, and maintenance problems to ensure safety, while minimizing costs and preventing operational delays.
* Complies, stores, and retrieves production data. Monitors physical inventory levels.
* Oversee employee training requirements.
* Additional major functions include planning, annual budgeting and monthly forecasting, reporting of department’s effectiveness, safeguarding assets, and environmental compliance.
* This position requires knowledge equivalent to that which normally would be acquired through a bachelor’s degree in mechanical, industrial, or chemical engineering, or related field.
* Ability to analyze, troubleshoot, critically think about, and resolve problems with field equipment.
* Make sure all equipment is mechanically sound, safe, and ready to work daily.
* Oversee the daily construction activities at work site, including scheduling of workers, delivery of equipment and materials and progress of the project.
* Professionally and positively motivate and direct activities of the crew to enable the completion of work in a safe environmentally responsible and timely manner.
* Daily pre-job preparation and organization for self and crew members, including safety meetings.
* Complete and turn in all paperwork and log in a professional, legible, and timely manner.
* Manage aggregate production to ensure goals and objectives are met.
* Responsible for maintenance and repair of all mobile and stationary equipment.
* Ensures that the workforce complies with policies, procedures, and regulations to produce a productive labor climate at plant facilities.
* Assist Plant Managers and Quality Control Departments as necessary to ensure quality products, accounts & service.
* Assist in development of riverbed aggregate sites, pit operations and reclamation.
* Equipment repair and preventative maintenance
* Interact with vendors and employees.
* Maintain a high degree of customers satisfaction and employee morale through problem solving.
* Ensure a safe working environment through daily inspections and monthly safety meetings.
* Supervise 1-2 aggregate plants (both fixed and mobile)

**Qualifications**

* High School diploma or equivalent
* A minimum of 5 years’ experience in the operations of a sand and gravel pit.
* Experience in a supervisory capacity
* Knowledge of MSHA rules and regulations
* Experience in planning, design, and project management
* Minimum of two years of operating experience
* Ability to understand and follow instructions.
* Ability to learn the methods and practices used in our business.
* Ability to perform strenuous work in varying weather conditions.
* Knowledge of heavy equipment including but not limited to loaders, dozers, and hydraulic excavators and off-road haul trucks. Plant processing includes, but is not limited to water pumps, generators, electrical control components, vibratory screens, sand screws, conveyors, radial stackers, material washers, scales, settling basins, vibratory feeders, and log washers.
* Ability to meet deadlines and multi-task.

**Physical Demands & Work Environment**

Must be able to walk on uneven terrain, climb stairs and ladders, occasionally lift up to 50 pounds, wear required PPE, and work extended hours as needed. Valid driver's license and ability to safely conduct site inspections required.

**NOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**

* Ability to understand and follow instructions.
* Ability to learn the methods and practices used in the Pits.
* Ability to perform strenuous work in varying weather conditions.

**What we offer**

Salary: $80,000 - $105,000 DOE

Bonus Potential: 10%

* Medical
* Telemedicine
* Health Advocate Service
* Dental & Orthodontics
* Vision
* 10% profit Sharing
* FSA Medical & Dependent Care
* Paid Parental Leave
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Employee Assistance Program
* Wellness Incentive Bonus Program
* Life and AD&D
* Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
* Paid Vacation
* Paid Holidays
* 401(k)

role.title: EXPERIENCED PLANT MANAGER
role.description:
Kingspan Insulated Panels North America, a division of the Kingspan Group plc headquartered in Ireland, is a global and trusted leader in the design, manufacturing, and supply of high-performance sustainable building products and solutions for the construction industry. As the most energy-efficient, cost-effective building envelope solutions, insulated metal panels are at the forefront of sustainability. We serve the architectural, commercial/industrial, cold storage and food processing markets, and are committed to delivering the most advanced building products on the market.

Learn about our Planet Passionate initiatives: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EEeIS55WMOk (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EEeIS55WMOk)

At Kingspan, our future success is based on the quality of our people, who's expertise and motivation have helped ensure that we remain at the forefront of the construction materials manufacturing industry. In joining Kingspan you become an important part of a growing organization with a reputation for innovative design and use of technology, technical expertise, product quality, service excellence, and dedication to sustainability.

***Ready to be part of our team?***

***We are looking for an Experienced Plant Manager for our Columbus, OH plant!***

* **Sponsorship is not available for this position.**

**Summary:** The Plant Manager is the senior site leader with full accountability for overall plant performance, overseeing all operations across the entire site, including continuous panel line manufacturing and ancillary processes. This role is responsible for aligning people, processes, and strategy to ensure the site produces high-quality products at standard manufacturing costs in a safe, efficient, and profitable manner.

Success is achieved through the direct leadership and development of subordinate managers and supervisors, while building a strong, engaged organization capable of delivering reliable operational and business results.

**Essential Duties**

**Operational Performance & KPI Accountability**

* Own and drive plant performance against key metrics, including safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, and employee engagement.
* Translate corporate and regional objectives into clear plant-level goals, priorities, and operating plans.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems, standard work, and KPI reviews.
* Hold leaders and teams accountable for results while removing barriers and providing necessary resources.
* Ensure customer requirements are met through effective production planning, quality control, and on-time delivery.

**Organizational Leadership & People Development**

* Provide visible, values-based leadership that sets clear expectations for behavior, performance, and accountability across all levels of the plant.
* Lead, coach, and develop managers and supervisors, ensuring they are equipped to lead teams, solve problems, and deliver results through others.
* Build a high performing leadership team through effective hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, and succession planning.
* Foster an inclusive, respectful, and engaged workplace culture where safety, quality, and continuous improvement are shared responsibilities.
* Communicate effectively and consistently with employees, reinforcing vision, priorities, and alignment to company objectives.
* Partner with Human Resources to address employee relations matters, labor strategy (where applicable), and workforce planning.

**Safety, Quality & Compliance Leadership**

* Champion a proactive safety culture by modeling safe behaviors, enforcing standards, leading incident investigations, and driving corrective actions.
* Ensure compliance with all regulatory, environmental, safety, and labor requirements.
* Maintain adherence to quality standards and lead continuous improvement efforts to reduce defects and variability.
* Act as the site authority for audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions.

**Continuous Improvement & Change Leadership**

* Lead lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives that improve performance and build organizational capability.
* Drive root-cause problem solving and data-driven decision making.
* Lead change initiatives effectively by engaging stakeholders, communicating clearly, and sustaining improvements over time.
* Balance short-term operational execution with long-term capability and talent development.

**Financial & Strategic Stewardship**

* Maintain full accountability for plant financial performance, including labor, operating costs, and capital investments.
* Participate in budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning. • Identify and mitigate operational and business risks to ensure continuity and stability.
* Evaluate and prepare CAPEX recommendations.
* Serve as the primary site representative to corporate partners, customers, and external stakeholders.

**General Responsibilities**

* Maintain accurate records and reporting across all operational areas.
* Participate in meetings, training, and development activities as required.
* Follow the Group Code of Conduct and Group Compliance.
* Follow Compliance requirements per “KNA-SOP-1705 Compliance Roles and Responsibilities.”
* Performs all other duties as assigned.

**Education/Experience:**

* Formal education is preferably a bachelor’s degree or above.
* 10 years of manufacturing experience, ideally in a continuous product environment.
* Knowledge and practice of modern manufacturing techniques.
* Knowledge of labor laws.
* Knowledge of the construction industry.
* Know the operation of the panel producing equipment and accessory equipment.
* Ability to calculate figures/amounts.
* Good oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to train and instruct employees.
* Good analytical problem-solving skills.
* Strong Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Proven track record of lean manufacturing experience.
* Must be highly proficient in all Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and Outlook.

**Personal Attributes**

The successful candidate will exhibit the following attributes:

**Senior Site Leadership**

* Serves as the visible, accountable plant leader, shaping performance, culture, and behavior.
* Builds long-term organizational capability while balancing operational urgency with people and succession needs.

**People-Centered, Results-Driven**

* Delivers results through strong managers and supervisors, not direct control.
* Sets clear expectations, fosters accountability and trust, and coaches leaders to manage performance fairly and effectively.

**Operational & Strategic Focus**

* Aligns KPIs and execution with business objectives, customer commitments, and financial results.
* Uses data, standard work, and problem-solving while maintaining both short-term execution and long-term excellence.

**Comfort with Complexity**

* Makes sound decisions in dynamic, ambiguous environments with competing priorities.
* Leads calmly and decisively through disruptions, pressure, and change.

**Influence-Based Leadership**

* Is visible on the factory floor, approachable, and accessible to team members, fostering open dialogue and trust.

role.title: Manufacturing Plant Manager
role.description:
**ClarkDietrich** offers a comprehensive lineup of products and services for both cold-formed steel framing and drywall/plastering finishing systems. We manufacture innovative products for interior and exterior framing, interior and exterior finishing, floor and roof framing, clips, connectors, metal lath, welded wire, barrier mesh, and accessories.

As the demands for higher performance in all aspects of today's building requirements rise, our leadership team's partnerships are focused on maintaning the highest quality standards in the commercial building industry. Our teams work with architects, engineers, building developers and owners, contractors, and more on projects of all sizes, scopes, and complexity. Far beyond products, our collaborations increasingly involve efforts and expertise that support a more ingenious installation and design. Are you a Leader that understands collaboration, trust and engagement? We are looking for incredible people to contribute to our future success and growth!

Join a team that is **STRONGER THAN STEEL**℠, by applying to become a **Manufacturing Plant Manager** at our **Woodland** location.

**SUMMARY**

The **Plant Manager** is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the entire manufacturing facility to include safety, quality, efficiencies, and meeting customer expectations. This includes driving strategic plans that ensure that production goals are met in the safest and most cost-effective manner, while delivering expected financial results.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Direct and manage plant operations for production, maintenance, quality, and shipping and receiving.
* Coordinate plant activities through planning with departmental supervisors/managers to ensure that all manufacturing objectives are accomplished in a timely and cost-effective manner.
* Oversee all aspects of the day-to-day plant operations, including production, maintenance, and logistics.
* Develop, monitor and control plant budget, through active planning and understanding of P&L to ensure financial targets are met.
* Understands employment laws and oversees the application of SOPs, policies and procedures.
* Implements cost effective systems of control over capital, operating expenditures, manpower, wages, and salaries.
* Leads the effort and drives Lean Manufacturing tools and techniques fostering continuous improvement within the facility. Acts in a proactive fashion regarding problem resolution.
* Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment; replace or adjust plant facilities and equipment when necessary. Investigate and recommend new equipment or process improvements.
* Actively participated with Regional Sales Management to develop and manage the Regional Operating Unit into a team-oriented environment.
* Establish and monitor overall plant performance for production and quality standards.
* Controls and minimizes labor overtime, premium freight, and repair expenses.
* Provides leadership and training to accomplish the company goals and objectives.
* Incorporates shop floor organization and plant cleanliness among plant personnel.
* Schedules and conducts plant communication which focused on key operative measurements and safety topics.
* Onsite contact for government agencies, landlords and various other vendors
* Engages team by overseeing employee relations, coordinates team events, employee performance recognition and rewards.

**SAFETY**

* Strives to improve the plant's safety accident record year after year in creating a positive safety culture for all employees. Conducts safety walks of the facility on a weekly basis.

* Monitors the activities of all employees and provides feedback and discipline to promote a safe workplace.
* Oversee the development and organization of all safety related documentation.
* Ensures and develops all required safety related training and promotes programs to lead safe behaviors.
* Audits equipment and the shop floor for safety related improvements.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Supervise plant staff and ensure employee safety.
* Mentor staff to create a productive and positive work environment.
* Accountable to Establish strong relationships that foster engaging collaborative influence.

Requirements:

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Mechanically Inclined.
* Problem Solver.
* Team Oriented.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in related field or five years plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment, strongly preferred.
* Working knowledge of budgets and financial statements.
* Background with manufacturing methods, process improvement programs and procedures required.
* Basic computer experience with Microsoft Word and Excel
* The military equivalent will be recognized in lieu of education and/or experience.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**

* Basic mathematical skills, addition, subtraction, multiplication and converting fractions into decimals.
* Ability to read a tape measure, micrometer, and caliper accurately.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Manufacturing facility exposed to heat and cold.
* Personal Protective Equipment is always required.
* Controlled Noise exposure
* Activity level is high-continuous movement.

**CLARKDIETRICH BENEFITS INCLUDE**

* Full benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, Flexible Spending Accounts and Life Insurance)
* 401(k) with company match
* Annual Incentive Program
* Paid Time Off
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Paid Community Service Day

Pay Transparency ClarkDietrich’s compensation program supports the company’s Vision and Values. We offer a competitive compensation, opportunities for advancement and a work-life balance.

role.description:
**Date Posted:**

2026-11-19

**Country:**

United States of America

**Location:**

US-CT-EAST HARTFORD-ETC ~ 400 Main St ~ BLDG ETC

**Position Role Type:**

Onsite

**U.S. Citizen, U.S. Person, or Immigration Status Requirements:**

The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance

**Security Clearance Type:**

DoD Clearance: Confidential

**Security Clearance Status:**

Active and existing security clearance required after day 1

At **RTX**, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world.

**Pratt & Whitney** is a world leader in the design, manufacture and service of aircraft engines and auxiliary power systems and has been revolutionizing modern flight for over 100 years. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense.

Pratt & Whitney is seeking a Senior Manager, Model-Based Quality Deployment, to lead the deployment and adoption of Model-Based Quality (MBQ) capabilities across the organization. This highly visible leadership role is responsible for driving strategic digital transformation initiatives, accelerating implementation of advanced quality technologies, and developing organizational capabilities that support long-term business objectives.

The successful candidate will provide direct leadership to the Model-Based Quality Deployment Team, with resources aligned to the module center structure including Cold Section, Hot Section, North Berwick, and Supply Chain. This position requires strong leadership, strategic thinking, organizational influence, and cross-functional collaboration to ensure successful deployment and sustainment of Model-Based Quality capabilities across programs, sites, and customers.

**What You Will Do:**

* Lead the Model-Based Quality Deployment Team, providing direct leadership, coaching, mentoring, and performance management.
* Establish operational priorities, deployment strategies, and resource allocation plans to achieve business and organizational objectives.
* Drive enterprise-wide adoption of Model-Based Quality tools, technologies, and processes across engineering, quality, operations, manufacturing, and customer organizations.
* Lead cross-functional collaboration to align stakeholders, resolve barriers, and accelerate execution of strategic deployment initiatives.
* Develop team capabilities through talent development, succession planning, training, and employee engagement activities.
* Monitor deployment progress, performance metrics, and organizational adoption to ensure successful execution and sustainment.
* Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance quality performance, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.
* Identify and mitigate risks associated with deployment activities while ensuring alignment with program and customer requirements.
* Serve as a subject matter expert and advocate for Model-Based Quality, supporting enterprise digital transformation objectives.
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, and customer focus across the organization.

**Qualifications You Must Have:**

* Bachelor's Degree and 10+ years of experience in Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Program Management, or a related field; or an Advanced Degree and 7+ years of relevant experience.
* Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives, technology deployments, or business transformation activities.
* Strong knowledge of GD&T (ASME Y14.5), 3D model-based engineering practices, and manufacturing quality requirements within an aerospace or highly regulated manufacturing environment.
* Experience developing and executing strategic plans in a manufacturing, quality, or engineering environment.
* Demonstrated leadership experience with direct responsibility for people development, performance management, and team execution.
* Proven ability to lead organizational changes and drive adoption of new technologies and business processes.

**Qualifications We Prefer:**

* Demonstrated expertise in Model-Based Quality, Model-Based Enterprise (MBE), Digital Thread, or related digital transformation initiatives.
* Experience leading teams within aerospace, defense, manufacturing, or highly regulated industries.
* Strong understanding of Pratt & Whitney quality systems, manufacturing processes, and business operations.
* Experience influencing and aligning stakeholders across multiple organizations and levels of leadership.
* Excellent project management, communication, and organizational leadership skills.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement certification.
* Experience supporting strategic initiatives across multiple programs, customers, sites, and supply chain partners.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and data-driven performance management tools.

**Learn More & Apply Now!**

Please ensure the role type defined below is appropriate for your needs before applying to this role. **This position is classified as:**

**Onsite**: Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products.

Candidates will learn more about role type and current site status throughout the recruiting process. For onsite and hybrid roles, commuting to and from the assigned site is the employee’s personal responsibility.

role.title: Supply Chain Director of Operational Excellence
role.description:
1.0 FTE Full time Day - 08 Hour R2655441 Hybrid 108400006 SC Administration Business & Administration PALO ALTO, 1840 Embarcadero, California

If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.

 
Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)

**This is a Stanford Health Care job.** 
 
**A Brief Overview** 
The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. With system‑wide influence and a seat at the leadership table, this role partners closely with the Chief Supply Chain Officer and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives to turn strategy into measurable results. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact. 
 
**Locations** 
Stanford Health Care 
 
**What you will do**

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

**Required Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Must have strong leadership and interpersonal skills and be effective at people management including the ability to delegate assignments and share decision-making with team members and direct reports as appropriate.
* Excellent communication skills including the ability to present, and to write in a clear and understandable manner.
* Ability to understand complex verbal or written instructions and translate to action to deliver quantitative and qualitative results.
* Must be well organized and systematic, and able to design, implement and maintain standard work processes.
* Knowledge of project management methodologies to lead complex project teams and large scope projects, including managing resources (people, costs, time).
* Familiar with and able to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts and techniques including value stream mapping, kaizen, Five Whys, VoC, RCA etc. for structured process improvement.
* Demonstrated expertise in leading change management initiatives within Agile delivery environments.
* Ability to multi-task and handle multiple priorities while managing aggressive deadlines. Knowledge of Supply Chain functions, practices, and operational challenges.
* Understanding of healthcare and clinical concepts.

**Licenses and Certifications**

* Lean Six Sigma Certification preferred .
* PMP - Project Mgmt Professional preferred .
* CMRP (Certified Materials & Resource Professionals) preferred.

**Physical Demands and Work Conditions** 
**Blood Borne Pathogens**

* Category II - Tasks that involve NO exposure to blood, body fluids or tissues, but employment may require performing unplanned Category I tasks

**These principles apply to ALL employees:** 
 
**SHC Commitment to Providing an Exceptional Patient & Family Experience** 
 
*Stanford Health Care sets a high standard for delivering value and an exceptional experience for our patients and families. Candidates for employment and existing employees must adopt and execute C-I-CARE standards for all of patients, families and towards each other. C-I-CARE is the foundation of Stanford’s patient-experience and represents a framework for patient-centered interactions. Simply put, we do what it takes to enable and empower patients and families to focus on health, healing and recovery.* 
 
*You will do this by executing against our three experience pillars, from the patient and family’s perspective:*

* Know Me: Anticipate my needs and status to deliver effective care
* Show Me the Way: Guide and prompt my actions to arrive at better outcomes and better health
* Coordinate for Me: Own the complexity of my care through coordination

**Equal Opportunity Employer Stanford Health Care (SHC) strongly values diversity and is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination in****all of****its policies and practices, including the area of employment. Accordingly, SHC does not discriminate against any person on the basis of race, color, sex, sexual orientation or gender identity and/or expression, religion, age, national or ethnic origin, political beliefs, marital status, medical condition, genetic information, veteran status, or disability, or the perception of any of the above. People of all genders, members of all racial and ethnic groups, people with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply. Qualified applicants with criminal convictions will be considered after an individualized assessment of the conviction and the job requirements.**

Base Pay Scale: Generally starting at $81.59 - $108.12 per hour

The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, internal equity, experience, education, specialty and training. This pay scale is not a promise of a particular wage.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
**Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for leading and optimizing all aspects of business unit operations (water, wastewater and natural gas) to achieve exceptional safety performance, operational excellence, customer satisfaction, workforce development, and profitable growth. This role serves as a key member of the leadership team, translating strategic objectives into operational execution while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and innovation. The role develops leaders, drives operational consistency, and champions the company's values while positioning the organization for long-term success.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Direct supervision of 3-4 managers and provide leadership in support of subordinate managers within a 90+ employee business.

**Hiring Requirements:**

* Four years Technical/Business Administration degree or equivalent, plus extensive (10+ years) experience in the utility industry or equivalent.
* 5+ years of experience in a leadership position responsible for directing and coordinating staff, subcontractors and consultants, and making organizational decisions.
* Excellent financial, business development, customer interaction, and sales skills, with the ability to manage profit and loss responsibilities.
* Thorough understanding of contract administration, specifications, and applicable laws
* Experience in developing strategic plans, leading initiatives, and managing multiple complex priorities to achieve results within demanding timeframes and budgets.
* Excellent writing and presentation, communication (verbal and written) skills required. Computer proficiency with MS Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* Proven track record of excellent customer service, strong interpersonal skills, problem-solving ability, and the capability to engage with prospective customers at the leadership level.
* OSHA 10 General Industry Certification, or ability to obtain during pre-employment (company provided online training).
* Pass pre-employment drug screen and physical.
* Ability to obtain and maintain a valid unrestricted Driver's License.

For more than 40 years, WhiteWater has been managing, operating, and maintaining municipal and private water and wastewater facilities throughout the northeast with pride and professionalism. We are a subsidiary of R.H. White, an award-winning construction services and solutions company, that has been in business since 1923.

WhiteWater was named 2019 Utility of the Year by the New England Water Works Association and is passionately focused on safely performing great work with our people for our clients. Help us fulfill our mission of protecting public health and (the environment) our most precious natural resource - water.

WhiteWater is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, we encourage all qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

role.description:
More Information about this Job:

**Regional Director Operations**

**Must Reside in Houston, Austin or San Antonio Area**

**$140,000-$160,000**

**This role is bonus eligible 25% and equity eligible**

**Position Summary**

American Medical Response (AMR) seeks a strategic, results-driven Regional Director of Operations to lead operational excellence, financial performance, and business growth across an assigned region. This leadership position builds a collaborative culture, drives operational excellence, strengthens customer and community partnerships, develops high-performing teams, and ensures quality patient care aligned with organizational objectives. This position oversees 13+ locations and manages multiple direct reports.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight of regional operations to achieve financial, operational, and organizational objectives.
* Drive revenue growth, profitability, market expansion, and business development initiatives.
* Manage budgets, financial forecasts, profit and loss performance, and operational expenses.
* Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, enhance service delivery, and maximize resources.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with healthcare partners, government agencies, community leaders, and key stakeholders.
* Lead, coach, and develop teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure exceptional customer service, contract performance, and long-term client retention.
* Oversee regulatory compliance, safety standards, emergency preparedness, and company policies.
* Partner with regional and corporate leadership to execute strategic initiatives and organizational priorities.
* Support labor relations, workforce planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
* Champion operational best practices, innovation, and quality patient care.

**Minimum Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

**Experience**

* Minimum of five years of progressive management experience, including financial oversight and employee leadership.
* Demonstrated success in operational management, strategic planning, and relationship development.
* Healthcare or emergency medical services industry experience is strongly preferred.
* Air Medical Industry experience is highly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Strong business and financial acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, and profit and loss management.
* Proven ability to lead teams, execute strategic initiatives, and deliver measurable business results.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, negotiation, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
* Knowledge of healthcare operations, regulatory requirements, and clinical practices preferred.
* Ability to travel approximately 50% within assigned areas as needed.
* Must meet AMR's driving and insurability requirements.

Why Choose GMR? Global Medical Response (GMR) and its family of solutions are dedicated to delivering compassionate, quality medical care, primarily in the areas of emergency and patient relocation services. Here you’ll embark on meaningful work that will make an impact on you and the customers we serve. View the stories on how our employees provide care to the world at www.AtaMomentsNotice.com.

GMR’s Core Behaviors—keep care at the center, raise your hand, seek to understand, find a way together and be accountable—unite our teams and set us apart in emergency medical services.

EEO Statement:

Global Medical Response and its family of companies are an Equal Opportunity Employer, which includes supporting veterans and providing reasonable accommodations for individuals with a disability.

Visit our benefits page to explore comprehensive benefits options.

role.title: 7 Brew Director of Operations
role.description:
Description:

**Why 7 Brew? Because We Invest in YOU!**

At 7 Brew, it’s more than coffee—it’s about brewing smiles one cup at a time. We’re built on kindness, connection, and community, and every guest interaction is an opportunity to make someone’s day brighter.

Brewtopia, a passionate franchise group, is proud to bring the bold energy of 7 Brew to Southeast Michigan. With proven success in quick-service restaurants, we’re dedicated to operational excellence, people-first leadership, and a high-energy drive-thru experience that stands out.

We’re looking for a high-energy, people-first Director of Operations to lead our drive-thru coffee operations. This is a unique opportunity to shape the culture, systems, and guest experience from the ground up—and to grow with us as we expand.

**OUR VALUES**

* Strive for Excellence – We raise the bar every day.
* Elevate Others – We build people up.
* Results Driven – We focus on impact.
* Visionary – We dream big and lead with purpose.
* Exceed Expectations – We go beyond what’s expected.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

* **Competitive Salary:** $125,000 base per year
* **Performance Bonus:** 15% target, tied to KPIs and company performance
* **Comprehensive Benefits:** Health insurance, 401K with competitive match, generous PTO
* **Car Allowance:** Up to $500 /month
* **Cellphone Stipend:** Up to $25 a pay
* **Growth & Learning:** Clear development plans and a culture of continuous improvement
* **More Than Coffee:** Infused energy drinks, Italian sodas, smoothies, teas, and more!

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

The Director of Operations ensures consistency, quality, and efficiency across all locations—protecting the brand and growing guest loyalty. This role optimizes profitability, develops strong leaders, and executes strategic growth initiatives with relentless focus on the guest.

* **Operations & Guest Experience:** Oversee day-to-day operations across multiple drive-thru shops, ensuring speed of service, drink quality, food safety, cleanliness, and brand consistency.
* **Team Leadership & Development:** Lead, mentor, and develop Regional Leaders and General Managers, fostering a culture of accountability, recognition, and continuous growth.
* **Financial Management & Strategic Growth:** Own the P&L, manage labor and COGS, drive sales and flow-through, and collaborate with leadership to execute growth strategies and support new shop openings.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

* **Drive Growth & Profitability:** Regularly review and adjust the budget and financial reports to ensure cost goals are met. Implement strategies to optimize labor, track performance against financial goals, and ensure key profit-driving actions are executed in a timely manner.
* **Ensure Operational Excellence:** Conduct daily operational reviews to ensure adherence to brand standards. Regularly assess performance metrics, respond to customer feedback, and implement action plans to improve service quality.
* **Lead & Develop Teams:** Hold weekly one-on-one coaching sessions with Regional Managers, ensuring consistent training and development. Work with HR and other departments to fill staffing gaps quickly and develop training programs that align with business needs.
* **Foster Guest Satisfaction & Compliance:** Address and resolve guest concerns within 24 hours, ensuring that guest satisfaction is prioritized.
* **Collaborate & Align:** Actively participate in weekly leadership meetings, contribute to discussions, and align team goals with corporate objectives. Share progress updates and ensure all team members are informed and working toward shared priorities.
* **Culture Keeper:** Foster a recognition culture, coach privately and praise publicly, and promote healthy competition and collaboration across locations.

Requirements:

**ESSENTIAL SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Leadership & Team Management:** Proven ability to build, coach, and scale high-performing multi-unit teams
* **Financial Acumen:** Budgeting, P&L ownership, labor modeling, KPI-driven decisions
* **Operational Excellence:** Multi-unit drive-thru/QSR expertise with a bias for speed, quality, and safety
* **Problem-Solving and Decision-Making:** Data-driven, resourceful, and decisive in a fast-paced environment
* **Communication:** Clear, candid communicator across shop, field, and corporate partners
* **Customer Focus:** Passion for delivering exceptional guest experiences consistently
* **Strategic Planning & Execution:** Translate goals into disciplined, scalable routines
* **Compliance & Safety:** Knowledge of health, safety, and regulatory standards
* **Technology Proficiency:** POS/back-office, labor scheduling, spreadsheets/dashboards

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Multi-unit leadership in QSR/coffee/drive-thru; ideally **2+ years in a director-level role**
* Bachelor's in business management, Hospitality, or related field is a plus

**PHYSICAL AND TIME REQUIREMENTS**

* **General Mobility:** Sit, stand, bend, and move for extended periods during meetings, presentations, or line work
* **Manual Dexterity:** Proficiency in typing and using office equipment such as computers, printers, and phones
* **Visual and Auditory Acuity:** Ability to read printed and digital documents; clear hearing for communication
* **Lifting and Carrying:** Ability to lift and carry items weighing up to 50 pounds
* **Travel:** Frequent travel to multiple locations (>75%)

**TIME REQUIREMENT**

* Availability to primarily work during areas of business growth, including nights and weekends.

**Ready to bring the brew and bring your best?**

Join the Brewtopia movement today! If you’re ready for an epic, energetic, and rewarding journey, we’d love to have you on the crew. But first – let’s get to know you better! Start your journey with us by completing a quick **5-7 minute Culture Index survey**. It's a key part of the process, and we promise – it’s quick, easy, and essential!

Survey Link: https://surveys.cultureindex.com/s/y8HlLcvMA4/93831

**Disclaimer**

This job description outlines the general responsibilities and expectations of the role. It is not an exhaustive list of all duties, skills, or requirements.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants will be considered fairly and without discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status. Hiring decisions are made solely on job-related qualifications and business needs.

role.title: Managing Director, Academic Program Operations
role.description:
**About Achievement First**

Achievement First (AF) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization that currently supports 41 public charter schools in New York, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. Consistently rated as one of the top charter school networks in the country for almost 25 years, AF is committed to continuous improvement, programmatic evolution for enhanced student outcomes, and sustainable growth. The majority of AF students are Black and Latinx children from low-income families who will be the first in their families to graduate from college. AF currently employs more than 2,200 staff — 64% of whom identify as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color — who collectively educate nearly 15,000 students in Brooklyn and Queens, NY; New Haven, Bridgeport, and Hartford, CT; and Providence, RI.

The mission of Achievement First is to deliver on the promise of equal educational opportunity for all of America's children. AF knows that every child—regardless of race, zip code, or economic status—deserves access to great schools. At AF, students realize their potential and develop the skills they need to graduate from high school, succeed in college, thrive in a competitive world, and serve as the next generation of leaders in their communities. At AF, students and staff embark on a shared journey to fulfill their incredible potential.

*We are looking for a* Managing Director of Academic Program Operations *to join our Academic Strategy & Execution team.*

**Your Impact**

The Managing Director of Academic Program Operations will serve as a senior strategic partner and operations expert working with the Academic Program Team to deliver on the implementation of Achievement First's school model & instructional priorities. This role is ideal for someone who has a deep knowledge of schools both as instructional institutions but also the intersection with funding, finance, operations, and talent practices. The Managing Director of of Academic Program Operations will partner with the Deputy Chief of Academic Strategy & Execution and other senior program leaders to deliver on a cohesive & coherent experience of our school model and support the change management involved in refining our model to align to our aims for our Achievement First graduates anchored in knowledge of self & community, college, career, & life readiness, and purpose & leadership. The Managing Director of Academic Program Operations does not need to be the content expert in any given domain, but should be a fast learner able to bring people together to solve challenges & inspire change, and be able to communicate across a variety of stakeholders including school leaders & school based staff, as well as leaders of functional teams in the organization.

*Reporting directly to the Deputy Chief of Academic Strategy & Execution you will be responsible for:*

* Managing the implementation of our current school design and instructional priorities
* + Run the project-to-operations transition gate for school design changes. Accept finished projects into standing ownership only once standard work, calendars, budget, reporting, and escalation paths are in place.
 + Set service levels for each recurring function and run an annual improvement cycle that names what to automate, transition, or outsource.
 + Manage vendor and contract relationships for recurring academic infrastructure, including renewals and performance against agreed terms.
 + Lead the Academic Operations portion of the work and talent review: inventory current work, classify it as keep, stop, or transfer, and match people to defined roles.
 + Oversee the annual planning, operations actions and execution needed across curriculum, assessment, professional learning operations, school budget development, calendar and the operations behind our instructional priorities needed to deliver our current model and priorities with excellence
 + Partner with Deputy Chiefs of School Design, and senior Academic Program leads to operationalizing our current design, recommend operational decisions for the following year and execute once decided around current policies and strategies.
 + Organize the Academic Operations team around needed capabilities and organizational impact
 + Manage Academic Operations team budget and set up monitoring systems to ensure accurate monthly forecasting each month
 + Manage a team of 4-6 direct reports who support implementation, decision making and execution of our current model.

* Drive excellence and improvement across all Academic Program infrastructure and operations
* + Curriculum and materials: Own purchasing, publication, distribution, and materials planning for network curriculum, so every classroom has what it needs before the first day of school.
 + Assessment: Run administration of state, College Board, and internal assessments, including testing windows, platforms, compliance, audits, and score reporting. Maintain the network assessment calendar. Identify which steps can be automated or outsourced to free up team capacity.
 + Professional learning: Oversee the operations behind summer and school year PD. This covers calendars, venues, registration, materials, logistics, and completion tracking. Partner with the content owners who design each training.

* Define distinct recurring academic operating functions from school management related services
* + Publish and maintain a scope map for Academic Operations and School Management Services that names what each team owns and partners on, with RAPID roles for shared decisions.
 + Own the network-level version of recurring infrastructure: academic calendar, assessment windows, materials timelines, and PD calendars.
 + Build one intake path for school and regional requests.
 + Hold the regional support work currently carried by current team until the School Management Services defined then hand it off with documented standard work.
 + Review the boundary twice a year. Track misrouted or duplicated work and move it to its right home before either team turns into a catch-all.

* Strategic Leadership, Annual Planning and Cross-Functional Operations Management (yearly & ad-hoc)
* + Set clear standards of excellence for each function, performance manage, and build specialized expertise on the team.
 + In partnership with senior project managers, oversee and manage a cohesive approach to planning for the upcoming school year each year. Deliverables include school regional calendars, comprehensive network policies/consistent practices for schools and serving as a gatekeeper on recurring academic tasks and events added to the school calendar.
 + Serve as a key thought partner to senior leaders to ensure efficiency, effectiveness and optimal use of all available resources and personnel across program teams.
 + Strategize with senior leaders on academic policy development and problem resolution; ensure implementation plans are effectively communicated and managed.

Additionally, this role will support the work of the team with ad hoc needs, including building operational documents, peer review of detailed resources, data entry, etc.

**Candidate Profile**

All candidates for this position will have a bachelor's degree and 2+ years of experience managing managers and leading complex, recurring operations across multiple stakeholders. An ideal candidate will have 2+ years of successful teaching experience, and/or a background in school operations or school leadership. There is a preference for candidates based in the regions where our schools are located (New York, Connecticut, and Rhode Island). The successful candidate must commit to being on-site in New York, Connecticut, and/or Rhode Island during July and August.

*In addition, the following characteristics are required to be successful on this team:*

* Track record of managing managers: setting clear standards of excellence, giving direct and timely feedback, and building specialized expertise on a team
* Judges success by results for schools. Willing to stop, automate, or outsource work that isn't producing them
* Owns problems through to resolution, works with peers before escalating, and brings escalations with options and a recommendation attached
* Acts on what the work needs without waiting to be asked, and brings a clear point of view when a decision sits above the role
* Experience building and running recurring operations at scale, including standard work, service levels, annual planning calendars, and continuous improvement
* Experience managing a department budget with accurate monthly forecasting, plus vendor and contract management
* Experience running large, multi-site training events and logistics
* Comfort with assessment and data platforms, and the ability to turn operational data into clear reporting
* Experience leading a team through organizational change, including role changes and new ways of working
* Confident in interacting with and influencing individuals at all levels, including state departments of education and external partners
* Exceptional eye for detail, follow-up, and organization
* Excellent verbal and written communication, with the ability to explain complex ideas simply
* Belief in the Achievement First mission and educational model

**Travel Expectations**

This is a hybrid role. The expectation is that the person in the role would be able to come into the Network Support office (NYC, CT, or RI) at least three times a week. There may be additional travel to regions outside of your own on a monthly basis.

**Compensation** 
Achievement First sets salaries through a lens of equity, based on the skills, education, and experience the role requires. The salary range for this position is $150,331 to $183,002. We place new hires within this range based on their years of experience in a comparable position, using the same criteria for every candidate. Most new hires should expect an offer at or below the midpoint of the range ($166,667). Additionally, Achievement First offers all regular, full-time employees a comprehensive benefits package that includes paid time off, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, a 403(b) retirement plan with match, and paid Family Leave.

*Achievement First is an equal opportunity employer and an organization that values diversity. People from all diverse backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply. Spanish language proficiency is a plus. You can learn more about diversity at Achievement First here:* *http://achievementfirst.org/about-us/diversity/*

role.title: Director, Enterprise Strategy and Operations (R5626)
role.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

Shield AI is seeking a Strategy & Operations Director to help define enterprise strategy and ensure its operational execution. This role offers immersive exposure to the company’s most critical decisions — spanning aircraft systems, AI software (Hivemind), autonomy hardware, and international growth.

As a core member of the Strategy & Operations team, you’ll apply structured problem‑solving, financial rigor, and operational discipline to turn strategic priorities into actionable, measurable outcomes. The role combines high‑performance expectations with a strong learning and development environment — ideal for professionals seeking to grow into future strategy, operations, or general management leaders.

What you'll do:

 - Enterprise Strategy Development:
 
 - Lead the multi‑year strategic planning and annual operating strategy cycles.
 
 - Evaluate portfolio tradeoffs across platforms, software, hardware, and emerging growth vectors.
 
 - Conduct market sizing, competitive analysis, and scenario modeling across U.S. and allied defense markets.
 
 Capital Allocation & Business Case Rigor:
 
 - Build financial models and analytic frameworks for investment decisions (new platforms, manufacturing, international expansion).
 
 - Assess TAM, margin structure, capital intensity, payback, and risk‑adjusted returns.
 
 - Contribute to the development of enterprise‑wide capital allocation frameworks and governance processes.
 
 Operationalization of Strategy:
 
 - Translate strategic priorities into cross‑functional execution plans with defined KPIs and milestones.
 
 - Track and report on progress through structured operating cadences (monthly and quarterly performance reviews).
 
 - Identify bottlenecks, analyze root causes, and recommend actionable solutions to sustain execution velocity.

Required qualifications:

 - Min 12+ years of experience with Bachelors, 8+ with Masters, and 5+ with PhD.

 - Min 4+ years’ experience in a top-tier strategy consulting, corporate strategy or other high‑rigor roles.

 - Strong analytical and conceptual problem‑solving abilities.

 - Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive insight through analysis.

 - Financial modeling and analytical capability (unit economics, forecasting, scenario analysis).

 - Experience or strong interest in complex, technical, or regulated industries (aerospace, defense, AI, or advanced manufacturing preferred).

 - Ability to work collaboratively across teams and influence senior stakeholders.

 - U.S. citizenship required (ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance).

#LI-AD7

#LF

Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity

 

Temporary employee offer package:

Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)

 

Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.

Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.
