role.title: Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking) 5680
role.description:
**Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking)**

**Direct Hire**

**Onsite - Windsor, CO**

**Position Summary**

The Director, Manufacturing Operations (Bulking) provides leadership and accountability for sterile and non-sterile bulking operations within a regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environment. This role is responsible for safe, compliant, reliable, and efficient execution of manufacturing activities, including production performance, product quality, process reliability, workforce capability, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead day-to-day bulking operations across multiple products, processes, and shifts.
* Ensure production schedules are executed safely, compliantly, and efficiently while meeting business and customer commitments.
* Drive performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, capacity, yield, cycle time, right-first-time, and equipment reliability metrics.
* Establish operating standards, performance management routines, and accountability systems across the organization.
* Partner with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, MS&T, Validation, Supply Chain, and Regulatory teams to improve process performance, resolve operational challenges, and support strategic objectives.
* Provide leadership for deviations, investigations, CAPAs, change controls, audits, inspections, and regulatory compliance activities.
* Support technology transfers, process scale-up, validation, equipment qualification, automation initiatives, and implementation of new manufacturing technologies.
* Develop managers, supervisors, technical specialists, and manufacturing teams while building organizational capability and succession pipelines.
* Lead Lean, Six Sigma, standard work, and continuous improvement initiatives to improve reliability, reduce variability, and increase operational efficiency.
* Manage operating budgets, capital investments, staffing plans, and resource allocation while supporting future growth and capacity requirements.

**Knowledge, Skills & Abilities**

* Strong knowledge of pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, including aseptic processing, contamination control, and cGMP requirements.
* Ability to lead a diverse portfolio of complex manufacturing processes while establishing consistent standards across products, teams, and shifts.
* Demonstrated success leading and developing managers and frontline teams in a regulated manufacturing environment.
* Strong understanding of process control, equipment reliability, validation, technology transfer, and manufacturing scale-up.
* Ability to interpret production, quality, capacity, and financial data and translate it into clear priorities and executable plans.
* Proficiency in risk assessment, root cause analysis, deviation investigation, CAPA, and change management.
* Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery, cost, workforce capability, and operational performance through disciplined execution.
* Strong judgment and decision-making skills, including the ability to balance patient safety, compliance, supply, and business needs.
* Effective communicator with the ability to influence senior leaders, technical partners, and frontline teams and represent Manufacturing during audits and inspections.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional work with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, MS&T, Validation, Supply Chain, and Regulatory partners.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, tiered management, standard work, or comparable continuous improvement systems.
* Strategic, hands-on, and adaptable leadership style suited to a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Biological Sciences, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or another STEM discipline required; advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments, including significant production operations leadership experience.
* Significant experience in sterile or aseptic manufacturing operations required; experience with formulation, compounding, bulking, filling, or related processing strongly preferred.
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including leadership of leaders and/or multi-shift manufacturing teams.
* Demonstrated success improving operational performance, building workforce capability, and leading cross-functional change in a regulated environment.

role.title: Sr Manager, Quality Assurance Engineering (Hybrid - Acton, MA)
role.description:
**Job Summary**
This Senior Manager, Quality Engineering role is a key leadership position responsible for overseeing Insulet’s global Design Transfer Quality Engineering team and ensuring new and modified Omnipod products and manufacturing processes are successfully transferred, validated, and sustained in compliance with FDA and ISO quality standards. The position leads a team of Quality Engineers supporting product launches, manufacturing expansion, process validation, risk management, CAPA, and continuous improvement initiatives across global manufacturing sites. The ideal candidate brings extensive medical device quality experience, deep expertise in design transfer, process validation, and regulatory compliance, along with proven people leadership skills. Success in this role requires partnering across Manufacturing, Operations, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, and Quality organizations to drive quality strategy, support global growth initiatives, and maintain high standards in a complex, high-volume regulated manufacturing environment.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Quality Engineering leads Insulet's global Design Transfer Quality Engineering team, ensuring new and changed Omnipod products and manufacturing processes are successfully transferred to production, validated and sustained in compliance with the Insulet Quality System, FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485 and ISO 14971. The Sr. Quality Engineering Manager leads a team of Quality Engineers to support design transfer, capacity expansion, and process controls across Insulet's manufacturing sites. The Senior Manager establishes quality strategy, owns key QMS procedures and metrics, represents Quality throughout major design transfer and global expansion initiatives, and partners closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, R&D, Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders. The ideal candidate is an experienced medical device quality leader who builds strong teams, makes sound risk-based decisions and drives continuous improvement in a highly regulated, high-volume manufacturing environment at a global scale.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Lead, coach and develop a team of Quality Engineers; set priorities, manage workload and resourcing, conduct performance reviews and development plans, and lead hiring.
* Serve as Quality lead for the design transfer of new products and product design changes, ensuring quality deliverables (e.g. Project Quality Plans, Design Transfer Plans, Product Launch Plans) are created and properly executed through each phase gate.
* Serve as global process owner for Production & Process Controls and Design Transfer including procedure continuous improvement, performance monitoring of KPIs, and development of new or expanded processes to support Insulet’s growing production capacity.
* Support manufacturing process validation, equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) and Test Method Validation for new manufacturing lines, capacity expansion, site transfers and equipment upgrades; review and approve plans, protocols and reports.
* Drive process risk management across all sites, including pFMEA governance and integration of nonconformance and production data into risk management.
* Lead remediation and compliance initiatives and provide Quality oversight of CAPAs, investigations, quality events and nonconformances, ensuring effective root cause analysis and verification of effectiveness.
* Partner with global manufacturing sites and contract manufacturers to deploy harmonized quality and process improvements.
* Provide Quality leadership for enterprise systems and digital initiatives (e.g. SAP, MES, eDHR, eQMS).
* Prepare and present quality metrics and project status for operations leadership, QMS process owner forums, and management review.
* Support internal and external audits as a subject matter expert, maintain inspection readiness, and serve as the escalation point for cross-functional quality questions from Operations, Engineering and Supply Chain.

**Education And Experience**

* BS degree in engineering, a technical or scientific discipline; and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Master's degree in engineering or technical or scientific discipline preferred.
* Minimum 10 years' experience in Medical Device Quality Assurance.
* 3-5 years' experience managing people, including leading engineers and technical staff.
* In-depth knowledge of FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 and ISO 14971.
* Demonstrated experience leading design transfer and process validation for high-volume manufacturing of single-use products, preferably on automated manufacturing equipment.
* Experience with process risk management (pFMEA), CAPA, nonconformance and change control processes; QMS process ownership experience preferred.
* Experience with statistical methods (e.g. statistical process control, sampling plans, Test Method Validation, gauge R&R, and capability).
* Experience working with global manufacturing sites and contract manufacturers.
* Experience with eQMS/PLM, ERP and data visualization tools, as well as word processing, spreadsheet and database programs.

**Skills/Competencies**

* Proven ability to build, lead and develop high-performing teams, including effective delegation and succession planning.
* Strategic thinking with the ability to organize, judge and balance priorities across multiple complex projects.
* Sound, risk-based decision making in a highly regulated environment.
* Strong verbal (including presentation) and written communication skills, with the ability to influence and present to executive leadership.
* Effective collaboration and communication with individuals at multiple levels and across functions, sites and geographies.
* Strong problem solving / root cause analysis skills.
* Ability to generate and maintain organized and accurate records, and to follow up with task owners to close out open items.

**Other Expectations**

* Flexibility to work across multiple time zones, outside of normal working hours.
* Travel (International) – 10%

*NOTE: This position is eligible for hybrid working arrangements (requires on-site work from an Insulet office).*
**Additional Information**
Compensation & Benefits: For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $138,700.00 - $208,000.00 This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation. We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
 
 

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off (PTO)
* And additional employee wellness programs Application Details: This job posting will remain open until the position is filled. To apply, please visit the Insulet Careers site and submit your application online. Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.
 
 
We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!
 
 
At Insulet Corporation all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.
 
 
(Know Your Rights)

role.title: Sr. Director of Quality
role.description:
The Senior Director of Quality is responsible for leading quality, regulatory compliance, and functions at an assigned facility while providing strategic leadership, guidance, and support to Quality departments across multiple FCAH locations and operating companies. This role ensures compliance with applicable FAA, EASA, customer, and industry requirements while driving consistency in quality standards, processes, audit readiness, corrective actions, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.

The Senior Director serves as a hands-on quality leader at their assigned location while partnering with site leadership and other Quality leaders to strengthen quality systems, address regulatory and operational risks, develop quality teams, and promote a culture of accountability, safety, and excellence across the organization.

**Essential Job Functions:**

**Site Quality Leadership**

* Lead and manage the Quality department at the assigned facility, ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company requirements.
* Partner with site leadership, Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other departments to integrate quality into daily operations and decision-making.
* Oversee site quality personnel, including staffing, performance management, training, development, and accountability.
* Ensure the facility maintains required certifications, approvals, manuals, procedures, and quality systems.
* Monitor site quality performance, identify areas of risk, and develop action plans to address deficiencies and improve operational performance.

**Multi-Site Quality Leadership & Support**

* Provide leadership, guidance, and support to Quality departments and leaders across other First Class Air operating companies and locations.
* Partner with site Quality leaders to identify challenges, strengthen quality processes, and improve regulatory compliance and operational effectiveness.
* Promote consistency in quality standards, processes, procedures, and best practices across locations where appropriate.
* Assist other locations with quality initiatives, regulatory concerns, audit preparation, corrective actions, customer issues, and process improvement efforts.
* Conduct site visits to evaluate quality systems, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide support to local Quality teams.
* Share lessons learned, recurring quality issues, and best practices across locations to prevent repeat findings and improve overall organizational performance.
* Help develop and implement company-wide quality initiatives while allowing for site-specific requirements, certifications, and regulatory differences.
* Escalate significant regulatory, operational, customer, or quality risks to executive leadership.

**Regulatory Compliance & Oversight**

* Ensure compliance with applicable FAA, EASA, UK CAA, , customer, and other regulatory requirements, as applicable to company operations.
* Maintain strong working knowledge of FAA regulations, including Part 145, Part 43, and Part 21, as applicable.
* Serve as a point of contact for regulatory authorities, customer representatives, and external auditors, as appropriate.
* Monitor regulatory changes and ensure applicable requirements are communicated and implemented across affected locations.
* Ensure maintenance, repair, overhaul, inspection, manufacturing, and other applicable activities are performed in accordance with approved technical data, regulatory requirements, and established procedures.
* Maintain organizational readiness for regulatory, customer, and third-party audits.

**Quality Management Systems**

* Develop, implement, maintain, and continuously improve Quality Management Systems (QMS) at the assigned location and across other locations as needed.
* Establish and promote consistent quality standards, policies, procedures, and best practices across the organization.
* Oversee the development, revision, and implementation of quality manuals, procedures, inspection programs, and supporting documentation.
* Ensure appropriate document control, records management, inspection processes, calibration programs, personnel qualifications, training, and other critical quality system controls are maintained.
* Partner with site and enterprise leadership to improve quality processes, reduce risk, and enhance operational performance.

**Audits, Corrective Actions & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead and oversee internal, external, regulatory, customer, and third-party audits at the assigned facility.
* Support and provide guidance to other locations in preparation for and execution of audits.
* Develop and support risk-based audit schedules and audit strategies.
* Ensure audit findings and quality issues are appropriately investigated, contained, corrected, and documented.
* Oversee corrective and preventive action (CAPA) processes and ensure root cause analysis is appropriately performed.
* Verify corrective actions are effective and prevent recurring issues.
* Identify recurring findings, systemic quality issues, and trends across locations and implement improvements where appropriate.

**Airworthiness & Technical Quality**

* Provide oversight of airworthiness and return-to-service processes across applicable repair station operations.
* Ensure appropriate controls are maintained for FAA Form 8130-3, EASA Form 1, inspection, certification, and related airworthiness documentation, as applicable.
* Ensure receiving, in-process, and final inspections are performed in accordance with applicable procedures and requirements.
* Oversee the management and control of capability lists, personnel authorizations, technician and inspector qualifications, stamps, and related records.
* Ensure calibration programs and control of tools, equipment, and test instruments meet applicable requirements.
* Assist other locations with technical quality concerns, inspection processes, airworthiness issues, and regulatory interpretations as needed.

**Customer & Supplier Quality**

* Provide leadership and support in resolving significant customer quality concerns, escalations, and recurring issues.
* Partner with Sales, Operations, Maintenance, and other departments to ensure customer quality expectations are understood and met.
* Monitor supplier-related quality trends and recurring issues.
* Support supplier corrective actions, quality investigations, and improvement initiatives as needed.
* Serve as a quality escalation resource for customer and supplier issues across locations.

**Quality Performance, Reporting & Risk Management**

* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, KPIs, trends, and reporting processes for the assigned facility.
* Support the development and implementation of company-wide quality dashboards and performance metrics.
* Evaluate quality data to identify trends, recurring issues, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Communicate significant quality concerns, regulatory risks, audit findings, and improvement initiatives to site leadership and executive leadership.
* Partner with leadership to prioritize quality initiatives and allocate resources appropriately.
* Provide visibility into quality performance across locations and recommend actions to improve overall company performance.

**Requirements:**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in aviation, aerospace, MRO, manufacturing, or another highly regulated environment.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive leadership experience in Quality, Regulatory Compliance,, Inspection, or related functions preferred.
* Significant experience leading Quality functions within aviation maintenance, repair, overhaul, manufacturing, or FAA-certified repair station environments.
* Experience supporting multiple departments, facilities, locations, or business units.
* Experience working directly with FAA, EASA, UK CAA, customer representatives, or other regulatory authorities preferred.
* Demonstrated experience leading regulatory, customer, internal, and external audits.
* Experience developing, implementing, and maintaining Quality Management Systems.
* Strong working knowledge of FAA regulations, particularly Part 145, Part 43, and Part 21, as applicable.
* Knowledge of EASA, UK CAA,, and other applicable regulatory requirements preferred.
* Strong understanding of Quality Management Systems (QMS), corrective and preventive action (CAPA), root cause analysis, risk management, audit processes, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to interpret technical data, regulatory requirements, manuals, procedures, engineering documentation, and quality standards.
* This role will require 20%-30% travel to other facilities

role.title: Director of Quality Assurance & CI
role.description:
**Lead the Transformation. Build a Culture of Excellence. Deliver Results That Last.**

The Director of Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement provides strategic leadership for the company's quality and continuous improvement functions, ensuring products, processes, and services consistently meet the highest standards of quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving the Quality Management System (QMS) while driving a culture of operational excellence across the organization. Leading enterprise-wide Lean initiatives, Kaizen events, root cause analysis, and structured continuous improvement programs, this position delivers measurable improvements in quality, productivity, cost, and operational performance. Working closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, the Director establishes quality strategies, drives compliance with customer and regulatory requirements, and champions sustainable improvements that support the company's strategic growth objectives.

**What Success looks Like**

* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the company's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry standards, including ISO certifications.
* Establish enterprise-wide quality strategies, policies, and governance while serving as the executive leader for quality-related decisions impacting customers, operations, and suppliers.
* Drive a culture of operational excellence by leading Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and structured continuous improvement initiatives across all business functions.
* Develop and execute strategic cost reduction initiatives that improve productivity, eliminate waste, reduce the Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and enhance overall operational performance.
* Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, and executive leadership to identify, prioritize, and deliver sustainable business improvements.
* Champion the voice of the customer by leveraging customer feedback, warranty data, and field performance to improve product quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead enterprise-wide root cause analysis and corrective action processes to resolve quality issues, prevent recurrence, and strengthen operational performance.
* Oversee internal and external audit programs, ensuring compliance with quality, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements while proactively managing organizational risk.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Quality and Continuous Improvement organization while coaching leaders throughout the business to embed a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Establish, monitor, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) that measure quality, delivery, cost savings, productivity, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement performance.
* Translate strategic business objectives into measurable quality and operational improvement initiatives that deliver sustainable financial and operational results.
* Build trusted relationships across the organization and with external stakeholders, influencing decision-making and driving alignment to achieve the company's strategic objectives.

**Qualifications That Shine**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master's degree or other advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive quality leadership experience, including 10+ years leading people and 5+ years leading corporate or multi-site quality organizations.
* Proven success developing and leading Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a manufacturing environment, including ISO implementation, certification, and ongoing compliance.
* Professional certifications such as ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, and Lean certification are strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading Lean transformation, Kaizen events, and enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that deliver measurable business results.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), statistical process control (SPC), and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence executive leadership and build collaborative partnerships across operations, engineering, supply chain, finance, and commercial teams.
* Exceptional communication, presentation, and organizational skills with the ability to translate strategy into execution and drive organizational change.
* Strategic, data-driven leader with a track record of improving quality, operational performance, customer satisfaction, and financial results through operational excellence initiatives.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here**

* **You’ll Be Empowered** **–** You’ll have autonomy in your role, supported by a team that trusts your judgment
* **You’ll Grow With Us** **–** We invest in your training, development, and long-term career path
* **You’ll Be Rewarded** **–** Competitive pay, performance incentives, 401(k) with profit sharing, and great benefits
* **You’ll Make a Real Impact** **–** Your work supports businesses across North America and shapes the future of finishing technology
* **You’ll Join a Great Team** **–** We’re growing fast, we value collaboration, and are committed to your success

**Transparent Rewards** 
 
At GFS, we recognize the dedication behind every role and ensure that our compensation reflects both your impact and our shared success.

**Pay Range:** $124,518 – $156,746 per year, based on your experience, skills, and qualifications.

**Bonus Eligibility:** This position is eligible for an annual individual incentive based on company performance. Maximum bonus amounts may vary depending on role.

**Benefits:** Eligible for standard company benefits, including health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, paid time off, and other employee programs. More detailed information is available at 2026 GFS Benefits.

Actual compensation will be determined by factors including experience, education, certifications, skill level, and market conditions. For remote or hybrid positions, the listed pay range applies to applicants in the specified location.

**About GFS**

Global Finishing Solutions is the leading manufacturer of paint booths and finishing systems serving automotive, aerospace, industrial manufacturing, marine, military, rail, trucking, and wood finishing markets. We specialize in building custom solutions that meet each customer’s unique needs—and we do it with a team that thrives on collaboration and innovation because we're different.

What makes us different is our unwavering commitment to our core values of family, respect, partnership, improvement, and integrity. We are a family-oriented organization that still values the little things, creating a workplace where you can thrive, fairness guides every decision, and collaboration drives shared success. Small town in spirit but big-hearted in impact, here you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a team that grows together, celebrates together, and builds lasting value together. That’s the difference. Join us.

Apply now at www.gfscareers.us

About GFS 
Watch Us in Action 
Connect on LinkedIn

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

***GFS is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants***. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or any other status protected by law. Employment offers are subject to successful completion of pre-employment drug screening and physicals, consistent with applicable laws.

*Note to recruiters: GFS only works with agencies that have signed a contract with our HR team. Resumes sent directly to hiring managers without a prior agreement are considered unsolicited and the property of GFS. Placement fees will not be paid without a formal contract.*

role.title: Director, Operations & Quality Compliance
role.description:
**Summary**

We are seeking a Director, Global Safety Operations & Quality Management to provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership across Immunic's PV operations, quality management, compliance, and inspection readiness activities for our development and post-marketing portfolio, reporting to the VP of Pharmacovigilance & Patient Safety as a key member of the Global PV leadership team. You will oversee global safety reporting, ICSR processing, aggregate reporting, safety surveillance, quality management systems, compliance, and inspection readiness, ensuring PV activities are governed, risk-based, and scalable, while providing executive-level oversight of CROs, vendors, and external service providers to ensure governance, performance management, and continuous improvement of outsourced PV activities.This is a highly collaborative and strategic role, where you must operate effectively in an evolving biotech to translate regulatory and business requirements into practical operating models, and build high-performing teams and sustainable PV capabilities.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement pharmacovigilance processes, policies, SOPs, and safety database/PV systems.
* Lead cross-functional governance, benefit-risk assessment, signal detection, and risk management efforts.
* Chair the executive safety review committee, oversee safety data exchange with partners, and contribute to industry-wide safety initiatives.
* Partner with clinical development to integrate safety into protocols, risk management plans, and safety charters.
* Provide PV oversight for regulatory filings (IND/BLA/MAA) - including Clinical Overviews, ISS, and RMPs - and review IBs, DSURs, and key CSR sections; participate in regulatory meetings as needed.
* Lead medical review of ICSRs and oversee PV team operations, quality, and compliance with global safety regulations.
* Monitor and assess CRO performance on pharmacovigilance activities.
* Recruit, hire, train, mentor, and coach PV staff, and oversee project deliverables and performance evaluations.

**Qualifications & Education**

* Healthcare professional (RN, PharmD, MD) with clinical and industry experience and a proven track record leading pharmacovigilance teams.
* Minimum of 15 years' experience in drug safety and pharmacovigilance roles in the biotech or pharmaceutical industry.
* Proven leadership expertise, including a track record of building and leading high-performing teams.
* In-depth knowledge of global pharmacovigilance regulations and compliance requirements (EMA/FDA/ICH).
* Strong leadership and strategic decision-making abilities to drive safety initiatives and ensure regulatory compliance.

Immunic Therapeutics is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status.

**Please note, Immunic does not accept unsolicited resumes from external agencies or recruiters. Submission of a resume without a prior written agreement does not create any express or implied contract between Immunic and the agency. Immunic will not pay any fees related to unsolicited resumes.**

Compensation Range: $220K - $260K

role.title: Health, Safety, Environmental & Quality (HSEQ) Director
role.description:
**Join Ferrovial: Where Innovation Meets Opportunity**
======================================================

Are you ready to elevate your career with a global leader in infrastructure solving complex problems and generating a positive outcome on people’s lives? At **Ferrovial** , we are not just a company; we are a community of innovators and trailblazers. Ferrovial is also leading the development of the New Terminal One at JFK International Airport. Ferrovial shares trade under the ticker symbol FER on two stock markets: Nasdaq in the U.S. (Nasdaq100 Index) and the Spanish Stock Exchanges (IBEX 35). Ferrovial is included in globally recognized sustainability indices such as the Dow Jones Best-in-Class Index. We operate in more than 15 countries and have a workforce of over 22,000 professionals worldwide. Ferrovial’s activity is carried out through our business units, including Highways, Airports, Construction, and Energy.

 

Ferrovial’s activity is carried out through our business units, including Highways, Airports, Construction, and Energy.

 

**Why Ferrovial?**

* **Global presence, local impact** : Be part of a company that is shaping the future of infrastructure worldwide, with challenging roles and projects that make a real difference.
* **Collaborative excellence** : Work alongside talented professionals in a collaborative environment where your ideas and contributions are valued.
* **Inclusive Culture:** Thrive in an innovative and respectful workplace that values every voice, celebrates what makes us unique and turns differences into innovation.
* **Career growth** : Benefit from global and cross-business unit mobility, with development processes designed to ensure your professional growth.
* **Compelling benefits and employee wellbeing** : Enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that rewards your hard work and dedication and take advantage of initiatives designed to support your physical and psychological health.
* **Productivity tools** : Utilize cutting-edge tools like Microsoft Copilot to enhance your productivity and efficiency.

 

**Job Description:**
====================

**About the role:**

The HSEQ Director develops and implements health, safety, environmental, and quality programs for I-24 Mobility Partners and ensures compliance with OSHA, U.S. DOT, EPA, and Tennessee requirements. The Director owns the Quality Management System and Quality Management Plan, verifies program effectiveness through audits, inspections, and investigations, and has authority to stop work when there is an imminent hazard to people, property, or the environment.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Review design-builder and sub-consultant quality and safety plans for alignment with the concessionaire's plans, and work with the Chief Infrastructure Officer on quality oversight of design and construction.

* Liaise with TDOT, the design-builder, the independent engineer, and external auditors on quality, safety, and environmental matters.

* Develop, implement, and continuously improve HSEQ programs, and communicate regulatory requirements and action plans to the team.

* Oversee the quality management personnel, and document control, and report HSEQ performance to stakeholders.
* Support case management of occupational injuries and illnesses, including light-duty programs, return to work, and workers' compensation information.

* Implement and own the Quality Management System and Quality Management Plan, and fulfill the Quality Manager duties assigned in the concession agreement.

* Stop work when there is an imminent hazard to the health and well-being of employees, property, or the environment.

* Lead periodic Management Reviews of the quality and environmental management systems, and promote compliance with ISO standards.

role.title: Vice President of Operations
role.description:
Vice President of Operations

**Good Hearts Gear**

Position Summary

Good Hearts Gear is seeking a strategic, hands-on Vice President of Operations to lead and scale our operational infrastructure. This executive will oversee day-to-day operations while building the systems, processes, and performance standards needed to support growth, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, and healthy margins.

The VP of Operations will lead key functions including supply chain, inventory, fulfillment, vendor management, production coordination, process improvement, and customer support operations. This role will also oversee the operational execution of private label and custom product programs, ensuring strong quality, timelines, and scalable processes.

The ideal candidate is an experienced operations leader who can think strategically, execute effectively, and collaborate cross-functionally with sales, marketing, e-commerce, and leadership to support revenue growth and product launch success.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead and manage overall operations for Good Hearts Gear, ensuring efficiency, consistency, and scalability
* Develop and improve operational systems, workflows, SOPs, controls, and KPIs
* Oversee inventory planning, purchasing, fulfillment, logistics, warehousing, and vendor performance
* Improve inventory accuracy, service levels, order accuracy, and cost efficiency
* Lead operational execution for private label and custom product initiatives from development through delivery
* Manage vendor and factory relationships, production timelines, quality standards, sampling, and compliance
* Build repeatable processes for product specifications, approvals, launch readiness, and fulfillment
* Partner with sales, marketing, and e-commerce teams to align operations with demand planning, promotions, launches, and customer expectations
* Monitor operational performance, margin support, productivity, and service quality through dashboards and reporting
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing operations team focused on accountability, responsiveness, and continuous improvement

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive operations leadership experience, including 3–5 years in a senior leadership role
* Experience in apparel, branded merchandise, promotional products, consumer products, e-commerce, distribution, or light manufacturing strongly preferred
* Proven success managing supply chain, inventory, purchasing, fulfillment, and vendor relationships
* Experience supporting private label, custom product programs, and product development operations
* Strong background in process improvement, SOP development, KPI reporting, and operational scaling
* Experience partnering cross-functionally with sales, marketing, e-commerce, and finance
* Familiarity with ERP, inventory management, order management, and reporting systems
* Experience supporting wholesale and/or big box retail requirements is a plus
* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain, or related field preferred

**Key Skills**

* Strategic operations leadership
* Supply chain and inventory management
* Fulfillment and distribution optimization
* Private label and custom product operations
* Vendor and factory management
* Product development coordination
* Process improvement and performance management
* Financial and margin awareness
* Cross-functional leadership and executive communication

*Full job description available upon request, and will be provided when an interview request is made.*

Pay: From $175,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
Description:

**Join Weiss-Aug – A Leader in Precision Manufacturing and Innovation**

Be part of a company that’s shaping the future of manufacturing where your ideas, skills, and passion matter.

Weiss-Aug, is a leading provider of advanced manufacturing and engineering solutions with advanced facilities across the U.S. and Mexico for over 50 years.

**Why Join Us?**

At Weiss-Aug we are driven by a commitment to excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement. As a recognized leader in the industrial and commercial sectors, specializing in high-volume metal stamping, thermoplastic molding, and value-added assembly solutions for the medical, aerospace & defense, automotive, interconnect, telecommunications and consumer goods industries, we take pride in cultivating a collaborative and forward-thinking work environment.

We're currently seeking a passionate and skilled ***Director of Operations*** to join our team and contribute to our mission of delivering high-quality, engineered solutions to our customers worldwide. In this role you will be responsible for planning and directing line management and related manufacturing support activities including manufacturing floor inspection, manufacturing engineering, materials management and safety/environmental engineering. Establishes and implements manufacturing policies, controls and procedures to further the company's interest in efficiently producing quality products. Contributes to achievement of sales objectives and to the establishment. Prepares or assists in the annual budgets for all departments and is responsible for profit and loss of the division. Manages Manufacturing Managers of Molding and Stamping, Purchasing, Warehouse, Manufacturing Engineering, Customer Service/Planning.

**Responsibilities**

* Management of manufacturing operations. Plans, schedules, organizes, and staffs manufacturing and manufacturing support functions. Assures that all groups within manufacturing organization are properly staffed and coordinated; and that personnel in each group are properly qualified, directed and trained to perform their duties effectively.
* Interprets company sales forecasts and shop orders and establishes accurate manufacturing plans to assure that our customers' requirements are met, that is, defect free product on time.
* Coordinates with Engineering, Sales and new product development engineering to maintain an awareness of current and future product plans.
* Develops and manages material control, manufacturing control, production scheduling, and planning systems to assure achievement of output schedules which will meet company sales requirements.
* Maintains material and parts inventories which are adequate to ensure the fulfillment of production schedules with minimum inventory expense.
* Plans and develops manufacturing facilities and equipment for efficient production of products.
* Works with tooling/engineering to investigate product quality and manufacturing problems and determine the most cost-efficient solutions.
* Develops and assists with the annual budget of all departments; develops and is responsible for all standard costs. Recommends pricing based on the profit objective of the company. Is responsible for the profit and loss of the division.
* Meets or exceeds all TQM measurements as agreed upon annually.
* Is a member of the executive team and steering team which are responsible for the development of company policies and plans.
* Participates with other top managers in the development of company business policies as needed.

Requirements:

* Bachelor's degree Mechanical or Industrial Engineering.
* 8-10 years precision manufacturing experience including some experience in molding. (10 years in management role).
* Strong leadership skills.
* Should have a working knowledge of computerized manufacturing systems.

This position is at our ***East Hanover, NJ*** location.

Pay Range: $150,000 - $180,000

**Other Benefits Include**

* Medical, Dental and Vision
* 401 (k) with company match
* Holiday, Vacation and Sick Time
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Health Savings Accounts (HSA)
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Cigna Wellness Incentive Program
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Short Term Disability
* Group Life and Accidental Insurance
* Sun Life – Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance
* Smoking Cessation Program
* Pet Insurance

**US Pay Transparency**

The base salary for this role will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, experience, and internal consistency.

If your salary requirements exceed the advertised range and you remain interested in Weiss-Aug, we encourage you to apply.

Weiss-Aug is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. Applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other characteristics protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

role.title: Director of Strategy and Operations
role.description:
ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more.

We are seeking a hands-on Director to join our Strategy & Operations team and lead high-impact initiatives that improve how ShipMonk works across departments. Reporting to our Senior Director of Strategy and Operations, you will take our most important cross-functional problems from a blank page to a deployed solution: framing the problem, defining success, building the answer, and proving the results. Your first major initiative will be transforming how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse workforce. 
 
What you'll do: 
 
Lead Cross-Department Initiatives

* Lead major initiatives that improve processes across departments, especially where work, systems, and ownership break down between teams.
* Frame ambiguous problems, define the outcome, and work backward into a solution that teams actually adopt.
* Lead on-site discovery with leaders and frontline teams to understand how work really gets done.

Transform Workforce Management

* Lead the redesign of how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse teams, starting from what the business needs to achieve.
* Pilot solutions in one fulfillment center and scale what works across our network.
* Track the outcomes that matter, such as labor cost, staffing coverage, and retention.

Drive Continuous Improvement

* Help the whole organization work better, improving quality, speed, and the employee and merchant experience, not just cost.
* Spot recurring friction across teams, prioritize the biggest opportunities, and help teams adopt improvements that last.
* Make structured problem solving a habit at every level of the organization.

Strengthen Our Governance

* Support the organization as it matures how it sets priorities, makes decisions, and follows through on commitments.
* Partner with leaders to build governance practices that fit how each team works rather than imposing one structure.
* Bring clear analysis and decision materials to executive discussions.

Analyze, Build, and Drive Adoption

* Analyze productivity, capacity, cost to serve, and profitability, and build models that quantify trade-offs and turn decisions into action.
* Prototype tools and workflows hands-on with AI tools such as Claude, and partner with Engineering and Data to take them to production.
* Spend meaningful time on-site, leading change management so improvements stick rather than fade after launch.

What you'll need:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, supply chain, or a related field
* 3-5 years of experience in operations transformation, strategy, or management consulting, including leading implementations from requirements through deployment and adoption
* A track record of solving ambiguous, cross-functional problems with structured, KPI-driven thinking
* Experience leading process redesign and change management across departments; Lean, Six Sigma, or similar experience is a plus
* Strong analytical and financial modeling skills; SQL or BI experience is a plus
* A hands-on ownership style: comfortable on the warehouse floor and personally driving execution and adoption
* Experience building with AI tools such as Claude to prototype solutions
* Exposure to fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing operations; workforce management experience is a plus
* Strong executive communication and the ability to influence without direct authority
* Ability to travel 25–35%, with more time on-site during discovery and rollouts

**About ShipMonk**

ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL; we're a **growth partner for merchants**. We provide cutting-edge technology and a network of owned and operated fulfillment centers that empower high-growth ecommerce and DTC brands to stress less and grow more. With over 2,500 employees across five countries, we're on a mission to revolutionize fulfillment by providing everything from the fastest click-to-delivery and real-time inventory to custom solutions—all with a **merchant**-**first** mindset.

**Why ShipMonk?**

We believe in building for the long term, and our success is powered by five key differentiators that help us become true partners to our merchants.

* **Global Fulfillment Network:** Our 12+ owned and operated fulfillment centers span the US, Canada, the U.K., and Mainland Europe. We never outsource, ensuring quality and consistency. 
 + **Proprietary Technology:** We've eliminated the need for tribal knowledge with our AI-powered platform. It provides a real-time, unified view of inventory and orders, giving our merchants the control and visibility they need to succeed.
 + **Unrivaled Support:** We provide hands-on, "mom and pop" support with a global reach. Our dedicated teams are on-site at every fulfillment center, ready to jump into action.
 + **Transparent Pricing**: We believe in honest, long-term partnerships. Our all- inclusive pricing means predictable costs, with no hidden fees or surprises.
 + **Committed to the Future:** We invest over $10 million annually in research and development to ensure our technology and services continually evolve, helping merchants plant roots with a partner who is here to stay.

**Our Core Values**

Our values are the heart of our culture. We're looking for individuals who embody these principles every day.

* **Merchant-first:** We handle the logistics so our merchants can focus on what they do best—growing their business.
* **People make ShipMonk:** We believe in our team and invest in our people.
* **Own it:** We take ownership of our work, our mistakes, and our successes.
* **Get sh\*t done:** We're a fast-paced, high-growth company that values action and results.
* **Change the score:** We challenge the status quo, constantly innovating and improving.

 

ShipMonk is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
JELD-WEN is currently seeking a Plant Manager to join our growing team.

 

JELD-WEN is currently seeking a Plant Manager – Craigsville, WV, to join our team.

 

**Summary:** Under the general direction of the Regional Operations Director, the Plant Manager (PM) position is responsible for and directs and manages all plant operations. This position has the overall responsibility for production at their respective manufacturing facility, and for driving JELD-WEN’s Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s), including, but not limited to, SQDCI, JOS, and Continuous Improvement (CI) activities and initiatives in direct support of JELD-WEN’s Mission Statement for their respective product line.

 

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities** include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

 

* Directs and manages all plant operations following JELD-WEN’s Mission Statement and Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s).
* Coordinates all plant activities by working with the management team to ensure that total manufacturing objectives are accomplished in a timely, cost-effective, and efficient manner.
* Develops, controls, plans, and implements the plant budget to maximize profits by utilizing SQDCI, JOS, OTD, and Continuous Improvement (CI) initiatives.
* Implements cost-effective systems of control over operating expenditures, manpower, wages, and salaries, and manages capital asset/improvement projects.
* Establishes and monitors overall plant performance for safety, production, and quality standards, working closely with support groups where appropriate.
* Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment; replaces or submits requests for adjustments to plant facilities and equipment when necessary and as needed.
* Coordinates plant and production activities through strategic planning with the Director of Operations to ensure that total manufacturing objectives are aligned following JELD-WEN’s Mission Statement and KPI’s.
* Oversee the implementation of safety and preventative maintenance programs, incorporating and driving safety procedures and plant cleanliness as a priority.
* Provides leadership and training to accomplish corporate goals/objectives/KPI’s.
* Provides direction, development, and leadership to managerial personnel.
* Hires, trains, develops, and appraises staff effectively. Takes corrective actions as necessary and in a timely manner, following company policy. Consults with Human Resources, Legal, and/or corporate offices as needed on the same.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree in Wood Science/Forest Resources, Engineering, Business, or a related field, and at least seven (7) to ten (10) years’ experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Advanced knowledge and experience in production and manufacturing process improvement techniques including, but not limited to, SQDCI, TPS, OTD, and Continuous Improvement (CI) initiatives and methodologies.
* LEAN manufacturing and/or production process experience is a must.
* Strong knowledge of business, finance, quality control systems, and standards.
* Advanced leadership, interpersonal, technical aptitude, and problem-solving skills, and the ability to lead and drive manufacturing process improvement techniques through the production process skillfully and deliberately.
* A team player, and the ability to coach and mentor managerial personnel, and instill JELD-WEN’s Mission and cultural values in all plant personnel.
* Superior motivational skills and the ability to train and drive CI methods and initiatives into managers and subordinate personnel.
* Fundamental knowledge of engineering principles and practices.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills to include corporate personnel and managers, and rank-and-file plant personnel.
* Advanced knowledge of management principles and practices.
* Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
* Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from corporate, groups of managers, clients, customers, and the general public.
* Proficient in Microsoft Office and other position-applicable software applications.
* Strong knowledge of plant/OSHA health and safety standards and compliance.
* Travel: up to 15% +/-.

 

#LI-KC1

 

**About JELD-WEN Holding, Inc.**

 

JELD-WEN Holding, Inc. (NYSE: JELD) is a leading global designer, manufacturer and distributor of high-performance interior and exterior doors, windows and related building products serving the new construction and repair and remodeling sectors. Based in Charlotte, North Carolina, the company operates across North America and Europe. Our associates are dedicated to bringing beauty and security to the spaces that touch our lives through our market-leading product brands across the world. The JELD-WEN family of brands includes JELD-WEN® worldwide, LaCantina® and VPI™ in North America, and Swedoor® and DANA® in Europe. For more information, visit corporate.JELD-WEN.com or follow LinkedIn.

JELD-WEN has been named by *Forbes* as one of ‘America’s Best Employers’ and by *Newsweek* as one of the ‘World’s Most Trustworthy Companies’.

 

**What We Offer**

Investing in People is one of our Core Values, we strive to attract & retain great people! As such, JELD-WEN offers competitive compensation & benefits packages. As a global organization, specific benefits may vary, however typically including medical & dental, generous leave policies, retirement program, etc.

JELD-WEN is an equal employment opportunity employer and does not tolerate discrimination, harassment, and/or retaliation based on individuals’ physical traits, beliefs, and/or other characteristics that are protected under applicable laws.

JELD-WEN does not accept unsolicited resumes from headhunters, recruitment agencies, or fee-based recruitment services.

role.description:
*At Rockport we understand that quality care starts with safe, efficient, and well-maintained environments. Behind every great facility is a great operations leader—and we’re looking for a* ***Regional Director of Plant Operations******- SoCal/Central Cal*** *who is ready to take charge and make an impact across multiple long-term care communities.*

*If you have hands-on nursing home maintenance experience and know what it takes to keep a healthcare environment compliant, comfortable, and safe, this is your opportunity to lead with purpose and join a team that feels like family!*

***We believe in taking care of our team the way we care for our residents, wholeheartedly!***

* ***Competitive Pay:*** *Your leadership deserves to be rewarded.*
* ***Comprehensive Health Benefits:*** *Health, dental, and vision insurance for you and your family.*
* ***401(k)*** *Plan for your future.*
* ***Paid Time Off & Sick Leave:*** *Recharge, recover, and take care of what matters.*

***Your Role as Regional Director of Plant Operations:***

* *Oversee plant operations and physical maintenance across multiple nursing home and long-term care facilities.*
* *Lead and support on-site Maintenance Directors and teams to ensure full regulatory compliance and operational excellence.*
* *Coordinate all maintenance services and activities with nursing, administration, and other departments.*
* *Direct and oversee a comprehensive preventive maintenance program and ensure each facility maintains a complete and updated Life Safety Binder****.***
* *Develop and maintain written policies, procedures, manuals, job descriptions, work logs, and operational reports.*
* *Monitor building systems including* ***boilers, HVAC, compressors, generators, sprinkler systems****, and other* ***mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems****.*
* *Diagnose, evaluate, and resolve complex facility issues while developing strategic plans for improvements and compliance.*
* *Ensure all facilities meet or exceed local, state, and federal building codes and* ***Life Safety requirements****.*
* *Read and interpret* ***blueprints*** *to plan, manage, and oversee repairs, renovations, and capital improvements.*

***Who we’re looking for:***

* *Must have experience in a nursing home maintenance position*
* *Thorough knowledge of Life Safety regulations and building codes*
* *Hands-on experience with mechanical systems including boilers, HVAC, generators, plumbing, and electrical systems*
* *Ability to read and interpret blueprints and building schematics*
* *Strong leadership skills to diagnose, strategize, and implement facility-wide plans*
* *Skilled in organizing and directing all maintenance programs and staff*
* *Ability to collaborate effectively with other departments and external vendor*
* *Excellent documentation and reporting habits*

Pay: $110,000.00 - $125,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

role.description:
**Plant Manager**

Company: Norris Cylinder Company

Primary Location: 521 Green Cove Road SE, Huntsville, AL 35803 USA

Workplace Type: On-site

Employment Type: Salaried | Full-Time

Function: General / Executive Management

Equal Opportunity Employer Minorities/Women/Veterans/Disabled

**Main Duties & Responsibilities**

**POSITION SUMMARY** 
The Plant Manager is responsible for the facility’s overall operational and financial performance, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and employee engagement. This role leads a team of approximately 120-150 direct and indirect manufacturing employees, including key support functions such as quality, maintenance, shipping/receiving, order management, and supplier management. The position leads steel fabrication and associated support functions and develops the people, processes, and operating discipline required to meet customer and financial objectives.

**PLANT AND FINANCIAL LEADERSHIP** 
Lead plant operations with full accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and operating profit. 
Develop and execute budgets, forecasts, staffing plans, productivity targets, and capital plans. 
Monitor financial and operating performance; address adverse results through clear corrective actions. 
Control labor costs, overtime, premium freight, scrap, rework, outside processing, downtime, and operating expenses. 
Coordinate with engineering, supply chain, commercial, finance, human resources, and other business functions.

**SAFETY AND ENVIRONMENTAL COMPLIANCE** 
Establish safety as the plant’s highest operational priority and ensure compliance with company, OSHA, environmental, permitting, and regulatory requirements. 
Maintain effective controls for machine guarding, lockout/tagout, hot work, powered industrial trucks, overhead cranes, welding fumes, PPE, and emergency response. 
Conduct plant walkthroughs and incident reviews; ensure hazards, injuries, near misses, and environmental concerns receive timely corrective action. 
Maintain high standards for housekeeping, material storage, scrap management, aisle control, and movement of steel and heavy components.

**MANUFACTURING OPERATIONS AND QUALITY** 
Direct steel fabrication processes, including cutting, bending, rolling, forming, welding, machining, assembly, finishing, inspection, and testing, as applicable. 
Establish daily management of production schedules, staffing, equipment, materials, capacity, and customer priorities. 
Ensure employees follow approved work instructions, process parameters, quality requirements, and standard operating procedures. 
Maintain controls for steel grade, material certification, heat or lot traceability, welding procedures, fabrication tolerances, dimensional accuracy, coatings, and final testing. 
Ensure compliance with ISO 9001 and applicable AWS, ASME, DOT, customer, and product requirements. 
Lead root-cause analysis and sustainable corrective action for customer complaints, nonconforming material, scrap, rework, and recurring process failures.

**CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT AND ASSET MANAGEMENT** 
Lead Operational Excellence and Lean methods, including 5S, standard work, visual management, value-stream mapping, setup reduction, mistake-proofing, and structured problem solving. 
Maintain a prioritized improvement plan with defined owners, timelines, expected benefits, and validated results. 
Ensure facilities, equipment, tooling, fixtures, cranes, ventilation, utilities, and material-handling systems are safely and effectively maintained. 
Establish preventive and predictive maintenance programs based on equipment risk and production requirements. 
Manage capital projects from justification through installation, validation, and post-implementation review.

**PEOPLE LEADERSHIP** 
Provide direction, coaching, and development to managers, supervisors, and other plant leaders. 
Establish clear expectations and hold leaders and employees accountable for results and behaviors. 
Build capability through hiring, onboarding, training, cross-training, succession planning, and leadership development. 
Partner with Human Resources on staffing, attendance, turnover, employee relations, performance management, and workforce planning. 
Promote positive employee relations through visible leadership, consistent communication, fair treatment, and shop-floor engagement.

**KEY PERFORMANCE MEASURES** 
Safety and environmental performance; on-time delivery and schedule attainment; first-pass yield, scrap, rework, and customer complaints; labor efficiency, productivity, and overtime; operating profit and conversion cost; equipment uptime; inventory accuracy; project performance; and employee turnover, attendance, training, and engagement.

 

**Qualifications**

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE** 
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations management, business, or a related field. 
Seven or more years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including leadership of managers, supervisors, or multiple manufacturing functions. 
Experience in steel fabrication, welding, machining, metalworking, heavy manufacturing, or a comparable industrial environment. 
Demonstrated responsibility for plant financial and operational performance, budgeting, production planning, quality systems, maintenance, supply chain, and Lean manufacturing. 
ISO 9001 experience and familiarity with applicable AWS, ASME, DOT, customer, or product standards preferred. 
Advanced degree, Lean Six Sigma certification, and experience with capital installations or automated fabrication processes preferred.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES** 
Strong safety leadership, manufacturing knowledge, financial judgment, and ability to translate business results into operating actions. 
Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, communication, and organizational skills. 
Proven ability to develop leaders, build accountable teams, manage multiple priorities, and lead during operational disruptions. 
High integrity, accountability, resilience, and attention to detail.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT** 
The position works in office and manufacturing environments and regularly enters fabrication, welding, machining, finishing, warehouse, and shipping areas. Exposure may include noise, heat, welding operations, fumes, dust, oils, moving equipment, and heavy materials. Required PPE must be worn. Availability to support multiple shifts, shutdowns, equipment issues, and significant customer or production concerns may be required.

**Benefits**

Benefit offerings include Medical Insurance and Prescription Drugs, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Flexible Spending Accounts, Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability Insurance (for eligible employees), Employee Assistance Plan (EAP), Paid Time Off (may include vacation and sick time), Retirement Program, and Other Voluntary Benefits.

role.title: Director of Operations (Skiatook)
role.description:
**Overview:** 
Hayden Industrial is a rapidly scaling manufacturer of advanced industrial cooling and thermal management systems serving high-growth markets including data centers and infrastructure. We are seeking a Director of Operations (Site Leader – Mingo Facility) to lead our Tulsa operation with full ownership of manufacturing, supply chain, and warehousing.

This role is designed for a leader currently operating at—or ready to step into—the scope of a **$100M+ manufacturing site**. You will have broad authority to shape how the operation runs, scales, and performs.

You will be responsible for both **building the next-generation operating model** and **driving immediate performance improvements**. The mandate is clear: create a highly disciplined, scalable operation that can support significant growth while improving cost, delivery, and quality.

This is a **high-impact, high-visibility role** with the opportunity to build a best-in-class operation within a company that is investing heavily in its future.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

 

* **Full Site Ownership**

o Own end-to end performance of the Tulsa site across safety, quality, delivery, and cost.

o Lead manufacturing, supply chain, and warehousing as a fully integrated operation.

o Establish clear accountability and performance standards across all functions.

o Act as the **site leader**, setting expectations, pace, and operating discipline.

* **Build + Scale the Operation**

o Design and implement the **operating system** required to support a $100M+scale operation.

o Build structure, process discipline, and management routines that drive consistency and predictability.

o Develop capacity strategies aligned with aggressive growth targets.

o Lead capital planning and deployment with a focus on throughput, efficiency, and ROI.

* **Drive Operational Performance**

o Improve on-time delivery, schedule adherence, and overall reliability.

o Increase throughput without proportional cost increases.

o Drive labor productivity and cost efficiency across the site.

o Identify and eliminate bottlenecks, constraints, and inefficiencies.

* **Supply Chain & Material Flow Excellence**

o Refine a **high-performing, production-aligned supply chain** at the plant level.

o Improve material availability, planning accuracy, and supplier coordination.

o Optimize inventory levels, accuracy, and working capital performance.

o Lead warehouse operations to ensure efficient flow from receiving through shipping.

* **Continuous Improvement with Measurable Impact**

o Lead Industrial Engineering and Continuous Improvement as core drivers of performance.

o Implement Lean principles focused on outcomes – not activity.

o Establish structured problem-solving and root cause discipline.

o Reduce cost of poor quality (COPQ), including scrap, rework, and inefficiencies.

* **Leadership & Team Transformation**

o Build and lead a high-performance leadership team across all functions.

o Upgrade talent where needed and develop strong internal capability.

o Create a culture of accountability, urgency, and execution.

o Develop succession plans and leadership depth to support continued scale.

* **Cross-Functional Integration**

o Partner with Engineering to ensure manufacturability and smooth new product introduction.

o Align closely with Supply Chain and Commercial teams to match production with demand.

o Ensure operational commitments are realistic, executable, and consistently delivered.

* **Safety & Quality Leadership**

o Champion a safety-first culture with zero tolerance for shortcuts.

o Drive improvements in quality, process capability, and consistency.

o Ensure robust systems are in place and followed across the operation.

 

**Hayden Industrial has determined this position involves safety-sensitive job duties and will be considered a safety-sensitive position for purpose of the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana and Patient Protection Act (“The Unity Bill.”) effective August 29th, 2019.**

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelors degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or Supply Chain

* 12 – 20 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.

* Proven track record leading **large, complex manufacturing operations (approaching or exceeding $100M in scale).**

* Experience with full site ownership including **manufacturing, supply chain, and warehouse operations.**

* Demonstrated success in both:

o Building operational structure in evolving environments

o Driving measurable performance improvements

* Experience in high-growth or scaling environments is strongly preferred.

**Key Traits:**

* **Thinks and operations like business leader**, not just a functional head
* Builder: can create systems, structure, and teams from evolving foundations
* Operator: drives disciplined execution and consistent results
* Hands-on and visible on the floor
* High accountability and ownership mindset
* Pragmatic and results-oriented

**Success Metrics (KPIs):**

* On-time deliveryand schedule adherence
* Labor productivity and cost performance
* Inventory turns, accuracy, and working capital
* Warehouse efficiency and on-time shipment performance
* Cost of poor quality (COPQ)
* Throughput and capacity utilization
* Leadership team strength and retention

**Supervisor Responsibility:** 
This position has supervisory responsibilities.

**Work Environment:** 
Non-temperature controlled environment with loud noises, dust, dirt, and metal particles that are usually associated with metal fabrication shops. All employees are required to wear personal protective equipment to include noise/hearing protection, safety glasses with side shields, (paint masks, respirator, when required) and OSHA compliant safety boots/shoes within the manufacturing facility.
