role.title: Sr. Manager - Operations
role.description:
**Senior Manager of Operations**

**Scottsdale Mint | Casper, Wyoming** 
**Employment Type:** Full-Time | Salaried

**Company Summary**

Founded in 2008, Scottsdale Mint is a U.S.-based precious metals manufacturer recognized globally for its innovation, quality, and American craftsmanship. As a privately held producer of premium gold, silver, and platinum bullion, the company serves sovereign nations, central banks, Fortune 500 companies, industrial clients, and authorized distributors worldwide.

Operating from its advanced manufacturing facility in Casper, Wyoming, Scottsdale Mint specializes in high-purity bullion, legal-tender coin programs, and custom-branded precious metal products. The company combines artistic design, scientific precision, and advanced minting technology to deliver products recognized for their quality, detail, and authenticity.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Manager of Operations is responsible for overseeing the daily performance and overall effectiveness of Scottsdale Mint's Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing departments. This position provides leadership and direction to approximately 30 employees, ensuring manufacturing operations are safe, efficient, productive, and aligned with company objectives.

The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader capable of managing multiple manufacturing functions, developing departmental supervisors, establishing accountability, and improving operational performance while supporting current production requirements and future manufacturing growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Manufacturing & Operations Management**

* Oversee daily operations and production performance across Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing.
* Establish departmental priorities, production goals, and performance expectations in coordination with senior management.
* Coordinate labor, equipment, and resources to maximize productivity, throughput, and manufacturing capacity.
* Monitor production schedules and workflow, identifying bottlenecks and implementing solutions to improve output and efficiency.
* Coordinate with Planning & Inventory Control, Fulfillment, Maintenance, Marketing, and other departments to support production requirements and company objectives.
* Develop, monitor, and report on departmental KPIs to optimize workforce utilization and ensure production schedule adherence.

**2. Leadership & Workforce Management**

* Provide leadership, direction, and accountability to departmental supervisors and employees.
* Manage staffing levels, scheduling, attendance, and labor allocation to meet production requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for employee performance, productivity, communication, and workplace conduct.
* Conduct performance reviews, address personnel matters, and establish development objectives for direct reports.
* Develop supervisory capabilities and ensure employees receive appropriate training to perform their responsibilities effectively.
* Foster a professional work environment emphasizing teamwork, accountability, ownership, and employee development.

**3. Safety, Compliance & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain consistent operating standards, manufacturing procedures, and a strong safety culture across all assigned departments.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety policies, and applicable workplace requirements.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including production output, labor efficiency, downtime, quality, and schedule attainment.
* Evaluate manufacturing processes to identify safety concerns, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
* Promote proper equipment operation, preventative maintenance, housekeeping, and organization throughout manufacturing areas.
* Ensure operational and safety issues are addressed promptly and corrective actions are implemented.
* Communicate departmental performance, challenges, and improvement initiatives to senior management.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 5–7 years of progressive manufacturing supervisory or management experience, preferably overseeing multiple departments.
* Experience managing production teams and workforces of approximately 25–50 employees preferred.
* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production workflows, labor management, and operational efficiency.
* Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and manufacturing safety requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production objectives, develop supervisors, and hold employees accountable for performance.
* Strong organizational, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and manufacturing-related reporting systems.

**Position Expectations**

The Senior Manager of Operations is expected to take ownership of the overall performance of the assigned manufacturing departments. This individual must provide consistent leadership, establish clear priorities, and ensure departmental supervisors are effectively managing their teams and achieving established objectives.

Success will be measured by the ability to meet production goals, maintain safe and efficient operations, effectively manage workforce resources, improve manufacturing performance, and develop a capable and accountable team.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee discount
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid time off
* Referral program
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

role.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
role.description:
**Company Description**

Domino’s Pizza, which began in 1960 as a single store location in Ypsilanti, MI, has had a lot to celebrate lately: we’re a reshaped, reenergized brand of honesty, transparency and accountability – not to mention, great food! In the rise to becoming a true technology leader, the brand is now consistently one of the top five companies in online transactions and 65% of our sales in the U.S. are taken through digital channels. The brand continues to ‘deliver the dream’ to local business owners, 90% of which started as delivery drivers and pizza makers in our stores. That’s just the tip of the iceberg…or as we might say, one “slice” of the pie! If this sounds like a brand you’d like to be a part of, consider joining our team!

 **Job Description**

The Director, Continuous Improvement leads the Supply Chain-wide capability for identifying, prioritizing, enabling, and sustaining improvements that increase business performance and organizational effectiveness across functions and end-to-end processes. This role establishes a culture of continuous improvement, advances operational and business process excellence, and enables measurable improvements in productivity, cost, quality, service, and capacity.

Working closely with cross-functional Supply Chain leaders, this position standardizes processes, uses data and insights to prioritize opportunities, and implements sustainable solutions aligned with strategic objectives. The Director maintains a strong connection to frontline operations by working directly in Supply Chain Centers and other functional environments to understand processes firsthand and translate observations into meaningful improvements.

**What You’ll Do**

* Develop and execute a comprehensive Continuous Improvement strategy and multi-year roadmap aligned with Supply Chain priorities, and advise Supply Chain leadership on opportunities that improve productivity, efficiency, cost, service, quality, capacity, and organizational effectiveness.
* Lead the deployment of consistent Continuous Improvement methodologies, tools, governance, performance expectations, and resource prioritization across Supply Chain functions.
* Work directly with Supply Chain Centers and functional teams to observe work at the point of execution, identify process variation and non-value-added activities, and implement standardized processes, operating practices, management systems, standard work, and process controls.
* Lead cross-functional transformation and productivity initiatives, including process redesign, technology-enabled improvement, automation, and new ways of working, in partnership with functional leaders, the PMO, Finance, and other stakeholders.
* Establish measurable outcomes, baselines, KPI definitions, reporting standards, dashboards, and processes for tracking, validating, and sustaining financial benefits, productivity improvements, and business value.
* Build organizational Continuous Improvement capability through training, coaching, structured problem-solving, knowledge sharing, and the development of CI team members and functional leaders.
* Lead change management and cross-functional alignment, manage risks and barriers, strengthen process integration, and communicate priorities, progress, results, and recommendations to Supply Chain leadership and key stakeholders.

**What You’ll Bring**

In addition to the technical and functional requirements of this role, successful candidates demonstrate Domino's Hungry for MORE Ways of Working:

Be Curious

* Seeks clarity, asks thoughtful questions, and uncovers root causes to solve problems effectively.
* Actively pursues learning opportunities, applies feedback, and continuously develops new skills.

Connect the Dots

* Uses information and insights to identify opportunities and drive informed decisions.
* Builds strong partnerships across teams and considers the broader organizational impact of decisions.

Aim High

* Sets ambitious goals, challenges the status quo, and focuses on work that drives meaningful business results.
* Uses feedback and data to continuously improve performance and outcomes.

Shift Fast

* Adapts quickly to changing priorities and business needs while maintaining focus on results.
* Demonstrates resilience, sound judgment, and the ability to learn from setbacks.

Deliver More

* Takes ownership, executes with discipline, and consistently produces measurable results.
* Identifies opportunities to create additional value for customers, team members, and the business.

Leadership Expectations

* Builds and develops high-performing teams aligned to Domino’s Ways of Working.
* Creates accountability, fosters collaboration, and delivers results through others.
* Leads confidently through change while maintaining team engagement and performance.
* Demonstrates enterprise thinking and drives cross-functional alignment to achieve business goals.

 
**Qualifications** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline; an advanced degree or MBA is preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, business transformation, operational excellence, or related disciplines, including demonstrated leadership experience in complex, cross-functional organizations.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing Continuous Improvement strategies and delivering measurable business results across multiple functions or complex organizations.
* Strong knowledge and practical application of Lean Six Sigma, structured problem-solving, process optimization, standardization, and change management methodologies.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional improvement initiatives, influence stakeholders, and drive organizational change without direct authority.
* Demonstrated hands-on experience leading Continuous Improvement initiatives in manufacturing, distribution, logistics, or other complex operational environments, including the ability to engage frontline employees, site leaders, and senior executives to diagnose issues, implement solutions, and deliver measurable results.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including experience identifying, quantifying, and validating productivity improvements, cost savings, and business value.
* Well-developed team building and influencing skills, unquestioned integrity, and the experience and confidence to work effectively across multiple functions and levels of the organization.
* Experience developing performance management frameworks, leveraging data analytics, and translating insights into actionable business recommendations.
* Demonstrated ability to build organizational capability through coaching, talent development, and deployment of Continuous Improvement methodologies.
* Strong strategic thinking, communication, collaboration, and executive presentation skills.
* Experience managing complex improvement portfolios, prioritizing competing business needs, and delivering sustainable outcomes.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent demonstrated Continuous Improvement expertise is preferred.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including Canada, as business needs require. Expected travel is up to 50%

 
**Additional Information**

Benefits: 

* Paid Holidays and Vacation
* Medical, Dental & Vision benefits that start on the first day of employment
* No-cost mental health support for employee and dependents
* Childcare tuition discounts
* No-cost fitness, nutrition, and wellness programs
* Fertility benefits
* Adoption assistance
* 401k matching contributions
* 15% off the purchase price of stock
* Company bonus

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

role.title: Director, Operations and Infrastructure in Stead, NV
role.description:
The University of Nevada, Reno (UNR) appreciates your interest in employment at our growing institution. We want your application process to go smoothly and quickly. Final applications must be submitted prior to the close of the recruitment.

 

If you need assistance or have questions regarding the application process, please contact our recruitment helpline at (775) 784-1495 or jobs@unr.edu .

**Job Description**

The Department of Physics at the University of Nevada, Reno seeks applications for a Director of Operations and Infrastructure position. The position will support the growth and development of the Applied Sciences Institute for National Security (ASI), **located at the SAGE facility in Stead, NV.**

 

The Director of Operations and Infrastructure provides strategic and operational leadership for the Institute’s administrative and financial, facilities and infrastructure, and safety and security functions. The position is responsible for ensuring that the Institute’s personnel, facilities, financial resources, information systems, and operational practices effectively support its research, education, and workforce-development missions.

 

The Director of Operations and Infrastructure serves as the Institute’s principal operational liaison with University Facilities Services and other university offices on the development of new research capabilities, modernization of infrastructure, and maintenance of the Institute’s facilities and key experimental systems. The position represents the Institute in operational discussions with university leadership, government agencies, national laboratories, sponsors, contractors, and other external partners.

 

The Director of Operations and Infrastructure is also responsible for the safe and secure working practices within the facilities, ensuring staff are creating and following appropriate procedures, students are being trained appropriately and following procedures, and the facility and experimental capabilities meet or exceed requirements for safe and secure operating conditions.

 

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree and five (5) years of related professional experience **OR**

Master’s degree and three (3) years of related professional experience.

**Related Work Experience** : Progressively responsible leadership overseeing complex operations, multidisciplinary teams, budgets and contracts, facilities and infrastructure, safety and risk management, compliance, and collaboration with senior leadership and external stakeholders or related experience.

 

**Schedule or Travel Requirements**

Occasional travel and weekends/evenings to support events or deadlines.

 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience leading operations in a research laboratory environment.
* Experience developing and implementing safe work practices for hazardous facilities and research activities.
Experience addressing security requirements and export control considerations in a research or technical environment. 

 

**Compensation Grade**

Administrative Faculty – C

Typical salary range for this position is $102,589 (Mid Q2) to $122,576.

 

Candidates will be hired at the level that is comparable to their experience, knowledge, skills and abilities. To view the salary schedule for this position, please visit: Salary Schedules and select Administrative Faculty by Grade. Salary is competitive and commensurate with related education and experience.

 

**Remarkable Retirement**

Our retirement plan is beyond compare. Your 19.25% contribution is generously matched by the University. With the faculty retirement plan, you are 100% vested your first day. Sit back and watch your retirement dollars grow! All permanent employees on an annual "A" or "B" contract who are employed at least 50% full-time are eligible to participate in the NSHE retirement program unless they are members of PERS of Nevada.

**Perks of Working at UNR**

* Health insurance options including dental and vision - Health Insurance
* Generous annual and sick leave and life insurance – Faculty Benefits
* E. L. Wiegand Fitness Center offers annual or semester memberships and spouse/domestic partner membership options. E.L. Wiegand Fitness Center
* Reno is proud to be a University town! Many local businesses offer discounts to WolfCard holders
* Mountain EAP supports employees (and eligible dependents) through life's difficult moments. Mountain EAP is located in Reno and specializes in counseling and advising services for personal or interpersonal issues.
* Faculty Senate is the principal representing body for faculty. Its membership includes representatives from each academic and administrative major unit of the University. Faculty Senate
No state income tax! 

**Grants-in-Aid for Faculty Employees**

The University is proud to provide a reduced-rate tuition benefit to faculty and qualified dependents. Faculty can take up to six credits per semester at a reduced rate. Dependents of faculty have unlimited credits, but in order to be eligible children must be unmarried and under the age of 24 and must receive at least 50% of their financial support from the employee and/or employee’s spouse or domestic partner. Faculty Grants-in-Aid

**Faculty Dual Career Assistance Program**

The University of Nevada, Reno recognizes the importance of addressing dual-career couples’ professional needs. We offer a dual career assistance program to newly hired faculty spouses/partners that provides resources and assists them to identify career opportunities in Northern Nevada. Dual Career Assistance Program

 

**Department Information**

The Department of Physics at the University of Nevada, Reno manages the SAGE facility, located only 11 miles north of the main campus. SAGE is a 182,000 sq ft. cold war era building that is home to an assemblage of unique research laboratories built to create and explore extreme material states. The research program is growing rapidly, with numerous projects from DOE and DoW sponsors, supporting a significant expansion of student research activities, all with a focus on supporting a transition into impactful careers. Please see here for more information: https://www.unr.edu/physics

 

**Contact Information**

Beth Jacobsen at 775-682-8787 or jacobsenb@unr.edu

**Exempt**

Yes

**Full-Time Equivalent**

100.0%

**Required Attachment(s)**

Please note, once you submit your application the only attachment/s viewable to you will be the attachment/s to the resume/CV section of the application. Any additional required attachment/s to the cover letter, references, additional documents sections of the application, will not be viewable to you after you submit your application. All uploaded attachment/s will be on the application for the committee to review. To request updates to attachments, prior to the committee review of applications, please contact the candidate helpdesk at jobs@unr.edu .

**Please attach the following documents to your application:**

1) Resume/CV

2) Cover Letter

3) Contact Information for Three Professional References

 

**Posting Close Time**

This posting will close at 12:00 am on the date listed below. The posting will no longer be available to apply to after 11:59 pm the day prior.

**Posting Close Date**

12/20/2026

Note to Applicant

A background check will be conducted on the candidate(s) selected for hire.

HR will attempt to verify academic credentials upon receipt of hiring documents. If the academic credentials cannot be verified, HR will notify the faculty member that an official transcript of their highest degree must be submitted within thirty days of the faculty member’s first day of employment.

References will be contacted at the appropriate phase of the recruitment process.

Applicants hired on a federal contract may be subject to E-Verify.

As part of the hiring process, applicants for positions in the Nevada System of Higher Education may be required to demonstrate the ability to perform job-related tasks.

For positions that require driving, evidence of a valid driver's license will be required at the time of employment and as a condition of continued employment.

Schedules are subject to change based on organizational needs.

The University of Nevada, Reno is committed to providing a place of work and learning free of discrimination on the basis of a person’s age (40 or older), disability, whether actual or perceived by others (including service-connected disabilities), gender (including pregnancy related conditions), military status or military obligations, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, national origin, race (including hair texture and protected hairstyles such as natural hairstyles, afros, bantu knots, curls, braids, locks and twists), color, or religion (protected classes).

**About Us**

The University of Nevada, Reno is a leading public research university committed to the promise of a future powered by knowledge. Founded in 1874 as Nevada’s original land-grant university, the University serves more than 23,000 undergraduate and graduate students from all 50 states and 63 countries.

Classified by the Carnegie® Classification of Institutions of Higher Education as an R1 (“Very High Research”) university, it is also recognized in the Carnegie® Community Engagement classification. The University is also ranked by U.S. News & World Report among the “Best National Universities” and “Best National Public Universities.” It also ranks in the top tier of the WSJ/Times Higher Education World University Rankings and the New York Times’ “Top Colleges for Economic Diversity.”

Since 2009, nearly $1 billion has been has invested in advanced labs, facilities, and residence halls on the main campus. The University is home to Nevada’s first medical school – the University of Nevada, Reno School of Medicine and the Wayne L. Prim Campus at Lake Tahoe, where education, research, and creative work thrive in a stunning mountain setting. The University delivers on its original land-grant mission with outreach across the state through the University of Nevada, Reno Extension, Nevada Agricultural Experiment Station, Nevada Bureau of Mines and Geology, Nevada Small Business Development Center, the Nevada Seismological Laboratory, and Wolf Pack Athletics.

The main campus is in Reno, Nevada, a burgeoning global technology hub with a vibrant midtown and downtown. Found where the high desert of the Great Basin meets the High Sierra and Lake Tahoe, the beautiful, 290-acre main campus is also a Nevada State Arboretum. The University’s physical infrastructure is expanding with ongoing construction of the newly named John Tullock Business Building, set to open in fall 2025. Groundbreaking is also planned for a new State Public Health Laboratory Building on campus, alongside the recent acquisition of 16 parcels near campus, known as “University Village,” to provide affordable housing for graduate students and early career faculty.

Collaborating with world-renowned organizations, the University fosters innovation through initiatives such as the Digital Wolf Pack partnership with Apple, which ensures equitable access to technology for students, providing new incoming freshman or transfer students with an iPad Air and accessories. Google’s TechWise initiate is an 18-month program that fully supports undergraduate students in becoming entry-level software engineers by graduation.

In 2023, the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Economic Development Administration (EDA) announced that Nevada – led by the University of Nevada, Reno – was named one of the inaugural 31 Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs (TechHubs). Nevada was selected from a competitive pool of 489 applicants from across the United States and its territories. Nevada’s Tech Hub will strengthen America’s lithium batteries, critical elements and other electric vehicle materials industry sectors within the state.

Through its commitment to high-impact education, world-improving research and creative activity, and outreach that’s transforming Nevada’s communities and businesses, the University continues its 150-year tradition of benefitting our state, nation and world.

The University recognizes that diversity promotes excellence in education and research. The inclusive and engaged community on campus recognizes the added value that students, faculty, and staff from different backgrounds bring to the educational experience.

Today, the University delivers on its original land-grant mission of access to education and knowledge by investing in the academics, facilities, support, engagement and vibrant campus life that promote our diverse students’ cognitive growth and academic achievement – all while remaining one of the best values in American higher education.

For more information, please visit the University’s website .

**University of Nevada, Reno**
------------------------------

role.title: Head of Operational Excellence
role.description:
**Overview:** 
 
Vanguard is building an enterprise Operational Excellence capability to strengthen end-to-end process ownership, improve efficiency, and embed continuous improvement across the organization. This newly created, highly visible role will serve as the architect and builder of that capability. The leader in this role will establish and scale Vanguard’s enterprise Operational Excellence management system, creating the strategy, operating model, process taxonomy, standards, methods, governance, tools, training, measures, and operating rhythms that enable business leaders to own and continuously improve their end-to-end processes.

The central capability will enable the businesses rather than execute improvement on their behalf. Success will require deep Operational Excellence expertise, enterprise-level operating model design, executive presence, and the ability to translate a technically rigorous discipline into a clear and compelling business imperative.

**What You Will Do:**

* Architect the enterprise Operational Excellence strategy and management system, including the operating model, governance, process taxonomy, decision rights, standards, methods, and management routines.
* Establish a federated model that clearly defines what the central team owns and what business-area leaders own, reinforcing accountability for process performance and sustained improvement.
* Create an enterprise framework for critical and high-risk processes, clarifying end-to-end ownership, expected outcomes, escalation paths, and review cadences.
* Build a common measurement system for process health, including definitions, benchmarks, performance indicators, executive dashboards, and business-area drill-downs that support transparent decision-making.
* Embed disciplined Lean Six Sigma and DMAIC practices, root-cause analysis, process redesign, simplification, and continuous improvement across a large, complex organization.
* Build and lead a new Operational Excellence organization, expected initially to include approximately 8 to 10 professionals, and define the capabilities, roles, talent strategy, and development model needed to scale.
* Partner with senior leaders across business, risk, technology, data, finance, and other enterprise functions to identify systemic issues and translate them into an integrated improvement portfolio.
* Influence prioritization and investment decisions using evidence, balancing client value, risk reduction, productivity, resilience, controls, strategic importance, and long-term enterprise value.
* Integrate existing transformation, risk, control, and process-improvement efforts into a coherent enterprise approach that builds on current foundations rather than creating a disconnected program.
* Build enterprise capability through standards, training, coaching, benchmarking, and practical tools, including the thoughtful use of automation, data, process mining, and AI-enabled approaches.
* Provide decision-ready insights and recommendations to senior officer audiences, Senior Staff, and the Board on process health, progress, emerging themes, dependencies, and investment needs.
* Create clarity, momentum, and followership by articulating what Operational Excellence means for Vanguard, why it matters, and what leaders and teams must do differently.

**What It Takes:**

* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in Operational Excellence, enterprise transformation, business operations, process excellence, quality, or a related discipline, including leadership of complex, cross-functional initiatives.
* Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of training and experience. A graduate degree or relevant Operational Excellence certification is preferred.
* Deep expertise in Lean Six Sigma, DMAIC, continuous improvement, process redesign, root-cause analysis, process measurement, and quality or process-management systems.
* Master Black Belt certification or equivalent depth of practical expertise strongly preferred. The successful candidate must be capable of establishing the methodology, not simply sponsoring work performed by others.
* Demonstrated success designing, launching, or materially transforming an enterprise-scale Operational Excellence capability, center of excellence, management system, or federated process-management model.
* Proven ability to move beyond individual projects and create common standards, tools, governance, accountability, and adoption across multiple businesses or functions.
* Experience building a function, team, or capability from the ground up, including organization design, talent selection, capability building, and resource prioritization.
* Executive presence and communication skills, with a record of influencing highly senior leaders, translating technical concepts into business language, navigating resistance, and creating followership without relying solely on formal authority.
* A results orientation supported by quantifiable improvements in efficiency, cycle time, quality, defects, cost, operational risk, controls, client outcomes, automation, or sustained process performance.
* Strong business, risk, data, and technology acumen, with the judgment to connect process health and improvement priorities to enterprise value.

**Special Factors**

**Sponsorship**

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

**About Vanguard**

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

**How We Work**

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

role.title: Operations Director
role.description:
**Aveanna Healthcare is growing!**

**We are seeking a Home Health Operations Director to join our team, based in Englewood, Colorado.**

**Salary: $82-85K/YR +** **Quarterly Incentive Potential up to 20% of salary dependent on office success**

**Why Choose Aveanna?**

* Health, Dental, Vision Insurance

* 401(k) Savings Plan with Employer Matching
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Company-Paid Life Insurance
* Paid Holidays, Paid Vacation Days, Paid Sick Days
* Easy access to state-of-the-art technology for electronic charting during point of care 24/7 Team Support for direct clinical and scheduling assistance

* Cell phone and mileage reimbursement
* Room for growth and advancement

Position Overview 
The Operations Director (hereafter referred to as “OD”) is responsible for managing and overseeing leadership and administrative functions of an Aveanna location. The OD collaborates with cross-functional teams including operations, clinical and business development ensuring annual business growth, patient care outcomes and financial objectives are met or exceeded. 
 
Serving as the leader of their respective branch team, the OD offers a dynamic work environment where individuals can contribute their expertise in either clinical or non-clinical capacities. The OD embodies Aveanna’s Core Values by building and strengthening relationships with patients, families, field staff, and referral sources while serving as an advocate and trusted mentor for their location team. The OD possesses strong written and verbal communication skills and assures the adoption of all branch-level processes and training standards. The OD ensures their location fully adheres to all Federal and State regulations governing home care agencies. 
 
Essential Job Functions 
Lead, develop, and support a high-performing team by recruiting qualified staff, ensuring timely performance evaluations, establishing and monitoring goals, promoting employee development, and maintaining consistent communication with supervisors and area/regional leadership. 
Build and strengthen relationships with patients, families, caregivers, referral partners, and business development teams by supporting effective introductions, periodic patient home visits, referral source assessments, satisfaction survey follow-up, and growth-oriented partnership objectives. 
Drive branch growth and operational performance by planning and implementing effective growth strategies. 
Successfully address the referral pipeline with urgency, and monitors referral management, admissions and start-of-care timelines. 
Oversee caregiver staffing, productivity, reporting deadlines, and overall service delivery. 
Manage financial and business performance by interpreting financial statements, activity reports, and other performance data; monitoring revenue, billing, collections, productivity, and expense control. 
Identify opportunities for cost mitigation and process improvement. 
Identify operational barriers, implement solutions that improve efficiency and branch outcomes, and partner with area and regional leadership to align priorities with business goals and organizational initiatives. 
Ensure operational readiness and compliance by maintaining adherence to company policies, payor requirements, and applicable federal and state regulations; 
Partner with clinical and operational leaders to address quality concerns; implement corrective actions and support continuous improvement. 
Monitor branch performance indicators to identify trends, mitigate risk, improve patient, caregiver, and business outcomes, and promote a culture of accountability, compliance, service excellence, and operational readiness. 
 
Requirements 
Minimum of an associate’s degree or equivalent work experience in a related field. 
2-3 years’ management experience. 
Satisfies all state requirements, including background checks and any applicable required work authorization. 
 
Other Skills/Abilities 
Must be able to adhere to confidentiality standards and professional boundaries at all times. 
Ability to comfortably work in homes of families with limited resources. 
Quick-thinking and astute decision-making skills. 
Attention to detail. 
Time Management. 
Effective problem-solving and conflict resolution. 
Excellent organization and communication skills. 
Ability to remain calm and professional in stressful situations. 
Strong commitment to clinical excellence. 
 
Leadership skills 
Ability to train and supervise staff. 
 
Preferences 
4-Year College Degree preferred. 
Healthcare and/or pediatric home care experience a plus. 
 
Physical Requirements 
Must be able to speak, write, read and understand English. 
Must be able to travel as needed. 
Occasional lifting, carrying, pushing and pulling of 50 pounds. 
Prolonged walking, standing, bending, kneeling, reaching, twisting. 
Must be able to sit and climb stairs. 
Must have visual and hearing acuity. 
Must have strong sense of smell and touch. 
 
Environment 
Must be able to function in a wide variety of environments which may involve exposure to allergens and other various conditions. 
 
Other Duties 
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. 
 
**Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis for this role and can be submitted by applying to this job posting or by visiting our career page at:** **| Aveanna Healthcare Careers**

As an employer accepting Medicare and Medicaid funds, employees must comply with all health-related requirements in all relevant jurisdictions, including required vaccinations and testing, subject to exemptions for medical or religious reasons as appropriate.

Job Description
 
 
Director, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Strategy & Operations
 
 
Position Description
 
 
The Director, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Strategy & Operations is a key leadership role responsible for shaping and advancing the strategic and operational priorities of the U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases Business Unit.
 
Reporting directly to the SVP, U.S. Vaccines & Infectious Diseases, this individual will serve as a strategic thought partner to the SVP and Leadership Team, translating business strategy into action, driving alignment across priorities, and enabling disciplined execution. The role requires a strong balance of strategic thinking, operational excellence, influence, and change leadership, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, connect across the organization, and accelerate progress against the BU's most important priorities.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:** 

* Lead the BU strategic planning and operating process, including annual priority setting, Trimester planning and tracking, and ongoing assessment of progress against key objectives.
* Partner with the SVP and Leadership Team to translate strategy into action, identifying priorities, surfacing opportunities and risks, and driving alignment and accountability across the organization.
* Lead high-priority, cross-functional initiatives that advance BU strategy, transformation, and organizational capabilities, including evolving commercial capabilities, new ways of working, AI, and other emerging business priorities.
* Drive leadership effectiveness and decision-making by shaping and facilitating Leadership Team meetings, leader forums, strategic planning sessions, and other key business forums that enable alignment and action.
* Shape BU communications and engagement strategy, ensuring business priorities, strategic direction, and key messages are translated into clear and compelling communications across the organization, including Town Halls and other leadership forums.
* Partner with Leadership Team sponsors to advance talent, culture, and organizational priorities, including Talent & Culture working groups, employee development initiatives, and efforts to strengthen organizational capability and engagement.
* Partner across key financial planning processes, including forecasting, Profit Plan, and investor relations connecting strategic priorities with financial considerations and partnering across Finance and business stakeholders to enable informed decision-making.
* Identify opportunities to strengthen BU effectiveness, simplify ways of working, build organizational capabilities, and accelerate execution of strategic priorities.

**Required Experience:** 

* Bachelor's degree required.
* Minimum of 5 years of experience in marketing, sales, market access, strategy and operations, marketing support, within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.
* Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to assess complex business challenges, identify strategic choices, and develop clear recommendations.
* Proven ability to influence and lead without direct authority across complex, matrixed organizations.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, with the courage to challenge thinking, bring an independent point of view, and constructively navigate differing perspectives.
* Ability to navigate ambiguity and evolving priorities, quickly create structure from white space, and move work forward with sound judgment and learning agility.
* Demonstrated ability to prioritize competing demands, maintain focus on the highest-impact work, and align teams around clear priorities.
* Ability to inspire, motivate, mentor, and align others around a shared vision and clear priorities, with or without direct reporting relationships.
* Strong balance of strategic orientation and operational discipline, with the ability to move seamlessly between long-term priorities and near-term execution.
* Demonstrated ability to connect insights and priorities across functions and levels of the organization, bringing an enterprise perspective while maintaining focus on BU objectives.

**Preferred Experience and Skills:** 

* Vaccines and/or Infectious Diseases experience.
* Experience supporting or leading strategy and operations within a complex commercial organization.
* Experience leading enterprise or cross-functional transformation, capability-building, or change initiatives.

role.description:
**What makes DHL great?** Our People! We know each employee’s individual contributions make us the #1 Express Delivery and Logistics Company in the world.

***Distinguished as No. 1 World’s Best Workplace™ by Great Place to Work and Fortune Magazine***

DHL Express is committed to maintaining an environment that empowers every team member to make the greatest possible impact on our business. Our culture is about personal commitment – to our business, to each other and to our global communities. DHL is dedicated to being a great place to work. In addition to competitive compensation packages, our employees enjoy a range of programs, services and benefits that bring the best to their personal lives.

**Start YOUR career with DHL today…**

The **Sr. Director Operations** is responsible for providing strategic input and leading the implementation of the Courier and Pick-up & Delivery strategy. This role ensures the safe, secure, timely, and accurate transportation and delivery of mail, parcels, small packages, and legal documents between locations, in alignment with business objectives, operational requirements, corporate guidelines, and policies.

**Key Accountabilities:**

* Provide input to develop Couriers, Pick-up & Delivery operations strategy to deliver effective collection, transportation, and delivery of parcels while maintaining exceptional service quality and customer satisfaction.
* Plan, organize and control preparation of annual business plans, operational budgets, workforce planning, and resource allocation for delivery operations.
* Provide expertise, coaching, and leadership to frontline managers and supervisors to ensure execution of daily operational activities, achievement of performance targets, and development of future leaders.
* Manage and control service point operations to enable efficient collection, handling, and distribution of shipments while maintaining compliance with operational standards.
* Manage and control scheduling of transportation capacity, traffic volumes, route structures, and delivery resources to maximize productivity and service performance.
* Lead a workforce of more than 1,000 employees across multiple facilities, fostering a culture of accountability, engagement, safety, and operational excellence.
* Demonstrate strong knowledge and experience operating in unionized environments, including labor relations, contract interpretation, grievance resolution, workforce planning, and effective collaboration with union leadership.
* Oversee large independent contractor (IC) networks and transportation providers, ensuring contractual compliance, operational performance, cost management, and service reliability.
* Drive operational expense (OPEX) management through disciplined financial oversight, productivity initiatives, route optimization, and continuous improvement programs to achieve profitability objectives.
* Partner closely with Network Operations, Gateway Operations, Brokerage, Customs, Aviation, and Commercial teams to ensure seamless execution of customer commitments and network requirements.
* Deploy structured approaches to manage operational procedures including shipment processing, sorting, loading/unloading, documentation, scanning compliance, manifests, secure handling, and custody control.
* Implement reporting standards, performance metrics, and operational dashboards to provide visibility into service performance, cost drivers, productivity, and customer experience measures.
* Anticipate changes in customer demand, economic conditions, labor markets, and transportation trends to proactively adjust operational strategies and resource requirements.
* Identify opportunities to improve transportation, delivery, and customer service solutions through process redesign, technology implementation, and network optimization.
* Monitor operational performance and implement continuous improvement initiatives focused on service quality, productivity, safety, employee engagement, and cost control.
* Lead multiple delivery bases and service centers across geographically diverse markets, ensuring consistent execution of operational standards and business objectives.
* Champion safety, security, and compliance programs while maintaining adherence to company policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
* Build strong relationships with key customers, local business leaders, and internal stakeholders to support growth initiatives and enhance the overall customer experience.
* Drive organizational change initiatives, workforce transformation efforts, and strategic projects across the region while maintaining high levels of employee engagement and operational performance.

**Skills/Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* 8+ years of experience in operations and leadership roles.
* Demonstrated experience in budgetary management and financial accountability.
* Strong background in business and operations management, including managing complex operational environments.
* Experience leading courier, Pick-up & Delivery, dock, and transportation operations.
* Proven ability to lead change management and operational improvement initiatives.
* Strong strategic planning and execution capabilities.
* Demonstrated experience in stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration.
* Proven leadership experience managing a department or business unit comprising multiple teams, including Managers and/or Team Leaders.
* Strong ability to lead, develop, and influence leaders and teams to achieve business and operational objectives.
* Experience establishing priorities, managing resources, and driving performance across multiple operational functions.
* Demonstrated ability to drive employee engagement, foster an inclusive and high-performing culture, and develop strategies that strengthen employee experience, retention, and organizational effectiveness.

role.title: Director of Quality Assurance & CI
role.description:
**Lead the Transformation. Build a Culture of Excellence. Deliver Results That Last.**
The Director of Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement provides strategic leadership for the company's quality and continuous improvement functions, ensuring products, processes, and services consistently meet the highest standards of quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction. This role is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving the Quality Management System (QMS) while driving a culture of operational excellence across the organization. Leading enterprise-wide Lean initiatives, Kaizen events, root cause analysis, and structured continuous improvement programs, this position delivers measurable improvements in quality, productivity, cost, and operational performance. Working closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, the Director establishes quality strategies, drives compliance with customer and regulatory requirements, and champions sustainable improvements that support the company's strategic growth objectives.
 
 
**What Success Looks Like**

* Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the company's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry standards, including ISO certifications.
* Establish enterprise-wide quality strategies, policies, and governance while serving as the executive leader for quality-related decisions impacting customers, operations, and suppliers.
* Drive a culture of operational excellence by leading Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and structured continuous improvement initiatives across all business functions.
* Develop and execute strategic cost reduction initiatives that improve productivity, eliminate waste, reduce the Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ), and enhance overall operational performance.
* Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, and executive leadership to identify, prioritize, and deliver sustainable business improvements.
* Champion the voice of the customer by leveraging customer feedback, warranty data, and field performance to improve product quality, reliability, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead enterprise-wide root cause analysis and corrective action processes to resolve quality issues, prevent recurrence, and strengthen operational performance.
* Oversee internal and external audit programs, ensuring compliance with quality, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements while proactively managing organizational risk.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Quality and Continuous Improvement organization while coaching leaders throughout the business to embed a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Establish, monitor, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) that measure quality, delivery, cost savings, productivity, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement performance.
* Translate strategic business objectives into measurable quality and operational improvement initiatives that deliver sustainable financial and operational results.
* Build trusted relationships across the organization and with external stakeholders, influencing decision-making and driving alignment to achieve the company's strategic objectives.

**Qualifications That Shine**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field required; Master's degree or other advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive quality leadership experience, including 10+ years leading people and 5+ years leading corporate or multi-site quality organizations.
* Proven success developing and leading Quality Management Systems (QMS) within a manufacturing environment, including ISO implementation, certification, and ongoing compliance.
* Professional certifications such as ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, and Lean certification are strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated success leading Lean transformation, Kaizen events, and enterprise-wide continuous improvement initiatives that deliver measurable business results.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), statistical process control (SPC), and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Proven ability to influence executive leadership and build collaborative partnerships across operations, engineering, supply chain, finance, and commercial teams.
* Exceptional communication, presentation, and organizational skills with the ability to translate strategy into execution and drive organizational change.
* Strategic, data-driven leader with a track record of improving quality, operational performance, customer satisfaction, and financial results through operational excellence initiatives.

**Why You’ll Love Working Here**

* You’ll Be Empowered – You’ll have autonomy in your role, supported by a team that trusts your judgment
* You’ll Grow With Us – We invest in your training, development, and long-term career path
* You’ll Be Rewarded – Competitive pay, performance incentives, 401(k) with profit sharing, and great benefits
* You’ll Make a Real Impact – Your work supports businesses across North America and shapes the future of finishing technology
* You’ll Join a Great Team – We’re growing fast, we value collaboration, and are committed to your success

**Transparent Rewards**
At GFS, we recognize the dedication behind every role and ensure that our compensation reflects both your impact and our shared success.
 
 
**Pay Range:**
$124,518 – $156,746 per year, based on your experience, skills, and qualifications.
 
 
**Bonus Eligibility:**
This position is eligible for an annual individual incentive based on company performance. Maximum bonus amounts may vary depending on role.
 
 
**Benefits:**
Eligible for standard company benefits, including health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan with company match, paid time off, and other employee programs. More detailed information is available at 2026 GFS Benefits .
 
 
Actual compensation will be determined by factors including experience, education, certifications, skill level, and market conditions. For remote or hybrid positions, the listed pay range applies to applicants in the specified location.
 
 
**About GFS**
Global Finishing Solutions is the leading manufacturer of paint booths and finishing systems serving automotive, aerospace, industrial manufacturing, marine, military, rail, trucking, and wood finishing markets. We specialize in building custom solutions that meet each customer’s unique needs—and we do it with a team that thrives on collaboration and innovation because we're different.
 
 
What makes us different is our unwavering commitment to our core values of family, respect, partnership, improvement, and integrity. We are a family-oriented organization that still values the little things, creating a workplace where you can thrive, fairness guides every decision, and collaboration drives shared success. Small town in spirit but big-hearted in impact, here you’re not just joining a company—you’re joining a team that grows together, celebrates together, and builds lasting value together. That’s the difference. Join us.
 
 
Apply now at www.gfscareers.us
 
 
🌐 About GFS
 
 
📹 Watch Us in Action
 
 
🔗 Connect on LinkedIn
 
 
**Equal Opportunity Employer**
**GFS is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants**
. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, sex, age, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or any other status protected by law. Employment offers are subject to successful completion of pre-employment drug screening and physicals, consistent with applicable laws.
 
 
Note to recruiters: GFS only works with agencies that have signed a contract with our HR team. Resumes sent directly to hiring managers without a prior agreement are considered unsolicited and the property of GFS. Placement fees will not be paid without a formal contract.

role.title: Director, Quality
role.description:
**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.
 
 
Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.
 
 
**What You’ll Do As a Director Quality**

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:

+ Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
+ Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
+ Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
+ Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
+ Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
+ Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
+ Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
+ Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.

* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**Required**
**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.
* Strong expertise in analytical methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement methods.
* Excellent interpersonal, as well as verbal and written communication skills in order to develop and maintain rapport and effective internal and external relationships to support business success.
* The ability to work hard and deliver results under pressure, as well as the willingness to address and shift priorities in rapidly changing markets.

**Preferred**

* Advanced degree.
* Experience with statistical analysis software and Visio.
* Experience in medical device industry.

**Other**

* Excellent problem-solving skills.
* Focus on identification of potential issues and continuous improvement.
* Experience working on cross-functional teams and on own initiative.
* Demonstrated excellent organizational, oral, and written communications skills.
* Must have PC experience, as well as working familiarity of desktop applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

**What STERIS Offers**
We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and financial future.
 
 
**Here Is a Brief Overview Of What We Offer**

* Market competitive pay
* Extensive paid time off and (9) added holidays
* Excellent healthcare, dental, and vision benefits
* Long/short term disability coverage
* 401(K) with company match
* Maternity and parental leave
* Additional add on benefits/discounts for programs such as pet insurance
* Tuition reimbursement and continued educational programs
* Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career

Pay range for this opportunity is $144,500.00 - $187,000.00. This position is eligible for bonus participation.
 
 
Minimum pay rates offered will comply with county/city minimums, if higher than range listed. Pay rates are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to local labor market costs, years of relevant experience, education, professional certifications, foreign language fluency, etc.
 
 
STERIS offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits portfolio. Click here for a complete list of benefits: STERIS Benefits
 
 
Open until position is filled.
 
 
STERIS is a leading global provider of products and services that support patient care with an emphasis on infection prevention. WE HELP OUR CUSTOMERS CREATE A HEALTHIER AND SAFER WORLD by providing innovative healthcare and life sciences products and services around the globe. For more information, visit www.steris.com.
 
 
If you need assistance completing the application process, please call 1 (440) 392.7047. This contact information is for accommodation inquiries only and cannot be used to check application status.
 
 
STERIS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity to ensure that persons are recruited, hired, trained, transferred and promoted in all job groups regardless of race, color, religion, age, disability, national origin, citizenship status, military or veteran status, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, and any other category protected by federal, state or local law. We are not only committed to this policy by our status as a federal government contractor, but also we are strongly bound by the principle of equal employment opportunity.

* 60-741.44(k), shall be available to all employees and applicants for employment for inspection upon request. The program may be obtained at your location’s HR Office during normal business hours.

role.description:
Our purpose,
*Refresh the world and make a difference*
, is uniquely us, and part of our vision includes making a positive difference in people's lives, communities, and our planet by doing business the right way.
 
 
The Director, Field Quality plays a critical role within the North America Operating Unit Supply Chain QSE organization. This position is responsible for driving the consistent execution of quality and food safety programs across company-owned and co-manufacturing operations within assigned regions. The role ensures facilities maintain audit readiness, comply with internal and external regulatory requirements, and fosters a culture of continuous improvement. By providing technical expertise and leadership, this role enables operational excellence and ensures our products meet the highest standards of quality and safety
 
 
**What You’ll Do For Us**

* Provide leadership and technical guidance for quality programs across assigned regions.
* Ensure facilities comply with internal standards, regulatory requirements, and maintain audit readiness.
* Implement and maintain foundational quality systems, including adherence to the TCCC and NAOU Quality requirements.
* Monitor regional quality metrics, consumer complaint data, and operational trends to identify and mitigate risks proactively.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action planning for quality system failures and IMCR events within assigned regions.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot issues and support commercialization processes for new products and packages.
* Deliver quality training programs to build plant-level expertise and ensure consistent execution of standards.
* Champion digital tools and data-driven approaches to enhance quality performance and operational efficiency.

**Requirements & Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Science, Engineering, or related technical field.
* HACCP/PCQI Certification required.
* 8+ years of experience in quality and food safety within FMCG (Fast-Moving Consumer Goods) or pharmaceutical sectors.
* Experience implementing quality assurance, quality control, and management system programs (e.g., HACCP, GFSI, ISO9000/22000, SPC).
* Strong problem-solving skills and experience with root cause analysis.
* Familiarity with digital quality and compliance systems (e.g., EtQ, SAP, SPC/InfinityQS).
* Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, and presentation).
* Exposure to lean/six sigma tools and methodologies preferred.
* Ability to travel 50–75% within North America.

**Skills**
Regulatory & Food Safety Knowledge, Cross-Functional Collaboration, Technical Leadership, Continuous Improvement Mindset, Quality Systems Management
 
 
**What We Can Do For You**
 
 

* Innovative Technology:  We utilize and lead the market with our large supply chain network and state-of-art technology we use each day.
* Exposure to World Class Leaders: Availability to global technology leaders that will expand your network and exposure you to emerging technologies and techniques.
* Agile Work Environment: We embrace agile with management that believes in removing barriers, so you are empowered to experiment, iterate, and innovate.

role.title: Director of Quality Assurance
role.description:
**About this Director of Quality Assurance role:**

The Director, Quality Assurance provides strategic leadership for the company's quality organization and Quality Management System across multiple locations. This position is responsible for ensuring product quality, regulatory and customer compliance, and the effectiveness and integrity of quality systems supporting both high-mix, low-volume and high-volume manufacturing operations. The Director leads the development of the quality organization, drives continuous improvement and operational excellence, and partners with cross-functional leadership to strengthen quality performance and support the organization's growth.

**Reports to:**
VP Operations & QA

**Primary Responsibilities:**

* Provide strategic leadership and direction for the quality organization across all company locations.
* Maintain and continually develop the Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring process integrity and compliance with applicable customer, regulatory, and industry requirements, including AS9100 and ISO 9001.
* Establish quality strategies, standards, and control plans that support product quality, operational performance, and customer requirements.
* Lead and develop the Quality team, establishing clear expectations and building organizational capability to support current and future business needs.
* Monitor and analyze quality and manufacturing performance metrics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen product quality, reduce scrap and rework, improve operational efficiency, and enhance customer satisfaction.
* Drive effective corrective and preventive actions and promote systematic problem-solving to address quality issues and prevent recurrence.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other functional leaders to improve product and process quality throughout the organization.
* Ensure products and processes meet applicable customer, regulatory, contractual, and company quality requirements.
* Provide leadership and oversight for customer quality issues, supplier quality performance, audits, and other significant quality matters.
* Maintain organizational readiness for customer, registrar, and regulatory audits and ensure appropriate resolution of identified findings.
* Support capital planning, equipment investments, facility needs, and long-term manufacturing strategies from a quality and operational risk perspective.
* Promote a culture of quality, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.
* Comply with all company policies and applicable quality, safety, cybersecurity, customer, and regulatory requirements, including ITAR/export control, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) handling, and Foreign Object Damage (FOD) prevention.
* Complete all required training and use approved methods to protect company and customer information.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree or higher, ideally in Mechanical Engineering.
* 10+ years of progressively responsible quality leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Experience leading quality operations across multiple locations.
* Experience supporting both high-mix, low-volume and high-volume manufacturing environments.
* Demonstrated experience leading quality organizations through periods of significant growth and operational change.
* Demonstrated knowledge of Quality Management Systems and applicable quality standards, including AS9100 and ISO 9001.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* US Citizen, Permanent Resident, or Protected Individual (as defined by 8 U.S.C. § 1324b(a)(3)) preferred due to ITAR responsibilities.
* ASQ certification such as Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) or Certified Quality Engineer (CQE).
* Experience in aerospace, defense, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
* Experience with government contracting quality requirements.
* Lean/Six Sigma certification or demonstrated continuous improvement experience.
* Experience scaling quality systems to support organizational growth.

Our client is an equal opportunity employer.

role.title: Director of Quality, Regulatory & Improvement
role.description:
***Title: Director of Quality, Regulatory and Improvement***

**Job Summary:**

This senior leadership role leads the quality departments for all Deringer-Ney locations globally. The Director implements best practices and metrics to coordinate all teams under a unified Quality Management System and is responsible for ensuring that the company's products, services, and manufacturing processes comply with strict government laws, industry standards, and internal quality systems. The role plans, coordinates, and directs the activities of the quality assurance and compliance programs to ensure the production of consistent, reliable products that meet or exceed established standards, and leads the continuous improvement team to support, train, and execute the DNIOS system.

***Supervisory Responsibilities:***
*Yes*

**Duties/Responsibilities:**

* Manage all quality departments by formulating, developing, and overseeing global goals, objectives, policies, procedures, systems, and outcomes pertaining to quality controls, assessments, and audits.
* Quality Management Systems (QMS): Build, maintain, and continuously improve QMS frameworks (such as ISO 13485 and ISO 9001).
* Develop a high-performance team by acquiring, developing, training, coaching, cultivating, and managing talented Quality Control personnel.
* Maintain and improve the quality system through routine system audits and corrective actions, and ensure that corrective actions, whether internal or external, are handled in a timely manner.
* Risk & Lifecycle Management: Oversee design controls, validation packages, complaint handling, and post-market surveillance (such as Automotive Reporting).
* Manage and maintain quality inspection and product release programs for raw materials, work in process (WIP), and finished goods.
* Regulatory Compliance & Filings: Lead product submissions and act as the primary liaison during agency audits.
* Disseminate quality awareness, adherence, and developments to global stakeholders by scheduling and performing regional quality audits and by ensuring that ISO systems are managed and maintained.
* Serve as an active member of the DNI Leadership Team, sharing the function's progress toward its goals while setting, and driving toward, an aspirational vision for a best-in-class quality department.
* Create a Cost of Poor Quality metric for the organization and set specific goals to improve quality performance across the company.
* Lead the development of the Annual Strategic Planning (P.D.C.A.) Cycle to include the Improvement Process.
* Lead the organization in attaining key metrics based on Balanced Scorecard (BSC) Objectives. Understand the department's key performance indicators and leading and lagging indicators, and contribute to achieving these goals, both individually and as a team.
* With the CIP Team, perform systematic audits designed to confirm that process standards are being utilized and met (BSC One-Page Reports).
* Interact with and make recommendations and presentations to the Executive Leadership Group via standardized checks: weekly, monthly, quarterly, and year-end. Maintain the PDCA Cycle while focusing on BSC Objectives.

**Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Strong background in ISO 9000 system management, including training and auditing.
* Strong background in ISO 13485 system management and thorough knowledge of FDA requirements and other international standards that regulate the medical device industry.
* Knowledge of automated inspection equipment, including vision systems and coordinate measuring devices.
* Adept at delegating and managing multiple tasks with various levels of priority.
* Excellent communication skills; must be able to present ideas, results, and requirements effectively throughout the organization and to the customer on a timely basis.
* Expert skill set in applied statistics, reliability, design of experiments, MSA, GR&R, and project management.
* Fluency with various software packages commonly used in project management, database, SPC, word processing, and data acquisition.
* Analytical, problem-solving, project management, facilitation, and decision-making skills are essential.
* Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, coach, resolve conflict, and promote teamwork.
* Ability to see and hear the facts from several viewpoints while promoting success through interactive problem solving and teamwork.

**Experience & Education Requirements:**

* Technical degree (BS, BSE, or BSME) with a minimum of 10 years' experience in quality engineering or quality management.
* Strong preference for relevant industry experience in a metals or electrical connectors company or similar.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Control, or Regulatory Affairs within a regulated field such as medical devices, automotive, or defense.
* Preferred certifications: Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or Certified Quality Engineer (CQE).
* Demonstrated project management skills in the areas of process control, SPC, automotive PPAP submission, and statistical analysis.
* Lean Green Belt or Black Belt certification, Six Sigma, and DMAIC process experience.
* Actively continuing training through courses and seminars.

***Physical Requirements:***

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times.
* Must be able to access and navigate each department at the organization’s facilities.
* Travel to other locations as required.
