role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
Director of Operations

**Overview**
------------

Join Diversified Maintenance! We’re committed to delivering exceptional cleaning, landscaping, and restoration services for commercial facilities. Be part of a welcoming and collaborative team where innovation meets excellence. We offer steady, reliable work in janitorial management, full-time and part-time janitorial roles, maintenance, landscaping, and metal restoration. If you want to make a meaningful impact and build a lasting career, we have opportunities for you. Join us and grow with a leader in the industry!

**Job Description**
-------------------

Diversified Maintenance is hiring a Director of Operations. The Director of Operations oversees day-to-day operations of janitorial services for a specific business division. This senior level position is responsible for the development and implementation of a variety of strategies to maximize profits, while maintaining a high level of service quality within their division. Through continual evaluation and improvement, the Director of Operations positively impacts key performance indicators such as operational cost, service quality, and team development. This position provides oversight and leadership to team members and follows up on staff assignments.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Lead and manage the day to day operation through a team of top performers
* Manages the P&L for their operations
* Hold executive responsibility for all vertical operations, employee management, finances, and people related functions, sales growth, startups, account management, legal, and other operating elements of the business.
* Responsible for client relations and retention
* Manage and build performance teams, providing coaching, development and mentoring to a team of managers
* Develop and hold the team accountable to managing key performance indicators
* Stay current in business vertical and identify opportunities for company growth opportunities
* Provide timely feedback and guidance for team members on operational issues and concerns

**QUALIFICATIONS (MUST HAVE):**

* High school diploma or equivalent
* Minimum of five (5) years of management experience in janitorial industry
* Business level oral and written communication skills; ability to speak, read, and write fluently in English
* Ability to multitask and adapt to changing environments
* Excellent customer service skills; active listening skills
* Ability to lead and encourage teamwork; ability to negotiate and resolve conflict
* Ability to work in a team environment and demonstrate sound judgment
* Able to think independently
* Ability to analyze and deliver effective solutions
* Excellent organizational skills to include astute prioritization skills
* Proficient computer skills to include Microsoft and Google products

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (NICE TO HAVE):**

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in business management
* Bilingual; ability to speak, read, and write in Spanish, French, or other languages
* Prior cleaning or janitorial experience
* Familiarity with custodial practices and commercial cleaning standards
* Knowledge of floor care techniques including buffing and waxing
* Experience in industrial cleaning or facilities maintenance

**BENEFITS:**

* Medical, dental, vision, basic life, AD&D, retirement plan and disability insurance
* Eight paid holidays annually, five sick days, and four personal days
* Vacation time offered at an accrual rate of 3.08 hours biweekly. Unused vacation is only paid out where required by law.

**Closing**
-----------

Diversified Maintenance is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race/ethnicity, age, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, genetic information, disability, protected veteran status or relationship/association with a protected veteran, or any other basis or characteristic protected by law.

If you have difficulty using the online system and require an alternate method to apply or require an accommodation, please contact our local Human Resources department.

role.title: Regional Director of Operations
role.description:
At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. Whether that means specialized training, a clearly laid out career trajectory or collaborating cross-functionally, we are committed to the success of our people the same way we’ve been committed to the success of the El Pollo Loco brand for the last 50 years. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
 
 
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
 
 
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
 
 
Let’s Get Loco!
 
 
What’s in it for you!
 
 

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:** 
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
 
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
 
 
**Education/Work Experience:** 
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
 
 
**License/Certifications:** 
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
 
 
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:** 

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
 
 
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
 
 
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

role.title: Vice President Quality Control
role.description:
Position Overview:

Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.

Company Overview:

The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
 
 
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki. 
 
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers

Job Description:

Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.

What you will do

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

Minimum qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

Preferred qualifications

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.
* Global leadership within a contract development and manufacturing organization supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing.
* Experience scaling Quality Control from clinical development through process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Working knowledge of the following: Food and Drug Administration; European Medicines Agency; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency; International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; and European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; as well as applicable data‑integrity expectations.
* Experience deploying global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation.
* Credentials from the American Society for Quality, and training in Lean and Six Sigma or equivalent quality and operational excellence disciplines.

If you are a strategic, hands‑on executive who thrives at the intersection of science, operations, and leadership, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and help us raise the bar for quality worldwide.

The US salary range for this position is $272,000 to $325,000. Pay within this range varies by work location and may also depend on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

Our programs are designed to focus on maintaining and enhancing all pillars of health with a robust benefits package including medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage with the option of a Health Savings Account with company contributions. In addition, we offer an industry leading 401(k)savings plan, insurance coverage, employee assistance programs and various wellness incentives. We support life-work balance with paid vacation time, sick time, and company holidays. Explore a supportive environment that enriches both your personal and professional growth!

This is a global position that will support all our FUJIFILM Biotechnologies sites. Benefits and compensation will be governed by the location that you are based from and considered your home site.

As part of any recruitment process, FUJIFILM Biotechnologies collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants. The organisation is committed to being transparent about how it collects and uses that data and to meeting its data protection obligations and may share this as part of the global recruitment process with hiring managers in Europe and the United States.

To all agencies: Please, no phone calls or emails to any employee of FUJIFILM about this requisition. All resumes submitted by search firms/employment agencies to any employee at FUJIFILM via-email, the internet or in any form and/or method will be deemed the sole property of FUJIFILM, unless such search firms/employment agencies were engaged by FUJIFILM for this requisition and a valid agreement with FUJIFILM is in place. In the event a candidate who was submitted outside of the FUJIFILM agency engagement process is hired, no fee or payment of any kind will be paid.

 
EEO Information:

Fujifilm is committed to providing equal opportunities in hiring, promotion and advancement, compensation, benefits, and training regardless of nationality, age, gender, sexual orientation or gender identity, race, ethnicity, religion, political creed, ideology, national, or social origin, disability, veteran status, etc.

ADA Information:

If you require reasonable accommodation in completing this application, interviewing, completing any pre-employment testing, or otherwise participating in the employee selection process, please direct your inquiries to our HR Department (fdbglobaltalent@fujifilm.com).

role.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
role.description:
**Bold Thinking. World Changing.**
At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
**Explore what’s possible.**
Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
**Step into the future.**
SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
**Are you bold thinking?**
Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective**
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas Of Accountability**

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.
* Wafer Planning and Customer Delivery: Partner with Wafer Planning and Program Management to align schedules, capacity, and customer priorities; identify delivery risks and oversee recovery plans to maintain on time delivery (OTD) performance.
* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.

role.title: Sr. Manager Manufacturing Engineer
role.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
DESCRIPTION:
 
 
As a Sr. Manager, Manufacturing Engineering at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will guide and support engineering teams to drive operational excellence and innovation across our manufacturing facilities. You will provide strategic direction and technical leadership for manufacturing processes, automation initiatives, and continuous improvement projects while ensuring compliance with quality and regulatory requirements. Working collaboratively with cross-functional teams, you'll optimize production efficiency, implement new technologies, and deliver solutions that enable our mission of making the world healthier, cleaner and safer.
 
 
REQUIREMENTS:
 
 

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in regulated manufacturing environments (pharmaceutical, medical device, or related industries)
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Chemical) or related technical field. Strong focus on Automation required.
* Industry certifications in Six Sigma, PMP, or related areas are beneficial
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical teams and facilitating organizational change
* Demonstrated success implementing automation, digitalization and continuous improvement initiatives
* Strong understanding of cGMP, ISO standards and regulatory compliance requirements
* Experience with new product introductions, technology transfers and process validation
* Expertise in lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodology and practical process improvements (PPI)
* Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans aligned with business objectives
* Strong project management skills and experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities with data-driven decision making
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills to engage stakeholders at all levels
* Proficiency with manufacturing systems, automation platforms and quality tools
* Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
* Experience with capital project planning, budgeting and resource allocation
* Relocation: Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
* Work Authorization: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer-sponsored work authorization.
* Pre-Employment Screening: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of all applicable pre-employment requirements, including a background check and drug screening, in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

**Compensation And Benefits**
The salary range estimated for this position based in New Jersey is $155,100.00–$232,650.00.
 
 
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
 
 

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
* Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
* Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

role.title: Director - Corporate Continuous Improvement
role.description:
**Description**
****Position Summary****
The Director of Corporate Continuous Improvement (CI) leads MacAllister’s enterprise CI strategy, Corporate CI team, and improvement portfolio. In partnership with the owner, executive team, and divisional leaders, the Director helps establish and build alignment around MacAllister’s CI vision, strategy, priorities, and multi-year roadmap. The Director identifies and prioritizes high-value opportunities, builds organizational problem-solving capability, and leads improvement work from opportunity identification through execution and sustainment.
 
 
The role establishes CI standards, tools, and training; coaches, mentors, and influences leaders and teams across the organization; and communicates CI priorities, results, and opportunities for support.
 
 
The ultimate objective is to build and sustain a culture in which continuous improvement becomes habitual and is reflected in how leaders and employees think, act, solve problems, and improve the way work gets done.
 
 
****Position Duties/Responsibilities****
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Partner with the executive team, and divisional leaders to develop and maintain MacAllister’s CI strategy, multi-year roadmap, priorities, and operating model aligned with company goals. Build leadership alignment and shared ownership of CI priorities and expectations across the organization.
* Own CI project identification, prioritization, approval, execution, and close-out, focusing on where CI creates the most value; support employee-driven improvement alongside leader-sponsored initiatives.
* Maintain consistent project close-out documenting results, lessons learned, and sustainment plans; verify improvements and results are sustained and take corrective action as needed.
* Set organization-wide CI standards, tools, and terminology; guide Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA application grounded in facts, data, and root cause analysis; coach project teams and facilitate select high-impact improvement events.
* Lead improvement-related change management, engaging affected employees early and ensuring process adoption and sustainment.
* Oversee CI training tailored to responsibility levels using consistent terminology and live projects; coach and support CI-trained departmental leaders who remain in their home departments outside CI.
* Define CI value primarily through capability measures—leaders solving problems independently, AI use cases adopted, and idea-to-approval cycle time—with financial results as supporting evidence.
* Communicate CI initiatives, results, and available support so leaders know when and how to engage the team; share success stories and recognize improvement contributors.
* Use coaching-first leadership to build team autonomy, confidence, and influence; foster problem reporting, experimentation, and learning from mistakes by supporting people publicly and coaching privately.
* Hire, develop, and manage CI personnel; oversee budget, resource allocation, and team structure as needs evolve.
* Play a leadership role in MacAllister’s Center of Practice for CI, AI, and problem-solving leadership, incorporating AI and other emerging technologies into CI methods where they improve problem solving, decision making, or productivity. Partner with MacAllister’s enterprise AI leadership on broader AI strategy, standards, and adoption.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises the Corporate CI team and oversees day-to-day operations of the CI department. Mentors and coaches CI team members to strengthen their capabilities as problem solvers, facilitators, coaches, and trusted business partners.
* Reviews and evaluates the work and performance of reporting employees; has authority for hiring and disciplinary actions.

****Position Requirements****
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, or a related field.
* 10 years or more of experience in continuous improvement, operations, or business transformation.
* 5 years or more of experience leading leaders.
* Proven success coaching others to identify and solve problems independently.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA.
* A valid driver’s license.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in business or a related discipline.
* Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt or equivalent depth of experience designing and delivering CI training.
* Experience at a Caterpillar dealership or in the equipment sales, service, or rental industry.
* Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn and apply emerging technologies, including AI, to strengthen problem solving, process improvement, decision support, and organizational productivity. Experience applying AI in these areas is preferred but not required.
* Experience building on an existing CI function and growing its influence across a multi-location organization.

****Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities****

* Strong coaching and leadership development skills; leads through influence rather than authority.
* Ability to connect improvement work to business priorities and help leaders choose where to focus.
* Curiosity about and practical comfort with AI as a business tool.
* Exceptional communication and facilitation skills with all levels, from the front line to executives.
* Ability to build and maintain trusted relationships with executives, senior managers, and teams.
* Respect for existing culture and relationships, with the judgment to improve without unnecessary disruption.
* Strong organizational, prioritization, and project management skills.
* Effective computer skills with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn proprietary systems.

****Other Requirements of Position****

* Works under broad supervision. Designs and carries out programs and far-reaching objectives independently, informing management as appropriate.
* Major responsibilities require a wide degree of creativity and latitude.
* If an error is made while in this position, it will require some effort to identify and can significantly impact the company financially.
* Frequently communicates with coworkers, customers, company executives, and management.
* Maintain equipment and supplies to avoid waste, damage to areas and equipment, and to prevent accidents.

The duties and responsibilities outlined in this posting are not exhaustive and may evolve based on business needs.
 
 
All MacAllister Machinery companies are an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, including Disabled and Veteran applicants.

role.title: Director of Engineering & Continuous Improvement
role.description:
**Position Summary**

The Director of Process Engineering & Continuous Improvement is the company's technical authority for how meals are made and the owner of its improvement engine. This hands-on leader combines deep manufacturing process engineering with a disciplined continuous improvement approach to make production operations more consistent, efficient, safe, and cost-effective across Mom's Meals.

The role will focus primarily on kitchen and production operations, supporting a highly automated manufacturing environment through process design, equipment performance, root cause problem solving, and structured improvement projects. The position will also support fulfillment operations by identifying automation and process opportunities that improve throughput, labor efficiency, accuracy, and customer service.

The Director partners closely with Production, Fulfillment, Supply Chain, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance, R&D, IT, and Finance to execute strategic projects and deliver measurable, sustained improvement across the enterprise. This is a player-coach role: the Director is expected to engage directly on the production floor, lead technical problem solving, and develop the engineers and improvement practitioners on the team.

***This position will travel to our other facilities 25-50% at varying times.***

***Ideally, the selected candidate will work out of one of our Production facilities (Ankeny/Grinnell, IA, Oklahoma City, OK, or North Jackson, OH) but are open to remote for the right skills and experience.***

**Position Responsibilities may include, but not limited to**

Process & Technical Engineering

* Serve as the company's process authority for meal production, owning process design, line layouts, standard work, and process specifications for cooking, chilling, portioning, and packaging
* Lead structured process control plans, risk assessments, and capability studies to reduce variation and improve consistency
* Drive yield, discard, and portion-control improvements through engineering-based solutions
* Partner with Production, Food Safety and Quality, Maintenance and R&D teams to ensure process changes are validated, documented, and sustained on the production floor
* Reduce downtime and defects through root cause analysis and hands-on, engineering-based problem solving
* Evaluate emerging manufacturing technologies and process innovations that improve efficiency, quality, and scalability
* Ensure engineering and process solutions comply with USDA, FDA, food safety, sanitary design, and regulatory requirements

Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence

* Build and lead a multi-site continuous improvement program, maintaining a prioritized project portfolio with defined savings targets validated with Finance
* Champion Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies (such as A3, DMAIC, value stream mapping, changeover reduction, and standard work)
* Drive waste reduction, productivity improvement, and labor optimization initiatives
* Evaluate operational KPIs, including OEE, yield, labor productivity, and discards, and use data analytics to prioritize improvement opportunities
* Coach kitchen and production leaders and engineers in structured problem solving, and ensure improvements are standardized and sustained
* Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across operations

Kitchen & Production Engineering

* Lead engineering efforts supporting highly automated meal production operations
* Drive equipment performance, uptime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) improvements
* Identify ideal equipment required to produce Mom's Meals to specification at scale, including equipment that should be replaced or decommissioned and equipment that can deliver OEE improvements and a measurable return on investment
* Partner with Production leadership and Commercialization team to identify bottlenecks and improve throughput
* Lead facility expansion projects, line installations, equipment upgrades, and process redesign initiatives

Capital & Automation Projects

* Develop and manage the engineering capital plan, prioritizing projects by safety, quality, and measurable return
* Lead project prioritization, design, budgeting, vendor selection, implementation, and startup activities
* Ensure projects are completed safely, on time, and within budget
* Manage external engineering firms, contractors, equipment suppliers, and system integrators
* Build a practical, multi-year automation roadmap focused on productivity, yield, and labor efficiency
* Establish project governance, reporting, and post-implementation performance reviews

Maintenance & Reliability Partnership

* Partner with Maintenance leadership on standards for asset management, equipment lifecycle planning, and preventative, predictive, and reliability-centered maintenance practices
* Use maintenance KPIs, including downtime, PM completion rates, equipment failure rates, and maintenance costs, to prioritize engineering and improvement work

Leadership & Team Development

* Provide coaching, mentorship, and technical leadership to process engineering, continuous improvement, and engineering personnel
* Develop future engineering leaders, improvement practitioners, and technical subject matter experts
* Promote a culture focused on safety, engagement, accountability, and operational excellence

**Required Skills and Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field
* **10+ years of progressive engineering leadership experience within manufacturing, food production, and highly automated operations, including leading process engineering or continuous improvement teams**
* Hands-on experience applying Lean and Six Sigma tools, with a demonstrated record of delivering quantified, sustained savings and performance gains
* Strong process engineering skills, including process design, root cause analysis, process capability, statistical analysis, and OEE and yield analytics
* Demonstrated success leading capital projects and automation implementations, including equipment installations and line upgrades
* Working knowledge of industrial automation, controls, packaging systems, and manufacturing technologies
* Knowledge of Sanitary Design Principles and Standards for food manufacturing.
* Experience leading teams in regulated manufacturing environments
* Proven ability to influence cross-functional leaders and drive enterprise-wide change

**Preferred Skills and Experience**

* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification
* Food manufacturing, packaged goods, pharmaceutical, and automated distribution experience
* Experience with Industry 4.0 technologies, predictive maintenance, and digital manufacturing tools
* Experience managing and understanding facility utility controls, including HVAC, water, and steam systems
* Professional Engineer (PE) license or advanced technical degree
 **Physical Requirements**

**Physical Requirements**

* Regularly required to use hands to feel, grab, or operate objects, tools, and controls while reaching with hands and arms
* Frequently required to stand, communicate, and listen
* Occasionally required to walk, stoop, kneel or crouch
* Occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds
* Visual perception to perform job including peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
* Able to perform repetitive movements
* Able to work in variable temperatures (cold/hot)

role.description:
This position is incentive eligible. 
 
 

##### **Medical City Healthcare**

##### **Division Director of Quality**

##### **Full Time, Exempt**

Want to join a team of daring managers who care without reservations or limits? Our Parallon team is looking for a(an) Division Director of Quality. HCA Healthcare is an advanced healthcare network that has committed up to $300 million to our incredible team members over the course of three years.

##### **Job Summary and Qualifications**

* Provide timely consultation and support to hospital QM departments and facility and division senior management.
* Direct and coordinate QM activities of market and division teams as needed and as delegated by the DVPQ.
* Assist division facilities in strengthening proactive quality management, and performance improvement processes.
* Develop, identify, analyze, and present data for division-wide QM initiatives; guide teams in using improvement data appropriately.
* Direct the division centralized quality coordinator team, maintaining regulatory compliance with timely completion of OPPE/FPPE.
* Support facility preparation for The Joint Commission (TJC) surveys, under the direction of the Division Director of Regulatory.
* Support facility during TJC surveys and collaborate during medical staff sessions to present OPPE/FPPE data.
* Coordinate quality improvement education for hospital and medical staff when requested by senior management.
* Orient newly appointed QM directors to division and market processes.
* Represent the division at corporate meetings when requested by the DVPQ.
* Uphold the Corporate Ethics and Compliance Program, HCA Code of Conduct, and Mission and Values.

**What qualifications you will need:**

* Bachelor's degree in a healthcare-related field or comparable experience required
* Master's degree in healthcare or related field preferred
* Texas or compact Nursing license preferred.
* CPHQ preferred

##### **Benefits**

Parallon, offers a total rewards package that supports the health, life, career and retirement of our colleagues. The available plans and programs include:

* Comprehensive medical coverage that covers many common services at no cost or for a low copay. Plans include prescription drug and behavioral health coverage as well as free telemedicine services and free AirMed medical transportation.
* Additional options for dental and vision benefits, life and disability coverage, flexible spending accounts, supplemental health protection plans (accident, critical illness, hospital indemnity), auto and home insurance, identity theft protection, legal counseling, long-term care coverage, moving assistance, pet insurance and more.
* Free counseling services and resources for emotional, physical and financial wellbeing
* 401(k) Plan with a 100% match on 3% to 9% of pay (based on years of service)
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan with 10% off HCA Healthcare stock
* Family support through fertility and family building benefits with Progyny and adoption assistance.
* Referral services for child, elder and pet care, home and auto repair, event planning and more
* Consumer discounts through Abenity and Consumer Discounts
* Retirement readiness, rollover assistance services and preferred banking partnerships
* Education assistance (tuition, student loan, certification support, dependent scholarships)
* Colleague recognition program
* Time Away From Work Program (paid time off, paid family leave, long- and short-term disability coverage and leaves of absence)
* Employee Health Assistance Fund that offers free employee-only coverage to full-time and part-time colleagues based on income.

Learn more about Employee Benefits

***Note: Eligibility for benefits may vary by location.***

HCA Healthcare is committed to research and clinical protocols. Do you want to impact standards of care and save lives across the country? Apply today to our Division Director of Quality and be a part of the innovation of ideas.

Medical City Healthcare strives to deliver excellence. We are committed to the care and improvement of human life. We provide the highest quality, cost-effective healthcare in the communities we serve. Medical City Healthcare is one of the North Texas region’s largest and most comprehensive healthcare providers. We have 16 hospitals, 5,000 physicians and more than 17,000 employees in Dallas-Fort Worth. Medical City Healthcare is the only healthcare system in North Texas with an adult and children’s hospital on the same campus. We are a part of HCA Healthcare. HCA Healthcare includes 185 hospitals in the United States and England. Medical City Healthcare has six hospitals that are Magnet® recognized by the American Nurses Credentialing Center Magnet Recognition Program®. We have been recognized by Texas Monthly as a Best Companies to Work for in Texas. HCA Healthcare has been named to LinkedIn’s 2021 Top Companies list of 50 best workplaces to grow your career.

HCA Healthcare has been recognized as one of the World’s Most Ethical Companies® by the Ethisphere Institute more than ten times. In recent years, HCA Healthcare spent an estimated $3.7 billion in cost for the delivery of charitable care, uninsured discounts, and other uncompensated expenses.

HCA Healthcare Co-Founder

Unlock your potential with a leading healthcare provider dedicated to its patients, colleagues and communities. Help guide our team as a(an) Division Director of Quality and **help us improve more lives in more ways**.

*We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.*

role.title: Head of Process Engineering Peptides API
role.description:
**Company Description**

**About AbbVie**

AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at www.abbvie.com. Follow @abbvie on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

 **Job Description**

**Position Summary:**

The **Sr Director Process Engineering Peptides API** sets enterprise direction and senior technical governance for process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing within AbbVie Strategic Investment.

The role supports Strategic Investments through engineering leadership, technical expertise, standards development, technical governance and project execution support across multiple manufacturing sites, strategic investments and technology platforms.

The role supports engineering activities associated with peptides manufacturing facility investments, new production capabilities, strategic capacity creation, advanced manufacturing platforms and new technology deployments across the Strategic Investment portfolio.

The role partners with Strategic Investments, manufacturing sites, operations, quality, EHS, validation / CQV and external engineering partners to deliver technically robust and business-aligned engineering solutions.

**Strategic Investment Context**

* Strategic Investment provides engineering leadership, technical governance, standards development and project execution support across AbbVie’s Strategic Investments and strategic capital portfolio.
* The organization supports new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing facilities, new platform deployments, strategic capacity creation, advanced biologics and CGT manufacturing capabilities and standards development for emerging technologies across Strategic Investments.
* Strategic Investment roles are expected to promote common standards, transfer lessons learned across regions and sites, and enable consistent engineering delivery across strategic capital investments.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Investment Governance and Standards:**

* Establish, maintain and deploy global engineering standards, technical practices and governance expectations for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery.
* Drive consistent application of technical standards, design principles, lessons learned and engineering playbooks across regions, sites and capital projects.
* Define enterprise standards, engineering requirements and technical guardrails for new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technologies, including requirements for consistent design, deployment, qualification, operation and scale-up across Strategic Investments.
* Ensure discipline strategies support AbbVie’s long-range Strategic Investment objectives, strategic investment programs and adoption of new technologies across future manufacturing platforms.
* Provide governance and escalation for technical decisions with material safety, quality, compliance, cost, schedule, operability or lifecycle impact.

**Strategic New Technology and Capital Investment Support:**

* Provide engineering leadership for strategic capital investments, including new biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy facility builds, technology platform deployments, new production capabilities, strategic capacity projects and lifecycle technology upgrades.
* Support front-end engineering, facility concept development, investment option evaluation, manufacturing capability assessments and site / platform planning activities for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy assets.
* Partner with Strategic Investments and project leadership to ensure technical assumptions, deliverables, risks and resource needs are integrated into capital program plans.
* Apply Strategic Investment lessons learned and standards to improve project quality, speed, reliability and readiness across the portfolio.

**Technical Leadership and Delivery:**

* Lead or support technical decision-making for biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery across multiple manufacturing sites, capital projects and technology platforms.
* Ensure engineering deliverables support safety, quality, compliance, operability, maintainability, reliability, sustainability and operational readiness.
* Coordinate technical input from project teams, site SMEs, external engineering partners, vendors and cross-functional stakeholders.
* Drive timely resolution of technical issues and ensure suitable escalation when decisions have broader project, network or business impact.

**Cross-Functional Integration:**

* Partner with Strategic Investments, manufacturing operations, quality, validation / CQV, EHS, site engineering, MS&T, supply chain, finance and related engineering disciplines.
* Ensure discipline decisions are integrated with biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing strategy, network capacity, technology platform deployment, regulatory expectations and site handover needs.
* Facilitate collaboration across Strategic Investments, sites and project teams to avoid fragmented solutions and drive consistency across the strategic capital portfolio.
* Represent Strategic Investment in technical reviews, project forums and risk discussions relevant to assigned scope.

**Capability Building and Continuous Improvement:**

* Share engineering best practices, lessons learned and technical knowledge across sites, regions and projects.
* Build capability through coaching, mentoring, technical review discipline and development of reusable engineering practices.
* Promote a culture of engineering excellence, safety, quality, reliability, collaboration, accountability and proactive risk management.
* Support continuous improvement of Strategic Investment standards, templates, knowledge management and project delivery approaches.

**Strategic Investment Leadership Expectations:**

* Collaborate across Strategic Investments to identify, develop and deploy best practices, technical standards, lessons learned and capability-building initiatives.
* Promote consistency, quality, reliability, sustainability and project delivery performance across regions, sites and capital projects.
* Support long-range manufacturing strategy, strategic investment planning and Strategic Investment capability development.
* Build technical capability through coaching, mentoring, standards governance, knowledge management and cross-functional collaboration.

**Stakeholder Interfaces**

Strategic Investments:

* Investment planning, portfolio alignment, technical assumptions, front-end engineering, biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technology deployment standards and strategic capital program support.

Manufacturing Sites and Operations:

* Network needs, site readiness, operability, maintainability, startup, handover and operational performance support.

Quality, Validation / CQV and EHS:

* Compliance expectations, validation strategy, qualification readiness, safety, risk review and inspection readiness interfaces.

Strategic Investment Disciplines:

* Cross-discipline technical integration, standards, design reviews, technical issue resolution and lessons learned.

External Engineering Partners, EPCM Firms, Vendors and OEMs:

* Technical oversight, deliverable review, issue escalation, supplier alignment and execution quality.

 
**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Science or a relevant technical discipline required; advanced degree preferred where relevant.
* Typically 15+ years of relevant engineering, manufacturing, capital project, technical operations or regulated manufacturing experience.
* Demonstrated technical capability in biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process engineering strategy, process platform deployment, process package design, technical assurance, manufacturing technology interfaces and project delivery.
* Experience supporting biologics drug substance, cell therapy, gene therapy, viral vector, mRNA, sterile biologics or similarly regulated biopharmaceutical manufacturing environments preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to work across global functions, manufacturing sites, project teams, suppliers, vendors and external engineering partners.
* Strong communication, risk management, technical judgment, stakeholder engagement and structured problem-solving skills.

**Technical Competencies:**

* Biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy process design and process package review
* Front-end engineering and concept development
* Biologics and CGT technology transfer, platform deployment and manufacturing scale-up
* Process safety and CQV interfaces
* Strategic Investment support
* Strategic capital investment and new biologics / CGT technology deployment support
* Engineering governance and standards
* Development of engineering standards and deployment requirements for emerging biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing technologies
* Technical understanding of bioreactor, harvest, purification, single-use, closed processing, aseptic processing, viral vector, cell processing and cryogenic / cold-chain interfaces as applicable to biologics and CGT platforms
* Technical risk management
* Project execution support
* Stakeholder management
* Vendor / partner technical coordination
* GMP and regulated manufacturing awareness
* Operational readiness and handover support

**Leadership Competencies:**

* Strategic thinking and enterprise mindset
* Matrix leadership and influence without direct authority
* Clear technical communication and executive-ready recommendations
* Risk-based decision making and issue escalation
* Collaboration across functions, sites, regions and external partners
* Capability building, mentoring and knowledge sharing
* Lead, coach and develop a high-performing technical engineering team with clear priorities, accountability, development plans and delivery expectations aligned to Strategic Investment objectives.
* Set technical direction for the engineering team, ensuring work is prioritized against safety, quality, compliance, business value, capital delivery needs and long-range manufacturing strategy.
* Build technical bench strength by identifying capability gaps, developing succession depth, mentoring senior engineers and enabling knowledge transfer across sites, projects and technology platforms.
* Create an inclusive, disciplined technical decision-making environment where engineers challenge assumptions, manage risk transparently and escalate decisions with material safety, compliance, cost, schedule or operability impact.
* Align team performance with enterprise standards by reinforcing consistent engineering practices, structured technical reviews, lessons learned adoption and measurable delivery outcomes.
* Continuous improvement and commitment to safety, quality and compliance

**Working Relationships:**

This role works globally with Strategic Investments, Strategic Investment disciplines, biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy manufacturing sites, quality, validation / CQV, EHS, operations, MS&T, supply chain, finance, external engineering firms, technology vendors and equipment suppliers. The role is expected to operate across multiple projects, manufacturing sites and technology platforms, supporting new biologics and CGT manufacturing investments, new production capabilities and enterprise standards for emerging biologics drug substance and cell and gene therapy technologies.

role.title: Senior Manager, Quality Management
role.description:
L3Harris is dedicated to recruiting and developing high-performing talent who are passionate about what they do. Our employees are unified in a shared dedication to our customers’ mission and quest for professional growth. L3Harris provides an inclusive, engaging environment designed to empower employees and promote work-life success. Fundamental to our culture is an unwavering focus on values, dedication to our communities, and commitment to excellence in everything we do.

L3Harris is the Trusted Disruptor in defense tech. With customers’ mission-critical needs always in mind, our employees deliver end-to-end technology solutions connecting the space, air, land, sea and cyber domains in the interest of national security.

***Job Title:*** ***Senior Manager, Quality Management***

***Job Code: 48241***

***Job Location: Orange, VA***

***Job Schedule: 4/10: Employees work 10 hour days, 4 days a week***

**Job Description:**

The **Senior Manager of Quality** will be responsible for leading all aspects of Quality Assurance throughout the product development lifecycle for L3Harris’ Culpeper, VA site. This position will have responsibility for direct supervision and leadership of ~60 quality personnel. The Sr. Manager will be responsible for driving continual process and product improvement ensuring product and process integrity, leading to customer satisfaction and overall mission success while supporting division quality, delivery and cost targets. This position will lead quality personnel and collaborate frequently with Program leadership, Engineering, Manufacturing and Supply Chain personnel. This is a hands-on, highly involved leadership position. Ability to obtain a Secret clearance is required for this position.

**Essential Functions:**

 

* Responsible for the Quality Engineering and Inspection functions, supporting all business practices, including quality planning, compliance monitoring and validation for programs, hardware, software and inspection.
* Responsibility for resolving technical challenges, ensuring successful tactical execution, as well as creating and implementing the strategic vision for the Quality department.
* Develop and implement strategic Quality initiatives and programs in support of the site promoting sound and effective principles as set forth in company procedures, government standards and directives, and commercially proven methodology and ensure that the department conforms to these principles.
* Promote a strong culture of quality focused on every employee engaged and enhancing the customer experience through rigorous attention to detail and prevention of defects.
* Work closely with the program teams and the functional organizations to ensure that all phases of the product life cycle, from early customer involvement through post-delivery support, meet the requirements for mission success.
* Ensure that manufacturing engineering, operations and design engineering interact sufficiently throughout the product planning and design phases to ensure a seamless hand-off during product transition to production including design reviews and facilitating quality concurrent Engineering.
* Responsible for the maintenance of quality records that document the quality status of material/products and provide necessary information and cumulative data for internal and external Customer responses.
* Develop, review and verify compliance of all Work Package Descriptions issued for Quality tasks for proposals and ongoing contracts/projects.
* Improve the efficiency of the Quality organization through effective leadership, individual and group training, and process improvement.
* Collect and analyze key quality measures such as Cost of Poor Quality to develop zero defect plans, improve yields and reduce rework during engineering and manufacturing efforts. Report to senior leadership on business performance including action plans to improve business execution and status of strategic initiatives.
* Maintain certification and compliance efforts for AS9100 and other required certifications.
* Business travel up to 10%.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 12 years of prior related Quality Management experience. Graduate Degree and a minimum of 10 years of prior related experience. In lieu of a degree, minimum of 16 years of prior related experience.
* Active Secret US Security Clearance.

**Preferred Additional Skills:**

 

* In depth knowledge of quality and reliability methods and procedures for hardware and software systems as they apply to the aerospace or electronic industry.
* Greenbelt or Blackbelt certification and/or proven education or work history in leading and implementing projects.
* Experience with Configuration Control management practices.
* ASQ certification preferred; Experience managing AS9100 certified business.
* 5+ years Quality management or operations leadership experience.
* Strong leadership and interpersonal skills including communications, facilitation, consulting, coaching, and influencing.
* Self-motivated and possess demonstrated ability to motivate others to achieve timely results.
* Highly collaborative style, capable of working across multiple functional areas to drive results.

In compliance with pay transparency requirements, the salary range for this role in Virginia is $121,500 – $225,500. This is not a guarantee of compensation or salary, as final offer amount may vary based on factors including but not limited to experience and geographic location. L3Harris also offers a variety of benefits, including health and disability insurance, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, EAP, education assistance, parental leave, paid time off, and company-paid holidays. The specific programs and options available to an employee may vary depending on date of hire, schedule type, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

L3Harris Technologies is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. L3Harris is committed to treating all employees and applicants for employment with respect and dignity and maintaining a workplace that is free from unlawful discrimination. All applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or other related medical conditions), gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, characteristic or membership in any other group protected by federal, state or local laws. L3Harris maintains a drug-free workplace and performs pre-employment substance abuse testing and background checks, where permitted by law.

Please be aware many of our positions require the ability to obtain a security clearance. Security clearances may only be granted to U.S. citizens. In addition, applicants who accept a conditional offer of employment may be subject to government security investigation(s) and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.

By submitting your resume for this position, you understand and agree that L3Harris Technologies may share your resume, as well as any other related personal information or documentation you provide, with its subsidiaries and affiliated companies for the purpose of considering you for other available positions.

role.title: Director, Operations
role.description:
Overview:

Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger.

The Director of Operations is responsible for overseeing daily production activities to drive efficiency, maintain quality, and ensure adherence to company standards. This role leads the development and implementation of organizational strategies, standards, and best practices to achieve world-class operational performance. Additionally, the Director of Production collaborates closely with site and business leadership, leveraging resources and expertise to ensure our products consistently meet customer expectations.

Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Responsibilities:

* Lead with a clear view of where the organization needs to be in 1-3 years; communicates strategic direction to employees and how it fits with the day-to-day actions and results being driven.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
* Implement and maintain value streams and SCQDCT management system within the site.
* Provide coaching and support to supervisors and frontline employees to enhance skills and performance.
* Set clear and measureable performance expectations, in line with corporate goals; proactively analyze and manage all relative operations performance metrics.
* Provide timely, accurate and complete reports on the operating conditions of the company.Ensure compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.
* Ensures alignment with functional leadership (e.g., Engineering, Finance, Quality, Facilities, and Human Resources) on performance management and talent development.
* Ensure the facilities operate within the Company’s ISO and FDA quality management system.
* Participate in the development of the location’s monthly revenue forecasts.
* Monitor and adjust production output and staff levels to support the location’s revenue and cost targets.
* Participate in the development and control of the location’s budgets and quarterly forecasts.
* Working with the senior leadership team, help to develop and implement winning strategies to grow revenues and profitability.
* Ensure the site maintains maximum confidentiality in a highly proprietary operationLead relationship with key intercompany customers to ensure maximum service throughout the value chain.

Required Qualifications:

* BS degree in a technical field, preferably engineering or life sciences.
* Prior experience managing a manufacturing department/organization in a regulated environment.
* Prior experience managing an engineering team.
* Experience working within a Lean, six-sigma organization.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Prior experience managing an independent manufacturing organization.
* Familiarity with contract manufacturing, ISO and FDA quality system requirements, medical device and diagnostics manufacturing.
* Lean, six-sigma green or black belt certified.
* Experience with Nitinol products and processing
* Experience wit Wire and Tube fabrication
* MBA or relevant business management experience.

Physical Demands:

* Ability to work long hours when necessary and to have a presence with a 24/7 operation.
* Domestic travel required

Compensation:

* The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000–$204,000.
* Our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

Resonetics offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, well-being, and financial security of our employees and their families. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance; a 401(k) retirement plan; paid time off (PTO); 10 paid holidays; Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA); life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) insurance; Short-Term Disability (STD) and Long-Term Disability (LTD) insurance; accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance. Eligibility and benefit offerings may vary based on employment status and applicable plan provisions.
