role.title: Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch
role.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.
 
 
With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.
 
 
**LOCATION:**
Remote with Travel
 
 
US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.
 
 
This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.
 
 
The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**Key Performance Metrics**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**Qualifications**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**Education And/Or Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**Physical Demands**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

The intent of this job description is to provide a representative summary of the essential duties and responsibilities performed by incumbents of this job. Incumbents may be requested to perform job-related tasks other than those specifically presented.

The compensation range for this position is $158,600.00 - $237,800.00, depending on experience. This position may be eligible for performance based bonus plan.
 
 
**Benefits Package**
Our comprehensive U.S. benefit offerings include: Health benefits, 401(k) retirement savings program with company match, PTO, and more. More information on our benefits and rewards can be found on our career page: https://www.idexcorp.com/careers/our-benefits-and-rewards/

role.title: Director of Quality
role.description:
Granite State Manufacturing is a leading contract manufacturer of large, complex, precision machined and welded components, supporting the US Navy in building submarines.

We specialize in high-mix, low-to-medium volume production, delivering precision, quality, and on-time performance on custom-engineered products. Our capabilities include:

* Large-format CNC machining
* Heavy fabrication and welding (MIG, TIG, FCAW, SAW)
* Assembly, inspection, and testing
* Program management for complex builds

We are known for handling tight tolerances, complex geometries, and demanding customer specifications.

Our work environment is supportive, providing what our people need to do great work.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

Plans, coordinates, and directs quality program designed to ensure continuous production of products consistent with established standards. Continuously increasing Quality Awareness across the company, with the goal of reducing and eliminating barriers and obstacles to throughput, while reducing overall cost and schedule. Leadership, both within the QC/QA staff, and across all departments, is expected to make it easier for employees to make quality products, and make it easier for customers to do business with GSM.

We strive to make things faster, better, and less expensively.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

* You will be the face of Quality to our customers, and will participate in program reviews with GSM and Customer senior management.
* Leading our Continuous Improvement efforts will provide you with the ability to make substantial changes to our internal processes and procedures across the board, in our constant efforts to be more efficient, more effective, and more valuable to our customers.
* Directs workers engaged in inspection and testing activities to ensure continuous control over materials, facilities, and products.
* In addition to the Quality Engineers and Quality Assurance Specialists, your direct reports will include the Quality Inspectors and Quality Administrators. Working closely together with your team you will make great use of complementary skills and experience, and be most effective in bringing GSM‘s performance to the next

* Build a path with continuous improvement efforts to be more efficient, more effective, and more valuable to customers. Strive to increase production speed, improve quality, and reduce
* Participates in evaluation of Vendor Quality.
* Demonstrates responsibility and accountability for creating a professional, safe, and clean environment evidenced by: being at work on time to perform assigned duties, following the policies of Granite State Manufacturing, always wearing safety glasses in designated areas, maintaining a neat and orderly work area, and following safety practices to prevent errors.
* Demonstrates commitment to teamwork by establishing effective relationships and networks with both managers/directors and workers, and collaborating with them to accomplish shared purposes and goals.
* Abides by GSM Code of Ethics and Business Conduct standards and strictly observes all U.S. and foreign laws and regulations.

**EEO STATEMENT**

Granite State Manufacturing (GSM) is an equal opportunity employer. GSM does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, citizenship, veteran status, age, physical or mental disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state, or local laws in its programs, activities, or employment.

 **Requirements**

**QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**

* **Bachelor's degree and related experience and /or training or equivalent combination of education and experience.**
* Knowledge of manufacturing methods, product design, metallurgy, customer requirements, military specification, NDT and documentation systems.
* **Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.**
* **Experience in defense/aerospace related job fabrication and welding environment**
* **Experience with manufacturing processes to include: CNC machining, painting, Fabrication techniques and weld processes in a heavily regulated environment such as DOD or Aerospace**
* **Ability to write technical reports, ISO procedures and correspondence.**
* **Ability to deal with difficult problems involving ambiguous circumstances in non-standardized situations.**

 
**Benefits**

**BENEFITS**

Compensation & Benefits

* Competitive salary
* Medical insurance
* Dental & Vision, Life insurance (Company paid)
* Disability benefits (Company paid)
* 401(k) & 401(k) company matching
* Paid time off and holidays
* Flexible spending accounts
* Health savings account
* Referral program
* Overtime opportunities (if applicable)
* Training and career growth in advanced manufacturing
* Employee assistance program

Why Join Us?

* Work on large-scale, one-of-a-kind projects
* Stable industry with strong customer demand
* Opportunity to grow in a flexible, high-skill environment
* Collaborative team focused on quality and craftsmanship

role.title: Director, Risk Management and Quality
role.description:
**Director of Risk Management and Quality**

**Who We Are:**

At Triangle Springs, we are committed to empowering and supporting a diverse and determined workforce who can drive quality, scalability, and significant impact across our hospitals and communities. In your role, you’ll support those that are in our facilities who are interfacing and providing care to our patients and community members. We believe that our collective efforts will shape a healthier future for the communities we serve. Our programs offer customized rehabilitation tailored to the specific needs of those recovering from a stroke, brain injury, neurological conditions, trauma, spinal cord injury, amputation or orthopedic injury.

**Why Choose Us:**

* Affordable medical, dental and vision plans provided to meet the needs of full-time employees and their families
* Competitive Paid Time Off
* Tuition reimbursement, continuing education opportunities and apprenticeship programs for eligible employees
* 401(K) retirement plans
* Flexible spending and health savings accounts

**How you’ll contribute:**

The Director of Risk Management and Quality is responsible for the development and administration of Performance Improvement, Risk Management, and Staff Development activities throughout the hospital to ensure that all state, federal, and Joint Commission standards for care are consistently met. The Director collects and analyzes data on hospital performance, incidents, and documentation to improve hospital performance and ensure provision of quality care. The Director works closely with all department leaders to recommend and provide required staff development and tailored programs based upon data analysis. The Director monitors, investigates, and as required, reports all hospital incidents. 
 
**Essential Functions:**

To perform this job, an individual must perform each essential function satisfactorily with or without reasonable accommodation.

* Provides oversight and continuous monitoring of the hospital’s quality program, ensuring alignment with organizational objectives and best‑practice standards.
* Demonstrates comprehensive expertise in all applicable regulatory requirements, including The Joint Commission (TJC), Medicaid, and state and federal healthcare laws.
* Serves as a key advisor to department leaders by interpreting regulatory standards, offering guidance, and supporting compliance readiness.
* Partners with hospital staff to proactively identify risk and safety concerns, leading the development and execution of corrective action plans.
* Collects, analyzes, and interprets performance data to evaluate hospital outcomes and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Oversees the incident reporting process, ensuring timely documentation, investigation, data analysis, and reporting to the Quality Council and the Chief Executive Officer.
* Utilizes the Plan‑Do‑Check‑Act (PDCA) methodology to design, implement, and measure improvement initiatives that enhance quality and patient safety.
* Ensures ongoing organizational compliance with all regulatory standards and applicable laws, maintaining survey readiness at all times.
* Always exhibit the company’s core values of champion patient care, do the right thing, embrace individuality, act with kindness, and making a difference together.

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in counseling, Social Work, Nursing, or related clinical field from an accredited school required. Master’s degree in clinical field from an accredited school preferred.
* Counseling, Social Work, or Registered Nurse license preferred.
* Three years of risk management and regulatory compliance in a healthcare setting are required.
* CPR certification is required within 30 days of employment and prior to any patient contact.
* De-escalation certification is required within 30 days of employment and prior to any patient contact.

**EEOC Statement:**

Triangle Springs is committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunities for all applicants and employees and complies with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination against any employee or applicant for employment because of color, race, sex, age, religion, national origin, disability, genetic information, gender identity, sexual orientation, veterans' status or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

role.title: Administrative Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations, Department of Medicine
role.description:
Department Overview:

The Department of Medicine (DoM) at OHSU is comprised of a diverse community of faculty, staff, clinicians, researchers, educators, and learners dedicated to advancing patient care, education, and research across ten divisions.

The Director of Inpatient Quality and Operations provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, quality management, and performance improvement support for inpatient clinical services across the Department of Medicine's ten specialty divisions and care sites. Reporting to the Vice Chair of Clinical Practice and partnering closely with the Vice Chair for Administration, this position serves as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and clinical effectiveness initiatives.

Function/Duties of Position:

Working collaboratively with DoM and OHSU Health quality leaders, division leadership, hospital operations, finance, revenue cycle, informatics, care management, nursing leadership, clinical documentation teams, and physician leaders, the Director advances the Department's inpatient quality, operational, clinical, and financial goals through the design, implementation, and oversight of standardized processes, performance improvement efforts, operational reporting, and strategic initiatives.

Emphasis is placed on quality programing and outcomes, patient safety, clinical documentation integrity, coding accuracy, revenue cycle performance, operational efficiency, provider productivity, inpatient capacity management, and growth planning across all Department of Medicine inpatient services. The Director supports a broad portfolio of inpatient programs spanning multiple clinical specialties and care settings.

This position functions within a highly matrixed environment and serves as a key liaison between departmental leadership and enterprise partners, ensuring alignment with OHSU Health strategic priorities, quality objectives, and high-reliability organizational principles.

**Inpatient Quality and Operations Leadership and Oversight**

* Work in direct partnership with the DoM Vice Chair of Clinical Practice, DoM Associate Vice Chair of Inpatient Services, Healthcare quality leaders, and other institutional leaders to oversee and coordinate quality-focused inpatient care across Department of Medicine divisions.
* Provide strategic administrative leadership and operational oversight for Department of Medicine inpatient programs and services.
* Serve as the Department's primary administrative leader for inpatient quality, patient safety, operational performance, and performance improvement initiatives.
* Partner with division heads, section heads, medical directors, healthcare administrators, quality leaders, and physician leaders to identify and address operational and quality barriers affecting patient safety, access, efficiency, provider experience, and clinical outcomes.
* Shape and implement standardized inpatient quality, safety, and operational best practices across medicine specialties.
* Coordinate departmental quality improvement initiatives focused on reducing medical errors, serious safety events, healthcare-associated infections, hospital-acquired conditions, avoidable readmissions, preventable complications, and patient harm.
* Lead administrative efforts related to inpatient quality programs, patient safety activities, inpatient capacity management, patient flow, consult services, discharge efficiency, care coordination, and service-line optimization.
* Support departmental participation in mortality reviews, safety event reviews, quality committees, accreditation activities, regulatory preparedness efforts, and institutional quality initiatives.
* Establish and maintain departmental quality and operational governance structures, including scorecards, dashboards, performance reviews, and accountability processes.
* Partner with healthcare quality teams to identify opportunities for improvement and coordinate development of corrective action plans.
* Serve as the primary administrative liaison between Department of Medicine leadership, inpatient programs, Healthcare quality teams, and hospital operations leadership.
* Monitor operational, quality, and patient safety performance measures and drive action planning to improve outcomes.
* Facilitate multidisciplinary teams and stakeholder groups responsible for advancing inpatient quality, safety, throughput, and operational effectiveness.

**Revenue Cycle, Billing, Coding, and Clinical Documentation Integrity**

* Serve as the Department's operational lead for inpatient professional revenue cycle performance.
* Partner with Revenue Cycle, Professional Coding, Clinical Documentation Integrity (CDI), Finance, Compliance, and physician leaders to improve revenue capture, reimbursement, and operational performance.
* Evaluate and improve inpatient provider documentation practices, coding accuracy, charge capture processes, and billing workflows.
* Lead provider education efforts related to documentation requirements, coding regulations, payer expectations, reimbursement methodologies, and compliance standards.
* Monitor inpatient professional fee performance, wRVU generation, Case Mix Index (CMI), coding trends, denials, reimbursement outcomes, and documentation quality measures.
* Develop dashboards and performance reporting tools that support transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify specialty-specific opportunities for revenue optimization, operational efficiency, and documentation improvement.

**Performance Improvement and Strategic Initiatives**

* Conduct workflow analyses and redesign efforts to eliminate inefficiencies, reduce variation in care delivery, and improve service performance.
* Collaborate with Quality, Analytics, Finance, Informatics, and Operations teams to establish measurable goals and monitor outcomes.
* Develop project charters, implementation plans, success metrics, and performance benchmarks for strategic initiatives.
* Support departmental strategic planning activities and implementation of enterprise priorities related to inpatient growth, quality, and operational excellence.
* Advance high-reliability organization principles and support compliance with accreditation and regulatory requirements.

**Data Analytics, Reporting, and Financial Performance**

* Develop and maintain operational, financial, quality, patient safety, and utilization reporting structures for departmental and divisional leadership.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive inpatient quality scorecards and dashboards.

 + Benchmark Department performance against institutional, regional, and national metrics when available.
 + Support financial forecasting, business case development, and investment planning for inpatient growth initiatives.

* Provide subject matter expertise regarding inpatient quality, safety, operational performance, workflow redesign, and professional revenue optimization.
* Lead communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management activities for major inpatient initiatives.
* Support development of a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, patient safety, and operational excellence throughout Department of Medicine inpatient programs.

Required Qualifications:

* Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives within healthcare organizations.
* Experience working collaboratively with physician leaders, nursing leadership, and hospital operational teams.

* Strong knowledge of inpatient healthcare operations and physician practice management.
* Strong knowledge of healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, performance measurement, and high-reliability organizational principles.
* Knowledge of inpatient reimbursement methodologies, documentation requirements, clinical coding, and revenue cycle practices.
* Knowledge of regulatory, accreditation, and quality reporting requirements affecting inpatient healthcare delivery.

* Demonstrated ability to develop quality scorecards, operational dashboards, and executive-level performance reporting.
* Ability to analyze complex clinical, operational, financial, and quality data and translate findings into actionable improvement strategies.
* Demonstrated ability to manage large-scale operational and performance improvement initiatives across multiple clinical specialties.
* Experience leading multidisciplinary efforts focused on reducing medical errors, improving patient outcomes, and advancing a culture of safety.
* Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes without direct authority.
* Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, Epic, reporting platforms, and healthcare analytics tools.

* Experience with quality reporting, patient safety programs, accreditation activities, and regulatory readiness.

* Matrix leadership experience.

Demonstrated ability to leverage advanced analytics, financial modeling, forecasting tools, artificial intelligence-enabled technologies, and other data-driven methodologies to improve operational efficiency, inform strategic decision-making, optimize resource allocation, and support sustainable program growth.

Professional office environment; may include occasional travel to affiliate and partner sites. In-person work schedule expected, with limited telework acceptable.

role.description:
**Director of Quality Assurance** 
Location: 203A Log Canoe Circle, Stevensville, MD 21666 
Shift Hours: 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, Monday through Friday 
Pay Range: $135,000 -175,000 + Bonus Eligibility!

**Hydrasearch,** a proud affiliate of The Dixon Group, is looking for a **Director of Quality Assurance** to join our team in **Stevensville, MD**! The Director of Quality Assurance will lead the organization's quality management strategy and ensure compliance with customer, industry, and regulatory requirements. This role is responsible for overseeing quality assurance programs, driving continuous improvement initiatives, managing quality personnel, and partnering with operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to maintain high standards of product quality and operational excellence.

**At Hydrasearch, we value the contributions of our Military Veterans and proudly employ our nation’s heroes. Veterans are strongly encouraged to apply.**

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead and manage the Quality Assurance function across the organization.
* Develop, implement, and maintain the Quality Management System (QMS).
* Ensure compliance with AS9100D and ISO 9001, customer requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Establish quality objectives, metrics, and reporting processes to drive continuous improvement.
* Oversee internal audits, external audits, and customer quality assessments.
* Manage corrective and preventive action (CAPA) programs and root cause analysis initiatives.
* Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Operations leadership to improve product and process quality.
* Analyze quality data and performance trends to identify improvement opportunities.
* Lead customer complaint investigations and resolution efforts.
* Develop and drive supplier quality programs. Actively work with vendors to address quality concerns.
* Build, mentor, and develop quality personnel and future leaders within the organization.
* Support new product introduction activities by ensuring quality standards are incorporated into design and manufacturing processes.
* Prepare and present quality performance updates to executive leadership.

**What We're Looking For:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, or a related technical field required; Master's degree in Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive quality leadership experience within manufacturing, maritime & aerospace defense, industrial, or related industries required; experience supporting defense, military, or government-contract manufacturing environments preferred.
* 5+ years of experience leading quality teams and managing direct reports.
* Strong working knowledge of AS9100D & ISO 9001 quality systems.
* Experience leading internal and external audits.
* Demonstrated success implementing continuous improvement programs and driving measurable results.
* Experience with root cause analysis methodologies and corrective action processes.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and quality management tools.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and statistical process control methodologies is a plus!
* This hands-on leadership position requires extensive maritime and aerospace defense quality experience, strong knowledge of industry standards and regulations, and proven success managing external audits and compliance initiatives.

**What We Offer:**

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your family
* Competitive salary
* Bonus programs
* 401K retirement plan
* Training opportunities
* Tuition reimbursement
* Paid vacation, PTO, and holidays
* Gym reimbursements, and more!

**Who We Are:** Hydrasearch is a U.S. manufacturer specializing in fluid-transfer and control systems for maritime, aerospace, and defense applications. Since its founding in 1962, Hydrasearch has developed capabilities in hose assemblies, valve fittings, and customer machined parts, often to meet MIL-SPEC and naval standards.

**Join us and be a part of a team that values your contributions and supports your goals!**

role.title: Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance (Commercial)
role.description:
At Kailera, we are bold, authentic and committed to our mission of developing therapies that give people the power to transform their lives and elevate their overall health. Rooted in an entrepreneurial spirit and a team-oriented culture, we are working together to advance Kailera's mission to advance novel therapies for obesity and related conditions.
 
 
We are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes collaboration, integrity, and excellence. As we expand, we seek the most talented individuals with diverse backgrounds, cultures, perspectives, and experiences to join our team.

**What You'll Do:**

Kailera is preparing to bring its therapies to patients, and the Senior Director, GMP Quality Assurance will lead the quality strategy that gets us there. Reporting to the Head of Quality Assurance, you will be accountable for GMP Quality across drug substance, drug product, packaging/labeling, testing, stability, and product release as Kailera moves from late-stage clinical supply to commercial manufacturing and launch. You will develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy, build the quality systems and team needed for a compliant and reliable commercial supply chain, and serve as a trusted quality leader with Technical Operations, Regulatory, Supply Chain, and our network of contract manufacturers and testing laboratories.

 

*Required location: Waltham, MA (hub-based, onsite 3-4 days per week) OR Remote (home-based, onsite at a hub 1 week every other month).*

 

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute the commercial GMP Quality strategy and roadmap, aligned with company and functional objectives, to support registration, launch, and lifecycle supply of Kailera products
* Be accountable for the performance and results of the GMP Quality function, including key quality initiatives, goals, and product assets
* Evolve the Kailera Quality Management System from clinical phase to commercial readiness, including change control, deviations/CAPA, complaints, product quality reviews, supplier management, training, and data integrity
* Define GMP quality metrics and KPIs for Quality Management Review, and use trends to anticipate risks and drive continuous improvement across the manufacturing network
* Advise senior leadership on quality risks, compliance trade-offs, and changes in the global regulatory environment, translating external trends into Kailera's quality strategy
* Lead the quality aspects of commercial readiness, including oversight of process performance qualification (PPQ), process and analytical method validation, commercial specifications, and stability programs
* Lead pre-approval and pre-license inspection (PAI/PLI) readiness across Kailera and contract manufacturing sites; host or support health authority inspections and drive timely, effective responses and commitments
* Partner with Regulatory CMC to ensure commercial manufacturing and controls are consistent with marketing applications; provide QA review of CMC sections of regulatory filings, post-approval supplements, and variations
* Establish and oversee commercial batch record review and lot disposition, ensuring final disposition complies with approved registrations and supporting QP certification for EU supply
* Build post-market quality processes, including product complaint handling, regulatory reporting (e.g., Field Alert Reports), recalls, and annual product quality reviews.
* Oversee quality requirements for commercial packaging, labeling, artwork control, and serialization (DSCSA and other market requirements)
* Ensure Good Distribution Practice (GDP) compliance for commercial distribution, including qualification of third-party logistics providers, temperature excursion management, and returns

* Develop and lead risk-based quality oversight of CDMOs, contract testing laboratories, and other GMP suppliers, including qualification, audits, and performance management.

* Use independent judgment to resolve highly complex or novel quality issues, such as major deviations, OOS investigations, and supply disruptions, balancing patient safety, compliance, and supply continuity

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing GMP Quality team as Kailera scales to commercial operations, including organizational design, hiring, and succession planning
* Drive followership by leading with trust, understanding, and adaptability; coach managers and team members, recognize contributions, and foster a culture of quality, accountability, and psychological safety
* Manage GMP Quality budget and resources, including the use of external consultants and auditors

* Expert knowledge of cGMP and GDP requirements, including 21 CFR Parts 210, 211, and 11, EudraLex Volume 4 (including Annex 16), and ICH Q7, Q9, and Q10; working knowledge of 21 CFR Part 4 and DSCSA preferred
* Track record of successfully hosting or supporting FDA, EMA, and/or other health authority inspections
* Extensive experience leading quality oversight of CDMOs and contract laboratories, including audits and Quality Agreements
* Proficient in Veeva QualityDocs and Veeva QMS or a comparable electronic quality system
* Recognized expertise in GMP quality, with the judgment to give clear, risk-based quality advice that balances compliance with business needs
* Exceptional communication skills; tailors messages to executives, cross-functional partners, contract manufacturers, and health authorities, and explains the rationale behind decisions to build buy-in
* Proven ability to guide teams through complex change and ambiguity, anticipate problems before they escalate, and keep work focused on defined outcomes in a fast-paced, growing company
* Builds trusting relationships internally and externally, and navigates conflict through open dialogue and collaboration
* Brings creative, practical solutions to complex problems and encourages others to take calculated risks that challenge the status quo while maintaining compliance

 

**Education:**

* BA or BS degree in a scientific discipline required; advanced degree preferred

role.title: Director of Quality (Head of Quality)
role.description:
Division Department: Therapeutics | Quality

Position Title: Director of Quality (Head of Quality)

Reports To: Corporate Head of Quality (proposed; final reporting structure to be confirmed)

Salary - $225-250,000 based on experience

**PharmaLogic is expanding our therapeutics business line. Our therapeutics business, Agilera, is the** **world’s only cGMP-compliant CDMO currently manufacturing and distributing commercial radiopharmaceutical therapeutics across more than 30 countries. In this role,** **you will have the opportunity to work as part of a unique environment that is involved in the entire value chain, from the preclinical phase to the commercial production and distribution of radiopharmaceuticals.**

**Role Summary:**

The Director of Quality serves as the Head of Quality for PharmaLogic’s newly acquired therapeutics business, leading the quality organization and establishing the systems, capabilities, and culture needed for reliable GMP manufacturing. This leader is accountable for the pharmaceutical quality system and Quality oversight of sterile therapeutic drug manufacturing, testing, and release under applicable 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211 requirements. As a member of the site leadership team, the Director partners with Operations, Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, and corporate Quality to support clinical supply, technology transfer, commercialization, and growth. The role requires independent judgment, visible leadership on the manufacturing floor, and the ability to translate quality requirements into practical execution while protecting patient safety and product quality.

**Job Responsibilities and Duties:**

**Quality Leadership and Governance**

Lead the Quality function, including Quality Assurance and oversight of Quality Control and microbiology activities within the assigned organizational scope. Set strategy, staffing, budgets, objectives, and development plans; build a capable team with clear accountability.

Maintain the Quality unit’s independent authority to approve or reject materials and drug products, including outsourced products; approve quality-impacting procedures and specifications; and ensure documented responsibilities and appropriate escalation to corporate Quality and executive leadership.

Own batch disposition through authorized Quality personnel. Ensure production and laboratory records, deviations, and required test results receive appropriate review before release. Place materials or product on hold and stop affected operations when quality or compliance concerns warrant.

**Quality Systems and Sterile Manufacturing**

Establish and continuously improve systems for deviations, investigations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, document control, training, complaints, product quality reviews, and quality risk management. Require scientifically sound root-cause analysis and verification of CAPA effectiveness.

Provide Quality oversight of aseptic processing and contamination control, including cleanrooms, environmental and personnel monitoring, gowning qualification, aseptic process simulations, sterilization, disinfection, and container closure integrity, as applicable.

Oversee laboratory controls, specifications, analytical method validation and transfer, stability programs, and investigations of out-of-specification and out-of-trend results. Ensure complete, accurate, traceable data and effective controls for electronic records and computerized systems.

Approve qualification and validation strategies, protocols, and reports for facilities, utilities, equipment, manufacturing processes, cleaning, and computerized systems. Ensure a documented lifecycle approach and continued process verification.

**Manufacturing Readiness and External Partners**

Lead Quality readiness for new products, technology transfers, process scale-up, and commercial launches. Establish clear acceptance criteria and readiness decisions with Development, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.

Serve as the primary site Quality representative for FDA inspections and customer audits. Lead inspection preparation, responses, and commitments; maintain sustained readiness and timely, effective remediation.

Manage supplier qualification, contract laboratory and manufacturer oversight, audits, and quality agreements. Define responsibilities with CDMO customers and ensure outsourced activities meet agreed quality requirements.

**Acquisition Integration and Regulatory Partnership**

Lead the acquisition Quality integration plan: assess inherited systems and commitments, prioritize gaps by risk, align governance and procedures with corporate standards, and manage changes without disrupting compliant product supply.

Partner with Regulatory Affairs on manufacturing and quality content for filings, change assessments, and regulatory commitments. Lead quality defect assessments and support recalls, field actions, and required notifications with designated functions.

For radiopharmaceutical therapeutics, oversee appropriate controls for isotope and precursor quality, radiochemical testing, time-sensitive manufacturing and disposition, and stability. Partner with Radiation Safety and EHS on safe, compliant execution.

**Quality Performance and Continuous Improvement**

Present quality performance and material risks to site and corporate leadership. Use management reviews and meaningful metrics to improve investigation quality, CAPA effectiveness, release reliability, training, and inspection readiness.

**Job Requirements, Skills and Education:**

**Required Qualifications**

Bachelor’s degree in chemistry, biology, microbiology, pharmacy, engineering, or a related scientific discipline.

Typically, 10 or more years of progressive pharmaceutical Quality experience, including at least 5 years leading teams or major Quality programs in a GMP manufacturing environment.

Demonstrated Quality leadership in sterile injectable manufacturing, with substantial knowledge of aseptic processing, contamination control, laboratory controls, validation, and data integrity.

**Strong working knowledge of 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, applicable electronic records requirements, and relevant FDA guidance and ICH quality principles.**

Experience leading regulatory inspections, complex investigations, remediation, and batch disposition, with sound scientific judgment and the ability to defend quality decisions.

Experience supporting technology transfer, clinical or commercial manufacturing, and cross-functional delivery of significant quality or operational improvements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

Experience with therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals or radioligand therapies; CDMO operations and pharmaceutical customer partnerships; and commercial launch or preapproval inspection readiness.

Experience integrating an acquisition, building or transforming a quality organization, and implementing electronic quality management systems. Advanced scientific degree or relevant professional certification.

**Leadership and Working Expectations**

A visible, hands-on leader who develops people, communicates clearly, and holds teams accountable. Able to challenge decisions constructively, escalate risks promptly, and make timely decisions under pressure. Regular onsite presence in manufacturing and laboratory areas, compliance with required gowning and safety practices, and availability for critical quality events are expected. Travel requirements will be defined for the role. Essential functions may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

Come join our winning team and begin a fulfilling career with us by applying today. 
 
PharmaLogic is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other protected class.

**Benefits Include:**

401(k) retirement benefit program

Medical

Dental care

Disability insurance

Employee assistance program

Life insurance

On-site parking

Paid time off

Vision care

role.title: Director of Quality, Risk, and Compliance
role.description:
At Snoqualmie Valley Health, we’re not just in the business of healthcare; we’re in the business of empowering our community to live boldly and live well. Our commitment to excellence and innovation calls for team members who will build trust, obsess over excellence, lead innovation, and deepen connections within our community. We are guided by our core values, and we’re looking for someone who can embody those principles as part of our dynamic and growing team.

Located in a trailblazing, adventure-loving town at the base of the Cascades, Snoqualmie Valley Health is an independent public hospital district serving a vibrant community that thrives on both adventure and connection. This is more than a job—it’s an opportunity to be part of something bigger.

JOB TITLE: Director of Quality, Risk, and Compliance

POSITION SUMMARY: The Director plays a critical role in cultivating a culture of patient safety, continuous improvement, and regulatory excellence to ensure the highest standards of care for the community. This position leads the organization’s quality, risk, and compliance programs, partnering closely with clinical and operational leaders to strengthen performance and drive measurable improvements in patient outcomes.

The Director oversees the development, implementation, and evaluation of key quality initiatives, ensuring strict adherence to regulatory requirements and accreditation standards. This includes identifying trends, prioritizing improvement opportunities, and guiding hospital departments in the execution of effective corrective actions. Serving as a strategic resource, the Director provides expert leadership and consultative support to hospital and medical staff in achieving regulatory success and maintaining organizational compliance across all quality improvement activities.

This role also manages the coordination of certification standards and survey readiness, including the drafting and revision of policies and procedures related to quality, compliance, and risk management. The ideal candidate brings extensive experience in survey preparation and functions as a Subject Matter Expert in quality, championing a strong culture of safety and operational excellence throughout the organization.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

Build Trust: We exhibit integrity, transparency and compassion in every interaction.

* Oversee patient complaints and grievance processes ensuring compliance, documentation, followup, service recovery, and improvement.

* Investigate and address incident reports resolving care issues and recommending prevention strategies.

* Ensure confidentiality of all qualityrelated data and provide accurate reports to the Board of Commissioners and leadership

* Respond to and prepare information for public record requests.

role.title: Director, Quality Assurance Operations
role.description:
**Director, Quality Assurance Operations**

At Vericel Corporation, we are pioneers in advanced cell therapies for sports medicine and severe burn care, transforming patient lives through cutting-edge regenerative medicine. Our commitment to innovation, patient-centered focus, and scientific excellence drives us to develop groundbreaking treatments including MACI (knee cartilage repair), Epicel and Nexobrid (burn care).

**Position Summary**

The Director of Quality Operations is responsible for the strategic leadership and performance of Quality Assurance Operations, Document Control, and Supplier Quality Management. This role provides oversight of product disposition and release, labeling and documentation controls, deviations, CAPAs, product complaints, supplier quality management, tech transfer activities, controlled documentation, and internal audits. The Director translates business objectives and quality risks into operational strategies, resource plans, and measurable outcomes. This position develops organizational capability through effective leadership, succession planning, and talent development while driving cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement. The Director exercises independent, risk-based decision-making within delegated authority to ensure compliance, operational excellence, and sustained product quality.

**Schedule:** This position is onsite Monday through Friday at our Burlington office, with one day per week at our Cambridge office.

**Essential Functions:**

**Quality Operations and Department Management**

* Provide strategic oversight and accountability for product disposition and release, deviations, CAPAs, complaints, supplier quality management, documentation controls, labeling review, and internal audit programs and tech transfer activities; ensure activities are executed in compliance with regulatory requirements and business objectives.
* Establish department strategy and annual operating plans aligned with organizational priorities, quality objectives, and risk management principles; determine resource, staffing, and budget requirements to support business growth and compliance commitments.
* Serve as the Quality Operations representative in cross-functional governance, planning, and decision-making forums involving Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Technical Operations, Product Development, and Project Management.
* Make and oversee complex quality decisions within delegated authority using scientific rationale, regulatory requirements, and risk-based assessments; escalate significant compliance or product quality risks with recommended mitigation strategies.
* Develop, implement, and maintain departmental policies, procedures, standards, and governance processes to ensure consistent and effective execution across all areas of responsibility.
* Ensure continuous inspection readiness; lead departmental support for regulatory inspections, customer audits, and internal audits, and ensure timely completion of all commitments and corrective actions.

**Continuous Improvement and Quality Metrics**

* Lead a portfolio of strategic, cross-functional quality improvement initiatives designed to enhance compliance, strengthen quality systems, improve operational efficiency, reduce deviation recurrence, and increase right-first-time performance.
* Establish measurable objectives, success criteria, timelines, and effectiveness metrics for improvement initiatives; monitor progress and ensure sustainable implementation of results.
* Analyze performance trends, quality metrics, audit findings, and CAPA effectiveness data to identify systemic risks, prioritize resources, and drive data-informed decision making.
* Partner with Quality leadership to establish performance indicators and business reviews that ensure accountability and continuous improvement.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

**Staff Management and Leadership Development**

* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Quality Operations organization through effective organizational design, workforce planning, talent acquisition, and succession planning.
* Develop leadership capability through coaching, mentoring, performance feedback, and individualized development plans; cultivate future leaders and ensure organizational readiness for key roles.
* Delegate authority and accountability appropriately while maintaining oversight of critical quality and business outcomes.
* Foster a culture of engagement, collaboration, continuous learning, and accountability that supports both employee growth and organizational objectives.
* Provide ongoing coaching and performance management, including recognition, corrective action, and career development guidance as appropriate.

**Performance Management and Accountability**

* Establish and communicate clear goals, priorities, performance expectations, and timelines; hold leaders and employees accountable for achieving results in accordance with company values and quality standards.
* Maintain effective communication through regular leadership meetings, team meetings, one-on-one discussions, and skip-level engagements.
* Address performance concerns promptly through documented coaching, performance improvement planning, and follow-up actions to ensure sustained improvement and accountability.
* Promote transparency, collaboration, and decision-making discipline across the department to support operational effectiveness and employee engagement.

**Qualifications, Education, & Experience:**

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 14 years of experience in a biotech or pharmaceutical regulated industry (minimum of 10 years in Quality/8 years directly related to management of personnel). Prior leadership experience required.
* Master’s degree with a minimum of 12 years of experience in the life sciences regulated industry (minimum of 10 years in Quality/8 years directly related to management of quality personnel). Prior leadership experience required.
* Strong working knowledge of ICH, FDA, ISO, and cGMP regulations.
* Excellent technical writing and presentation skills.
* Strong leadership and personnel development experience
* Excellent communication skills at organization, team, and individual levels.
* Demonstrated experience leading Quality Operations functions within a regulated GMP environment.
* Proven ability to lead regulatory inspections and manage interactions with FDA and other regulatory authorities.
* Experience developing and leading managers and building succession pipelines within a Quality organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Medical device, biotechnology, cell and gene therapy, or combination product experience strongly preferred.
* Proficient in Auditing, both internal and vendor.
* Prior International experience.

**Working Conditions & Physical Demands:**

* Ability to lift up to 30 lbs.
* Ability to travel if required.
* Must be able to support holiday coverage.
* Must be able to gown into the CNC areas when required

**Why Vericel?**

* **Mission-Driven Work:** Help bring potentially life-enhancing cell therapies to patients with serious medical conditions.
* **Innovative Products:** Work with a first-in-class therapy backed by clinical success and provider trust.
* **Career Growth:** Be a part of a growing organization with opportunities to expand your impact.
* **Collaborative Culture:** Join a supportive, cross-functional team that values passion, integrity, and excellence.

The salary range Vericel reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of this posting is $206,000 - $225,000 annually.

The actual salary offered will be determined based on factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, experience, and skills. Bonus, incentive pay, equity and benefits may be provided in addition to the base compensation listed above.

In accordance with Massachusetts law, Vericel provides the pay range that it reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for a particular and specific employment position at the time of posting or offer. This range is subject to change based on business needs, market conditions, and individual qualifications. Employees and applicants may request the pay range for their position or for a position to which they are applying. Retaliation for making such a request is strictly prohibited.

**EEO Statement**

*All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, or protected veteran status and will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Vericel Corporation is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer.*

*Vericel Corporation is VEVRAA federal contractor and desires priority referrals of protected veterans for job openings at all locations within the state.*

role.title: VP, Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations - Santa Clara, CA - Hybrid
role.description:
At Gigamon, our purpose is to protect the hybrid networks and data of the largest, most complex organizations on the planet. Certified as a Great Place to Work, we offer a deep observability pipeline that efficiently delivers network-derived intelligence to cloud, security, and observability tools. This helps our customers to eliminate security blind spots, optimize network traffic, and dramatically reduce tool cost and complexity, enabling them to better secure and manage their hybrid cloud infrastructure. Gigamon has served more than 4,000 customers worldwide, including over 80 percent of Fortune 100 enterprises, 9 of the 10 largest mobile network providers, and hundreds of governments and educational organizations. 
 
The VP, Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations leads the strategy and execution of Gigamon’s global supply chain and manufacturing operations. This executive oversees planning, procurement, supplier management, manufacturing, logistics, and operational execution to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality products to customers worldwide. The role partners closely with Engineering, Quality, Finance, Sales, and Customer Support to align operational capabilities with business priorities and product growth. Through disciplined execution, risk management, and continuous improvement, this leader strengthens scalability, resilience, and customer satisfaction. 
 
What you’ll do:

* Define and execute a global supply chain and manufacturing strategy aligned with Gigamon’s business objectives, product roadmap, and customer requirements.
* Lead demand and supply planning, materials management, procurement, contract manufacturing, production scheduling, inventory optimization, order fulfillment, logistics, and distribution.
* Establish scalable operating processes, systems, metrics, and governance to improve forecast accuracy, capacity utilization, delivery performance, inventory turns, cost, and working capital.
* Develop and maintain strategic relationships with contract manufacturers, suppliers, logistics providers, and other key partners.
* Drive supplier selection, qualification, performance management, capacity planning, commercial negotiations, and continuity planning.
* Build resilience across the supply chain by identifying operational risks, developing contingency plans, and ensuring effective responses to disruptions.
* Partner with Engineering and Product teams on new product introduction, product lifecycle management, design-for-manufacturability, component strategy, and engineering change control.
* Collaborate with Quality and Engineering to establish and maintain product, supplier, and manufacturing quality standards.
* Oversee global manufacturing and fulfillment operations to ensure products are delivered on time, at the required quality level, and in accordance with customer and regulatory requirements.
* Ensure compliance across global trade, tariffs, export controls, environmental requirements, and product regulations, including country-specific certifications and regulatory approvals, in partnership with Legal, Engineering, Quality, and relevant teams.
* Manage reverse-logistics operations, including customer returns and repair; oversee return-material-authorization (RMA) processes and the performance of repair providers and other service partners.
* Lead cross-functional efforts to improve operational efficiency, reduce complexity, and optimize total cost of ownership.
* Oversee product-cost and inventory governance, including standard-cost reviews, bill-of-materials (BOM) cost changes, purchase-price variance (PPV), and excess and obsolete (E&O) inventory, in partnership with Finance.
* Establish clear performance expectations and develop a high-performing, globally distributed operations organization.
* Provide executive-level reporting, recommendations, and accountability for supply chain and manufacturing performance.

What you’ve done:

* Led global supply chain, manufacturing, and operations organizations in a technology, networking, telecommunications, electronics, or similarly complex product environment.

role.title: VP, Operations
role.description:
**Building the people that build the world.**

With platforms in HVAC and Detection and Measurement, SPX Technologies builds innovative solutions that enable a safer, more efficient, sustainable world. Through our RiSE talent development framework, we Reach, Identify, Strengthen, and Engage our employees to support them in their continued development. We’re a global company of problem solvers, collaborators, and innovators, and our businesses build solutions that impact the world.

As part of HVAC Cooling, SPX Cooling Technologies is a leader in high quality industrial HVAC equipment used to cool large facilities like hospitals, data centers, and power plants. With cooling towers, fans, and refrigeration units, companies rely on brands like Marley, Recold, and SGS to provide comfort and mission critical and industrial cooling solutions.

 

**How You Will Make an Impact**

The Vice President, Operations is a key member of the business unit leadership team and is responsible for the global operations strategy and execution for a rapidly growing business scaling beyond $1.5 billion in annual revenue. This leader will have responsibility for a global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities and will ensure the operations organization has the capacity, capabilities, systems, talent, and processes required to support significant organic and inorganic growth.

The VP, Operations will establish and execute a scalable global operating model that delivers world-class performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, working capital, and customer service. This leader will drive greater consistency and integration across manufacturing locations while ensuring the operating footprint, capital investments, supply chain capabilities, and organizational structure are positioned to support long-term growth.

A critical priority will be building an operations organization capable of operating at significantly greater scale. The VP will develop strong plant and functional leaders, create clear accountability across the operations network, institutionalize continuous improvement, and partner closely with Commercial, Engineering, Product Management, Finance, Human Resources, and Supply Chain to translate business strategy into operational execution.

**What You Can Expect in This Role**

* **Develop and execute the global operations strategy** to support the business unit's growth, financial objectives, customer commitments, and long-term strategic plan.
* **Lead the global manufacturing network of 8+ facilities**, establishing common operating expectations, performance metrics, management systems, and accountability across locations.
* **Build the operational capacity and capabilities required to support a $2B+ business**, anticipating future requirements for facilities, equipment, automation, technology, supply chain, and talent.
* **Own manufacturing footprint and capacity strategy**, including plant utilization, expansions, greenfield/start-up operations, consolidations, transfers of production, and other network optimization opportunities.
* **Drive world-class performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and Working Capital**, establishing clear performance expectations and corrective actions across the global operating organization.
* **Champion a culture of safety**, ensuring consistent leadership practices, risk identification, corrective actions, compliance, and continuous improvement across all manufacturing locations.
* **Establish a disciplined Lean operating system** utilizing standard work, daily management, Kaizen, problem solving, value-stream optimization, and other continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustained performance improvement.
* **Improve operational scalability and productivity** through automation, manufacturing technology, process redesign, labor productivity, plant layout optimization, and improved utilization of assets.
* **Lead operations planning and execution**, ensuring alignment between customer demand, production capacity, labor, materials, inventory, and capital requirements through disciplined SIOP/S&OP and scheduling processes.
* **Optimize material flow and working capital**, improving inventory turns, supplier performance, schedule adherence, throughput, and overall cash conversion.
* **Develop and execute the global capital strategy for Operations**, prioritizing investments based on growth requirements, productivity, safety, quality, capacity, automation, and return on invested capital.
* **Partner with Engineering and Commercial leadership** to improve manufacturability, new product introduction, quote-to-delivery execution, capacity planning, and responsiveness to changing customer requirements.
* **Support acquisition integration and business expansion**, establishing operating standards, identifying synergies, integrating newly acquired manufacturing operations, and accelerating performance improvement.
* **Build a high-performing global Operations leadership team**, strengthening succession depth and developing Plant Managers and functional leaders capable of leading increasingly large and complex operations.
* **Create a culture of accountability and operational excellence**, ensuring leaders use data, metrics, structured problem solving, and operating rhythms to identify issues early and deliver commitments.
* **Serve as a strategic advisor to the President and business leadership team**, bringing an operations perspective to growth strategy, investment decisions, customer commitments, acquisitions, organizational design, and long-range planning.

**Key Measures of Success**

Success in this role will be demonstrated through:

* Sustained improvement in employee safety and environmental performance
* World-class product quality and reduction in customer quality issues
* 95%+ on-time delivery performance and improved schedule adherence
* Year-over-year productivity and manufacturing cost improvement
* Improved inventory turns and working capital performance
* Effective deployment and return on capital investments
* Capacity and manufacturing footprint aligned with business growth
* Successful operational integration of acquisitions and new facilities
* Strong succession depth and leadership capability across Operations
* Consistent implementation of operating systems and best practices across the global manufacturing network

**What We Are Looking For**

**Required Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive operations and manufacturing leadership experience, including significant leadership of complex, multi-site operations.
* Demonstrated experience leading a large-scale global or geographically dispersed manufacturing organization.
* Experience operating within a business of significant scale and complexity, ideally $1B+ in revenue with demonstrated experience supporting substantial growth.
* Proven ability to scale manufacturing capacity, systems, processes, and organizations during periods of rapid growth.
* Demonstrated success improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost, and working capital performance across multiple manufacturing locations.
* Strong experience in Lean manufacturing and building sustainable continuous improvement cultures.
* Experience developing manufacturing footprint strategies including plant expansions, start-ups, consolidations, transfers, and capacity investments.
* Demonstrated success developing senior operations leaders and building strong succession pipelines.
* Experience working effectively within a matrixed, global organization and influencing across functions.
* Experience operating in both union and non-union manufacturing environments preferred.
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or manufacturing operations strongly preferred.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Enterprise-level strategic thinking combined with a strong bias for execution.
* Ability to translate aggressive business growth plans into executable operations, capacity, talent, and capital strategies.
* Strong financial and business acumen with an understanding of operating margin, manufacturing economics, capital allocation, working capital, and return on investment.
* Demonstrated ability to establish operating systems, metrics, governance, and accountability across a diverse manufacturing network.
* Strong change leadership capability and demonstrated success leading organizations through significant growth and transformation.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to operate effectively from the plant floor through the executive leadership team.
* Ability to identify emerging operational risks, resolve near-term issues, and simultaneously build the capabilities required for long-term growth.
* Strong knowledge of ERP, planning, manufacturing technology, automation, and data-driven operating environments.

**Education & Certifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field required.
* MBA or advanced degree strongly preferred.
* Lean/Six Sigma or comparable continuous improvement certification preferred.

**Travel & Working Environment**

* Significant domestic and international travel required to maintain strong leadership presence across the global manufacturing network.
* Regular interaction within manufacturing environments with varying levels of noise, temperature, and other plant conditions.

**How we live our culture**

Our culture is at the center of what we do and, more importantly, who we are. Our core values set a standard for how we manage ourselves, and our Leadership Model sets the standard for how we engage with each other. Whether you are an individual contributor or you lead a large team, each of us leads at SPX.

**What benefits do we offer?**

We know that the well-being of our employees is integral. Our benefits include:

* Generous and flexible paid time off including paid personal time off, caregiver, parental, and volunteer leave
* Competitive health insurance plans and 401(k) match, with benefits starting day one
* Competitive and performance-based compensation packages and bonus plans
* Educational assistance, leadership development programs, and recognition programs

**Our commitment to embrace diversity to build a culture of inclusion at SPX**

We value different backgrounds, experiences, and voices at SPX, and we are committed to challenging ourselves, openly communicating, and striving to improve every day. We believe in creating an inclusive work environment where everyone has a voice and is encouraged to realize their fullest potential.

SPX is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer committed to making selection decisions without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation or identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis.
