role.title: Sr. Director, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation
role.description:
Location:
Buffalo, NY, US, 14213

Req ID: 41812

Segment: Supply Chain

Rich’s, also known as Rich Products Corporation, is a family-owned food company dedicated to inspiring possibilities. From cakes and icings to pizza, appetizers and specialty toppings, our products are used in homes, restaurants and bakeries around the world. Beyond great food, our customers also gain insights to help them stay competitive, no matter their size. Our portfolio includes creative solutions geared at helping food industry professionals compete in foodservice, retail, in-store bakery, deli, and prepared foods, among others. With more than 13,500 associates working globally in 100 countries and annual sales of $5.9 billion, Rich’s is a global leader with a focus on everything that family makes possible. Rich’s®—Infinite Possibilities. One Family.

**Purpose Statement**
---------------------

The Senior Director/VP, Global Manufacturing Strategy & Network Transformation will shape and drive the long-term manufacturing strategy for the enterprise, with primary accountability for the global TCCS manufacturing network and a broader mandate to identify opportunities across the total manufacturing enterprise. Reporting to the Head of Operations, this leader will guide critical decisions around manufacturing footprint, capacity and capability, capital deployment, technology, and operating standards across businesses and regions.

This role will be instrumental in ensuring the manufacturing network is positioned to support significant global growth and evolving business needs. The leader will take an enterprise-wide view of manufacturing, connecting sites, regions, and businesses to optimize existing assets and capabilities, identify network opportunities, anticipate future capacity requirements, and inform strategic investments.

Working across regional and business manufacturing organizations, Supply Chain, Quality, R&D, Finance, Procurement, and Commercial, this executive will bring together complex operational and business inputs to establish clear manufacturing priorities and translate strategy into an actionable, long-range network roadmap. The role will also serve as a trusted manufacturing advisor to the Head of Operations and broader executive leadership team.

**Key Accountabilities and Outcomes**
-------------------------------------

* Set the long-term vision and network roadmap for global TCCS manufacturing, aligned to the Enterprise TCCS strategic plan and Vision 2030, and help shape the broader enterprise manufacturing strategy.
* Act as the manufacturing business partner to the EBU lead: bring manufacturing input into the annual strategic planning cycle, flag where growth plans require new lines or capabilities, and coordinate regional responses through one point of contact.
* Partner with Supply Chain Planning to model capacity against growth plans over a five-year horizon, identifying where and when the network will run short and recommending the best response: add lines, build new capacity, use open capacity in another region, or consolidate.
* Lead network optimization and footprint scenarios across regions, such as building new capacity in one country versus using available capacity in another, or rebalancing frozen and aseptic/UHT capacity, recognizing that idle capacity also carries cost.
* Partner with Finance on major capacity and capability investments, including greenfield and brownfield projects: bring the operational view to the business case, test assumptions on cost, capacity, risk, and timing, and help shape recommendations for executive approval.
* Prepare the network for strategic global customers and programs by anticipating long-lead equipment needs, including when to pre-purchase or hold critical equipment so growth is not delayed by equipment lead times.
* Set equipment strategy across sites, including where to standardize equipment and line design (for example, common aerators and processing equipment), and define required certifications, specifications, and hygienic design standards.
* Partner with Procurement on equipment sourcing, including qualifying new and lower-cost vendors and using economies of scale when several lines are installed in different regions at the same time.
* Support the capital planning process, led by Finance, by working with plants and regional leaders to build the right capital requests, grounded in growth plans, equipment age and life cycle, and historical spend, so capital goes where it creates the most value.
* Design a global critical spare parts strategy, including hub- or region-based stocking of high-value parts such as homogenizer blocks, to lower cost while protecting uptime.
* Use manufacturing KPIs across the TCCS network (yield, OEE, cost, uptime, and resource use such as water per liter produced) to benchmark sites, spot gaps, and identify the biggest opportunities to optimize performance and cost.
* Turn those opportunities into results by working with program and functional leaders, including TPM, Smart Factory, Engineering, Quality, Procurement, and the regional manufacturing teams, to prioritize, launch, and track improvement initiatives, capture gains before adding capacity, and scale proven practices across the network.
* Support high-priority global customer launches by coordinating across regions when issues arise, such as shifting production to another site or country.
* Partner with regional manufacturing leaders as a peer and strategic advisor: align on network priorities, co-develop multi-year regional roadmaps, and support delivery through clear governance, milestones, decision gates, and measurable outcomes.
* Build organizational capability in manufacturing strategy, network optimization, and capital planning across the TCCS network, and lead a small, high-impact team that supports the regions.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Experience**
-------------------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, manufacturing, operations, or engineering, including at least 5 years at the Director level or above with multi-site and multi-country responsibility.

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
Description:

The Plant Manager is responsible for all Operations employees within the facility. The Plant Manager is also responsible for managing all tasks related to the maintenance of the building. The Plant Manager distributes and monitors the workload within the Operations areas, while maintaining the highest level of quality and productivity possible. The Plant Manager will make sure that all instructions are thoroughly followed, and that accurate documentation is recorded correctly for all work produced. This role will demonstrate highly effective and advanced time management, organizational and planning capabilities, strong attention to efficiency and provide exceptional internal and external customer satisfaction.

Requirements:

Other duties may be assigned as needed.

* Read, interpret, and understand the work order completely and plan work to ensure meeting of customer specifications, including reviewing materials that operators are going to use for as specified on the work order.
* Distribute work to each machine with a focus on how long it should take the operator to complete the assigned work and with a focus on what work is a priority.
* Ensure completion of jobs in a timely manner, meeting quantity requirements and maintaining a high degree of quality in all work performed.
* Effectively communicate status of equipment and work in process to VP-Operations.
* Check daily reports to ensure that reprints are being completed in a timely manner and that work orders are being closed in a timely manner.
* Check daily reports to ensure that all postage receipts are done completely and in a timely manner.
* Run end of shift reports with the use of Clarity and OPALS.
* Work with vendors to maintain equipment regarding preventive maintenance and down machines.
* Make recommendations to improve workflow, quality, efficiency, and safety: in turn reducing operating problems and improving product quality within the manufacturing area.
* Enforce all safety rules are being followed during the operation, maintenance, set-up, changing parts, or any other activity taking place.
* Enforce that no employee ever removes, disables, or otherwise tampers with the function of any safety devices installed on company property or equipment. Notify management immediately if you suspect any safety device to be malfunctioning, broken, or missing.
* Keep accurate records of work performed and materials used in accordance with Content Critical Solutions procedures.
* Enforce the return of all tools and accessories used to their proper location clean and in good condition.
* Enforce that all employees maintain a neat and orderly area. Assist in general housekeeping in common areas.
* Treat coworkers with respect and courtesy.
* Perform all reasonable requests from upper management.
* Read, understand, and comply with all written work instructions.
* Work as a team and participate in Content Critical Solutions efforts to ensure continuous improvement of processes, methodologies, productivity, and quality while reducing costs.
* Manage all tasks related to the maintenance of the building.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* This job has management responsibilities over all Operations employees in the facility.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Able to understand written and verbal instructions in English.
* Able to handle a rapidly paced work environment.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* High School diploma or GED.
* Prior experience working in direct mail manufacturing preferred but not required.
* Prior experience managing a facility preferred but not required.
* Knowledgeable in Microsoft Office Suite.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**

* Ability to read and comprehend instructions, correspondences, and memos.
* Ability to verbally communicate effectively with coworkers and upper management.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**

* Ability to perform simple addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

role.title: Vice President of Operations
role.description:
**About the Role:**

The Vice President of Operations in a manufacturing environment is responsible for overseeing and optimizing all operational aspects to ensure efficiency, quality, and profitability. This role requires strategic leadership to align operational goals with the company’s overall vision and market demands. The VP of Operations will drive continuous improvement initiatives, manage cross-functional teams, and implement best practices to enhance production processes and supply chain management. They will also play a critical role in financial planning, resource allocation, and risk management to support sustainable growth. Ultimately, this position ensures that manufacturing operations meet customer expectations while maintaining compliance with industry standards and regulatory requirements.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations.
* Proven track record of strategic planning and successful execution in a complex manufacturing environment.
* Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.
* Demonstrated ability to lead large teams and manage cross-functional projects.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA) or relevant advanced degree.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Familiarity with advanced data analytics tools and enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
* Previous experience in a senior executive role within the manufacturing industry.
* Certifications related to operations management or leadership development.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and execute comprehensive operational strategies that support the company’s business objectives and growth plans.
* Lead and mentor senior management and operational teams to foster a culture of high performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Oversee production planning, quality control, supply chain logistics, and maintenance to maximize operational efficiency and product quality.
* Collaborate with finance to manage budgets, forecast operational costs, and analyze financial performance to inform decision-making.
* Utilize data analytics to monitor key performance indicators, identify operational risks, and implement corrective actions promptly.
* Drive talent development initiatives to build a skilled and motivated workforce aligned with organizational goals.
* Communicate operational plans, progress, and challenges effectively to the executive leadership team and stakeholders.
* Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental regulations, and industry standards across all manufacturing sites.

**Skills:**

The required skills such as Executive Presence and Leadership are essential for inspiring and guiding diverse teams while representing the operations function at the executive level. Strategic Planning and Execution skills enable the VP to develop actionable roadmaps that align operational activities with long-term business goals. Operational Strategy expertise is applied daily to optimize manufacturing processes, improve supply chain efficiency, and ensure product quality. Communication and Presentation skills are critical for articulating complex operational plans and performance metrics to stakeholders clearly and persuasively. Delegation, Financial Planning and Analysis, Data Analysis, and Talent Development skills are utilized to empower teams, manage resources effectively, make data-driven decisions, and cultivate a high-performing workforce that drives continuous operational excellence.

role.title: VP Operations
role.description:
Daubert Chemical Company is seeking a Vice President of Operations at our specialty chemical plant near Midway airport. The VP leads the functional areas of chemical production, customer service, supply chain, engineering, maintenance and reliability, and EHS. The VP of Operations is a member of the executive team reporting to the CEO, and is accountable for achieving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective operations while consistently meeting product quality standards, customer commitments, and regulatory requirements. This leader will establish clear performance and behavioral expectations, execute with the appropriate sense of urgency, develop organizational capabilities, and drive accountability across all operational functions. 
The successful candidate will balance day-to-day operational execution with long-term strategic planning, continuous improvement and corrective action programs, ensuring that plant equipment, processes, systems, and people are positioned to support business growth and operational excellence. 
This position requires a hands-on, visible leader who demonstrates sound judgment, urgency, follow-up, disciplined problem-solving, and a commitment to improvement and resolution of issues via a methodical corrective action program. The VP of Operations must effectively lead through others, collaborate across departments, and develop sustainable solutions that improve safety, productivity, reliability, product quality, waste reduction, and regulatory compliance. 
 
**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES** include, but not limited to the following.

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of functional managers and operational leaders, establishing clear responsibilities, performance standards, and accountability. Build leadership capability at all levels through coaching, performance feedback, succession planning, and professional development.
* Evaluate organizational structure, staffing levels, technical competencies, and resource requirements to ensure effective operational support.
* Lead operational decision-making with a strong sense of urgency, appropriate prioritization, and consideration of safety, quality, cost, and customer impact.
* Develop and manage departmental operating budgets, control expenditures, evaluate variances, and identify opportunities to improve financial performance.
* Collaborate with Sales, R&D, IT, Procurement, Quality, Finance, and other functions to align operational capabilities with business requirements.
* Provide leadership to production management to optimize plant capacity, equipment utilization, labor resources, product mix, and material availability.
* Develop and ensure execution of a long-range capital investment plan; provide strategic leadership and oversight of plant engineering, equipment performance, reliability initiatives, and capital improvement projects that align with business priorities and integrate safety and environmental considerations.
* Direct the team in the development and effectiveness of preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs.
* Provide executive oversight of EHS programs and ensure compliance with applicable OSHA, EPA, state, local, and other regulatory requirements.
* Support effective safety inspections, regulatory audits, incident investigations, corrective actions, and ongoing risk-reduction initiatives.
* Champion the use of structured problem-solving, root cause analysis, 5S, and other appropriate improvement methodologies.
* Foster a culture of respect, teamwork, ownership, continuous learning, and personal accountability.
* Demonstrate and reinforce the company's Core Values: **Reliable, Improving, Fair, and Caring.**

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Directly manages functional leaders. Performs managerial responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws, such as recruitment, selection, training, goals, performance expectations and accountability, compensation management.

 **QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline required; Chemical Engineering strongly preferred. MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing and operations leadership experience, including at least five years leading managers and multiple operational functions.
* Significant leadership experience in specialty chemical manufacturing, batch processing, or a comparable process manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
* Demonstrated responsibility for managing and improving cost optimization with a multi-million-dollar operational budget in manufacturing operations, engineering, maintenance, equipment reliability, capital projects, and resource allocation.
* Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment with strong safety, environmental, and process compliance requirements.
* Proven experience developing and executing operational improvement initiatives with measurable business results.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams and managing competing operational priorities in a manufacturing plant.
* Support change management and transactional integrity within the new ERP, Microsoft Dynamics - D365.
* Expertise in methodologies like Lean or Six Sigma to streamline plant throughput and reduce waste.
* Exhibits solid judgement along with decision making skills.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills as well as interpersonal, analytical and presentation skills.
* Must read, speak and write English fluently.
* Strong attention to detail with solid organizational and planning skills.
* High degree of professional integrity, ethics and confidentiality.
* Ability to learn company ERP. Requires advances proficiency with MS Office suite i.e. Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, etc.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

* Base salary range $209,000-235,000, plus management incentive bonus plan
* BCBS of Illinois Medical & Dental. Vision Service Plan.
* 401(k) Savings Plan + generous company match
* Paid time off with 11 annual Holidays
* Disability, Family, & Military Leave
* Life Insurance, Identity Protection, and more!

Relocation assistance is not available. Must be authorized to work in the U.S.

Daubert Chemical Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer: Disability/Veteran.

role.title: Director of Manufacturing
role.description:
***Ready to lead a function, not just a shift? This is your next step.***

American Armor Gloves makes high-quality nitrile gloves here at home in South Carolina. Healthcare workers, first responders, and essential workers across the country rely on what we build. Our purpose is simple: **We strengthen America by building quality protection at home.**

We're a lean, growing manufacturer scaling toward 320–350 people, and we've spent the past year building the foundation for that growth: a redesigned organization, a clear vision with quarterly milestones, defined leadership roles, and a new leadership and compensation architecture. Manufacturing is the heart of that growth, and we need a leader ready to own it.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The Director of Manufacturing is one of the most essential roles in our company. You'll own the end-to-end performance of our Manufacturing department, turning business plans into consistent, safe, high-quality production results.

This role is built for an accomplished Manufacturing Manager who is ready to take the next step. You've proven you can run a strong operation. Now you're ready to **lead through systems and leaders rather than personal effort on the floor**, and to build a manufacturing function that performs at a high level no matter which team is on shift.

Reporting to our VP of Operations, you'll be the bridge between enterprise strategy and shift-by-shift execution. You'll set the systems, build the leaders, and own the results.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* **Own manufacturing performance.** Deliver results across safety, quality, OEE, throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, scrap, and downtime through accountable leaders and strong systems.

* **Build repeatable production systems.** Design shift handoffs, accountability routines, labor deployment standards, and scheduling so performance never depends on heroics.

* **Lead and develop your Shift Manager team.** Coach your Shift Managers as leaders, not only as production operators, and build the next generation of manufacturing leadership.

* **Integrate compounding and batching.** Keep material availability, formulation compliance, and production demand aligned and well governed.

* **Drive continuous improvement.** Lead projects that reduce waste, improve workflow, raise OEE, and close performance gaps, in partnership with Process Engineering.

* **Partner across the business.** Work side by side with Quality, Process Engineering, Maintenance, Logistics, and People & Culture to remove barriers to production.

* **Build workforce capability.** Own training plans, manufacturing career pathways, and engagement so our workforce is ready to support growth.

**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**

You'll set daily and weekly production priorities, deploy labor across shifts, manage Shift Manager performance, and direct improvement projects within manufacturing. You'll shape manufacturing KPI targets, capacity planning, equipment needs, and staffing structure through your recommendations to the VP of Operations. You'll lead Shift Managers, Production Planning, and Batching/Compounding leadership, with a frontline team of Production Supervisors and Manufacturing Associates across multiple shifts.

**A REAL CAREER PATHWAY**

We grow leaders deliberately, and this role is designed as a launch point, not a ceiling. Our leadership framework defines exactly what it takes to grow from functional leadership into executive leadership, and we invest in getting high performers there.

* **Where you go next.** The Director of Manufacturing is a direct pathway to VP of Operations or other senior operations leadership, based on demonstrated enterprise judgment, cross-functional partnership, and the strength of the leadership bench you build.

* **How you get there.** Expect direct mentoring from the VP of Operations, exposure to enterprise planning and capital decisions, cross-functional visibility, and formal leadership development.

* **A clear standard.** Your growth is measured against the same competency framework used for job descriptions, performance reviews, and succession planning, so you always know where you stand and what comes next.

* **Visibility at the top.** Our annual bench-strength review puts strong leaders on the executive team’s radar early.

**WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW**

* **Essential to the mission.** Every glove we ship runs through the function you lead.

* **Build, not just run.** Our organization is lean and still forming, so you'll shape systems and standards that scale with the business.

* **A clear operating rhythm.** A shared vision, quarterly milestones, and a common scorecard keep leaders aligned and connect your work to company priorities.

* **Leave a legacy.** You'll develop Shift Managers into future Directors and Supervisors into future Shift Managers, building a team that carries the company forward.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, Business, or a related field, or equivalent progressive leadership experience

* 8–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership in a high-volume environment

* Proven success leading multiple shifts and developing frontline leaders

* A track record of owning department performance through KPIs, systems, and accountable leadership

* Strong cross-functional partnership with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and HR

* Solid knowledge of OSHA safety requirements and manufacturing quality systems

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, ERP/MRP systems (NetSuite preferred), KPI dashboards, production scheduling, and QMS

**Bonus points for:** experience in medical device, PPE, chemical processing, or FDA-regulated manufacturing; Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement practice; ERP implementation; and leading through growth and scale.

**HOW YOU LEAD**

You lead safely, every shift, not only when incidents happen. You hold leaders accountable through systems, not by stepping in for them. When something breaks, you fix the system, not just the shift. You raise problems early and directly. You treat Quality, Engineering, and Maintenance as partners, and you understand how manufacturing affects the entire business.

**READY FOR YOUR NEXT STEP?**

If you're a Manufacturing Manager ready to own a function, build leaders, and grow into enterprise leadership with a company that's scaling with purpose, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today.

*American Armor Gloves is an equal employment opportunity employer and does not discriminate against employees or job applicants on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, mental or physical disability of a qualified individual, veteran or military status, pregnancy, marital status, familial status, genetic information, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state or local law.*

role.title: Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch
role.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

**LOCATION:** Remote with Travel

US Valve is growing rapidly, driven by critical customer demand in data center and other high-growth markets, creating increasingly complex new product development programs with multiple manufacturing paths. The Director, NPI Program Management & Manufacturing Launch will build and lead the function responsible for taking these programs from business case through stable production, whether manufactured at US Valve, at sister IDEX business units, through external supply chain partners, or through a hybrid model. The role ensures that product design, manufacturing processes, suppliers, supply chain, quality systems, and commercial launch mature together against one integrated plan.

This leader is the single point of accountability for integrated NPI execution and owns end-to-end program results, including schedule, budget, quality, supplier readiness, manufacturing readiness, launch readiness, and ramp performance. The role organizes Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Sales, Finance, BU partners, and external suppliers under one plan. The Director ensures APQP and launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections, are completed on time and to standard. Success isn't design release; it is demonstrating that the full value stream can repeatedly meet customer demand with the required quality, cost, and delivery performance.

The right leader is a builder and results driver with the technical and operational credibility to walk the factory floor, challenge supplier capacity, identify manufacturing constraints, and lead cross-functional recovery. This person establishes the PMO, sets objective gate criteria and metrics, holds functional leaders and partners accountable without direct authority, challenges unrealistic plans, and leads recovery when programs fall behind. The leader will model IDEX values of trust, team, and excellence and build a high-performing team that scales with the business.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Build and Lead the Function***

* Build and lead the Program Management Office (PMO), including organizational structure, staffing plan, talent development, and succession for program and launch managers.
* Establish standard NPD governance—stage-gate/tollgate process, templates, operating cadence, and decision rights—aligned with the IDEX Operating Model.
* Define objective gate-exit criteria and recommend Go, Conditional Go, Hold, or Re-scope decisions based on demonstrated evidence.
* Own the NPD and launch portfolio; prioritize programs using 80/20 principles and align resources to the highest-value customer and growth opportunities.
* Lead executive-level business case, tollgate, and launch-readiness reviews, driving clear decisions on scope, investment, timing, and manufacturing path.

***IDEX Connected Growth and Cross-BU Leadership***

* Drive programs across multiple sister IDEX business units, leveraging IDEX connected growth strategies to share capacity, technology, capabilities, and supply chain.
* Organize and align BU partners, supply chain partners, and internal manufacturing teams into a single integrated execution plan for each program.
* Maintain one integrated critical path and one objective program status across product, supplier, tooling, manufacturing, quality, material, and customer workstreams.
* Lead make, buy, partner, intercompany, and contract manufacturing strategies, including location, capacity, Capex, tooling, staffing, and timing.
* Establish cross-BU agreements, roles, and communication cadences that ensure clear accountability for deliverables across sites and partners.
* Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and Finance to align program strategy with BU and IDEX growth objectives.

***Quality Management and Launch Readiness Across Supply Chain Partners***

* Drive quality management across multiple supply chain partners, sister BUs, and internal sites to ensure consistent standards from development through production.
* Ensure APQP and product launch deliverables are completed on time and to standard, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, process flow diagrams, MSA, capability studies, and first article inspections.
* Partner with Quality and Supply Chain to qualify, develop, and audit suppliers and contract manufacturers, and drive corrective actions to closure.
* Lead launch-readiness and production-readiness gates, ensuring no program advances without required quality, validation, and capacity evidence.
* Separate product validation from production-rate validation; require evidence that the complete value stream can repeatedly achieve required volume, yield, quality, and delivery performance.
* Drive post-launch stabilization, ensuring yield, quality, and delivery targets are met before handoff to steady-state operations.

***Advanced Manufacturing and Capacity***

* Identify and drive advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and technologies needed to meet critical customer demand and scale production.
* Drive readiness of critical processes including welding and joining, filtration media and filter manufacturing, precision machining, assembly, automation, and production test.
* Lead capacity planning and implementation of new processes, including equipment selection, CapEx justification, facility changes, validation, and ramp plans.
* Partner with equipment providers, consultants, and IDEX sites to accelerate process development and transfer best practices.
* Champion design for manufacturability, lean, and continuous improvement in all new product introductions.
* Ensure process qualification, fixtures, tooling, controls, operator readiness, capacity, and rate trials are incorporated before design freeze and production release.

***Metrics, Visibility, and Results***

* Define and own program and launch KPIs, dashboards, and reporting that provide clear leadership visibility across BUs and partners.
* Identify risks early—schedule, resource, quality, sourcing, cost, capacity, and production readiness—and drive countermeasures and recovery plans.
* Challenge unrealistic timelines, resource assumptions, and commitments; escalate decisions and support needs to executive leadership.
* Deliver regular executive updates on portfolio status, risks, decisions, and results.
* Travel domestically and internationally up to 25% to support program execution, supplier engagement, site coordination, customer needs, and equipment-provider activities.
* Perform other related duties and support additional program, PMO, or business needs as assigned.

**KEY PERFORMANCE METRICS:**

* On-time milestone and launch attainment across the NPD portfolio.
* PPAP on-time completion and first-pass approval rate across internal sites, sister BUs, and supply chain partners.
* PFMEA, DFMEA, and control plan completion prior to required gates.
* Launch quality, including first-pass yield, PPM, and escapes at launch and 90 days post-launch.
* Ramp-to-rate performance, including time to target capacity and on-time delivery to customers.
* Critical manufacturing process readiness, including qualification and demonstrated capability for welding/joining, filtration manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test as applicable.
* Program budget, Capex, and product cost performance versus business case.
* Supplier and partner quality and delivery performance on launch programs.
* New product and IDEX-connected growth revenue enabled.
* PMO team capability, staffing, and retention.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Proven leader who has built and scaled a PMO, NPD launch, or program management function in a manufacturing environment.
* undefined
* Deep experience with APQP and product launch deliverables, including PPAP, PFMEA, DFMEA, control plans, and production part qualification.
* Track record driving quality and launch execution across multiple supply chain partners, contract manufacturers, and internal sites.
* Experience identifying and implementing advanced manufacturing processes, automation, and capacity expansions to meet demanding customer ramps.
* undefined
* Demonstrated success leading across multiple business units in a matrixed organization; multi-BU or IDEX experience preferred.
* Strong business acumen in make-versus-buy, multi-site manufacturing, CapEx, tooling, cost, capacity, and risk decisions.
* Builds metrics, dashboards, and operating cadence that drive accountability and measurable results.
* Influential leader able to align executives, BU partners, and suppliers, and hold owners accountable without direct authority.
* Strong executive communicator who turns complex program information into clear decisions and actions.
* Experience with welding/joining, filtration, pneumatics, fluid handling, pumps, compressors, blowers, valves, electromechanical products, precision manufacturing, data center, thermal management, or engineered industrial components preferred.
* Lean, Six Sigma, or PMP certification preferred; working knowledge of the IDEX Operating Model and 80/20 a plus.
* Proficient with project management tools, dashboards, and Microsoft Office applications.

**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, operations, supply chain, or a related field required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* 10+ years of program management, NPD, manufacturing launch, quality, or operations experience, including 5+ years leading teams, with experience in industrialization, supplier development, site transfers, and multi-site manufacturing.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

* While performing the duties of the job, the employee is required to move around and be still, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; talk and hear.
* Employee will occasionally lift up to 35 lbs.
* Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

role.title: Global Director, Operations & Supply Chain - Data Center Solutions
role.description:
**What you’ll do:**
-------------------

The Global Director of Operations provides strategic and functional leadership for manufacturing operations across multiple sites and regions. This role develops and executes operational strategies to deliver world-class performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer satisfaction while supporting business growth and long-term competitiveness.

The Global Director leads and influences across Manufacturing, Operational Excellence, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Materials and Logistics, Capital and Capacity Management, and digital manufacturing. This leader drives operational excellence through the Eaton Business System, continuous improvement, integrated planning, technology enablement, and development of high-performing teams. 
 
**Essential Responsibilities:** 

* Develop and execute the global operations strategy in alignment with business objectives, annual profit plan commitments, growth priorities, and customer requirements.
* Provide strategic and functional leadership across global manufacturing operations to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer satisfaction.
* Lead manufacturing capacity, utilization, capital investment, and footprint strategies to support current business requirements and future growth.
* Drive Integrated Operations across Manufacturing Excellence, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Materials and Logistics, Capital and Capacity Management, and SIOP/S&OE.
* Establish key performance indicators and operating rhythms to monitor operational and financial performance and drive accountability for results.
* Champion Environmental, Health and Safety and build a zero-incident culture with strong leadership and employee ownership.
* Drive a zero-defect culture through effective quality systems, disciplined root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous improvement.
* Lead operational excellence through the Eaton Business System, lean management systems, standard work, and structured problem solving.
* Advance digital manufacturing, automation, analytics, and Industry 4.0 capabilities to improve productivity and competitiveness.
* Partner cross-functionally to support new product introductions, manufacturing readiness, product transitions, and strategic growth initiatives.
* Build organizational capability through talent assessment, succession planning, leadership development, and workforce planning.
* Lead organizational change and build a high-performance culture focused on accountability, engagement, continuous improvement, and customer expectations.
* Ensure compliance with environmental, health, safety, quality, regulatory, and corporate governance requirements.
* Demonstrate leadership consistent with the Eaton Culture Model and Eaton Code of Ethics.

**Qualifications:**
-------------------

**Basic Qualifications:** 

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations/Manufacturing, Business Administration, or a related discipline.
* Minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, supply chain, operational excellence, engineering, quality, or related functions.
* Significant plant leadership and multi-site operations management experience.
* Experience leading complex operations within a large manufacturing organization.
* Demonstrated experience with manufacturing strategy, capacity planning, capital management, footprint optimization, and continuous improvement.
* Strong business and financial acumen with experience managing operational and financial performance.

**Preferred Qualifications:** 

* MBA or advanced degree preferred.
* Experience leading geographically dispersed operations within a global manufacturing organization.
* Prior profit and loss responsibility.
* Experience with lean management systems, SIOP/S&OE, MRP, ERP, and quality management systems.
* Experience with advanced manufacturing, automation, digital manufacturing, and Industry 4.0 technologies.
* Demonstrated experience leading organizational transformation and developing senior operations talent.

**Additional Information**
--------------------------

Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

At Eaton, we strive to provide compensation and benefits that attract, engage, and retain the best talent. This includes competitive pay and a variety of benefit programs for eligible employees. The expected annual salary range for this role is $182000 - $266000 a year. This role is also eligible for a variable incentive program. *Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.*

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.

To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. role.title: Director of Continuous Improvement
role.description:
*Job Seekers can review the Job Applicant Privacy Policy by clicking here (http://ryder.com/job-applicant-privacy-policy) .*

**Job Description** :

**Summary**

The Director of Continuous Improvement will support the AAI (Automotive, Aerospace, and Industrial) vertical. The services are primarily warehousing operations for distribution and inbound to manufacturing operations.

This position supports the Ryder Continuous Improvement culture across the Business Unit by actively promoting and facilitating the use of continuous improvement methods to support new and existing operations.

The Director will lead a team of CI Managers/Leads across the business to influence and drive change through data driven CI, Engineering, and Automation efforts to deliver higher levels of performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost and growth. Effectively leverage data analytics, engineering methodologies, and all Ryder lean tools to enable root cause identification and elimination.

This high influence position will interface with employees at all levels and functions across the business. This individual will work directly with his/her Operational peers in the business units to define and set a strategy for engineering efforts and continuous improvement activities. This position directly reports to the Group or Senior Director of CI with dotted-line reporting to the assigned Groub Director/VP of Operations (Business Unit/Vertical). This individual will work directly with his/her peers and their direct reports in the business units to define and set a strategy for engineering efforts and continuous improvement activities for new and existing operations.

**Essential Functions**

* Directs continuous improvement program and oversees engineering support functions .Supervise a team of continuous improvement Managers and quality professionals. Make employment decisions (hire, promote, coach, development) and manage performance. Develop CI Engineering bench to strategically support the BU/Vertical long term requirements. Manages and assigns CI resources for multiple and complex Supply Chain projects aligned with strategic and growth initiatives. Regularly interacts with Senior Management and/or customer(s).
* Aligns CI initiatives and project objectives to business strategy and prioritizes projects accordingly; includes key stakeholders in process, as required. Facilitate strategic planning (vertical blueprinting) and tactical process improvement events. Lead cross functional team to identify improvement opportunities and works with leadership to prioritize & plan initiatives. Present to executive leadership team on status and results of continuous improvement initiatives. Participate in regular business review session with VP of Operations, SCE team and Customers . Provide regular reports of data and actions to measure progress against strategic business objectives.
* Provide training, coaching, and mentoring: must be able to translate all Ryder Business System concepts and strategic objectives to local situations and help all levels of the organization develop understanding and application of tools for sustainable business improvements. Coach business owners to use Engineering, Data Analysis and Lean methods to achieve operational excellence. Support start-ups, retrofits and expansions including pricing inputs, go-live and steady state certifications.
* Work with vertical leaders to establish continuous improvement goals, and act as a liaison with finance to build continuous improvement budgets and validating actual improvement results. Develops, deploys and maintains account plans for assigned process areas designed to continually improve service offerings through the implementation of recognized engineering, quality, lean standards, continuous improvement strategies and demonstrated best practices. Manage monthly budget review process and financial reconciliation. Interfaces with senior level management to establish standard quality communications and action oriented forums (reviewing /analyzing operational performance, deploy policies and strategies, share best practices)
* Serve as the business owner, establish and regulate the standards for Quality Management Systems based on company and/or industry standards. Oversee internal auditing to ensure regulatory compliance and certification. Facilitate regular Performance Reviews with operations leadership and monitor metrics. Develop/implement strategy to manage scope and meet customer expectations. Support business start-ups, retrofits and expansions including pricing inputs, go-live and steady state certifications. Manage the design, implementation, monitoring and maintenance of the QMS based on established company and/or industry standards. Implement and monitor a standardized corrective action system. Support regulatory compliance and certification requirements. Oversee all functions related to Quality Assurance for a start-up or expansion
* Effective facilitation and execution of Value Stream Maps & Kaizen Events through all stages (A3 charter creation, pre-work identification and completion, delivery of results, regular follow up and follow through on sustainment). Independently identifies process gaps and recommends and leads CI Team to implement process improvement. Manage, track, and report the progress and value of the transformational activities and projects across customer accounts. Direct the assessment, development, implementation, and continuous improvement activities related to the implementation of lean processes across accounts.

**Additional Responsibilities**

* Manage the design, implementation, monitoring and maintenance of the QMS based on established company and/or industry standards.
* Implement and monitor a standardized corrective action system.
* Support regulatory compliance and certification requirements.
* Oversee all functions related to Quality Assurance for a start-up or expansion.
* Oversee internal auditing to ensure regulatory compliance and certification.
* Performs other duties as assigned

**Skills and Abilities**

* Microsoft Office Suite skills with emphasis on Access, Excel and PowerPoint & Visioexpert required
* Data visualization (PowerBI, Tableau) and database programming (SQL, DAX, etc.) intermediate preferred
* Expertise in developing and managing: Leader Standard Work, Visual Management Systems and Management Accountability Systems, Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, 5S/Workplace Organization expert required
* Understanding and experience in core engineering and data analysis functions (slotting, utilization, labor planning, layouts, metrics, etc.) and warehouse design tools such as CAD (e.gAutoCAD); slotting (e.gSlot3D), Predetermined Motion and Time Systems and methods (e.gMOST); Warehouse Management Systems (e.gManhattan Scale), and Labor MgtSystems expert preferred
* Knowledge of Warehouse Management operations, data analytics, Industrial Engineering, warehouse types (ambient, temp control, warehouse layout/ design and Lean methods
* Knowledge of material handling solutions and automation types such as: powered industrial truck (PIT) applications; racking and other storage solution designs, packaging equipment; conveyor and sortation equipment; and other automation solutions (e.gAS/RS)expert required
* Knowledge of Dedicated Services and Managed Transportation Networks
* Knowledge of all available equipment types such as; dry van, temperature control, flat bed, other specialized equipment
* Transportation Design Tools ie; JDA, Appian, Network Design Tools ie; Llamasoft, Transportation Management Systems ie; JDA, OTM, , Mapping Software ie; Tableau expert required
* Knowledge working with HRM systems (e.gWorkday) and associated HR processes
* Knowledge on team member hiring/on-boardingKnowledge of goal setting and performance management/resolutionadvanced preferred

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree required Engineering, Business, Supply Chain
* Master's degree preferred Supply Chain Management or Industrial Engineering
* Ten (10) years or more Fourteen (14) yrs or more in the Distribution, Warehousing and/or Manufacturing, Transportation, Supply Chain Logistics industry required
* Microsoft Office Suite skills with emphasis on Access, Excel and PowerPoint & Visio. expert required
* Data visualization (PowerBI, Tableau) and database programming (SQL, DAX, etc.) intermediate preferred
* Expertise in developing and managing: Leader Standard Work, Visual Management Systems and Management Accountability Systems, Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, 5S/Workplace Organization expert required
* Understanding and experience in core engineering and data analysis functions (slotting, utilization, labor planning, layouts, metrics, etc.) and warehouse design tools such as CAD (e.g. AutoCAD); slotting (e.g. Slot3D), Predetermined Motion and Time Systems and methods (e.g. MOST); Warehouse Management Systems (e.g. Manhattan Scale), and Labor Mgt. Systems. expert preferred
* Knowledge of Warehouse Management operations, data analytics, Industrial Engineering, warehouse types (ambient, temp control, warehouse layout/ design and Lean methods. Knowledge of material handling solutions and automation types such as: powered industrial truck (PIT) applications; racking and other storage solution designs, packaging equipment; conveyor and sortation equipment; and other automation solutions (e.g. AS/RS). expert required
* Knowledge of Dedicated Services and Managed Transportation Networks. Knowledge of all available equipment types such as; dry van, temperature control, flat bed, other specialized equipment. Transportation Design Tools ie; JDA, Appian, Network Design Tools ie; Llamasoft, Transportation Management Systems ie; JDA, OTM, , Mapping Software ie; Tableau. expert required
* Knowledge working with HRM systems (e.g. Workday) and associated HR processes. Knowledge on team member hiring/on-boarding. Knowledge of goal setting and performance management/resolution. advanced preferred
* Lean Six Sigma, required
* American Production Inventory Control Society (APICS) and/or Supply Chain Logistics Certification is preferred
* cPMP, ISO/QMS, preferred

**Travel** - 50% - 70% (Eastern and Central time zones)

This position is remote, when you are not traveling.

**Job Category:** Continuous Improvement

**Our Culture & Commitment** :

At Ryder, you’re trusted to make an impact—while enjoying room to grow and having a voice that’s heard. Our culture is built on respect, collaboration, and shared pride in doing great work rooted in innovation and safety.

Your Voice. Your Success. The Future We Build Together.

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
Advanced Mission Partners, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Science Systems and Applications, Inc (SSAI) seeks a Director of Operations to provide strategic and operational leadership across our aerospace component manufacturing, electronics manufacturing, and engineering services operations. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing daily operations, optimizing manufacturing performance, managing resources, and ensuring the successful delivery of high-quality products and engineering services. This position will play a critical role in driving operational excellence, improving profitability, strengthening customer relationships, and supporting the company's continued growth. 
The ideal candidate will have a strong background in aerospace and defense manufacturing, demonstrated leadership experience, and a proven ability to manage complex manufacturing operations while meeting demanding quality, cost, and delivery requirements.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's Degree (BS) in Engineering, Manufacturing, Business Administration, Project Management, Operations Management, or a related technical discipline.
* 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in program management, project management, manufacturing operations, or engineering.
* At least 5 years of experience managing complex technical or manufacturing programs, preferably within the aerospace, defense, or electronics manufacturing industries.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing operations, managing budgets, and improving operational performance.
* Experience working with aerospace and defense customers, including government agencies, prime contractors, and commercial aerospace organizations.
* Working knowledge of manufacturing processes, engineering development, quality assurance, and supply chain management.
* Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and implementing operational improvement initiatives.
* Strong financial, analytical, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
* Experience in aerospace component manufacturing, electronics manufacturing services (EMS), or precision manufacturing.
* Familiarity with printed circuit board assembly (PCBA), electronic systems integration, and aerospace manufacturing processes.
* Knowledge of AS9100, ISO 9001, IPC standards, and applicable aerospace quality requirements.
* Experience with government contracts, including FAR, DFARS, ITAR, and EAR requirements.
* Familiarity with Earned Value Management (EVM), program financial forecasting, and cost control methodologies.
* Experience using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and project management software, such as Microsoft Project or equivalent tools.
* Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), production transitions, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Demonstrated experience with manufacturing automation, process optimization, and production scalability.

**EOE, including disability/vets**

***Physical Requirements:*** *While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk, and use hands to touch, handle or feel objects, tools or controls. The employee frequently is required to talk and hear and occasionally required to reach with hands and arms and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. Must regularly lift and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and the ability to adjust focus.*

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**PLANT OPERATIONS CAREERS**

Plant Manager

Lead a healthcare laundry plant.

**Where** [City, ST]

**Reports to** General Manager / Regional Vice President

As Plant Manager, you'll lead the full plant (production, maintenance, quality, and logistics) with accountability for safety, budget, and the healthcare customers who depend on clean, safe linen every day.

Why you'll like it here

**Own the plant**

Daily operations, people, budget, and results.

**Lean in action**

Drive improvement with Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma.

**Lead leaders**

Develop supervisors, maintenance staff, and production Associates.

**Healthcare standards**

Run an operation held to OSHA and HLAC requirements.

What you'll own

* Lead and manage the Safety & Health Program within the production environment.
* Lead, motivate, and develop a team of supervisors, maintenance staff, and production associates.
* Oversee daily plant operations, including production scheduling, labor forecasting, staffing, and workflow optimization.
* Drive process improvements using Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Manage plant budget, including labor, maintenance, and operational expenses.
* Oversee inventory management to ensure consistent material supply and stock levels.

What you need

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Business Administration required.
* 5–7 years of leadership experience in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong end-to-end understanding of plant operations, including safety, quality, maintenance, and compliance.
* Proven experience managing P&L, budgeting, payroll, and cost controls.
* Strong problem-solving, analytical, and strategic thinking skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ERP systems.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

**Physical requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and move throughout a manufacturing facility for extended periods.
* Ability to occasionally lift up-to fifty (50) pounds.
* Comfortable working in a plant/production environment.
* Ability to push and pull carts of linen regularly.
* Ability to use required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, and work boots.

**Bonus points**

* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and/or Six Sigma methodologies preferred.
* PMP (Project Management Professional) certification.
* Willing to relocate- GOE flexibility.
* Prior military leadership experience (e.g., Sergeant or above) a plus.
* Familiarity with ISO 14001 / ISO 9001 and GMP standards.
* Experience with manufacturing systems and reporting tools

**We'll teach you:** Our plant network, operating standards, and the support of a national organization.

How we work

Every ImageFIRST Associate lives our four Core Values. These are our required competencies.

**Be Respectful**

Value all we come in contact with.

**Be Remarkable**

Create a positive moment with every interaction.

**Be Safe**

Keep ourselves and those around us safe.

**Be Honest**

Be guided by truthfulness in all we do.

Great work gets noticed

**Everyday recognition**

Coworkers nominate each other for going above and beyond, and those nominations go up in the office for everyone to see.

**All Stars & Council of Excellence**

Each year, Associates who live our values are nominated as All-Stars and earn a certificate and a cash award. Top winners join the Council of Excellence with an additional reward.

Benefits

Weekly pay

Medical, Dental, Vision

Pet, Legal, and Hospital Indemnity Insurance

401(k) with company match

Paid Time Off package

Paid Parental Leave

Tuition Reimbursement

Referral Program

Great company culture

Collaborative team environment

 

**MILITARY & VETERANS**

Served? Your skills fit here.

Officers and senior NCOs who led maintenance, logistics, or production operations: command a plant. Whether you're transitioning out, serving in the Guard or Reserve, or a veteran, we want to hear from you.

* Leading a unit leading supervisors, maintenance, and production
* Readiness and inspections safety, quality, and compliance
* Resource stewardship plant budget and cost control

Guard and Reserve members: we support your service commitments. Tell us your branch and specialty when you apply.

 

Who we are

ImageFIRST is the nation's largest medical-focused linen and laundry provider, serving health systems, hospitals, and outpatient facilities since 1967. We run more HLAC-accredited facilities than anyone else, and 97% of our customers stay with us.

Our mission: improving the lives of our associates, our customers, and the patients they serve.

**If you're ready to own a plant's results, apply today.**

 

**Equal Opportunity Employer / Drug-Free Workplace**

We maintain a drug-free workplace in compliance with state and federal law. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We are fueled by the talent, passion, and diversity of our associates.

role.description:
At Curaleaf, we're redefining the cannabis industry with a strong commitment to quality, expertise, and innovation. As a leading global cannabis provider, our brands—including Curaleaf, Select, and Grassroots—offer premium products and services in both medical and adult-use markets.

Join us at Curaleaf to be part of a high-growth, purpose-driven company that champions corporate social responsibility through our *Rooted in Good* initiative, supporting community outreach and positive change. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, drive innovation, and help shape the future of cannabis.

 

**Title:** Director of Operations 
**Location:** Webster, MA 
**Job Type:** Full Time | Exempt

**Who You Are:**

You're a strategic, hands-on operations leader who knows how to run complex, multi-site supply-side operations from end to end. You bring structure, accountability, and calm to fast-moving environments, with a deep understanding of what it takes to make and deliver at scale—safely, compliantly, and efficiently.

You have a proven ability to lead and coach field operations teams across cultivation, processing, manufacturing, logistics, supply chain, and facilities, while balancing day-to-day execution with long-term operational strategy. You're comfortable owning results and making decisions that directly impact revenue, cost, quality, and team performance.

You partner naturally across the business, working closely with Retail, Wholesale, Marketing, Finance, People & Culture, and Compliance to align priorities and execute against shared goals. You're detail-driven but not rigid, data-informed but people-first, and you continuously look for smarter, more efficient ways to operate.

Above all, you set the standard. You lead with safety, compliance, and quality at the forefront, drive continuous improvement, and build high-performing teams that deliver results while maintaining strong engagement and morale.

**What You'll Do:**

As a Director of Operations, you will lead and oversee all supply-side operations across cultivation, manufacturing, logistics, and facilities, ensuring safe, compliant, and efficient execution of the end-to-end make and deliver process while driving performance, quality, and profitability.

* Lead all day-to-day cultivation, manufacturing, and supply-side operations, planning and monitoring execution to ensure uninterrupted, efficient production
* Lead, develop, and coach site operations leadership teams, setting clear priorities, cascading goals, and driving accountability across all Make and Deliver functions
* Own metrics-based OKRs and drive operational excellence through continuous improvement, including Lean Six Sigma initiatives
* Maintain a strong field presence to support leaders and teams while fostering safe, compliant, and brand-appropriate manufacturing environments
* Oversee production planning, scheduling, logistics, and inventory flow from raw materials through finished goods
* Partner with Commercial, Retail, and Wholesale teams to translate demand, growth, and trends into accurate manufacturing forecasts and execution plans
* Collaborate with regional and national shared services to commercialize new products in the local market
* Ensure controlled substance inventory accuracy, variance resolution, SOX compliance, and adherence to all local, state, and national SOPs
* Maintain quality, safety, and compliance standards to reduce NOEs and non-conformances and ensure cost-effective operations in a GAP and cGMP environment
* Lead training, development, and recurring compliance initiatives across field operations
* Manage vendor and contractor relationships, bills of materials, standard costing, and ERP-related operational processes
* Lead capital improvement projects and oversee commissioning and maintenance of capital equipment
* Own site P&L, OPEX, labor standards, and org structures to control costs, reduce COGS, and improve operating margins

**What You'll Bring:**

* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing and logistics, with leadership experience in FDA-regulated, SQF, or cGMP production environments
* Experience supervising 25+ associates, with a proven ability to build, develop, and retain high-performing teams
* A hands-on, visible leadership style that earns credibility quickly and inspires trust across all levels of the organization
* A demonstrated track record of driving operational efficiencies, improving performance, and leading teams through change
* Strong people leadership, organizational, and collaboration skills, with the ability to build consensus through open dialogue
* The ability to work proactively and independently, bringing innovation, urgency, and ownership to both strategic and tactical goals
* Exceptional communication and negotiation skills, both internally and externally
* High School diploma required

**Even Better If:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, or a related field
* Experience in the cannabis industry
* Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma principles, with practical application experience
* Start-up or high-growth environment experience

* Career Growth Opportunities
* Competitive Pay and Benefits
* Generous PTO and Parental Leave
* 401(K) Retirement Plan
* Life/ Disability Insurance
* Community Involvement
* Referral Bonuses and Product Discounts

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
Chalk Point Generating Station, situated in Aquasco, Maryland, is a key power generation facility with a total capacity of approximately 1,618 MW. The station features a diverse lineup of nine generating units, including seven gas turbines and two steam turbines. This strategic configuration enhances efficiency and reliability, ensuring the station effectively meets regional energy demands.

**Opportunity Summary**

As the Plant Manager at Chalk Point Generating Station, you will oversee plant operations, maintenance, engineering, safety, environmental compliance, and administration to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective performance. Responsibilities include leading a union-represented workforce, managing budgets and contractual obligations, maintaining regulatory compliance, and driving operational improvements. Serving as the primary liaison between NAES and the Owner, you will also coordinate with regulatory agencies and community stakeholders to support facility objectives and maintain positive relationships.

***Your scope of responsibility as Plant Manager includes the following primary functions:***

* Direct plant operations, maintenance, safety, administrative, training, chemistry, NERC compliance, and environmental programs to ensure safe, efficient, and reliable performance while meeting operational targets.
* Oversee planned and forced outages, long-term maintenance planning, and asset reliability initiatives, optimizing schedules, resources, and contractor activities to minimize downtime and costs.
* Administer O&M, energy supply, service, and interconnection agreements while overseeing vendor performance and ensuring contractual compliance.
* Establish staffing, training, and qualification programs that support operational requirements, employee development, and facility objectives.
* Promote a strong safety culture through hazard identification, safe work practices, emergency preparedness, employee accountability, and adherence to established safety standards.
* Ensure environmental and regulatory compliance, including permits, landowner agreements, Management of Change (MOC) processes, and timely submission of required reports.
* Manage plant expenditures, operating and capital budgets, forecasting, procurement, and cost controls to achieve financial objectives and meet O&M Agreement requirements.
* Serve as the primary liaison with the Owner, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders, maintaining positive relationships and supporting community engagement.
* Monitor plant performance, reliability, and operating KPIs while supporting equipment troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and corrective actions to improve operational efficiency.
* Lead union-represented and management personnel through performance management, collective bargaining agreement administration, labor relations, and continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational and workforce effectiveness.
* Maintain reliable attendance and availability to support facility operations and management responsibilities.

* Carry out and complete additional special projects and tasks as needed.

**NAES Safe**

Safety is a core value at NAES, and as a condition of employment, all employees are expected to remain mentally alert and work safely at all times. All NAES managers and supervisors have a direct and important role in ensuring that all work is performed in a healthy and safe manner. Effectiveness in carrying out this responsibility is part of the evaluation of each Supervisor’s performance.

**Working Relationships**

The Plant Manager reports to the Operations Director and supervises the managers, technicians, and Plant Administrator. The Plant Manager is the single point of contact between NAES and the Owner on all matters pertaining to the operation, maintenance, and commercial management of the plant.

**Physical Requirements and Working Conditions**

Physical requirements include standing for extended periods of time, climbing stairs and ladders, working from elevated platforms and walkways at varying heights, and routinely lifting up to 50 pounds.

Power plant environment that may involve entering confined spaces, crawling through narrow areas, and handling hazardous materials, with exposure to fumes, extreme temperatures, and noise. Work may include high heat near equipment and varying outdoor weather conditions.

Some duties may require the use of protective equipment, which can include hard hats, safety glasses, and eye protection, air masks/respirators, ear protection, chemical suits, flame-resistant clothing (FRC), hot gloves, high-voltage protective gear, and fall protection. Fit testing for respirators may be required. Strict smoking restrictions apply in and around the facility.

**Fitness for Duty**

All employees will participate in the Fitness for Duty Program. This program includes a post-offer physical examination and drug screening and post-employment random drug screening.

**Work Schedule**

The Plant Manager works a standard Monday to Friday day-shift schedule. This position will require extended hours, flexible shifts, weekends, and holidays as needed to support plant operations and business needs and may also require callout availability. Depending on the position, on-call status may or may not apply.

Some travel may be involved to participate in Manager, Owner, User Group, or other offsite meetings.

**Compensation**

This position offers an annual base salary ranging from $214,000 to $250,000 and includes eligibility for an annual performance bonus.

**Professional Experience and Leadership Competencies**

* A Bachelor of Science degree in engineering or equivalent is desired, providing a strong foundation for understanding the technical aspects of power plant operations and management.

* Previous Plant Manager experience at a gas- or oil-fired power generation facility, or comparable leadership experience overseeing similar industrial operations, is preferred.
* Proven experience supervising technical, supervisory, and union-represented personnel, including collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and labor relations.
* Extensive knowledge of power generation operations, independent power producer business practices, commercial agreements, and contractual requirements.
* Demonstrated proficiency in environmental and regulatory compliance, including applicable NERC requirements, operating and capital budgets, financial controls, and contract administration.
* Strong technical understanding of gas and steam turbine operations, outage management, equipment reliability, root cause analysis, and long-term maintenance planning.
* Effective leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage employees, senior management, Owners, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders.
* Results-oriented approach to problem-solving, workforce development, emergency preparedness, change management, and continuous improvement across operational and financial functions.
* Must possess a valid, unrestricted U.S. driver’s license and ensure it remains in good standing at all times.

**About NAES**

NAES Corporation is a leading provider of operations, maintenance, and engineering services for energy facilities. We serve clients across the power generation, oil and gas, and renewable energy sectors throughout North America and internationally, supporting the full life cycle of power generation and other industrial facilities.

NAES is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. Employment decisions are based on merit and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability, military status, USERRA-protected status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

#### **Experience**

Preferred

* Previous Plant Manager experience at a gas- or oil-fired power generation facility, or comparable leadership experience overseeing similar industrial operations, is preferred.
* Proven experience supervising technical, supervisory, and union-represented personnel, including collective bargaining agreement administration, grievance resolution, and labor relations.
* Extensive knowledge of power generation operations, independent power producer business practices, commercial agreements, and contractual requirements.

* Strong technical understanding of gas and steam turbine operations, outage management, equipment reliability, root cause analysis, and long-term maintenance planning.
* Effective leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage employees, senior management, Owners, regulatory agencies, and external stakeholders.
* Results-oriented approach to problem-solving, workforce development, emergency preparedness, change management, and continuous improvement across operational and financial functions.

#### **Education**

#### **Licenses & Certifications**
